articles.title: Burn Management in Disasters.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Burn disasters are uncommon but uniquely resource-intensive mass casualty events, requiring prolonged multidisciplinary care that can rapidly exhaust the limited number of verified burn centers and beds. This article reviews the epidemiology and injury patterns of burn disasters, burn-specific triage and transport principles, and system-level planning built on regional burn networks. It examines the American Burn Association's role in center verification, regional response plans, and national burn bed capacity monitoring, alongside federal support mechanisms. Acute resuscitation, damage-control operative strategies, temporary wound coverage, workforce augmentation, and pediatric considerations are addressed, together with ethical decision-making, long-term recovery, and emerging technologies.

articles.title: Arthrocentesis.
articles.journal_full: The Medical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Arthrocentesis aspirates synovial fluid from a joint for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes in joint pain and effusion, evaluating inflammatory, infectious, crystalline, osteoarthritic, and hemorrhagic disease and enabling intra-articular injection. This review presents a generalizable, stepwise technique-consent, time-out, preparation, anesthesia, aspiration, injection-adaptable by joint. Safety points include low anticoagulation bleeding risk, prioritizing septic arthritis over prosthetic-seeding concerns, and avoiding anisotropy. We detail ultrasound guidance, in-plane and out-of-plane approaches, and estimating needle angle from targetdepth- to-distance ratio. Joint-specific landmark and ultrasound techniques cover shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, and ankle. Ultrasound improves accuracy, reduces pain, and builds confidence for clinicians managing joint diseases.

articles.title: Head injury hospitalisation among people aged ≥65 years in New South Wales, 2015-2022: trends and outcomes for residents of aged care facilities.
articles.journal_full: Australian health review : a publication of the Australian Hospital Association

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe trends in head injury hospitalisation among people aged ≥65 years in New South Wales, Australia, from 2015 to 2022, and to compare the treatment and outcomes of residential aged care facility residents with those of other patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective population-based study of emergency department presentations admitted with head injury, using linked emergency department, admitted patient and death registration data. Injury severity was estimated from the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision, Australian Modification codes. Trends in age-specific admission rates were tested using Poisson regression and 30-day mortality using multivariable logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 30,006 admissions were identified. Between 2015 and 2022, admission rates fell from 24.2 to 17.6 per 10,000 among people aged 65-84 years (relative decrease 27.1%, 95% CI 22.8-31.2%) and from 83.8 to 63.3 per 10,000 among those aged ≥85 years (24.5%, 95% CI 18.3-30.2%), with declines before 2020. Population rates of neurosurgery showed no significant trend, whereas long-stay admissions increased from 4.6 to 7.5% (P for trend <0.001). Residential aged care facility residents (n = 2490) had similar proportions with severe or critical head injury, but fewer intensive care admissions (1.53 vs 10.08%) and neurosurgical procedures (1.45 vs 8.09%), and higher 30-day mortality (23.21 vs 14.76%; adjusted odds ratio 2.16, 95% CI 1.91-2.44).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Head injury admissions among older people in New South Wales declined from 2015 to 2022, beginning before the COVID-19 pandemic, whereas prolonged admissions increased. Residential aged care facility residents received less intensive treatment and had twice the adjusted odds of death at 30 days, supporting early goals-of-care discussions in their care.

articles.title: Prehospital Tourniquet Use in Rhode Island: High Rates of Unjustified Application with Low Complication Rates.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Prehospital tourniquet placement has expanded from its initial use in combat settings to civilian trauma care. Educational efforts over the past decade for both laypeople and first responders have popularized the use of tourniquets in trauma scenarios. While tourniquets reduce mortality in severe extremity hemorrhage, concerns persist regarding overuse and inappropriate application. We evaluated the appropriateness and outcomes of prehospital tourniquet use at a Level I trauma center.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All patients with prehospital tourniquet application who were cared for at Rhode Island Hospital, a large Level 1 trauma center, between 2018 and 2024 were identified using the institution's trauma registry. Structured chart review and data analysis explored variables related to the justification of tourniquet placement and patient outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 232 patients met the inclusion criteria. Tourniquet utilization increased over the study period without a significant change in appropriateness. Patients with justified tourniquets had higher injury severity, greater physiologic instability (including lower blood pressure and higher shock index), and were more likely to require operative intervention and blood transfusion (p<0.05); 69.4% of the tourniquets placed were unjustified. Despite high rates of unjustified tourniquet placement, there were no significant differences in mortality, complications (including compartment syndrome and nerve palsy), or disposition between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prehospital tourniquet application was frequently unjustified but was not associated with increased complications or mortality in this cohort. While a permissive approach to tourniquet use appears safe, high rates of inappropriate application highlight the need for advanced or modified tourniquet education for first responders and laypeople.

articles.title: Seasonal Variation in Deaths Associated With Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease in the United States, 1999-2024.
articles.journal_full: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) mortality has risen sharply in the United States, but whether ALD-associated deaths vary by season, and whether any seasonal pattern exceeds that of general mortality, is unknown.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using CDC WONDER data, we constructed a monthly series (January 1999 to December 2024) of deaths among adults with ALD (ICD-10 K70.0-K70.4, K70.9) recorded as a multiple cause of death. Negative binomial harmonic regression with a month-length offset, a spline secular trend, and autocorrelation-robust standard errors estimated relative seasonal amplitude and peak timing, overall and by age, sex, region, urbanicity, place of death and race/ethnicity. We tested changes across study eras and pandemic periods, repeated analyses for underlying-cause deaths, and compared ALD with all-cause and non-alcohol chronic liver disease mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 606 017 ALD-associated deaths, deaths per day were highest in January (8.85% of the per-day total) and lowest in May (7.99%). At the January peak, the death rate was 4.22% (95% CI, 3.28-5.16) above the trend-adjusted mean. Seasonality did not differ between 1999-2010 and 2011-2024 (4.55% vs. 4.21%; p = 0.21), was disrupted in 2020-2021, and was stronger in 2022-2024 (6.56%). Findings were similar for underlying-cause deaths (4.15%). Relative amplitude was lower than that of all-cause (8.68%) and non-alcohol chronic liver disease mortality (5.82%). It was largest for outpatient/emergency department deaths (10.47%) and adults aged ≥ 65 years (8.29%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ALD-associated deaths in the United States follow a modest, stable winter-predominant pattern that largely reflects the background seasonality of mortality rather than an ALD-specific winter excess.

articles.title: An Adolescent Boy With Left Knee Pain During a Basketball Game.
Adolescent Girl With Upper Abdominal Pain.
Man With Right Eye Pain and Visual Loss.
Young Child With a Rash.
Woman With Sudden Painless Visual Loss.
A Teenage Boy With Abdominal Contusion.
Wide-Complex Tachycardia at 39 Weeks Pregnancy.
Management of Traumatic Pneumothorax in the Emergency Department: A Two-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe clinical characteristics, initial emergency department (ED) management strategy (conservative or chest drain) and outcomes of patients who present to the ED with traumatic pneumothorax.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of patients aged 14 years and older with an ED diagnosis of traumatic pneumothorax between January 2023 and March 2025 in two EDs. Pleural intervention was defined as needle decompression, thoracostomy, or chest drain. Descriptive data are reported, and logistic regression was used to identify predictors of ED-initiated chest drain insertion.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 339 eligible patients, 50 had a pre-hospital pleural intervention, of which 27 had chest drains inserted to formalise (finger) thoracostomy or needle decompression. A further 58 patients received an ED-initiated chest drain, for a total of 85 ED chest drains (25.1%). Of the 231 (68.1%) who were initially managed conservatively, 53 received a drain during their hospital stay, primarily as part of surgical management. The majority (71.9%) of drains were large-bore (≥ 24 Fr). Predictors of ED-initiated pleural drainage were: pneumothorax size > 35 mm (aOR 41.0, 95% CI 16.4-102) and presence of haemothorax (aOR 6.3, 95% CI 2.5-15.8). Thirty-six drained patients (22.8%) had a recorded complication. In-hospital mortality was 5.6%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Two-thirds of patients with traumatic pneumothorax were initially managed without drainage before departing the ED. Later drainage frequently reflected operative or broader trauma management rather than clinical deterioration. Pneumothorax size and haemothorax were independent factors associated with ED-initiated drainage. The predominance of large-bore drains and frequency of complications identify opportunities for structured selective management and drain-selection pathways.

articles.title: Left Without Treatment: An Observational Comparative Analysis of Emergency Department Patients Who Did Not Wait and the Treated Cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients who leave the Emergency Department (ED) before receiving care, known as Did Not Wait (DNW), pose potential safety risks that may reflect system pressures. Understanding differences between DNW patients and those who remain for care can inform strategies to reduce adverse outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A quantitative comparative observational study, guided by the STROBE checklist, was conducted in a quaternary ED in Victoria, Australia, comparing DNW patients with those who received treatment.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 37,137 presentations, 1064 (2.9%) were DNW, while 36,073 (97.1%) were treated. DNW patients were younger than treated patients (median age 37 vs. 46 years; p < 0.001), and more likely to be triaged to lower acuity categories (p < 0.001). Nevertheless, 36.4% of DNW patients were triaged as Australian Triage Scale Category 3. Compared with busy conditions severe overcrowding was associated with more than double the odds of DNW (AOR = 2.53; 95% CI: 1.99-3.24; p < 0.001), while dangerously overcrowded conditions increased the odds more than 15-fold (AOR = 14.99; 95% CI: 10.15-22.05; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Study findings suggest that extreme crowding, rather than patient characteristics, is the principal determinant of DNW. These shifts focus from descriptive patient profiling towards interpreting DNW as an indicator of system performance.

articles.title: Changes in the Number of Patients With Drug Overdose due to Deliberate Self-Harm Transported to the Hospital Emergency Department During the Past 12 Years.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Recently, over-the-counter (OTC) drug overdoses have increased. This study aimed to clarify the clinical characteristics and temporal trends of acute drug overdose and explore effective countermeasures in emergency medical settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included patients admitted to our hospital for acute drug overdose due to deliberate self-harm between January 2012 and December 2023. Data collected from medical records included sex, age, ingested substances, implementation of advanced interventions, and outcomes. Cases were categorized as prescription drugs only or OTC drugs present. Comparisons were made before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Severe cases were defined as those requiring advanced interventions; psychiatric care history was assessed in severe cases.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 1676 included patients (mean age 37.8 years), 74.4% used only prescription drugs, 15.0% used only OTC drugs and 5.1% used both. OTC drug-involved cases increased significantly from 15.7% before to 29.7% after the COVID-19 pandemic (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients aged 10-29 years also increased significantly (p < 0.001), as did their OTC drug use (p < 0.001). Severe cases accounted for 8.2% (n = 137) and 12 deaths (0.7%). The proportion of severe cases did not differ significantly between groups. Among the severe cases, psychiatric care history was more frequent in the prescription-only group (90.9%) compared to the OTC-involved group (54.5%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Since 2019, a marked increase in OTC drug overdoses among younger individuals has been observed. Emergency departments should play a key role in initiating multidisciplinary, community-based support systems to prevent recurrence.

articles.title: Ru-Modified High-Entropy NiFeCoMo-Layered Double Hydroxide With Boosted Electronic Modulation Toward Efficient and Long-Durable Oxygen Evolution.

abstract.text: High-entropy materials (HEMs) present a transformative approach to electrocatalysis, leveraging entropy-driven stabilization and multielement synergies to enhance performance. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs), with their tunable compositions and versatile layered structures, serve as an ideal host for constructing high-entropy catalytic systems. In this work, we report a high-entropy NiFeCoMoRu-LDH electrocatalyst synthesized via a one-step hydrothermal method on nickel foam. The incorporation of Ru, combined with the high-entropy effect, induces synergistic electronic modulation and significantly improves lattice stability. The resulting NiFeCoMoRu-LDH electrode exhibits outstanding oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity, achieving a low overpotential of 276 mV at 100 mA cm-2 and a Tafel slope of 46.7 mV dec-1 in KOH. More importantly, it demonstrates exceptional durability, maintaining stable operation for 500 h at 100 mA cm-2 in KOH. Under industrially relevant conditions of alkaline water splitting, the catalyst sustains 100 h of continuous electrolysis at 1000 mA cm-2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) configuration.

articles.title: Comparing Bristow and Latarjet procedures for anterior shoulder instability in competitive rugby players: a unique within-subject clinical analysis.
articles.journal_full: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Anterior shoulder instability is a significant concern in collision sports like rugby, often requiring surgical intervention. The Bristow and Latarjet procedures are commonly performed coracoid transfer techniques alongside Bankart repair; however, direct comparisons of their clinical outcomes within the same individuals remain unexplored. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of the Bristow and Latarjet procedures in competitive rugby players who underwent both surgeries on contralateral shoulders. We hypothesized that the Bristow procedure would yield superior patient-reported outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Between 2010 and 2022, 503 shoulders underwent coracoid transfer procedures with Bankart repair. Of these, 10 rugby players (20 shoulders) who received the Bristow procedure on one shoulder and the Latarjet procedure on the other were retrospectively investigated. Clinical assessments included postoperative range of motion, clinical scoring outcomes (American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons, Rowe score for instability of the shoulder, Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index (WOSI) , and satisfaction rate), recurrence rates, residual apprehension, and pain requiring injection treatment more than 2 years postoperatively, which were compared between 2 procedures. Additionally, postoperative graft healing and resorption were analyzed using computed tomography scan.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Both procedures led to significant improvements in clinical scores. However, the WOSI index at final follow-up was significantly better on the Bristow side (96 ± 100 vs. 373 ± 376, P = .014). Specific WOSI subdomains, particularly those related to physical symptoms and emotional factors, showed superior scores on the Bristow side. Only on the Latarjet side, an earlier return to play was statistically associated with a worse WOSI index. No recurrence was observed on the Bristow side, whereas 2 cases of subluxation occurred on the Latarjet side. Computed tomography evaluation revealed higher coracoid graft resorption rates on the Latarjet side.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Bristow procedure resulted in superior WOSI index scores compared to the Latarjet procedure within the same individuals among competitive rugby players.

articles.title: Factitious Disorder Presenting as Recurrent Aortic Emergencies: A Case Report.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of case reports

abstract.text: BACKGROUND Factitious disorder, historically known as Munchausen's syndrome, is a psychiatric condition characterized by the intentional fabrication or induction of symptoms without obvious external incentives. Patients frequently present with dramatic, medically convincing concerns that can mimic life-threatening illnesses and prompt extensive diagnostic evaluations. Although hemorrhagic presentations have been described, presentations mimicking catastrophic vascular disease are uncommon and pose unique challenges for emergency medicine and vascular teams. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man with a subsequently documented diagnosis of factitious disorder repeatedly presented to multiple hospitals with dramatic hematemesis concerning for an aortoenteric fistula. Over an 8-year period, he underwent multiple diagnostic evaluations and several aortic interventions, including endovascular aortic repair and later explantation, despite repeated studies showing no aortoenteric pathology. In 2024, he developed bilateral renal artery occlusions secondary to focal aortic dissection requiring emergent stenting. A psychiatric evaluation at an outside institution ultimately diagnosed Munchausen syndrome. Recurrent presentations across healthcare systems, repeatedly negative diagnostic evaluations, inconsistent objective findings, and family-reported discovery of vials containing a red blood-like fluid provided additional evidence concerning for deliberate symptom fabrication. CONCLUSIONS This case report shows how factitious disorder can mimic life-threatening vascular disease. While urgent pathology must be excluded, recurrent high-acuity presentations accompanied by inconsistent objective findings should prompt cross-institutional record review, multidisciplinary evaluation, and broader diagnostic consideration to prevent unnecessary procedural escalation and iatrogenic harm, facilitate earlier diagnostic recognition, and support appropriate psychiatric intervention.

articles.title: Outpatient Referral After Adolescent Sexual Health Emergency Department Visits Improves Follow-Up.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To evaluate which methods of outpatient referral during pediatric emergency department (ED) visits for sexual health are associated with increased follow-up among adolescents otherwise at risk of being lost to care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-institution retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients 14-20 years-old who underwent testing for any sexually transmitted infection during ED visits between 1/1/2018 and 12/31/2018 and were discharged home, excluding pregnant patients or those presenting following sexual assault. The primary outcome was any follow-up within 6 months of the index ED visit. The primary independent variable was referral at discharge. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,152 patients (median age 17 years; 76% female), 73% received a referral, and 36.5% were seen in follow-up within 6 months of the index visit. Referrals specifying time frame for follow-up were associated with increased follow-up (odds ratio [OR] 5.9, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.2-8.4), whereas "as needed" referrals were not. In multivariable modeling, attending a follow-up visit was associated with referral (adjusted OR [AOR] 3.6, 95% CI 2.5-5.2), female sex (2.74, 95% CI: 1.90-3.95), and prior preventive care (4.42, 95% CI: 3.36-5.81). Although associated with having follow-up visits, referrals were not associated with contraception initiation or decreased return to the ED within 6 months of the index visit.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Referral to outpatient care was associated with increased follow-up among adolescents with sexual health needs, particularly when referrals specified a follow-up time frame. Pediatric EDs should standardize discharge processes to include specific and consistent outpatient referrals.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Predictors of Severe Anaphylaxis in Infants and Toddlers: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.journal_full: International archives of allergy and immunology

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Anaphylaxis in infants and toddlers is increasingly recognized, yet knowledge on its clinical characteristics and predictors of severe disease remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the demographic, clinical, and immunological characteristics of anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months and to identify factors associated with severe anaphylaxis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included 68 children aged 0-36 months diagnosed with anaphylaxis at a tertiary pediatric allergy center. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, and outcome data were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with severe anaphylaxis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median age at presentation was 13.0 months (interquartile range [IQR], 7.0-23.0), and 58.8% of patients were male. Food was the leading trigger (80.9%), with tree nuts, hen's egg, and cow's milk being the most common allergens. Skin involvement was the predominant manifestation (94.1%), followed by respiratory and gastrointestinal involvement (both 57.4%). Respiratory involvement was more frequent in females, whereas gastrointestinal manifestations predominated in males. Non-atopic children had significantly higher rates of severe anaphylaxis, cardiovascular involvement, and multisystem reactions than atopic children. Non-food triggers were associated with a more severe clinical course. In univariate analysis, atopy was associated with lower odds of severe anaphylaxis, whereas drug-induced reactions had higher odds of severe disease than food-induced reactions. Neither atopy nor trigger category remained independently associated with severity after multivariable adjustment. All patients received intramuscular epinephrine under protocolized emergency care, and no biphasic reactions or fatalities occurred.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months has distinct clinical characteristics. Although food remained the predominant trigger, non-food triggers and the absence of atopy were associated with a more severe clinical phenotype. However, no baseline atopic or trigger-related factor independently predicted severe anaphylaxis after multivariable adjustment, highlighting the challenges of risk stratification in this age group.

articles.title: A Survey of Emergency Department Patients About Outpatient Health and Wellness Coaching.

abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) patients often have chronic conditions and could benefit from health and wellness coaching. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of adult ED patients from May-July 2026 to assess interest in post-ED health and wellness coaching from 0 (not interested) to 10 (extremely interested). Participants were told coaching would likely cost $100 each for 12 virtual or in-person sessions. We also assessed which areas of health the participants were interested in, barriers to care, perceived effects on return ED use. We had 137/143 respondents that completed the survey and reported their interest in coaching. Median interest in coaching was 0 (IQR, 0-4) with 70 of 137 (51.1%) selecting 0 (not interested). Higher education (beta = 0.49, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.85, P = .009) and PROMIS-10 Global Mental Health T-score (beta = -0.057, 95% CI -0.108 to -0.005, P = .032) were associated with interest in health and wellness coaching. Only 6.5% felt coaching would reduce a subsequent ED visit. Surveyed respondents were most interested in getting help with weight loss, sleep, healthy eating, exercise, and stress management. Post-ED coaching among surveyed ED patients was low despite interest in lifestyle domains used in coaching.

articles.title: Improving Rates of Screening for Health-related Social Needs in a Pediatric Emergency Department.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: In September 2024, our hospital implemented health-related social needs (HRSN) screening in the pediatric emergency department (PED). We aimed to increase rates of completed HRSN screens from a baseline of 18% in October 2024 to greater than 50% by December 2025.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, we implemented a new workflow that shifted from verbal to paper screening, posted screening posters in the PED, and provided stakeholders with education and weekly updates on screening rates. The primary outcome measure was the percentage of eligible patient encounters with a completed HRSN screen. The secondary outcome measure was the percentage of patients with a completed HRSN screen who requested to be connected with resources. We created statistical process control charts and performed chi-square tests or Fisher's exact tests to assess the associations between demographics and HRSN screen completion status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean screening rate increased from 18% to 40% during the course of 14 months. The mean rate of patients/caregivers requesting connection to resources on HRSN screens increased from 16% to 29%. Patients aged younger than 18 years, Black non-Hispanic patients, Hispanic patients, patients with public insurance, and patients who preferred the Haitian Creole language were less likely to have a completed HRSN screen.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Through our quality improvement initiative, we improved HRSN screening rates in our PED. We observed an increase in the rate of patients/caregivers requesting connections to resources. We could increase these rates in future studies through targeted interventions to engage patient groups that were less likely to complete screening and by improving stakeholder buy-in.

articles.title: Increasing Resident Involvement in Medical Resuscitations in the Pediatric Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Primary care and general emergency providers must recognize critically ill children and initiate life-sustaining interventions, yet trainees report limited experience and low confidence in this domain. The pediatric emergency department (PED) offers an optimal setting to improve resident exposure to pediatric medical resuscitations (MRs). We aimed to increase resident involvement in PED MRs from 45% to 70% during a 6-month period and evaluate the effect on resident confidence in managing critically ill children.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We implemented a disruptive alarm-based alert system and assigned 1 resident per shift to a defined MR-response role. The process measure was alert-system use per 25 MRs; the outcome measure was the percentage of MRs with resident involvement, defined by resident completion of the encounter note per 25 MRs. We assessed change over time using standard rules for special-cause variation. Residents voluntarily completed pre- and postintervention surveys.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Resident involvement in MRs in the PED increased from 45% to 64%. Use of the disruptive alarm increased from 0% to 33%. Residents initially indicated increased confidence in responding to MRs, but this confidence waned over time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A standardized disruptive alert system paired with designated MR roles increased resident involvement in MRs in the PED and may influence resident confidence in managing critically ill children.

articles.title: Interventions for Anxiety Following Spinal Cord Injury: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal_full: Topics in spinal cord injury rehabilitation

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate interventions targeting anxiety symptoms in people with traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI), identify gaps in knowledge, and propose avenues for research.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this systematic review, a research librarian searched for articles published from 1994 to September 6, 2024, in MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. Two independent reviewers selected studies based on the following inclusion criteria: adults with traumatic spinal cord injury; interventions including pharmacological, behavioral, and complementary and alternative medicine; presence of a comparator group; and a primary outcome of anxiety symptom reduction. Reviewers independently assigned a quality score using Hawker's guidelines and evaluated the risk of bias using Cochrane's risk-of-bias tools. Coauthors reconciled disagreements via unanimous consensus.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirteen of the 7927 articles met inclusion criteria representing 12 studies. Investigators evaluated individual and group behavioral interventions including an online mindfulness course and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy. Six of the studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), 3 were non-RCTs, 1 was quasi-experimental, and 2 were matched-control trials. Five studies reported a significant reduction in anxiety symptoms for the intervention versus control groups. Effective interventions included group coping effectiveness training, hyperbaric oxygen therapy combined with traditional Chinese medicine and psychotherapy, and supplemental physical rehabilitation techniques such as home automation training and vibration therapy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Clinicians may consider several interventions that show preliminary evidence of benefit in reducing symptoms of anxiety. Larger trials should compare effectiveness of available interventions and evaluate optimal delivery of interventions in practice.

articles.title: Preoperative roxadustat in major elective noncardiac surgery: a phase 2a randomised clinical trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Postoperative complications remain a leading cause of mortality. Experimental data indicate that roxadustat, a first-in-class prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, reduces ischaemia-reperfusion injury, accelerates wound healing, and enhances survival in sepsis. Therefore, preoperative administration of roxadustat might reduce perioperative organ injury. We examined the perioperative tolerability and the potential for adverse surgical interactions with roxadustat.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this phase 2a, single-centre, double-blind, randomised-controlled pilot trial, 150 patients undergoing major elective noncardiac surgery were allocated to preoperative roxadustat 100 mg or placebo for three alternate-day doses, with the last dose on the operative morning. The co-primary outcomes were preoperative adverse events and postoperative complications meeting standardised endpoint definitions within 30 days.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 148 participants (52 [35.1%] females; median age 65 [range 24-84] yr) receiving at least one drug dose, at least one preoperative adverse event occurred in 21 of 75 (28%) in the roxadustat group and 20 of 73 (27%) in the placebo group (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.50-2.12). No serious adverse reactions occurred. Among 143 participants who proceeded to surgery (52 [36.4%] females; median age 65 [range 26-84] yr), ≥1 complication occurred in 23 of 74 participants (31%) who received roxadustat compared with 21 of 69 participants (30%) who received placebo (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.51-2.10). Days alive out of hospital within 30 days was similar between the groups. The annualised enrolment rate was 90 per year, with high levels of drug compliance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Preoperative roxadustat was feasible in patients having major surgery. Uncertainty remains regarding the safety and efficacy of this intervention.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: www.anzctr.org.au; ACTRN12624000188538.

articles.title: Stable imaging-to-visit ratios mask major shifts toward cross-sectional imaging in emergency departments: A multicenter 10-year study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: The use of medical imaging in emergency departments (EDs) has increased over the past decades, with potential implications for radiology organization and workload. The purpose of this multicenter study was to evaluate temporal trends in imaging utilization associated with ED activity.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted, including 15 hospitals between 2014 and 2023. Imaging examinations requested from EDs were extracted from radiological information systems and analyzed by modality (computed tomography [CT], magnetic resonance imaging [MRI], ultrasound, radiography). ED visits were collected from institutional databases. Trends in imaging volume, imaging-to-ED visit ratios, and patient characteristics were assessed overall and according to center size.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Across the study period, ED visits increased overall (+20%), along with total imaging volume (+18%), while the number of imaging examinations per ED visit showed a slight decrease overall (-2%), with broadly stable imaging-to-visit ratios over time. CT utilization per ED visit increased from 10.9 to 15.8 per 100 ED visits (+45%), with a marked rise in absolute volume (+74%). MRI utilization also increased substantially (from 0.9 to 1.6 per 100 ED visits, +85%), and a rise of +122% in absolute term. In contrast, radiography use decreased (-19% per 100 ED visit), while ultrasound decreased (-9%). Overall directional trends were similar across center categories.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Emergency imaging activity has shifted toward increased use of cross-sectional imaging, particularly CT and MRI, without a marked global increase in imaging per ED visit. This evolution reflects changing diagnostic strategies and has major implications for radiology workload and organization.

articles.title: Swatting, Criminal Responsibility, and Risk in Forensic Psychiatry.
articles.journal_full: The journal of the American Academy of Psychiatry and the Law

abstract.text: Internet and social media use is ubiquitous and pervasive in mainstream culture. This rapid growth has coincided with the emergence of novel antisocial behaviors. One such behavior is swatting, which involves filing false reports of imminent danger to law enforcement, often by people outside of the report's jurisdiction, for the purpose of dispatching a Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) team to the victim's home. This is not a trivial crime; it places the lives of victims and law enforcement officers in danger. In this article, we review swatting and highlight five salient cases. This analysis and commentary provide a guide for forensic psychiatrists on the evaluation of swatting defendants, with a focus on key psycholegal concerns, including criminal responsibility, violence risk, civil litigation, and developmental considerations for adolescent perpetrators.

Autologous transfusion of noncitrated peritoneal blood in horses with haemoperitoneum.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Autologous blood transfusion in acute blood loss into the peritoneal cavity is widely used in small animal and human emergency medicine but is not well described in horses.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the outcomes of autologous transfusion of noncitrated blood from the peritoneal cavity in horses with haemoperitoneum.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective study of clinical records.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data were extracted from records of 19 horses diagnosed with haemoperitoneum in years 2020-2025, treated with autologous transfusions of noncitrated blood collected from the peritoneal cavity. Data on hospitalisation period, amount of transfused blood, number of transfusions, complications, short- and long-term outcomes were collected and analysed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nineteen cases of various aetiology (13 females and 6 males) were included in the study. Horses, aged 3-28 (median age 14), were diagnosed with haemoperitoneum based on transabdominal ultrasonography and abdominocentesis. Clinical findings on initial examination included manifestations of abdominal discomfort, tachycardia, prolonged capillary refill time and pale mucous membranes. All 19 horses underwent autotransfusion of whole noncitrated blood. Total blood volume transfused was 5-38.75 L (median 19.5 L; IQR: 18.5). Rapid clinical deterioration was observed in 3 horses, necessitating euthanasia. The remaining 16 horses (survival rate 16/19) survived until discharge following 3-22 days of hospitalisation (median 8.5 days).

abstract.label: MAIN LIMITATIONS
abstract.text: Retrospective design; heterogeneous, warmblood-oriented population; unbalanced sex distribution in the studied caseload; lack of control group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Autotransfusion of noncitrated blood may be a safe, time-saving, and cost-effective alternative to standard allogeneic blood transfusions and seems to be beneficial for haemoperitoneum treatment in selected haemorrhage cases.

articles.title: Critical Incident Technique to Identify Factors Influencing Acute Stroke Diagnosis.
articles.journal_full: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute stroke (AS) affects nearly 800,000 people/year in the US with diagnostic error occurring in ∼10% of patients. A qualitative methodology, the critical incident technique, was used to understand the diagnostic process for AS among physicians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Emergency medicine and neurology physicians, involved in evaluating suspected AS cases, were invited to take part in an interview using a standardized guide to learn about the (a) information gathered (e.g., history, exam, laboratory and imaging results); (b) relative importance of each type of information; (c) differential diagnoses; (d) factors affecting the diagnostic process. Interviews were conducted by video-conference, audio-recorded, and transcribed. Transcripts were uploaded into qualitative analytic software and inductively and deductively coded by 4 independent coders.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-five physician interviews were conducted, and 300 unique codes were reached by consensus. Codes were grouped into themes and identified 5 AS diagnostic process phases: (1) Evaluation initiation; (2) Information gathering; (3) Initial diagnostic impression (4) Detailed analysis; and (5) Final diagnosis. Barriers and facilitators of each phase were identified.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Findings suggest two key opportunities to improve the AS diagnostic process: (1) developing strategies to gather initial "event" information more rapidly and accurately, including the ability to acquire or confirm information from a witness and (2) reducing distractions and cognitive burden such as through a "sterile cockpit" during the diagnostic process.

articles.title: Incremental predictive value of public surveillance indicators for RSV and influenza hospitalizations in older adults.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To assess whether public surveillance indicators improve forecasts of influenza- and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated hospitalizations among adults aged ≥65 years beyond hospitalization history and seasonality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed U.S. FluSurv-NET and RSV-NET hospitalization rates from October 2018 through July 2026. We compared forecasts based on recent hospitalizations and seasonality with forecasts that also used older-adult emergency department (ED) percentages, all-age laboratory positivity, or national weighted influenza-like illness (wILI). Accuracy was assessed on identical forecast weeks using mean absolute error (MAE) differences and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Additional comparisons used the same historical observations and alternative seasonal curves.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: On 120 RSV forecast weeks, laboratory positivity improved MAE by 0.096 hospitalizations per 100,000 per week (95% CI 0.039 to 0.159). ED alone did not clearly improve forecasts (-0.059; -0.119 to 0.005), nor did ED added to laboratory positivity. On 74 influenza weeks, wILI improved MAE by 0.266 (0.064 to 0.567) under the primary seasonal model. Using the same historical observations preserved these principal findings. RSV laboratory gains also persisted with alternative seasonal curves, whereas the wILI estimate with a more flexible seasonal curve was 0.099 (-0.062 to 0.299).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: All-age laboratory positivity improved older-adult RSV forecasts across the examined seasonal specifications. The one-week influenza wILI increment depended on how seasonality was modeled. ED percentages provided no consistent one-week incremental benefit.

articles.title: Public Health Nurse-Led Infection Control in an Evacuation Center: Lessons from the Eaton Wildfire Response Case Report.

abstract.text: In January 2025, infection control strategies were implemented at an Eaton wildfire evacuation center. Standardized risk assessments, symptom screenings, and surveillance processes were implemented. Systematic daily monitoring of symptoms enabled early identification of respiratory illness (27.9%) and gastrointestinal (GI) illness symptoms (12.4%). This informed real-time decisions on isolation areas, staffing, and sanitation protocols. Despite resource-limited surveillance approaches, implementing public health nursing expertise can effectively support rapid decision-making and health prevention in disaster settings.

articles.title: Presenting Complaints for Children in US Emergency Departments: An Analysis of a Nationally Representative Sample.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine the presenting complaints for children in the emergency department (ED), both overall and within subgroups of age, acuity and pediatric ED status, and to evaluate changes in complaint patterns over time.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: We performed a serial, cross-sectional study using the 2014-2022 National Hospital Ambulatory Medical Care Survey, including ED encounters for children (<18 years). Our variable of interest was patient complaint, evaluated as (a) the chief complaint and (b) all reported complaints. We described the distribution of patient complaints using the Pediatric Emergency Reason for Visit Clusters (PERC) rubric and examined distributions across subgroups. We evaluated changes in complaints over time using survey-weighted logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 277,624,292 ED encounters, the most common chief complaints were fever (37,330,480; 13.4%), extremity injury or pain (30,546,932; 11.0%), cough (22,479,119; 8.1%), abdominal pain (16,867,178; 6.1%), and rash (14,181,775; 5.1%). Fever predominated from infancy through early childhood, whereas extremity injury or pain and abdominal pain became more prominent with increasing age; psychiatric/behavioral complaints emerged notably in adolescence. Fever was most common among immediate and urgent visits, psychiatric/behavioral concerns among emergent visits, extremity injury or pain among semi-urgent visits, and rash among nonurgent visits. Complaint patterns were similar between pediatric and general EDs. Overall findings were similar when considering all reported complaints.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Although the distribution of complaints was similar over time and between pediatric and general EDs, there were differences based on age and acuity. These findings provide a national characterization of patient complaints that inform pediatric readiness and resource planning.

articles.title: Mass-gathering medicine in an era of global mobility and climate stress.
articles.journal_full: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mass gatherings bring globally mobile populations into dense environments, creating infectious, environmental, traumatic, and health-system risks. This review examines an integrated, all-hazards approach to mass-gathering medicine.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a focused narrative synthesis of original studies, systematic and scoping reviews, public-health guidance, and surveillance reports, prioritizing evidence from 2020 to July 2026. Hajj and Umrah were considered alongside other pilgrimages, sporting events, and music festivals. Findings were interpreted by study population, case definition, and denominator.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Evidence from Hajj highlights respiratory symptoms, antimicrobial use, meningococcal vaccination gaps, and severe heat-related risks. Comparisons with sporting events and festivals illustrate the importance of cross-border surveillance, environmental exposures, crowd safety, and accessible on-site care. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneous ascertainment, convenience sampling, inconsistent denominators, and incomplete follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Mass-gathering medicine should operate as a continuously learning public-health system. Priorities include context-specific risk assessment, integrated clinical and environmental surveillance, predefined response thresholds, equitable access to preventive services, and transparent post-event evaluation.

articles.title: Machine learning-supported polytrauma triage decision support: A concept analysis for emergency nursing.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Polytrauma triage requires rapid prioritization under conditions of incomplete information, physiological instability, crowding, and high consequences of error. Machine learning (ML) is increasingly discussed as a means of strengthening emergency triage; however, the concept of ML-supported polytrauma triage decision support remains insufficiently defined for emergency nursing, particularly regarding its temporal and clinical boundaries within the emergency department.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This concept analysis clarifies the meaning, defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, empirical referents, and boundaries of machine learning-supported polytrauma triage decision support.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Walker and Avant's concept analysis method guided the analysis. A structured and traceable literature identification process was used to examine literature on polytrauma, initial emergency department triage, clinical decision support, machine learning in emergency and trauma care, digital nursing decision-making, and artificial intelligence safety. Sources were mapped using a concept-analysis matrix to identify concept uses, candidate attributes, antecedents, consequences, cases, empirical referents, and conceptual boundaries.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Machine learning-supported polytrauma triage decision support was defined as a human-in-the-loop clinical decision support process operating within the initial emergency department triage window, in which ML integrates polytrauma-relevant information available at or immediately before the first triage decision and generates time-critical acuity or near-term deterioration estimates to inform immediate prioritization without replacing clinician judgment. Three core defining attributes were identified: polytrauma-relevant initial-triage data integration, time-critical triage risk or acuity estimation, and human-in-the-loop clinical decision support. Model validation, workflow fit and interpretability, and performance governance were distinguished from defining attributes and positioned as antecedent or implementation conditions and empirical referents for safe clinical use.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The concept is distinct from conventional triage, trauma scoring, post-triage prognostic modeling, generic clinical decision support, and automated decision-making. Clarifying both its defining attributes and its temporal boundary positions ML as a support for the initial emergency nursing triage decision rather than as a substitute for professional judgment or a broader trauma management system.

articles.title: Understanding factors that influence time to surgery for hip fractures in South Africa: A qualitative study using the Model of Pathways to Treatment.

abstract.text: Although early surgery for hip fractures (HF) improves patient outcomes, in South Africa (SA) time to surgery often exceeds recommended durations. We explore factors influencing time to HF surgery in SA to inform interventions promoting earlier access. Data were collected through repeated in-depth interviews with 38 HF patients and their caregivers and 40 healthcare professionals (HCPs) and observations of clinical practice in five hospitals in Gauteng. Findings were informed by the four key "intervals" of the 'Model of Pathways to Treatment'. Appraisal: Personal beliefs that symptoms were due to other causes or that hospital visits were a "weakness", prompted initial self-management. Early care-seeking was prompted by pain intensity and further encouraged by family members. Help-seeking: Timely access to transport was impacted by ambulance shortages, long distances, and safety concerns for paramedics, and thus many patients relied on private transportation. High-impact trauma cases were prioritised over low-impact HF. Diagnostic: Patient pathways varied and were complicated by ambulance shortages and scheduling issues. Administrative requirements (referral letters) slowed referral processes, particularly for patients from outside hospital catchment areas. Caregivers found admission paperwork burdensome, while HCPs viewed it as helpful for coordinating care and avoiding later delays. While hospitals prioritised emergency cases (including HF), HCPs felt streamlining administrative processes could improve time to X-ray. Pre-treatment: Patients and caregivers reported long waits for surgery, with delays leading to complications and further setbacks. Surgeries were often postponed for other "emergencies", with HCPs describing difficulties with managing competing surgical priorities. This study, the first to explore factors that impact time to HF surgery in SA, highlights the agency of patients and caregivers in negotiating access to treatment, and health system processes that help or hinder access. Findings identify key leverage points for interventions targeted at each 'interval' in the care pathway to accelerate access to HF surgery.

articles.title: [Vestibular migraine-an underdiagnosed cause of vertigo? : A retrospective analysis of monocentric routine clinical data].

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In 2012, vestibular migraine was defined by specific diagnostic criteria in an international consensus paper by the Bárány Society and the International Headache Society (IHS) for the first time. Vestibular migraine is one of the most common causes of recurrent vertigo. As vertigo is diagnosed and treated interdisciplinarily by otorhinolaryngologists, general practitioners, neurologists, and emergency physicians, a comprehensive awareness and understanding of the differential diagnosis is essential. However, despite its frequency, vestibular migraine is still little known in clinical practice in Germany.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We aimed to draw attention to the importance of vestibular migraine in a neurologically managed vertigo outpatient clinic. We also aimed to characterize patients with vestibular migraine regarding features of headache migraine.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A descriptive retrospective evaluation of clinical data of the Outpatient West German Headache and Vertigo Center was conducted. Clinical data of patients visiting in 2023, including diagnosis, age, gender, and patient history of migraine symptoms, were analyzed. Due to German regulations, referral from another physician was required for consultation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: With a proportion of 51.6% (n = 259/502) of all patients, vestibular migraine was the most common cause for consulting our tertiary outpatient center for vertigo; 40% of the patients suffering from vestibular migraine had an additional vertigo-related comorbidity. The most common comorbidities associated with vestibular migraine were Menière's disease and benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Moreover, 40% of patients with vestibular migraine reported the presence of aura symptoms.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A greater awareness of vestibular migraine in clinical practice is necessary.

articles.title: Contextualized vs usual cardiopulmonary resuscitation skill stations: a simulation-based, randomized trial.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We aimed to investigate whether training on a contextualized skill station combined with in-bed cardiopulmonary resuscitation instructions improves the number of excellent chest compressions in a simulated in-hospital cardiac arrest scenario compared to a standard table-based skill station.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This randomized, multicenter trial included nurses and nurse assistants from two Danish emergency departments. Participants were trained in chest compressions on a contextualized skill station with the manikin on a bed (intervention) or on a skill station table (control). Participants completed two one-minute sessions with audiovisual feedback, repeated after 2-4 weeks. Skills were assessed in a 2-min in-hospital cardiac arrest scenario 4-8 weeks after the first training session. The primary outcome was the number of excellent chest compressions defined as guideline-compliant depth and rate.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 65 participants. The intervention group training on the contextualized skill station performed more excellent compressions with a median (quartile 1; quartile 3) of 70 (27; 140) vs 23 (2; 93) (p = 0.01) compared to the control group. In addition, the intervention group performed more compressions with guideline-compliant depth (118 (53; 155) vs 78 (16; 127), p = 0.02), and more compressions with guideline-compliant rate (134 (86; 152) vs 58 (22; 134), p = 0.01) compared to the control group. More participants in the intervention group initiated compressions by jumping onto the bed (85%) compared to the control group (43%), p = 0.002. There was no significant difference in time to first compression.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Training on a contextualized skill station with a manikin on a bed significantly increased the number of excellent chest compressions compared to skill station training with the manikin on a table. These findings highlight the importance of integrating clinical factors such as bed adjustments when implementing skill stations for CPR training in emergency departments to facilitate the transfer of skills.

articles.title: Definitive management without prior computed tomography in penetrating versus blunt renal trauma: an observational analysis of diagnostic pathways at a Latin American referral center.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Guidelines, derived mainly from blunt trauma, recommend computed tomography (CT) before managing renal injuries in stable patients. We described, by mechanism, how often renal injuries reached first definitive management without prior CT and the documented circumstances.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort of adults with renal injury at a Colombian referral trauma center (2013-2025). The primary outcome was no CT before first definitive management (nonoperative management, angioembolization or operation). We report exact 95% confidence intervals (CIs), grading source and Firth regression adjusted for instability, positive extended focused assessment with sonography for trauma (eFAST) and admission period.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 160 adults, 34 had penetrating and 126 blunt injuries. No CT preceded first definitive management in 23 penetrating (68%; 95% CI 49-83%) and 13 blunt patients (10%; 6-17%). Of these 23, 22 underwent laparotomy and 18 were unstable or had a positive eFAST. A positive eFAST preceded management without CT in 13 of 14 penetrating and 4 of 33 blunt patients (interaction P = 0.018); without one, penetrating mechanism remained associated with no prior CT (adjusted odds ratio 8.09; 95% CI 2.60-27.15), including stable patients (5/13 vs 5/76). Peritonitis, evisceration and trajectory were not recorded systematically.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Penetrating renal injuries were usually assessed at laparotomy rather than staged by CT, mostly after findings that prompt operation in penetrating trauma; after blunt injury, comparable findings usually led to CT. These observational data support prospective evaluation of CT-guided selection for stable penetrating renal trauma in this setting; they do not show that omitting CT is safe.

articles.title: Digital precision in the trauma bay: a roadmap for AI and robotics in hepato-pancreato-biliary injuries.

abstract.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics are revolutionizing elective hepato-pancreato-biliary (HPB) surgery, yet their integration into the chaotic, time-critical domain of HPB trauma remains an underexplored frontier. This review synthesizes current evidence for these digital technologies across the entire trauma care pathway-from initial triage to postoperative prediction.AI-driven tools for Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (eFAST) and radiography are already maturing, while emerging models for trauma imaging suggest a potential 10-20% increase in sensitivity for subtle biliary and pancreatic injuries based on elective data, though this theoretical advantage requires prospective validation in acute trauma populations. Intraoperatively, while robotics offer superior precision for fine repair, their utility is severely constrained by the reality of trauma; minimally invasive surgery is strictly limited to the narrow subset of patients who maintain absolute hemodynamic stability, as carbon dioxide pneumoperitoneum can critically exacerbate shock in an actively bleeding patient. Furthermore, we highlight that robotics currently cannot replace the rapid, four-quadrant abdominal exploration required for damage control.Postoperatively, we find that AI models must be fine-tuned to account for the unique "lethal triad" of trauma physiology rather than relying on elective datasets. Finally, this review identifies critical systemic barriers, including cybersecurity risks to emergency infrastructure and a regulatory landscape struggling to define liability in autonomous decision-making. By centering on these clinical and logistical realities, this review provides a pragmatic roadmap for bringing digital precision to the chaos of the trauma bay.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided Stellate Ganglion Block for Refractory Electrical Storm and Acute Upper Limb Ischemia.

abstract.text: Electrical storm (ES) and acute upper limb ischemia are life-threatening emergencies in which sympathetic activation may contribute to ventricular arrhythmogenicity and peripheral vasoconstriction. This case series describes the response to ultrasound-guided stellate ganglion block (SGB) in seven patients presenting to the emergency department: four with acute upper limb ischemia and three with refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT)/ES. SGB was performed at the C6 vertebral level using 0.25% bupivacaine (6-8 mL). All patients showed improvement after the procedure. In patients with limb ischemia, pain scores decreased, with improvement in limb warmth, capillary refill, and distal perfusion. In patients with refractory VT/ES, the frequency of VT episodes decreased and hemodynamic stability improved. No major procedural complications were observed. Ultrasound-guided SGB may be considered an adjunctive bedside intervention in selected patients with refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmias or acute upper limb ischemia, potentially serving as a temporizing measure while definitive treatment is being arranged or undertaken.

articles.title: Impact of a community urgent care and primary care center (CAU) on emergency department visits: A before-after analysis in an Italian health district.

abstract.text: BackgroundEmergency Department (ED) overcrowding, frequently driven by low-acuity visits, is a managerial and policy challenge for healthcare systems. In 2023, the Emilia-Romagna Region introduced Community Urgent Care centres (CAUs) to divert low-acuity presentations away from the ED. This study evaluated changes in ED utilization and chief-complaint case-mix associated with CAU implementation in the Forlì district.MethodsA retrospective observational study compared ED access patterns during the first 6 months after CAU activation (June-December 2025) with the corresponding period in 2024. Analyses included daytime visits (08:00-20:00) across 184 matched days. Visits were stratified by triage priority level and chief complaint categories. Paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Pearson's chi-square test.ResultsLow-acuity ED visits significantly decreased during CAU operating hours. TL5 visits declined by 48% (2489 vs 1294; p ≤ 0.001), while TL4 visits decreased by 8% (p ≤ 0.001). Conversely, higher-acuity (TL3-TL1) visits increased by 18% (5474 vs 6457; p ≤ 0.001), only partly explained by direct CAU-to-ED referrals. Significant reductions were also observed in respiratory and trauma-related presentations among low-acuity visits.ConclusionsCAU implementation was associated with reduced low-acuity ED utilization and a concurrent, only partially explained shift in ED case-mix toward higher-acuity complexity. This reduction was consistent with, and among the largest reported in, a region-wide evaluation of the Emilia-Romagna CAU network. While the observational, single-site design limits causal inference, these findings support the potential role of well-integrated community-based urgent care services in redistributing non-urgent healthcare demand.

articles.title: Terminology Without Consensus: A Thematic Analysis of Nomenclature Choice and Program Structure Among Expanded EMS Programs in a Single State.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Expanded emergency medical services (E-EMS) programs, such as mobile integrated health care (MIH) and community paramedicine (CP), are increasingly common in the United States (U.S.). Although an international consensus definition exists specifically for CP, the terminology used by active U.S. E-EMS programs is poorly described, yet has important implications for program visibility, stakeholder engagement, evaluation, and policy. We sought to characterize how E-EMS programs in a single state describe themselves and factors associated with their chosen terminology.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with E-EMS programs in Ohio. We used "E-EMS" as a historically established, neutral umbrella term to avoid prespecifying MIH, CP, or MIH-CP terminology during program identification. We identified E-EMS programs through voluntary reports to Ohio EMS, the Emergency Triage, Treat, and Transport (ET3) roster, publicly reported E-EMS programs on national dashboards, and snowball sampling. An interviewee from each E-EMS program participated in a recorded semi-structured interview focused on E-EMS program terminology, goals, services, and partnerships. Interview transcripts were reviewed by two coders, with discrepancies discussed with and adjudicated by a third reviewer. We used an inductive approach to develop the codebook, followed by thematic analysis to identify themes and subthemes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 58 E-EMS programs meeting inclusion criteria; 23 participated and were included in the analysis. Participants described inconsistent use and varying interpretation of common terms such as MIH, CP, or MIH-CP; one in four used alternative terminology (e.g., neighborhood paramedic, EMS outreach). Participants attributed their terminology choices to the variability in MIH definitions and to limited understanding of MIH or CP among patients or external stakeholders. Despite variation in program terminology, program goals were consistently focused on filling unmet community needs, and program services were uniformly described as adaptable and reliant upon partnerships outside of EMS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The terminology used to describe E-EMS programs in a single state varied considerably. Despite this, E-EMS program goals and services were consistent, suggesting early convergence upon the core mission of E-EMS programs. Participants perceived inconsistent or unfamiliar terminology as a barrier to patient awareness, referral generation, and stakeholder engagement.

articles.title: More Than a Tobacco Problem: Cigarette Smoking as a Marker of Poorer Cardiovascular Health Among Emergency Medical Services Clinicians.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Emergency medical services (EMS) work demands physical capacity, sustained alertness, and performance under stress, making cardiovascular health a workforce concern, not only a personal one. Cigarette smoking persists in portions of the EMS workforce, but whether it signals cardiovascular risk beyond tobacco exposure itself is unknown. We examined whether cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across the non-tobacco domains of the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework among nationally certified EMS clinicians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted an observational study and cross-sectional secondary analysis of a voluntary survey offered to nationally certified emergency medical technicians (EMTs), advanced EMTs, and paramedics upon completion of recertification (October 2023-April 2024). To isolate associations beyond tobacco exposure, the primary outcome was a modified composite score (mLE7) averaging the seven non-nicotine LE8 domains (0-100 scale). Ideal cardiovascular health was defined as mLE7 ≥ 80. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, educational, occupational, and organizational characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 36,436 survey respondents, 7,703 had complete data for smoking status and all seven non-nicotine domains. Of these, 48.8% had never smoked, 45.2% formerly smoked, and 6.0% currently smoked. Mean mLE7 scores were 59.2 among never smokers, 56.9 among former smokers, and 51.5 among current smokers. Compared with never smokers, current smokers had lower adjusted mLE7 scores (β, -6.02; 95% CI, -7.63 to -4.41) and lower odds of ideal cardiovascular health (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.61). Former smokers had intermediate results (β, -1.62; 95% CI, -2.37 to -0.87; aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.86). Current smoking was associated with poorer scores across diet, physical activity, sleep, blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose domains (p < 0.05). Clinicians at private and hospital-based agencies had lower adjusted mLE7 scores than those at fire-based agencies.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among EMS clinicians, current cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across nearly every non-tobacco domain, suggesting that smoking may serve as a readily identifiable marker of broader cardiovascular risk in this workforce. Agencies may consider pairing cessation support with broader cardiovascular health initiatives for clinicians who smoke. Sensitivity analyses addressing missing data yielded consistent results.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Disease in Cetaceans.

abstract.text: Cetaceans possess a highly specialized cardiovascular system that supports prolonged apnea, selective perfusion of vital organs, and tolerance to marked hemodynamic fluctuations during diving. Nevertheless, pathological and clinical observations show that they can develop a broad spectrum of cardiovascular disease (CVD). This review summarizes current knowledge on CVD in cetaceans across species and ecological contexts. We discuss the major disease phenotypes described to date, including stress cardiomyopathy, chronic myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy-like remodeling, inflammatory cardiac disease, vascular and ischemic lesions, valvular and functional abnormalities, and congenital defects. Among these, acute stress-associated myocardial injury is one of the best-supported phenotypes in stranded cetaceans, whereas chronic cardiomyopathy-like remodeling is most clearly documented in pygmy and dwarf sperm whales. Inflammatory cardiac disease appears less frequent and is usually associated with systemic infection, while vascular disease includes not only atherosclerotic and thrombotic lesions but also embolic and decompression-related pathology. Current knowledge remains limited by strong species and sampling biases, with most evidence derived from stranded animals and a smaller body of work from managed dolphins. Overall, cetacean cardiovascular pathology reflects the interaction between extreme physiological specialization, environmental exposure, systemic disease, and acute stress. Key words Cetaceans " Cardiovascular disease " Stress cardiomyopathy " Myocardial fibrosis " Myocarditis " Valvular disease " Diving physiology " Cardiovascular adaptation.

articles.title: Frequency of On-Scene Goal-Directed Field Interventions for Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in a Regional System of Care.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Early on-scene resuscitation improves outcomes from pediatric non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); however, for pediatric patients, the early evacuation strategy remains commonplace. We sought to determine the frequency of goal-directed interventions initiated by paramedics prior to transport for pediatric patients with OHCA in a regional emergency medical services (EMS) system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective observational study and cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) and linked electronic patient care reports (ePCR) data for patients aged <15 years treated by EMS for nontraumatic OHCA in Los Angeles (LA) County from January 2021 to December 2022. The primary outcome was the frequency of goal-directed therapies administered on scene prior to transport, which we defined as defibrillation for shockable rhythms and administration of epinephrine and fluid resuscitation for non-shockable rhythms. We also tabulated descriptive statistics regarding arrest characteristics, scene times, frequency of other prehospital treatments, and patient outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 176 eligible pediatric OHCA cases analyzed in CARES, 112 (64%) were male, the median age was 10 months (IQR 3-51), and 162 (92%) had an initial non-shockable rhythm. Of these, 156 patients were successfully linked to electronic patient care report (ePCR) records for analyses of prehospital interventions. Among 143 patients with non-shockable rhythms, EMS administered epinephrine before transport in 58 (41%) and fluids in 12 (8%). Among 13 patients with shockable rhythms, EMS delivered defibrillation before transport in 11 (85%). Bag-valve-mask (BVM) use was documented in 80 (51%) patients, although its timing relative to scene departure could not be determined. Median on-scene time was 10 minutes (IQR 5-18). Ten patients (6%) survived to hospital discharge, including 6 (3%) with a favorable neurologic outcome.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this regional EMS system, fewer than half of patients with non-shockable rhythms received a dose of epinephrine and fewer than one in ten received intravenous fluids prior to transport, whereas most patients with shockable rhythms were defibrillated on scene. Further work is needed to identify barriers to timely delivery of on-scene resuscitative interventions.

articles.title: Effect of the timing and setting of pulmonary rehabilitation on functional recovery after lung cancer surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.text: ObjectiveTo compare the effects of pulmonary rehabilitation initiated at different times and settings on functional recovery after lung cancer surgery, and to compare supervision modes in late-phase rehabilitation.MethodsPubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, CBM and Wanfang Data were searched from inception to October 2026 for randomised controlled trials comparing pulmonary rehabilitation with usual care. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed bias (RoB 2). Meta-analysis (RevMan 5.4) included sub-group analyses by timing (early in-hospital vs. late out-of-hospital) and supervision mode (fully vs. partially supervised).ResultsThirteen randomised controlled trials (1137 patients) were included. The primary outcomes were post-operative complications and length of hospital stay for early in-hospital rehabilitation, and 6-min walk distance (6MWD), peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak), forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) and quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30) for late-phase rehabilitation. Early rehabilitation did not significantly reduce complications (risk ratio = 0.55, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.25-1.24) or shorten hospital stay (mean difference = -0.08 days, 95% CI -1.19 to 1.04). Late rehabilitation significantly improved 6MWD (mean difference = 68.86 m, 95% CI 53.46-84.26), VO2peak (mean difference = 2.62 ml/kg/min, 95% CI 2.08-3.15) and FEV1 (mean difference = 0.52 L, 95% CI 0.22-0.81), but not quality of life. Fully and partially supervised modes did not differ significantly in 6MWD.ConclusionLate rehabilitation improved exercise capacity and pulmonary function after lung cancer surgery, whereas early in-hospital rehabilitation did not show clear short-term benefits. Partially supervised models may offer a feasible alternative to fully supervised rehabilitation. Staged, individualised pulmonary rehabilitation warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Asthma Blitz Days: An Innovative Approach to Asthma Management in Schools.

abstract.text: Asthma is the most prevalent chronic condition among school-aged children in the United States, contributing to emergency department visits, school absences, and diminished well-being. Inadequate asthma control is driven by medication nonadherence, psychosocial stressors, and social determinants of health. School nurses are pivotal in coordinating care, supporting medication management, and fostering asthma-friendly environments. In Pitt County, North Carolina, Asthma Blitz Days were developed as a collaborative, school-based intervention between Pitt County School Health Program and ECU Health (formerly Vidant) Maynard Children's Hospital Pediatric Asthma Program. Targeting Pre-K to 5th grade students with documented asthma, this program assessed symptoms, delivered age-appropriate education using the teach-back method, and improved medication and documentation compliance. School nurse-led, multidisciplinary interventions like Asthma Blitz Days offer a scalable approach to improving asthma control and promoting health equity in school communities.

articles.title: Factors associated with continuous naloxone infusion use following opioid overdose in the emergency department.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Contemporary data on naloxone infusion use are limited. We seek to identify factors associated with infusion use and characterize clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study of emergency department encounters between July 2019 and December 2024 involving patients with nonfatal opioid overdose who received naloxone. Sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, toxicologic findings, naloxone administration patterns, and clinical outcomes were compared between encounters with and without infusion. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with naloxone infusion use and selected clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,165 encounters met inclusion criteria, including 227 (19.5%) involving naloxone infusion.
