In adjusted analyses, fentanyl positivity (aOR 2.96, 95% CI 1.92-4.57) and combined opioid-stimulant positivity (aOR 3.00, 95% CI 1.99-4.53) were independently associated with naloxone infusion use, whereas opiate positivity was associated with lower odds of infusion (aOR 0.50, 95% CI 0.34-0.73). Infusion use increased over the study period, and prolonged infusions occasionally resulted in substantial intravenous fluid exposure.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Associations of fentanyl and stimulant positivity with naloxone infusion may reflect changing overdose patterns amid increasing fentanyl and stimulant co-exposure. Substantial fluid administration during prolonged infusions highlights a potentially underrecognized consequence of dilute preparations. Given the observational design, associations with infusion use are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as causal.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Evolving patterns of fentanyl and stimulant co-exposure may influence naloxone infusion use following opioid overdose.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics of unregulated psychoactive supplement exposures: a 15-year multicenter study of kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Unregulated psychoactive "supplements" including kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine are readily accessible, raising concern for toxicity and dependence owing to their GABA and opioid receptor activity; however, clinical features associated with their use are poorly characterized. We describe hospital presentations and management of kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine exposures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed data from the Toxicology Investigators Consortium (ToxIC) Core Registry, which prospectively collects information on patients managed by medical toxicologists (1 January 2010-31 December 2024). All cases involving kratom, phenibut, and/or tianeptine exposures were included. Demographics, exposure circumstances, clinical presentation, management, and outcomes were examined.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 152 patient encounters involving kratom (n = 97), phenibut (n = 44) and/or tianeptine (n = 11), with case counts increasing over time. Median age was 35 years (IQR 26-42 years), and 127 (83.6%) were male. Co-ingestions were common (n = 73; 48.0%) frequently involving other psychoactive supplements (n = 27; 17.8%), stimulants (n = 23; 15.1%) and/or opioids (n = 22; 14.5%). Most consultations involved intentional use (n = 131; 86.2%), including euphoria (n = 60; 39.5%), perceived therapeutic/wellness benefit (n = 18; 11.8%) and withdrawal self-management (n = 13; 8.6%). Thirty-five encounters (23.0%) resulted in intensive care admission and one patient died. Addiction treatment infrequently involved buprenorphine/naloxone (n = 15; 9.9%). At hospital discharge 16 (10.5%) patients received naloxone overdose prevention kit education and/or prescription.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Psychoactive supplement exposures evaluated by medical toxicologists were associated with substantial morbidity, with nearly one-quarter requiring intensive care unit admission. Withdrawal was common, and nearly half of encounters involved co-ingestants.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Hospital presentations involving kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine increased over time, supporting recognition of these substances as emerging drugs of misuse rather than benign supplements. These findings highlight opportunities to strengthen addiction-focused care, regulatory oversight and public education.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure in a multicentre emergency department cohort.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure are poorly characterised. We describe clinical features, outcomes and influence of common co-detections in patients with analytically massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective multicentre cohort study using the Emerging Drugs Network of Australia-Victoria registry. Patients presenting to 18 Victorian emergency departments between November 2021 and March 2026 with whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentrations ≥300 mg/L (2.9 mmol/L). Clinical features, complications, interventions, and outcomes were described. Multivariable logistic regression examined associations between whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration, opioid, benzodiazepine, and methamphetamine co-detection and five clinical domains: severe CNS depression (Glasgow Coma Scale of three), bradypnoea, hypoxaemia, hypotension, and hypothermia.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 154 patients were included. Median age was 33 years (IQR 28-40); median whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration 380 mg/L (3.7 mmol/L), IQR 340-470 mg/L (3.3-4.5 mmol/L). Severe CNS depression was common (116/154 (75%) had a first Glasgow Coma Scale of three), as were intubation 101/154 (66%), intensive care admission (103/154, 67%), hypotension (39/154, 25%), vasopressor use (31/154, 20%), and hypothermia (56/154, 36%). Polysubstance exposure occurred in 150/154 (97%). Opioid co-detection (31/154, 20%) was independently associated with hypotension (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.51, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.83-11.14) and hypoxaemia (aOR 3.64, 95% CI 1.14-11.67). Higher whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration was independently associated with hypotension but not CNS depression, bradypnoea, hypoxaemia, or hypothermia. One patient died (0.6%) and 42/154 (27%) were discharged directly from the emergency department.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure produced a remarkably consistent severe but largely reversible toxidrome. Within the massive exposure range studied, increasing gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration contributed principally to haemodynamic compromise, whereas common co-detections had little influence apart from opioid-associated hypotension and hypoxaemia.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure was associated with profound but largely reversible toxicity and excellent in-hospital survival with supportive care. These findings support aggressive early supportive management and identify haemodynamic compromise as remaining concentration-dependent in the massive exposure range.

articles.title: Low Prevalence of Adverse Outcomes in an 18-Month Follow-Up of Individuals With Chronic Pain Recently Certified for Medical Cannabis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Given the scarce data on adverse outcomes in people who use medical cannabis, the objective of this study was to assess the prevalence of adverse outcomes, including cannabis use disorder (CUD), opioid use disorder (OUD), hazardous alcohol use, cannabis diversion, cannabis-related injuries, and emergency room visits in individuals newly certified for medical cannabis for chronic pain in New York.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In an 18-month longitudinal cohort study, data were collected from 223 adults (mean age = 56.3 years, 54.3% female). At baseline and every 3 months, we assessed study outcomes using structured DSM-5 diagnostic interviews, standardized questionnaires, and study-specific questions. Medical and unregulated cannabis use were self-reported separately every 2 weeks via web surveys.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Over 18 months, 4.9% of participants met the DSM-5 criteria for CUD at 1 or more study visits, 0.9% for OUD, 6.7% for hazardous alcohol use, 4.0% for cannabis diversion, and 1.8% for cannabis-related injuries. The mean frequency of medical and unregulated cannabis use per 2-week period was 9.6 and 5.3 days, respectively, for those with CUD and 6.4 and 2.7 days, respectively, for those without CUD. No consistent patterns emerged for other adverse outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this cohort of adults with chronic pain newly certified for medical cannabis, adverse outcomes were infrequent during the 18-month follow-up, despite participants reporting regular use throughout the study. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution, as larger or longer term studies may detect risks not captured in this study. Continued patient education and monitoring remain important, and more research is needed to understand the long-term safety of medical cannabis use, particularly as policies continue to evolve.

articles.title: Decompression sickness following a dive to retrieve a mobile phone - a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Decompression sickness (DCS) results from inert gas bubble formation in tissues and blood following a rapid reduction in ambient pressure, most commonly associated with diving. Clinical manifestations range from mild musculoskeletal symptoms to severe neurological and systemic involvement. Early recognition and prompt treatment are essential to prevent progression and improve outcomes.

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: A previously healthy Confédération Mondiale des Activités Subaquatiques (CMAS) three-star diving instructor performed two consecutive deep dives to retrieve a mobile phone lost at sea. Following a rapid and uncontrolled ascent after gas depletion, he developed acute right-sided hemiplegia, cutis marmorata, and severe musculoskeletal pain. Computed tomography revealed intravascular gas within the hepatic parenchyma. The patient underwent hyperbaric oxygen treatment (HBOT) using the U.S. Navy Treatment Table 6. This resulted in rapid symptom resolution and complete recovery without the need for additional HBOT sessions.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case demonstrates that repeated deep dives combined with uncontrolled ascent can lead to severe DCS with systemic manifestations, highlighting the importance of adhering to safe diving practices and conducting appropriate risk assessment.

articles.title: Emergency Department Visits During a Recurrent Traditional Mass Gathering: An 18-Day Descriptive Record From Japan (2010-2018).
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Recurrent traditional mass gatherings can create a recurring pattern of emergency department (ED) demand, but single-center aggregate data cannot estimate incidence or individual risk.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe festival-related ED visits during the 2 annual September main-procession days of the Kishiwada Danjiri Festival, Japan, over 9 years (2010-2018).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective descriptive ecological study using daily aggregate records from a single hospital for the 18 main-procession days (2 days per year, 2010-2018), drawn from the hauler and spectator tabs of the source workbook (276 and 86 records, respectively; same facility and extraction criteria, no duplication across tabs). Visits were classified as heat-related, injury-coded, or other according to the source diagnosis field. Official daily maximum wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT) for the Sakai observation point (Japanese Ministry of the Environment) was linked by date. We calculated exploratory Spearman rank correlations between WBGT and daily visit counts, without causal interpretation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 362 festival-related ED visits across 18 days: 187 heat-related, 135 injury-coded, and 40 other visits; no visit was uncategorized. The daily total had a median of 20.5 (range, 5-37), and heat-related visits had a median of 7.5 (range, 1-32). Daily maximum WBGT had a median of 27.7°C (range, 21.7-30.9°C). WBGT was positively correlated with total visits (ρ = 0.78) and heat-related visits (ρ = 0.77); the correlation with injury-coded visits was weaker (ρ = 0.20).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This 9-year record shows recurring festival-related ED demand involving both heat-related and injury-coded presentations. The findings support standardized future collection of participant denominators, time of presentation, and clinical severity. The dataset does not estimate incidence, individual risk, or intervention effectiveness.

articles.title: Qualitative Analysis of Disaster Risks in Villages Near Industrial Zones: Findings From a Community-Based Disaster Risk Management Program in Johor, Malaysia.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Communities near industrial areas face overlapping risks from natural and anthropogenic hazards, yet their perceptions of these risks remain underexplored. This study examined disaster risks perceived by residents of 2 villages adjacent to industrial zones in Johor, Malaysia, to inform community-based disaster risk management (CBDRM) strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A phenomenological study was conducted in July 2022 involving 21 participants. Data were collected through focus group discussions, analyzed using inductive thematic analysis, and disaster risks assessed using a CBDRM risk assessment.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Five interrelated themes emerged relating to hazards, vulnerability, coping capacity, and community needs. Participants consistently identified floods, fires, and oil spills as major disaster events, while vulnerability was associated with proximity to industrial activities, inadequate infrastructure, deforestation, and limited preparedness. Existing coping capacities included community communication networks, local warning systems, and volunteer-based response efforts. Collectively, industrial pollution and environmental degradation are perceived by the communities as risks comparable to, and in some cases exceeding, conventional disaster threats.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The study highlights the interplay between environmental and industrial hazards for communities near industrial areas, further emphasizing the need for participatory approaches to integrate local risk perceptions into CBDRM initiatives for better disaster risk reduction in industrialized settings.

articles.title: A Pilot Investigation of Endocannabinoid System Markers and Lipopolysaccharide Responses to 10 Sessions of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy.
articles.journal_full: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

abstract.text: BACKGROUND Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) can modulate inflammatory and redox-sensitive pathways, but its effects on endocannabinoid system markers remain unclear. This exploratory biomarker subanalysis of a randomized controlled parent trial evaluated whether repeated HBOT was associated with changes in serum anandamide (AEA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) as primary outcomes. Cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2R), fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), and the baseline AEA-LPS association were assessed secondarily or exploratorily. MATERIAL AND METHODS The resource-limited, post-randomization sample included 17 healthy, physically active men: 9 from a pre-existing morning scheduling subgroup of the frequent-treatment HBOT arm and 8 controls selected before biomarker assays to improve baseline body mass index (BMI) comparability. HBOT consisted of 10 sessions performed 6 times weekly. Each session involved 60 minutes of 100% oxygen at 2.5 atmospheres absolute, delivered as three 20-min oxygen-breathing periods separated by two 5-minute air breaks. Fasting serum was collected before and after the protocol, and biomarkers were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. RESULTS No significant between-group differences in change scores were found for AEA (p = 0.597), CB2R (p=1.000), FAAH (p=0.885), or LPS (p=0.885). No significant within-group changes occurred in the HBOT group. Baseline AEA was positively associated with baseline LPS (Spearman's rho=0.505, p=0.039). CONCLUSIONS Receiving 10 HBOT sessions were not associated with significant changes in the measured circulating biomarkers. These exploratory findings do not exclude smaller effects, and the baseline AEA-LPS association requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.

articles.title: Traumaplasty for acetabular fractures: Factors associated with additional fracture fixation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute hip arthroplasty with additional fracture fixation, termed fix and replace (FAR), is an established option for selected acetabular fractures. The factors associated with adding fixation remain incompletely defined. We examined treatment selection in a mixed adult acetabular fracture cohort.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-centre study included 29 adults undergoing hip arthroplasty for acetabular fractures, including periprosthetic or peri-implant injuries. Sixteen received FAR and 13 received arthroplasty without separate fracture fixation, termed fracture joint replacement (FJR). Preoperative computed tomography was used to measure fracture displacement. An exploratory logistic regression included maximum fracture displacement and Paprosky grade, with 26 complete cases. A sensitivity model additionally included articular displacement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean age was 72.8 ± 13.3 years (range 36-94); 20 patients were male and 10 had periprosthetic or peri-implant fractures. Mean maximum fracture displacement was 19.95 ± 10.00 mm in FAR and 6.66 ± 5.84 mm in FJR. In the two-predictor model, greater displacement was associated with FAR (odds ratio [OR] 1.22 per mm, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-1.46; p = 0.021). The Paprosky grade 3 estimate was imprecise (OR 4.41, 95% CI 0.47-41.85; p = 0.196). The model's 50% probability point was 9.7 mm when Paprosky grade was held at its cohort mean. Adding articular displacement attenuated the statistical evidence for the fracture-displacement association (p = 0.128).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Greater fracture displacement was associated with additional fixation in an exploratory two-predictor model. The small, heterogeneous cohort and model sensitivity preclude a validated displacement threshold or a conclusion that fixation can safely be omitted. These findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Possible Semaglutide-Associated Acute Hepatocellular Liver Injury: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a diagnosis of exclusion that relies on a compatible temporal relationship between drug exposure and liver injury, the course after withdrawal of the suspected agent, and the exclusion of alternative etiologies. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), including semaglutide, are widely prescribed for type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity, and semaglutide was recently approved for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis; clinically significant hepatotoxicity has been reported only rarely. We describe a 56-year-old woman with obesity, without diabetes, who presented to the emergency department with right flank pain 89 days after starting oral semaglutide 3 mg once daily. Aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase levels were 14.6 and 10.2 times the upper limit of normal, respectively, with elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), mild hyperbilirubinemia, and a normal alkaline phosphatase level (R ratio 11.1, hepatocellular pattern). Serology for hepatitis A, B, C, and E and antinuclear antibodies were negative, creatine kinase was normal, and unenhanced abdominopelvic CT showed no significant biliary dilatation, choledocholithiasis, or features of acute cholecystitis. Semaglutide was discontinued, whereas fluoxetine and clonazepam, started approximately six months earlier, and olmesartan were continued. Liver tests improved progressively, with a 54% reduction in the elevation of alanine aminotransferase above the upper limit of normal (ULN) by day 7. The updated Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method (RUCAM) score was 6 (probable) for semaglutide, 4 (possible) for fluoxetine, and 2 (unlikely) for both clonazepam and olmesartan, and the injury was graded as mild. Transient biliary obstruction could not be completely excluded, as the abdominal ultrasound result and laboratory follow-up beyond day 7 were not available. This case suggests that semaglutide should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained hepatocellular liver injury and highlights the need for a structured causality assessment that includes the exclusion of biliary disease, a recognized complication of this drug class.

articles.title: Opioid prescribing trajectories for nonspecific low back pain: sociodemographic and clinical heterogeneity across 3 policy periods, 2012-2024.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Opioid prescribing for nonspecific low back pain (ns-LBP) has declined amid evolving policies, yet how prescribing trajectories differ across patient populations remains unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To assess temporal changes in opioid prescribing for ns-LBP across policy periods and identify patient characteristics associated with differential prescribing trajectories.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed electronic health records from 31,940 adults with ns-LBP from 2012Q1-2024Q4. 2,077 (6.5%) patients received an opioid prescription within six months of initial LBP diagnosis. Three policy periods were examined: A (2012Q1-2015Q1), B (2015Q2-2018Q3), and C (2018Q4-2024Q4). Multivariable logistic regression and time-characteristic interaction effects identified differential prescribing patterns. Ratios of odds ratios (RORs) quantified multiplicative interactions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Opioid prescribing declined from 12.7% in Period A to 4.4% in Period C, although reductions varied across patient populations. Black patients experienced greater reductions than White patients during Period B (ROR 0.33, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21-0.51), whereas Hispanic/Latino patients experienced smaller reductions during Period C (ROR 1.44, 95% CI 1.03-2.01). Older adults (≥61 years) experienced smaller reductions than younger adults (18-40 years) during Period B and C (ROR 1.69 / 1.55, 95% CI 1.23-2.32 / 1.16-2.07). Medicaid patients experienced accelerated reductions during Period B but attenuated reductions during Period C, while Medicare patients experienced smaller reductions during Period C than privately insured patients. Additional temporal interactions were observed across smoking status, social support, imaging utilization, and emergency department visit.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although opioid prescribing for ns-LBP declined substantially, reductions were heterogeneous across patient populations, with demographic differences narrowing, persisting, or emerging. Monitoring subgroup-specific prescribing alongside patient-centered outcomes may inform equitable pain management strategies.

articles.title: Common household foods fail to mitigate button battery esophageal injury in infants: an ex vivo dynamic model study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Button battery (BB) ingestion is a life-threatening pediatric emergency, particularly in infants at high risk of severe esophageal injury. This study evaluated whether readily available household food could mitigate BB-induced esophageal injury in infants.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A dynamic ex vivo porcine esophageal model simulating peristalsis, salivary flow, and body temperature was used. After insertion of a CR2032 lithium BB, 5 mL of agave syrup, soy drink, orange juice, ketchup, or honey was administered at 5, 15, and 25 min, then every 30 min for 2, 4, or 6 hours. Outcomes included macroscopic ulcer grade, histologic injury depth, esophageal pH, and residual battery voltage.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In this dynamic model, agave syrup, soy drink, and orange juice did not reduce ulcer severity or histologic injury compared with untreated controls (p>0.05). Ketchup markedly worsened injury, increasing ulcer grades and voltage loss at all time points (p<0.05). Protective effects suggested in static models for agave syrup and soy drink were not reproduced under dynamic conditions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Common household foods do not protect against BB-induced esophageal injury in a ex vivo experimental model. Dynamic testing is essential before recommending food-based prehospital therapies.

articles.title: Methamphetamine use and homelessness are risk factors for recurrent trauma and premature mortality in survivors of violent injury.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Methamphetamine use and homelessness have markedly increased nationally, and this trend is especially evident among those experiencing violent trauma. However, no study to date has examined the long-term outcomes of recurrent injury and death associated with methamphetamine use and homelessness in survivors of violent trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective single-institution study, the electronic medical records of patients who presented between 2015 and 2023 with violent injuries were reviewed for toxicology results, housing status, and recurrent injury. The coroner's database was queried to identify unnatural postdischarge deaths. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used in a time-to-event analysis, with recurrent traumatic injury and death as the events of interest, to analyze HRs associated with the risk factors of methamphetamine use and homelessness whereas adjusting for covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the 2,468 patients meeting our inclusion criteria, 1,039 (42.4%) tested positive for methamphetamine, and 800 (32.4%) were experiencing homelessness. There were 181 (7.3%) who returned at least once to the emergency department (ED) with a new traumatic injury and 106 (4.3%) who died postdischarge after a median of 4.3 years of follow-up. Methamphetamine-positive patients returned to the ED with a new traumatic injury at a rate two-thirds higher than methamphetamine-negative patients (HR, 1.67; 95% CI 1.18 to 2.36), and unhoused patients returned at twice the rate of housed patients (HR, 2.16; 95% CI 1.54 to 3.04). When compared with their counterparts, methamphetamine-positive patients had similar rates of postdischarge death (HR, 1.10; 95% CI 0.73 to 1.66), and unhoused patients had a threefold higher rate (HR, 3.19; 95% CI 2.11 to 4.83).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Methamphetamine use and homelessness significantly increase the risk of recurrent traumatic injury in survivors of violent trauma. Homelessness is also a significant risk factor for unnatural death after discharge. It is imperative that trauma care includes screening for substance use and housing insecurity.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, Prognostic/Epidemiological.

articles.title: Delayed Pericardial Tamponade After Left Ventricular Radiofrequency Ablation for Multifocal Premature Ventricular Complexes: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Radiofrequency ablation has become an effective treatment for premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), but its potential for serious complications, particularly delayed pericardial tamponade, remains a concern. We report a 70-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and cerebrovascular disease who presented with frequent, symptomatic, multifocal PVCs refractory to antiarrhythmic therapy. During the procedure, two morphological patterns of PVCs were identified using the ENSITE Precision Electroanatomic Mapping System (Medtronic). Ablation was performed sequentially at the left ventricular papillary muscle and the left ventricular posterolateral wall using a contact force sensing catheter (TactiCath), with power set at 40 W, temperature limit of 43°C, and contact force of 10-30 g. A total of 240 s of ablation was delivered at the papillary muscle site, and 180 s at the posterolateral wall. Anticoagulation was maintained with 8000 U of intravenous heparin. Approximately 1.5 h after the procedure, the patient developed sudden diaphoresis and profound hypotension. Bedside echocardiography revealed a large pericardial effusion with right ventricular diastolic collapse, and urgent pericardiocentesis drained approximately 800 mL of grossly bloody fluid. A pericardial drain was placed, but the patient later experienced recurrent hemodynamic instability and cardiac arrest. Despite aggressive cardiopulmonary resuscitation, blood product transfusion, and chest tube drainage, the patient succumbed to circulatory failure. This case highlights that prolonged and repeated ablation at the left ventricular papillary muscle and posterolateral wall carries a substantial risk of delayed cardiac tamponade, even when immediate post-procedural hemodynamics appear stable. High clinical vigilance and routine point-of-care ultrasound monitoring are essential for early detection and management of this life-threatening complication.

articles.title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy in Diabetic Retinopathy: Mechanistic Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Safety Considerations.

abstract.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) increases dissolved oxygen delivery to tissues and has been proposed as an adjunctive approach for diabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic macular edema (DME). Its role in the diabetic retina is biologically complex because tissue hyperoxia may reduce hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) signaling and retinal vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression, while HBOT can promote reparative angiogenic signaling in wounds and other ischemic tissues. This structured narrative review evaluates these opposing mechanisms and the direct clinical evidence in DR. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from database inception to 4 October 2026 using combinations of terms for HBOT, DR, DME, retinal hypoxia, VEGF, angiogenesis, inflammation, nitric oxide, oxidative stress, and adverse effects. Direct human DR studies were prioritized, while animal and non-retinal studies were used only for mechanistic context. Five clinical studies form the main direct evidence base summarized in a 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis. The only randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study included 50 patients and found no significant long-term difference in visual acuity or DR progression. Smaller prospective and open-label studies reported stabilization of DR, changes in retinal or choroidal thickness, or benefit when HBOT was combined with aflibercept. The 2025 meta-analysis of 463 eyes reported a small pooled improvement in best-corrected visual acuity of -0.05 logMAR (95% CI: -0.09 to -0.01) and a reduction in central macular thickness of -75.21 micrometers (95% CI: -90.04 to -60.38), but the visual acuity result was sensitive to removal of the largest study, and heterogeneity for macular thickness was substantial (I2 = 62%). HBOT therefore remains investigational for DR. Current evidence does not support replacing anti-VEGF therapy, laser photocoagulation, corticosteroid therapy when indicated, or vitreoretinal surgery with HBOT. Adequately powered retinal trials with standardized HBOT protocols and stage-specific outcomes are required before routine use can be recommended.

articles.title: An Unusual Case of Atraumatic Testicular Dislocation Case Report.

abstract.text: Testicular dislocation is an uncommon urologic emergency typically associated with blunt trauma, particularly motor vehicle collisions and straddle injuries. Atraumatic presentations are exceedingly rare and may pose diagnostic challenges in the emergency department (ED). We report the case of a 62-year-old male who presented to the ED with testicular dislocation following heavy lifting. Physical examination revealed an empty right hemiscrotum and tender mass within the right inguinal canal. Ultrasound demonstrated displacement of the right testis in the inguinal canal with preserved vascular perfusion and no evidence of torsion. Urology performed bedside manual reduction, and the patient was initially managed conservatively. Despite preserved testicular perfusion on subsequent imaging, he experienced persistent discomfort requiring multiple ED visits, with later imaging raising concern for testicular atrophy. This case describes a rare instance of atraumatic dislocation and the challenges associated with its diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Measured Posterior Neck-Fold Thickness and Tongue-Base Thickness as Anatomical Markers in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Pilot Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects nearly 1 billion adults globally. Polysomnography (PSG) is the diagnostic gold standard, but it is resource-intensive. Ultrasound assessment of posterior cervical soft tissue is underexplored.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the correlations involving ultrasound-measured posterior neck-fold thickness (PNFT) and tongue-base thickness (TBT) with PSG severity indices in OSA patients.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective study of 77 adults with PSG-confirmed OSA. Bedside ultrasound assessed PNFT and TBT. Neck circumference (NC) and indices (apnea-hypopnea index [AHI], oxygen desaturation index [ODI], and lowest oxygen saturation [LSAT]) were recorded.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 38 patients had mild-to-moderate OSA, and 39, severe OSA. The NC was larger in the severe group compared to the mild-to-moderate group (41.9 versus 38.4 cm respectively; p < 0.001). Neither the PNFT (mild-to-moderate group: 9.3; severe group: 10.2 mm; p = 0.184) nor the TBT (mild-to-moderate group: 65.9; severe group: 67.5 mm; p = 0.167) differed significantly between the groups; the small observed effect size (Cohen's d = 0.31 for TBT) reflects limited precision with this sample size rather than confirmatory evidence against a true difference. The PNFT correlated weakly with the AHI (r = 0.238; p = 0.037) and LSAT (r = -0.228; p = 0.048). The TBT showed a moderate correlation with the LSAT (r = -0.424; p < 0.001) and a weak correlation with the ODI (r = 0.238; p = 0.038). Except for the TBT-LSAT association, none of these ultrasound correlations remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The TBT showed a modest, sex-independent association with the LSAT, whereas PNFT's associations with OSA severity were largely attributable to sex rather than an independent anatomical effect.

articles.title: Total gastric and intragastric air volumes in immediate post-resuscitation whole-body computed tomography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: Association with airway management, aspiration, diaphragmatic position and initial blood gas analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Gastric distension (GD) may occur during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but quantitative human data after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remain limited. We quantified gastric volumes after OHCA and explored associations with prehospital airway strategy, CT-defined aspiration, diaphragmatic position, and initial blood gases.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-center study included OHCA patients undergoing post-resuscitation whole-body computed tomography (CT) within 180 minutes of emergency department (ED) admission between January 1, 2020, and March 31, 2025. Total gastric volume (TGV) and intragastric air volume (GAV) were quantified by CT volumetry.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 255 identified patients, 120 underwent CT within 180 minutes. Median TGV was 594 mL and correlated strongly with GAV (p < 0.001). Among patients with an advanced airway at ED arrival, neither TGV (p = 0.20) nor GAV (p = 0.24) differed significantly between the tracheal airway (TA; n = 87) and supraglottic airway (SGA; n = 28) groups. CT-defined aspiration was numerically more frequent with SGA than TA (78.6% vs. 57.5%; OR 2.7; p = 0.071), whereas neither TGV nor GAV was associated with CT-defined aspiration. Weak positive correlations were observed between initial pCO2 and both TGV (ρ = 0.16; one-tailed p = 0.037) and GAV (ρ = 0.19; one-tailed p = 0.018).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Gastric volumes were high in this selected post-OHCA immediate CT (< 180 minutes) cohort. No significant differences were detected according to recorded prehospital airway strategy, and gastric volume was not associated with CT-defined aspiration. Mechanisms and clinical consequences remain uncertain and require prospective studies before preventive/ therapeutic implications can be established.

articles.title: Dapsone-Induced Methemoglobinemia After Accidental Dose Duplication in a Patient Receiving Long-Term Therapy: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Dapsone is a synthetic sulfone antibiotic with immunosuppressive properties that is widely used for the treatment of dermatological and infectious diseases. Dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia (DIM) has been reported in literature upon chronic and acute exposure to dapsone. By reporting this case, we aim to provide valuable insight into the existing literature by elucidating the dose-response relationship in DIM. This is a case of a nineteen-year-old female patient who presented to our emergency department (ED) complaining of shortness of breath (SOB) and palpitations for one day. Emergency medical services paramedics found her to be desaturating at 84% on pulse oximetry. Initial testing revealed metabolic acidosis with a methemoglobin concentration of 21% and hemoglobin of 9.8 g/dL. She reported accidental ingestion of double her daily dapsone dose of 100 mg, which she had been taking for the past year for subcorneal pustular dermatosis. A diagnosis of dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia (DIM) was confirmed. Optimal treatments and supportive management were provided, and the patient was discharged 36 h later. Dapsone is a sulfone antibiotic that also has immunosuppressive effects. It is commonly used to treat a range of dermatological conditions and infectious diseases. Its dual antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory actions make it valuable in both infectious and immune-mediated skin disorders. Dapsone has been associated with the development of methemoglobinemia, a potentially life-threatening condition characterized by elevated levels of methemoglobin in the blood. Methemoglobinemia arises when the iron moiety within hemoglobin is oxidized from the ferrous (Fe2+) to the ferric (Fe3+) state, thus impairing oxygen-carrying capacity. Unlike most cases of DIM, which are associated with the prolonged use of therapeutic doses or the acute excessive consumption of dapsone, this unique case involves acute toxicity from a single accidental dose duplication. Therefore, our case explores the susceptibility to acute toxicity with a single additional dose of dapsone in a patient with prolonged exposure to it. This case adds to the existing literature on dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia and highlights the possibility of clinically significant toxicity following a single accidental dose duplication in a patient receiving long-term dapsone therapy.

articles.title: Association between addiction consult exposure and provider adoption of buprenorphine initiation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Addiction consult services (ACSs) increase inpatient treatment for opioid use disorder (OUD) and may support prescribing capacity among non-specialists. We evaluated whether cumulative provider-level ACS exposure was associated with independent buprenorphine initiation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of providers caring for hospitalized adults with OUD at an academic medical center (2018-2026). Providers entered at their first qualifying inpatient or emergency department encounter. Cumulative ACS exposure at initiation or censoring was categorized as 0, 1-2, 3-5, or ≥6 ACS-involved encounters. The outcome was time to first observed buprenorphine initiation during an encounter without an ACS consult. Sensitivity analyses examined consult-exposed providers, study-entry era, and exclusion of ED providers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3,410 providers, 582 (17.1%) independently initiated buprenorphine. Compared with providers with no ACS exposure, providers with ≥6 exposures had a higher average rate of independent initiation (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.74; 95% CI, 1.40-2.16), whereas estimates for 1-2 and 3-5 exposures were not significant. Among consult-exposed providers, ≥6 versus 1-2 exposures was associated with a higher initiation rate (aHR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.37-2.30). The association was present in both study-entry eras but not after excluding ED providers.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: High cumulative ACS exposure was associated with a higher average rate of subsequent independent buprenorphine initiation. The findings are consistent with workplace learning as one possible explanation for the observed associations.

abstract.label: SCIENTIFIC SIGNIFICANCE
abstract.text: Repeated ACS exposure may identify opportunities for deliberate skill transfer, particularly among ED providers.

articles.title: Association between polypharmacy, fall-risk increasing drugs, and fall characteristics in older adults discharged from the emergency department: cross-sectional data from the SeFallED study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Polypharmacy and fall-risk-increasing drugs (FRIDs) are known risk factors for falls in older adults. However, the prevalence of polypharmacy and FRIDs in high-risk older adults presenting to the emergency department (ED) after a fall, without hospitalization, is unclear. This study aimed to examine the prevalence of polypharmacy and FRIDs and their associations with specific fall characteristics in this population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The SeFallED study included individuals aged ≥ 60 years who visited an ED in Oldenburg, Germany, after a fall without subsequent hospitalization. Data on fall characteristics and medication use were collected within four weeks of the ED visit. Cross-sectional associations between medication use and fall characteristics were analysed using binary and multinomial logistic regression models. Fall characteristics were characterized by recovery status (recovered vs. unrecovered), location of the fall (indoor vs. outdoor), and direction of the fall (sideways, backward, forward, or collapse).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 335 participants (75.4 ± 9.1 years), the average number of regular medications was 3.6 ± 3.1; with polypharmacy present in 31.3%. FRIDs were identified in 44.5% of participants using STOPPFall medications and 8.4% using medications from the PRISCUS list. No significant associations were found between polypharmacy or FRID use and fall characteristics.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The high prevalence of polypharmacy and FRID use underscores the importance of systematic medication reviews, as recommended in the global guidelines for falls prevention. Implementing medication reviews at the point of care - such as during ED visits - may represent a valuable opportunity to reduce future fall risk in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Uncommon presentation of median arcuate ligament syndrome in a young male treated with simultaneous robot-assisted release and cholecystectomy: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Median arcuate ligament syndrome (MALS), also known as celiac artery compression syndrome, is a rare vascular and neurogenic disorder caused by external compression of the celiac artery and surrounding neural structures by the median arcuate ligament. It typically presents with postprandial abdominal pain, nausea, and weight loss and is most commonly reported in females between the third and fifth decades of life.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We present an unusual case of a 20-year-old male with persistent postprandial abdominal pain for years who lost 20 pounds over the past year. He was found to have peak systolic velocities consistent with greater than 70% hemodynamically significant celiac artery stenosis on mesenteric duplex ultrasound, indicative of vascular compression. Additional imaging demonstrated no significant biliary obstruction but identified gallbladder sludge, contributing to diagnostic complexity due to overlapping symptom profiles. The patient underwent simultaneous robot-assisted median arcuate ligament release with celiac plexus neurolysis and robot-assisted cholecystectomy. The procedure was completed without complications, with minimal blood loss, and the patient was discharged in stable condition on postoperative day one. In the weeks following discharge, the patient developed postoperative gastritis with episodic severe abdominal pain, with full symptomatic resolution confirmed at approximately one year postoperatively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case highlights an atypical demographic presentation of MALS and demonstrates the feasibility and safety of performing concurrent robotic procedures to address coexisting abdominal pathology in a single operative session. Increased awareness of atypical presentations may reduce diagnostic delay, while robotic-assisted approaches may offer a precise and effective minimally invasive treatment strategy for carefully selected patients.

articles.title: Effect of an educational program on pediatric nurses' performance within the critical golden hour following pediatric trauma.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Outcomes after pediatric trauma, a leading cause of childhood death and disability, depend substantially on care delivered during the first "golden hour". Nurses are the first to assess injured children, yet evidence shows persistent deficits in their trauma-specific preparation. This study evaluated the effect of a structured educational program on pediatric nurses' knowledge, practice, self-confidence, and attitudes regarding golden-hour trauma care.

abstract.label: DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: A one-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design was used. A convenience sample of 108 nurses in the pediatric emergency department of Beni-Suef University Hospital, Egypt, completed a five-part instrument covering the four outcome domains, received a structured researcher-delivered program on golden-hour pediatric trauma assessment and management, and were reassessed identically. Five pediatric nursing experts confirmed content validity, and internal consistency was acceptable (KR-20 = 0.86 and 0.79 for the dichotomous tools; Cronbach's α = 0.81 and 0.78 for the Likert tools). Paired t-tests and Spearman's correlations were used.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Before the program, 51.9% of nurses were unfamiliar with the golden hour and 88.9% had received no related training. Afterwards, mean knowledge rose from 66.3% to 85.9%, practice from 51.1% to 79.7%, self-confidence from 3.06 to 3.79, and attitudes from 2.48 to 2.76 (all p < .01). Knowledge correlated positively with practice (r = 0.684, p < .01), self-confidence, and attitudes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The program was associated with significant improvement across all four domains.

abstract.label: PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: Golden-hour training should be embedded in professional development for pediatric emergency nurses and reinforced with simulation, standardized protocols, and mentorship.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Semaglutide in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease.

abstract.text: Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) increasingly develop type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, yet are excluded from cardiovascular outcome trials, and the effects of semaglutide here are unknown. Using the TriNetX Research Network, we conducted a retrospective new-user active-comparator study of adults with ACHD and T2DM initiating semaglutide (n = 2,385) or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor (n = 2,889) from December 2017 to December 2025. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity score matched, yielding 1,422 pairs followed for 3 years, with a sensitivity analysis matched on 27 lesion categories. Semaglutide was associated with lower all-cause mortality (7% vs 12%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51 to 0.85), hospitalization (40% vs 55%; HR 0.68, CI 0.61 to 0.76), and emergency department (ED) visits (35% vs 43%; HR 0.85, CI 0.75 to 0.96). Major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.71), heart failure (HR 0.74), and stroke (HR 0.65) were also lower; myocardial infarction and arrhythmia were not. Mortality, hospitalization, and ED visits were significant at 1, 3, and 5 years and in every sensitivity analysis; the cardiovascular associations were not. Congenital aortic valve disease was twice as common among semaglutide initiators before matching (23% vs 12%), and every great-complexity lesion comprised ≤10 patients per arm. A prespecified negative control was elevated in every analysis. In conclusion, semaglutide was associated with lower mortality and acute care utilization in a predominantly simple-to-moderate complexity ACHD population, but an elevated negative control indicates residual differences in healthcare engagement; these findings are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Bedside ECMO Cannulation by Intensivists and Emergency Physicians.

abstract.text: The number of centers capable of initiating extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for critically ill patients with refractory cardiac or respiratory failure is expanding. Historically, patients were taken to the operating room or catheterization laboratory for ECMO cannulation by cardiothoracic surgeons and perfusionists. More recently, non-surgeons who have undergone specialized training are performing percutaneous ECMO cannulation and initiation of support at the bedside at some centers. This approach is attractive, in part, because of the timely initiation of ECMO and avoidance of the risk of patient deterioration during transport to a procedural area. The purpose of this article is to provide a roadmap for intensivists and emergency physicians to lead ECMO bedside procedures including veno-venous (VV), veno-arterial (VA), and hybrid veno-arteriovenous (V-AV) cannulation at ECMO-capable centers. These procedures demand cognitive and technical skills that are already foundational to critical care practice, including vascular access guided by point-of-care ultrasound and leadership during a dynamic resuscitation. A team-based approach to bedside ECMO cannulation is presented and illustrated with figures and video, including preparation, procedural execution, subsequent patient management, and programmatic considerations such as training and credentialing requirements.

articles.title: Vaping-Related Pneumomediastinum in Adolescents: Characterizing Work Up and Management.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Adolescent vaping, including nicotine and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) products, carries numerous adverse effects. Case reports, primarily in young adults, describe an association between inhaled substance use and pneumomediastinum, but management of affected adolescents remains unclear. This study sought to characterize this population and identify variations in practice patterns to improve future care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single center, retrospective descriptive study with 60-day follow-up was conducted. The hospital's radiology database was searched for imaging studies noting "pneumomediastinum" in patients >10 and 18 years from January 2014-May 2025. Patients with pneumomediastinum secondary to another etiology (ex: trauma, recent surgery) were excluded. Those reporting recent inhaled substance use were included.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-one adolescents met inclusion criteria. Median age at symptom onset was 16 years (range 14-18 years). Nicotine and THC vaping were reported in 73.2% and 78.0% of patients, respectively, with >50% using daily. Hospital admission occurred in 68.3% of cases with median length of stay of 2 days (IQR 1, 3). Three patients required intensive care unit admission, one of whom was hypoxic and obtunded at presentation necessitating intubation. Admitted patients underwent more chest radiographs than those discharged from the emergency department (median 2 vs 1, p=0.027). Nineteen patients underwent esophagram, none demonstrating injury. No interventions were required and no patient experienced recurrence during follow up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Management of vaping-related pneumomediastinum in adolescents, notably the use of imaging, varies considerably. Most patients may not require admission or transfer to a specialized pediatric facility unless presenting with hypoxia or respiratory distress.

articles.title: Readmission outcomes after left atrial appendage occlusion in older adults with atrial fibrillation and bleeding or anticoagulation-alternative indications: A landmark analysis of the nationwide readmissions database, 2018-2020.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is increasingly used in older adults with atrial fibrillation (AF) at risk of bleeding or contraindication to long-term anticoagulation, but its association with age and frailty is poorly described.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adults ≥65 years with nonvalvular AF at elevated thromboembolic risk whose index admission carried a coded bleeding event or an anticoagulation-alternative indication were identified in the Nationwide Readmissions Database (2018-2020). Patients alive at the 90-day landmark were stratified by LAAO vs. no LAAO within 90 days. The primary outcome was all-cause readmission during days 91-270. Survey-weighted logistic regression and propensity-score matching were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,244,671 patients, 2070 underwent LAAO at a mean of 52.4 ± 23.4 days after index. LAAO was associated with higher adjusted odds of all-cause readmission (aOR 1.31, 95% CI 1.15-1.49) and cardiovascular readmission (aOR 1.33, 1.14-1.55). Bleeding readmission was also higher. In-hospital death at readmission did not differ. Age-by-frailty-by-LAAO interaction was not significant (p = 0.85), although subgroup analyses were underpowered.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In older adults with AF and a bleeding event or an anticoagulation-alternative indication who were alive at 90 days, inpatient LAAO was associated with higher subsequent readmissions, including bleeding. Out-of-hospital deaths were not captured, and death competes with readmission, so higher readmission does not mean a worse net clinical outcome. These associations may reflect differences in baseline bleeding risk, inpatient exposure capture, and residual confounding.

articles.title: Fever management and parental anxiety in a pediatric emergency department: A cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fever, often associated with considerable parental anxiety, is one of the most common reasons for pediatric emergency department visits. Parental anxiety could be related to how parents manage childhood fever. This study aims to describe parental fever management practices and state anxiety among parents presenting to a pediatric emergency department and investigate the relationship between these variables.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted between November 2025 and February 2026 in the pediatric emergency department of a state hospital. The sample consisted of 360 parents of children aged 0-6 years who presented with fever and met the inclusion criteria. Data were collected through the Personal Information Form, the Parent Fever Management Scale, and the State Anxiety Inventory (STAI). Group differences were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). The relationship between parental state anxiety and fever management scores were analyzed using Pearson's correlation and hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: While the Parent Fever Management Scale mean score was 31.37 ± 6.82, the State Anxiety Inventory mean score was 48.47 ± 16.36. A significant positive correlation was found between fever management scores and parental state anxiety (r = 0.471, p < .001). Hierarchical regression analysis showed that after adjustment for the variables was included in the model, state anxiety was positively associated with fever management scores (β = 0.315, p < .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Parental fever management practices were positively associated with state anxiety levels. Healthcare professionals should consider parental anxiety when providing education and counseling about childhood fever management. Further intervention studies are needed to determine whether interventions addressing parental anxiety can improve the appropriateness and evidence-based nature of fever management practices.

articles.title: Development of a deep learning model to automatically localize anatomic landmarks important for intraperitoneal free fluid detection during focused assessment with sonography in trauma (FAST).

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) exam allows clinicians to rapidly identify intraperitoneal free fluid (FF), which can accumulate in several discrete anatomic locations. These locations represent potential spaces and are defined by adjacent key organ features. Satisfactory evaluation of these organ features is necessary to obtain a complete FAST exam. We sought to develop an algorithm that accurately identified relevant organs important for the FAST exam.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data was used from 218 prospectively enrolled subjects with positive and negative FAST exams yielding 2,218 videos and 323,304 frames. Images were frame annotated for the presence of the following key organ features: liver, caudal liver tip, spleen, caudal spleen tip, kidney, diaphragm, and bladder. Data were randomly split into training, validation, and test sets in a 6:2:2 ratio for training a deep learning model using the YOLOv5 object detection algorithm. Diagnostic accuracy of the test set is reported at the frame and video levels.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At the frame level, the mean average precision (mAP50) was 0.71. At the video level, the mean F1 score for organ detection was 0.85. Video level detection of anatomic locations (defined by the co-incidence of two relevant organ structures) of potential FF accumulation showed a mean F1 of 0.79. At the video level, the model was optimized to favor a higher mean specificity (0.90, 95% CI 0.89-0.92) at the expense of a slightly reduced mean sensitivity (0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.90). The inference speed was 26 ms per frame (38 frames per second) on a mobile tablet.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This organ detection algorithm identifies the key organ features and their interfaces, which are important for FF assessment. The algorithm has a low inference speed that approximates real time temporal resolution, providing a foundation for future work supporting automated image capture and quality assessment.

articles.title: Longitudinal optic nerve sheath diameter trajectories in neurocritical care patients after mechanical thrombectomy or decompressive craniectomy: A descriptive bedside ultrasound study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Longitudinal optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) measurements after neurosurgical procedures remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to describe postoperative ONSD trajectories in selected disease-surgery cohorts.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center prospective observational study included 80 patients with clinically and radiologically defined suspected intracranial hypertension: 40 undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for anterior-circulation ischemic stroke and 40 undergoing decompressive craniectomy (DC) for intracerebral hemorrhage or traumatic brain injury. Forty healthy volunteers provided a local reference. Bedside ONSD was measured with a standardized protocol on postoperative days 0-9 and summarized using observed daily means and linear mixed-effects spline models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 800 planned patient measurements, 733 were available. Healthy volunteers had a mean ONSD of 4.11 ± 0.54 mm. In the MT group, mean ONSD increased from 5.55 ± 0.62 mm on day 0 to an observed maximum of 5.91 ± 0.77 mm on day 5, then declined. In the DC group, daily means ranged from 5.18 to 5.33 mm.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In these selected cohorts, mean ONSD reached its observed maximum on postoperative day 5 after MT and varied within a narrow range after DC. Whether these changes exceeded measurement variability remains uncertain. Further validation is needed before using these observations to infer intracranial pressure changes or guide treatment.

articles.title: Clinical features, first aid practices, and hospital management of snakebites in Northern Uganda: A multi-facility cross-sectional study.

abstract.text: Snakebite envenoming is a neglected tropical disease with a disproportionate burden in sub-Saharan Africa, where weak surveillance, limited antivenom availability, and reliance on traditional remedies compound morbidity and mortality. Evidence on how snakebite cases are clinically managed in routine practice in Uganda remains scarce. We conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study with retrospective abstraction of records from four purposively selected health facilities in Gulu and Arua Districts of Northern Uganda. Snakebite case records from outpatient, inpatient, paediatric, and intensive-care service points covering the period 2017-2021 were reviewed using a standardised abstraction tool. Descriptive statistics were computed in Stata version 14, with frequencies and proportions for categorical variables and medians with interquartile ranges (IQR) for continuous variables, both of which were right-skewed. All analyses were complete-case, and the denominator is reported wherever it differs from the full sample. We analysed 227 snakebite case records. Of these, 58.6% were female and the median age was 21 years (IQR 13-38); students or pupils accounted for 26.6% of the 192 records in which occupation was described. Most bites involved the lower limb (85.9%) and occurred in the second and third quarters of the year (59.9%). Snake species was undocumented in 76.2% of records. No pre-hospital first aid was recorded in 59.1% of cases; where first aid was documented it was usually harmful, most often a tourniquet (29.3%) or a herbal remedy (8.9%). The dominant clinical manifestations were pain (60.8%), swelling or blisters at the bite site (68.7%), and fang marks (26.9%). One or more features suggestive of systemic envenoming were documented in 18.5% of cases, of whom 33.3% received antivenom. Overall, only 15.0% of cases received antivenom, while supportive care predominated (intravenous fluids 68.1%, analgesics 64.2%, antibiotics 53.1%). Coagulation testing was rare (20-minute whole blood clotting test 17.3%; INR 12.0%). Overall, 93.4% of patients recovered, 3.1% died, 0.9% were referred to other healthcare facilities, and the rest (2.6%) had missing information on the outcomes. Snakebite management in Northern Uganda is largely symptomatic, with critical gaps in species identification, syndromic assessment, coagulation testing, antivenom utilisation, and pre-hospital first aid practices. Strengthening health-worker training, improving documentation and surveillance, and community education on appropriate first aid are urgently needed to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Age-stratified sex differences in outcomes after lower extremity fracture fixation: A propensity-matched cohort study.

abstract.text: BackgroundOutcomes of open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) of lower extremity fractures vary based on patient sex and age.MethodsWe performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX national research database. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent ORIF of lower extremity fractures, including pelvis and acetabulum, between 2003 and 2023 were identified. We conducted 1:1 propensity score matching (male vs. female) to balance comorbidities, including age, race, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, BMI, osteoporosis, and smoking status. Patients were stratified into age groups (18-39, 40-64, ≥ 65 years). Postoperative outcomes at 90 days and two years were compared using risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals.ResultsOf 204,152 patients, 147,518 remained after matching. Males had significantly higher complication rates than females: deep vein thrombosis, 2.1% vs. 1.5%; pneumonia, 1.5% vs. 1.0%; nonunion requiring surgical treatment, 4.8% vs. 3.5%; and amputation, 1.1% vs. 0.5% (all p<0.001). Males also had higher rates of 90-day emergency department visits (4.6% vs. 3.8%) and readmissions (6.7% vs. 4.6%, p<0.001). These sex disparities were most pronounced in midlife (40-64 years). Conversely, females had higher rates of complex regional pain syndrome across all ages.ConclusionBoth sex and age are predictors of postoperative outcomes following lower extremity ORIF, with the largest sex disparities in patients aged 40-64 and higher CRPS rates in females across all age groups.

articles.title: What's Blood Got to Do with It? Identifying MPDS® Dispatch Codes Most Commonly Associated with Prehospital Blood Administration.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to identify Medical Priority Dispatch System (MPDS®) codes most frequently associated with prehospital blood utilization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We examined Delaware's prehospital blood database to determine dispatch codes where low titer group O positive whole blood (LTOWB) was administered. We calculated the number of blood units under each dispatch code within the study period (May 2023- February 2026). Using this data, we identified the MPDS® codes associated with the highest number of blood units, including the top five codes overall, top medical codes, and as well as blood utilization rates for penetrating versus blunt traumas.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The most frequent blood utilization came from the following dispatch codes: 29D02 (traffic collision, high mechanism) 32 patients, 27D04G (penetrating trauma with central wounds) 32 patients, 29D02M (auto versus pedestrian) 28 patients, 29D05 (traffic collision with entrapment) 24 patients, and 29D02L (auto versus bicycle/motorcycle) 20 patients. These five dispatch codes accounted for 29% of all prehospital LTOWB utilized within the 33-month study period. Analyzing blood utilization for non-traumatic dispatch codes revealed: 21D04/21D04M (dangerous hemorrhage, medical) 18 patients, 21D03/21D03M (hemorrhage, not alert, medical) 13 patients, 9E01/M9E01/M9E02 (cardiac or respiratory arrest/death, not breathing) 13 patients, and 21D05/21D05M (hemorrhage, abnormal breathing, medical) 7 patients. These four dispatch codes accounted for 11% (51 patients) of LTOWB utilization. When performing odds ratio analysis to determine odds of blood administration, we found 27D04G, 29D02M, and 29D02L to be statistically significant with 95% confidence intervals of [0.35- 0.87], [2.42- 5.72], [1.47- 3.91], and odds ratios of 0.55, 3.72, and 2.40, respectively. Additionally, our analysis demonstrated that patients with MPDS® coding for penetrating trauma with a delta level priority (27D) have higher likelihood of prehospital blood administration than delta priority high mechanism traffic incidents (29D). This comparison showed an OR of 10.40 that blood would be given to the penetrating trauma patient with a 95% confidence interval of [7.93- 13.66].

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Specific MPDS® codes are strongly associated with prehospital blood utilization. Identifying these patterns offers a unique opportunity for emergency medical services systems to implement automatic blood dispatch protocols based on dispatch code.

articles.title: Prolonged Onboard Storage of Red Blood Cells in Ground Ambulances for Prehospital Transfusion: A Real-World Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Permanent onboard storage of red blood cells (RBC) units could facilitate timely prehospital transfusion but may expose blood products to cumulative transport-related mechanical stress. We evaluated the quality of RBC units stored continuously in operational ground ambulances under real-world emergency medical service conditions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this randomized controlled experimental study of RBC units, leukoreduced RBC units were randomly assigned to continuous onboard ambulance storage from day 7 to day 42 (n = 12) or standard blood bank storage at 2-6 °C for 42 days (n = 14). Samples were analyzed on days 7, 28, and 42. The primary outcome was hemolysis. Secondary outcomes included plasma biochemistry and storage-induced microerythrocytes (SMEs), an emerging morphological marker associated with post-transfusion RBC recovery. Temporal trajectories of SME levels were assessed using repeated-measures multivariate analysis of variance and fixed-effects panel models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All RBC units remained below the European regulatory hemolysis threshold of 0.8% at day 42. Hemolysis was higher in ambulance-stored units at day 28 (Hodges-Lehmann difference, +0.043 percentage points; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.010-0.076; p = 0.015) and day 42 (+0.096 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.029-0.176; p = 0.008). The SME levels increased in both groups, with a significant time-by-group interaction (p = 0.034) indicating different temporal trajectories. Additional SME accumulation in ambulance-stored units occurred predominantly between days 28 and 42. At day 42, the mean between-group SME difference was +9.04 percentage points (95% CI, -0.66 to 18.73; p = 0.066). The available sample was insufficient to exclude moderate or larger between-group differences. Biochemical changes were broadly similar between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Continuous onboard RBC storage in operational ground ambulances maintained all units within regulatory hemolysis limits through day 42. However, higher hemolysis and late divergence in SME accumulation suggest that prolonged ambulance exposure may influence RBC storage quality. These findings provide preliminary support for the feasibility of continuous onboard RBC storage, particularly earlier in the storage period, but do not establish equivalence with conventional blood bank storage.

articles.title: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications after severe blunt liver trauma in children: a single-center retrospective cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Non-operative management is standard for hemodynamically stable pediatric blunt liver trauma, but the incidence and optimal surveillance for late intra-hepatic arterial complications remain uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To analyze late intra-hepatic arterial complications and their management in a cohort of children with severe blunt liver injury, to confirm a clinical protocol.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients younger than 18 years referred to a quaternary liver center for grade ≥3 blunt liver injury (American Pediatric Surgical Association grading). Demographic and clinical data, imaging findings, active arterial bleeding or pseudoaneurysm not suspected at presentation and/or not detected on initial computerized tomography, and surgical and interventional radiology procedures were collected.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-two patients (median age 14.9 years) with grade III (n=10), IV (n=5), and V (n=17) liver injuries were included. A total of 37 procedures were performed in 19 patients (59%), including peri-hepatic packing, early and delayed surgical explorations, angiography, and 12 embolizations in 11 patients. Overall survival was 100%. In 5 patients (16% of the cohort; all grade IV-V injuries), late intra-hepatic arterial complications were documented on elective follow-up computerized tomography at a median of 10 days after trauma (when patients were asymptomatic), and all were managed successfully by selective interventional radiology, without procedure-related complications. No deaths occurred in this series.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications were not rare in children with grade IV-V liver injuries. These findings support considering computerized tomography in children with very severe hepatic trauma, around days 10-15 after trauma, to allow pre-emptive interventional radiology management.

articles.title: Early arthroplasty versus conversion arthroplasty after failed PFNA in elderly patients with unstable intertrochanteric fractures: a multicenter matched cohort study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: In our study, the clinical and functional outcomes of early arthroplasty versus late conversion arthroplasty approaches were compared in individuals over 75 years of age who underwent PFNA for complex intertrochanteric fractures but whose treatment failed.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter, retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 136 patients treated between January 2023 and March 2025. The cohort consisted of 62 patients who underwent conversion arthroplasty after failed PFNA fixation and 74 patients who received primary early arthroplasty. Demographic characteristics, surgical parameters, complications, and functional and rehabilitation outcomes were compared between groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Early arthroplasty was associated with significantly better six-month functional outcomes, including higher Parker mobility and Merle d'Aubigné scores. The early arthroplasty group also demonstrated shorter times to effective weight-bearing and recovery of walking distance. Perioperative transfusion requirements and systemic complication rates were higher in the PFNA conversion group. However, the time to recovery of unassisted gait did not differ significantly between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Conclusion In elderly patients over 75 years of age with unstable intertrochanteric fractures, early arthroplasty was associated with better short-term functional outcomes, earlier effective weight-bearing and recovery of walking distance, and fewer systemic complications than conversion arthroplasty following failed PFNA. However, these findings should be interpreted in the context of the retrospective design and the functional deterioration that occurred between initial PFNA and subsequent conversion surgery. Primary arthroplasty may be a reasonable option in carefully selected patients with fracture patterns, poor bone quality, or clinical characteristics associated with a high risk of fixation failure.

articles.title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP.

abstract.text: In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend:EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should:Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include:External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquetsAirway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empiric bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with:Injuries that are incompatible with life (e.g., decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (e.g., rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.Resuscitation attempts may be discontinued in pediatric TOHCA patients who:Have no return of spontaneous circulation after provision of at least 15 minutes of high-quality CPR in addition to performance of other lifesaving interventions directed at treating potentially reversible causes of pediatric TOHCA.
