Longer durations of CPR, up to 30 minutes, may be considered for patients with positive predictors of survival such as organized rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander CPR, or with proximate access to a trauma center.Have known predictors of very low probability of survival such as penetrating trauma without proximate access to a trauma center, asystole, unwitnessed arrest, or lack of bystander CPR.Protocols guiding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA benefit from oversight by EMS physicians in collaboration with pediatric experts and local or regional trauma system stakeholders. Implementation of such protocols for pediatric patients benefits from involvement of community stakeholders including family representatives, law enforcement, medical examiner, and child fatality review committees.Considerations for protocol implementation include local resource availability, EMS clinician and public safety, psychosocial support to surviving family members and emergency responders, and dignified handling of the deceased patient.Training needs for EMS clinicians include techniques to communicate with family members regarding the death of a child and understanding the clinician's own response to this low-frequency, high-emotion experience.

articles.title: Predictive value of the modified geriatric trauma outcome score and Charlson Comorbidity Index for 30-day unfavorable outcome in geriatric patients with severe trauma (injury severity score ≥ 16).
articles.journal_full: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

abstract.text: BackgroundThe incidence of geriatric trauma is gradually increasing. Due to declining physiological reserves and a heavier burden of comorbidities, elderly patients have a significantly higher mortality rate than younger patients, making early prediction of unfavorable outcomes of great clinical significance.ObjectiveTo explore the prognostic significance of the MGTOS combined with the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) regarding 30-day unfavorable outcomes in geriatric patients with severe trauma.MethodsA retrospective collection of 213 patients treated in the emergency department of our Hospital from January 2024 to March 2026 was used as the research object. According to their 30-day clinical status, the cohort was stratified into favorable and unfavorable prognosis groups, and their baseline characteristics were compared. Multivariable logistic regression models were utilized to further assess the relationship between MGTOS, CCI, and unfavorable outcomes. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was applied to determine the prognostic accuracy of MGTOS and CCI for unfavorable outcome in geriatric patients with severe trauma.ResultsThere were significant differences in MGTOS and CCI between the favorable prognosis group and the unfavorable prognosis group (all P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified both MGTOS and CCI as independent predictors of unfavorable outcome in geriatric patients with severe trauma. ROC curve evaluation indicated that integrating MGTOS with CCI yielded the maximum area under the curve (AUC = 0.859, 95% CI: 0.787-0.931). Internal validation via repeated stratified sampling demonstrated stable discrimination (median AUC 0.853-0.854).ConclusionMGTOS and CCI have high predictive value for the prognosis in geriatric severe trauma.

articles.title: Interdisciplinary Collaboration as Key Factor for the Optimization of Advanced Heart Failure Treatment.

abstract.text: Heart failure (HF) remains a major global health problem, with outcomes in advanced stages continuing to be poor despite the development of medical therapy and interventional strategies. This report proposes the concept of Interdisciplinary Heart Failure Collaboration (IHFC), a structured framework designed to optimize patient outcomes through coordinated, cross-sectoral care, focusing on the management of advanced HF. The IHFC integrates a broad spectrum of healthcare professionals-including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, nurses, anesthesiologists, intensivists, psychologists, ventricular assist device (VAD) coordinators, and many others-to provide optimal care from outpatient diagnosis to post-discharge long-term management. The model consists of three core management phases: 1) pre-hospital management, which includes outpatient clinic visits, accurate diagnosis and timely referral; 2) intra-hospital management, comprising interventional and surgical treatment including durable VAD implantation and heart transplantation; 3) post-discharge management; post-interventional and post-operative care, rehabilitation and long-term follow-up, patient education and support for self-care. In addition, this report discusses current challenges in implementation, including the need for standardized protocols and effective communication among team members. Rather than replacing existing HF care systems, the IHFC provides a practical framework for integrating established multidisciplinary principles across the entire clinical trajectory of advanced HF and may be adapted to different healthcare settings.

articles.title: [The Impact of Circular Migration on People's Health and the Healthcare System: A Look at the Current Situation in Huelva (Spain)].

abstract.text: Circular migration is a regulated practice in Spain that allows for the recruitment of foreign nationals directly from their home countries. This recruitment typically occurs during seasonal campaigns-in the agricultural and service sectors-leading to a spike in Social Security registrations. Although migration processes can sometimes pose public health challenges, individuals migrating through this channel are subject to health screenings. Nevertheless, despite the generally good health of these individuals (the majority of whom are women), the working and living conditions they face-among other factors-can lead to physical and psychological illness, particularly for those employed in agriculture. In the province of Huelva (in the Autonomous Community of Andalusia), regardless of the ailments these women may develop during their time working in Spain, clinical follow-up care is inadequate-a situation that results in an increased reliance on emergency medical services.

articles.title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP.

abstract.text: In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend: EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should: ○ Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.○ Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include: ▪ External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquets▪ Airway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.▪ Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empirical bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.▪ External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.▪ Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.○ Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with: ○ Injuries that are incompatible with life (eg, decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).○ Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (eg, rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).○ Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.

articles.title: The Role of Droperidol in the Management of Acute Agitation: A Comprehensive Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute behavioral disturbance accounts for ~1.7 million emergency department visits in the USA annually, with 83% involving an underlying serious mental illness. A 2001 FDA black box warning regarding QT prolongation reduced use of droperidol, a butyrophenone antipsychotic, but recent data challenge these concerns.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We reviewed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and observational studies from 2000 to 2025 assessing droperidol's efficacy and safety.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Droperidol provides rapid, effective sedation, with onset within 3 to 10 minutes and median time to adequate sedation of 14 to 25 minutes. Sixty-four percent of patients achieved adequate sedation at 15 minutes with droperidol versus 25% to 35% with ziprasidone and 29% with lorazepam. QT prolongation occurred in 1.3% of 1009 patients, mostly those with pre-existing risk factors. Respiratory depression was less common with droperidol (12%) than with ziprasidone (36% to 39%) or lorazepam (48%). Droperidol-midazolam combinations achieved faster sedation and reduced need for rescue medications (41% vs. 62%). Droperidol-treated patients had shorter hospital stays. Large studies found negligible rates of torsades de pointes or extracardiac arrhythmias. Elderly and pediatric patients responded favorably to low-dose droperidol. The American College of Emergency Physicians now recommends droperidol as first-line treatment for severe agitation. Combined with benzodiazepines, droperidol shows synergistic effects and allows lower doses of both with fewer adverse effects.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Recent evidence contradicts earlier FDA concerns, supporting droperidol as a safe, effective treatment for acute agitation. Its rapid onset, efficacy, safety profile, and operational benefits, including shorter ED stay, support its return to routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Experiences From Implementation of a Hospital Ward Sepsis Response Team at a Large Academic Medical Center.

abstract.text: Hospital-onset sepsis is associated with high mortality and dedicated sepsis response teams can expedite identification and interventions for high-risk patients. Many such teams described in the literature are primarily active in emergency departments or intensive care units. For large academic medical centers with multiple care teams and nursing units, a sepsis response team focused on hospital ward (HW) patients may standardize care of hospitalized septic patients before they develop irreversible organ injury and require critical care stabilization. Here we present our experience establishing the Sepsis Emergency Response Team, an Advanced Practice Provider-led team designed to identify patients with early signs of sepsis on HWs across a large academic medical center.

articles.title: Time to Specialist Pain Service Referral and Variation in Analgesic Management Among Patients With Rib Fractures: A One-Year Clinical Audit.

abstract.text: Background Rib fractures can compromise respiratory function, particularly in older adults. This audit examined assessment, risk documentation, analgesic prescribing, and specialist pain service referral in a surgical inpatient cohort. Methods A single-centre retrospective baseline audit included 52 surgical patients admitted with rib fractures to St Peter's Hospital in Chertsey, UK, between October 2024 and October 2025. Collected audit data were summarised descriptively for patient characteristics, documented risk assessment, prescribing, assessment and referral intervals, regional analgesia, and inpatient outcomes. Results The mean age was 75.3 years. The median hospital stay was six days (IQR: 3-10; n = 52). The median intervals from emergency department (ED) presentation to initial ED doctor assessment and general surgical assessment were 1.33 hours (IQR: 0.73-1.87; n = 52) and 7.07 hours (IQR: 4.65-11.57; n = 45), respectively. The median interval from initial ED doctor assessment to Inpatient Pain Service (IPS) referral was 18.28 hours (IQR: 11.63-35.60; n = 41). Study of the Management of Blunt chest wall trauma (STUMBL)/Battle scores were documented in 15 (28.8%) patients. Initial prescribing varied across analgesic and supportive medication categories, and IPS recommendations addressed several opportunities for optimisation. Regional analgesia catheters were inserted in 13 (25.0%) patients. Pneumonia was recorded in 16 (30.8%), oxygen requirement in 17 (32.7%), and delirium in nine (17.3%); no intensive care admissions were reported. Conclusion The audit identified incomplete risk and pain documentation, variable prescribing, and variation in time to specialist referral. These findings informed a multidisciplinary electronic pathway. Its effect on care processes and patient outcomes remains to be evaluated.

articles.title: Prevention of fireworks-related injuries: a systematic review and practice management guideline from the Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fireworks-related injuries (FRIs) are an increasingly common and preventable problem worldwide. Fireworks have highly variable regulation, and yet there are no evidence-based guidelines for injury prevention.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A priori Population(s), Intervention(s), Comparison(s), and Outcomes (PICO) questions were created. PICO 1 asked, "For children (age<18), should their interaction with fireworks be restricted to professional fireworks displays as compared to private fireworks use to reduce incidence of any FRI, rates of amputation, mortality, vision loss, and burns, and increase return to school or work after injury?" PICO 2 asked, "For both adults and children, should restrictive fireworks-related legislation, as opposed to more lenient legislation, be enacted to decrease the same outcomes?" A systematic search and review of the literature was performed, and the quality of evidence was graded per the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology. Final evidence-based recommendations were developed with working group consensus.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: No studies were included to answer the question related to professional versus private firework displays due to the lack of direct comparisons. Ten studies were identified to analyze the impact of fireworks-related legislation. Eight studies had positive results, suggesting that more stringent legislation of fireworks sale and use is associated with a lower incidence of FRI, and two studies showed no difference. Quality was deemed to be very low.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although of very low quality, available data are consistent in showing that more stringent legislation is associated with a lower incidence of FRI. We therefore conditionally recommend restrictive legislation to limit the sale and use of Class C fireworks by non-professionals to reduce FRI. We cannot make any recommendations regarding private fireworks use because of limited available data, but it is important to note that very few reported injuries occurred at professional displays.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Guideline; Systematic review, level IV.

articles.title: Feasibility of a prehospital point-of-care bioassay in patients with mild traumatic brain injury (GFAP-TBI): a pilot simulation study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Rapid prehospital identification of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) after traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a challenge. Point-of-care (POC) bioassays of biomarkers of ICH, glial fibrillary acidic protein, and ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase L1 offer promise for early detection of intracranial injury and improved triage and prehospital treatment decisions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective pilot feasibility simulation study to evaluate operational implementation of a prehospital whole blood POC device (i-STAT Alinity, Abbott) performed by paramedics in Maryland. Emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians were trained to interact with physicians using a mobile communication platform, Pulsara, during a simulated prehospital encounter involving patients with mild TBI, Glasgow Coma Scale Score of 15, who would be eligible for a research protocol using the POC testing. Saline from a simulated IV was used in place of a blood draw. Time metrics were recorded, and participants completed postsimulation surveys assessing usability and workflow integration.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-four paramedics completed simulations. Median time for teleconsent was 2 (IQR 2-2.5) minutes, device data entry 1 (1-2) minutes, and blood transfer to assay 1 (1-2) minutes. Median total workflow time from consent initiation to assay completion was 6.5 (5-7) minutes. Survey responses demonstrated high usability, with over 90% of participants reporting that training was sufficient. The device was easy to operate, and the workflow could be integrated into routine EMS care. All participants indicated willingness to adopt the device in clinical practice.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this pilot simulation study, prehospital teleconsent and implementation of a whole blood POC bioassay by paramedics were feasible within simulated EMS workflows and could be completed within typical transport intervals. These findings support further clinical investigation of biomarker-based triage strategies for patients with suspected TBI.

articles.title: Gram stain results provide reliable guidance for antibiotic decisions in a surgical trauma intensive care unit.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The frequent use of broad-spectrum antibiotics and rising antimicrobial resistance in the intensive care unit (ICU) makes antimicrobial stewardship essential. Gram stain results have been used to guide initial therapy, but their role in de-escalation is less defined. This study evaluated the reliability of Gram stain results for early antibiotic de-escalation, hypothesizing that blood culture Gram stains are highly predictive compared with other specimen types.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study of cultures from patients admitted to a surgical/trauma ICU during a 1-year period. Gram stain results were compared with final culture results to assess concordance. Specimen types with fewer than 20 samples were excluded from secondary analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 319 patients, 109 (34%) had cultures collected (n=378). Blood (42%), lung (28%), and urine (21%) were most common. Overall, Gram stain results demonstrated 73% positive predictive value (PPV), 87% negative predictive value (NPV), and 84% accuracy. Blood cultures (n=157) had 100% PPV and NPV with 100% accuracy. Urine cultures were highly reliable for identifying infection (PPV 100%) but less so for ruling out infection (NPV 93%, accuracy 94%). Lung cultures showed poor predictability (PPV 44%, NPV 70%, accuracy 63%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Gram stain results can support early antibiotic de-escalation in the ICU. Blood culture Gram stains are highly reliable, urine moderately so, while lung specimens are less predictive. These findings may inform antimicrobial stewardship strategies in critical care settings.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Diagnostic tests-level III.

articles.title: Bedside electromagnetic neuronavigation for cranial access procedures in neurotrauma and neurocritical care.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Bedside cranial access devices (external ventricular drain (EVD), subdural evacuation port system (SEPS), parenchymal intracranial pressure (ICP) monitor) are foundational to neurotrauma and neurocritical care. Craniometric-based techniques are limited by aberrant anatomy, clot-filled ventricles, and complex extra-axial collections. Bedside electromagnetic (EM) neuronavigation registered to computed tomography (CT) imaging may enable precise targeting without requiring transport to the operating room, general anesthesia, or rigid cranial fixation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed patients undergoing bedside cranial procedures with EM-neuronavigation (Medtronic StealthStation) from November 1, 2025 to July 21, 2026 at our Level I trauma center neurocritical care unit for distorted anatomy, atypical targets, and/or high consequences of imprecision. Outcomes included device function, post-procedure neuroimaging confirmation of device placement, and navigation-related complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ten patients underwent 15 EM-navigated bedside procedures (11 EVDs, 2 SEPS, 2 parenchymal ICP monitors). Clinical indications included aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, traumatic brain injury, loculated subdural hematoma, ventriculitis, ventricular trapping, obstructive hydrocephalus, and intracerebral hemorrhage. Notably, EM-navigation enabled dual-catheter placement to access non-communicating ventricular compartments and optimized SEPS placements at maximal extra-axial collection thickness while avoiding vascular membranes. All procedures achieved intended device function and intended positioning on post-procedure imaging. There were no complications or revision procedures related to EM-navigation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this single-center proof-of-principle series, bedside EM-navigation was feasible, safe, and readily integrated into high-risk patient care workflows in neurocritical care. Whether bedside neuronavigation improves procedural precision, supports clinician education, or reduces operative and transport needs was beyond the scope of the current study and requires well-designed prospective evaluation.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level V, Therapeutic/Care Management.

articles.title: A rare case of Valentino syndrome presenting as acute right lower quadrant pain: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Valentino syndrome is a rare clinical entity in which a perforated peptic ulcer causes extravasation of gastrointestinal contents into the right lower quadrant, mimicking acute appendicitis. It is seldom reported in the literature but has significant diagnostic implications due to its deceptive presentation.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 33-year-old male presented with a 4-day history of worsening right lower quadrant abdominal pain accompanied by nausea. There was a long history of intermittent NSAID use. On physical examination, the right lower quadrant was tender with guarding and rebound tenderness. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis. Computed tomography demonstrated an 8-mm appendix suspicious for early acute appendicitis, together with mild prepyloric antral wall thickening and surrounding perigastric inflammatory changes, raising suspicion of a contained peptic ulcer perforation. Diagnostic laparoscopy was initially performed and was converted to open surgery after identification of the suspected gastric perforation. Intraoperatively, the appendix was mildly inflamed and hyperemic, and an appendectomy was performed. Further exploration revealed fibrinopurulent inflammatory changes over the anterior gastric region, with the suspected perforation contained by the omentum. No active leakage was observed, and the suspected perforation site was reinforced with omentopexy. The postoperative course was uneventful; the patient was discharged on postoperative day 5 with dietary, PPI and NSAID avoidance counseling.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Valentino syndrome should be included in the differential diagnosis of right lower quadrant pain, especially in patients with risk factors for peptic ulcer disease. Early imaging and thorough evaluation can prevent misdiagnosis and reduce morbidity.

articles.title: Neuroimaging in non-trauma patients presenting to the emergency department with recurrent seizures.
articles.journal_full: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Inappropriate use of diagnostic tests is associated with a range of adverse effects, including increased healthcare costs, use of emergency department resources and cumulative exposure to ionising radiation . The aim of this study was to determine the frequency, yield and influence of neuroimaging among patients that present to the emergency department (ED) with recurrent seizures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study was conducted in an adult ED in Australia and included patients with recurrent seizures without suspicion of acute traumatic brain injury. The primary outcome was the frequency of neuroimaging. Secondary outcomes were the proportion of abnormal imaging results, the influence of imaging results on acute patient management and the correlation between clinical factors and neuroimaging requests and results.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 398 eligible patient presentations, 84 (21.1%) underwent computed tomography of the brain (CTB) scans. Acute abnormalities were reported in eight (9.5%) instances and resulted in an acute change of management for six (7.1%) patients. A history of brain cancer was the sole clinical variable associated with both acute neuroimaging abnormalities and subsequent change in management.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this cohort of patients presenting with recurrent seizures, CTB scans were frequently performed, but changed clinical management only in the subgroup of patients with a history of brain tumour. The findings suggest that CTB scans have a limited role among ED patients with recurrent seizures and should only be considered in specific clinical circumstances. A more judicious approach to CTB scans has the potential to improve patient flow, patient experience and reduce healthcare costs.

articles.title: Implementing intestinal ultrasound in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: Practical framework for program development: Perspectives from the Pediatric Committee of the Intestinal Ultrasound Group of the United States and Canada.
articles.journal_full: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
authors: Intestinal Ultrasound Group of the United States and Canada (iUSCAN)

abstract.text: Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is a noninvasive, radiation-free tool that is well-tolerated and frequently preferred by children and families. Its ability to provide real-time assessments that facilitate timely decision-making is driving its adoption as an increasingly important monitoring standard in comprehensive pediatric inflammatory bowel disease care. IUS programs follow a common trajectory: begin by identifying and supporting a physician lead, then scale through additional trained physicians, a consultation service, and, where volume supports it, sonographer or hybrid models. Institutional planning should enable this growth while preserving the point-of-care delivery that defines IUS's clinical value. Sustainability requires institutional commitment to equipment, protected time, training (ideally embedded in fellowship), standardized documentation, and a reimbursement strategy. Equipment is attainable, not aspirational: a moderately priced cart-based system is sufficient and should be framed to leadership as essential infrastructure. Centers that adopt IUS with rigorous documentation and join collaborative registries from the outset will be positioned to generate the outcomes data needed to further advance the field.

articles.title: From stable high costs to variable low costs: A continuum of non-breeding energy expenditure strategies in North Atlantic seabirds.

abstract.text: In the wild, many animals track shifting resource availability, a capacity with profound implications for fitness and population viability. Mobile species capable of long-distance movement can access a variety of habitats when not breeding, driving individuals to employ distinct behavioural strategies as they move through environments with contrasting effects on energetic costs (e.g. locomotion or thermoregulation) or gains (e.g. food intake). How energy expenditure is managed during this period may influence the degree to which individuals must accommodate variable resource demand, while its accumulation over time may affect how easily individuals rebuild condition ahead of reproduction. Using light-level geolocation-immersion loggers, we modelled the coefficient of variation in weekly (WEECOV_NB; reflecting stable vs. variable energy expenditure) and total (TEENB) non-breeding season energy expenditure for 8 to 33 North Atlantic populations of six pelagic seabird species contrasting in movement ability and distribution. Within-species, we tested for population differences in WEECOV_NB and TEENB, and, within-individuals, a link between the two (i.e. whether periods of above-average weekly energy expenditure, WEE, accumulate over time or are offset by periods of below-average WEE, leading to lower TEENB). Between-population differences in WEECOV_NB and TEENB were strongest in diving species with high flight costs, where both metrics increased with decreasing individual encountered sea surface temperature (a driver of thermoregulatory costs) and WEECOV_NB increased with individual migratory distance (two diving species only). We further identified a continuum of energy expenditure strategies, with individuals of all species except northern fulmars spanning low TEENB-high WEECOV_NB to high TEENB-low WEECOV_NB. This suggests that multiple energetic pathways for navigating the non-breeding season are possible in this marine region. Ultimately, these analyses underscore energetic trade-offs shaping non-breeding season movement strategies, with implications for energy demand and fitness. As energy expenditure must be matched by intake, non-breeding seabirds in the North Atlantic likely differ in the magnitude and timing of resource requirement. These populations may thus differ in their vulnerability to stressors that further elevate costs or reduce access to prey and in their capacity to cope with environmental change.

articles.title: Primary Care Continuity During the Transition to Adulthood and Its Association With Acute Healthcare Utilization Among Youth With Eating Disorders.
articles.journal_full: The International journal of eating disorders

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The transition from pediatric to adult care is a high-risk period for youth with eating disorders (EDs), often characterized by care disruptions and disengagement from adult services. This study examined whether patterns of primary care continuity during this transition are associated with acute healthcare utilization post-transition.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study of 1106 youth discharged from a tertiary pediatric ED program in Ontario, Canada. Primary care continuity was categorized into five groups based on dominant general practitioner (GP) patterns before and after age 18. Outcomes included emergency department visits (EDVs) and hospitalizations within 2 years post-transition. Multivariate logistic regression models estimated associations, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors, and corresponding pre-transition acute healthcare utilization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Compared with maintaining the same dominant GP before and after age 18 (Group 1), no dominant GP in either period (Group 5) was associated with lower odds of any EDV (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.32-0.73), any hospitalization (OR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.16-0.76), and MH-related hospitalization (OR: 0.30, 95% CI: 0.08-0.81). A dominant GP before but not after 18 (Group 4) was associated with lower odds of MH-related EDVs (OR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.29-0.95). Sensitivity analyses generally supported these findings.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Primary care continuity was not associated with acute healthcare utilization among youth with EDs, highlighting a complex relationship between GP continuity, healthcare needs, and healthcare use. Lower utilization among those without a dominant GP may not indicate lower need or better outcomes. Future research should clarify these patterns, while transition planning should continue to support timely and sustained primary care involvement for youth with EDs.

articles.title: Clinical and Radiographic Characteristics of Pneumococcal Pneumonia in Children: A Case Series.

abstract.text: Given the decline in pneumococcal infections related to widespread childhood vaccinations in the United States, we evaluate the rate of Streptococcus pneumoniae and also report the demographic and radiographic characteristics of children with pneumococcal pneumonia in the post-pneumococcal conjugate vaccine era. We studied the prevalence of medical comorbidities, clinical presentations and outcomes, antibiotic susceptibility results, and radiographic findings among children aged less than 18 years presenting to a pediatric Emergency Department between 2010 and 2023 with a diagnosis of pneumonia and detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae in blood and/or pleural fluid. Of the 31 cases of pneumococcal pneumonia, over 50% occurred among children less than 5 years of age, and 71% of children had medical comorbidities. Eighty percent of children had radiographic pneumonia; the most common radiographic findings included opacities (71.0%), consolidation (29.0%), and pleural effusion (25.8%). Given high rates of antibiotic overtreatment, these findings may help clinicians to judiciously use antibiotics for children with pneumonia.

articles.title: Predicting mortality in pediatric cases with severe traumatic brain injury: is the Eppendorf-Cologne Scale more reliable than Glasgow Coma Scale?
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
authors: TraumaRegister DGU® of the German Trauma Society (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Unfallchirurgie; DGU)

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) in children is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, requiring reliable tools for early assessment and prognosis. While the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is the standard neurological evaluation tool, it has limitations in pediatric patients. The Eppendorf-Cologne Scale (ECS), originally developed for adults, emphasizes pupil size, reactivity, and motor response and may offer advantages in children.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter cohort study analyzed TraumaRegister DGU® data from 5,851 pediatric patients (mean age 9.6 years). Documentation included prehospital and in-hospital assessments, injury characteristics, and outcomes. ECS and GCS scores were evaluated based on first recorded prehospital values. Predictive performance for mortality and severe TBI was assessed using AUROC analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the cohort, 2,582 patients (44.1%) had severe TBI and 476 (8.1%) died in hospital. GCS showed slightly higher accuracy for predicting severe TBI (AUROC 0.778, 95% CI 0.766-0.791) than ECS (AUROC 0.745, 95% CI 0.731-0.758). For mortality prediction, ECS performed marginally better (AUROC 0.943, 95% CI 0.929-0.957) than GCS (AUROC 0.910, 95% CI 0.896-0.924). Mortality rates were 90% in the worst ECS category and 55% in the worst GCS category.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: GCS showed higher discrimination for severe TBI, whereas ECS showed higher discrimination for in-hospital mortality among patients with severe TBI. ECS may provide complementary prognostic information, but its clinical utility and role alongside GCS require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Blunt anatomical cardiac injury (BACI) - lessons from a single trauma center cohort.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Patients with anatomical damage to the heart after blunt trauma are rarely seen in hospital settings due to their elevated prehospital mortality. The aim of this study is to review our center experience with this entity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: After institutional research board approval, a local Trauma Databank search (Qatar National Trauma Registry) was performed from 2016 to 2025. Cases presented with blunt trauma and anatomical changes to pericardium or heart, detected in imaging or surgery, in patients above 13 years old were diagnosed as blunt anatomical cardiac injury - BACI and included.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Amongst 17542 blunt trauma cases admitted to our Trauma Center during the study period, 15 patients (0.09% incidence) met the inclusion/exclusion criteria. All patients were males, with average age of 43 years (ranges 26-75), with ISS of 32 (ranges 10-75). The most common mechanism of injury was pedestrian struck (5cases -33%). Hypotension at trauma room assessment was common (8 cases - 53% of patients) and 8 patients (53%) required surgery. FAST, echocardiogram and computed tomography were used as diagnostic tools. The patients presented in 4 anatomical patterns: (a) intracardiac/valve damage; (b) pericardial effusion; (c) pericardial laceration and (d) cardiac rupture. Three patients (20%) died, all during emergent surgery and sustaining cardiac rupture.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: BACI is uncommonly seen at Emergency Departments and carries elevated early mortality in cases with cardiac rupture, requiring high index of suspicion for diagnosis. Different clinical presentations of BACI were observed and described in this series. Further studies with larger number of patients are needed to further clarify possible differences in severity, surgical requirement and mortality according to the BACI structural presentation.

articles.title: Projections of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease incidence and its driving factors in 195 countries and territories to 2050: a modeling study.

abstract.text: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. This study aims to characterize historical trends in COPD burden from 1990 to 2021, project incidence through 2050 by age, sex, year, and location, and quantify the impact of key risk factors on future COPD incidence. We analyzed historical COPD burden across 204 countries and territories using Global Burden of Disease 2021 estimates from 1990 to 2021, including incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). Temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression and Age-Period-Cohort (APC) modeling. Future COPD incidence was projected to 2050 for 195 countries and territories with compatible age-, sex-, year-, and location-specific population forecasting data using a Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort (BAPC) model. Population attributable and impact fractions were calculated to estimate the benefits of reducing modifiable exposures. By 2050, global COPD incidence is projected to continue rising with annual new cases expected to reach 32.3 (95%UI 13.6-50.9) million, though the age-standardized rate may decline by 3.0%. Although sex disparities are narrowing, significant geographic inequalities will persist. China, India, and the United States are forecasted to remain the largest contributors, jointly accounting for nearly half of global incident cases. Eliminating smoking and ambient particulate matter pollution could prevent up to 33.0% and 30.1% of new cases, respectively. Despite modest declines in age-standardized incidence rates, the absolute number of new COPD cases is projected to nearly double by 2050. Marked disparities by age, sex, and geography highlight the need for targeted and equitable public health interventions. Strengthening tobacco control and air pollution mitigation policies could prevent millions of future cases and significantly reduce the global COPD burden.

articles.title: Functional echocardiography for management of shock in neonates- a randomized clinical trial.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Neonatal shock is associated with a high case fatality rate. Detection and management of shock by monitoring only clinical parameters may be inadequate due to inconsistent association with tissue perfusion. We evaluated the efficacy of adding functional echocardiography to standard clinical assessment in improving short-term outcome in neonates with shock. This was an open-labelled randomized clinical trial conducted in level III NICU of a tertiary care hospital in India. Neonates born at 28-42 completed weeks of gestation and developing shock defined by presence of at least two of seven prespecified criteria: tachycardia, hypotension, prolonged capillary refilling time, low perfusion index, increased central-to-peripheral temperature difference, oliguria and metabolic acidosis were randomized into two groups: Echo group-shock managed using both standard clinical assessment and functional echocardiography and, Clinical group- shock managed using only standard clinical assessment. Primary outcome was survival without inotropic support at 72 h post-randomization. Secondary outcomes were time to hemodynamic stability, survival to discharge and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or cystic periventricular leukomalacia. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable in the two groups. Survival without inotropic support at 72 h was observed in 28 (73.7%) of 38 neonates in the Echo group and 13 (33.3%) of 39 neonates in the Clinical group (RR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.36-3.58, P = 0.0004; adjusted RR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.33-3.59). Hemodynamic stability was reached earlier in the Echo group (median, 3 vs. 5 h; P = .001). Survival to discharge (73.7% vs. 59.0%; RR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.90-1.73) and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or cystic periventricular leukomalacia (10.5% vs. 7.7%) did not differ significantly.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this single-center, open-label trial, adding protocolized functional echocardiography to clinical assessment increased survival without inotropic support at 72 h after randomization. Survival to discharge and severe brain injury did not differ significantly; the trial was not powered for these outcomes. Multicenter trials with blinded outcome assessment are needed.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Clinical Trial Registry of India Identifier (CTRI/2023/08/056672), registered on 21st august 2023.

abstract.label: WHAT IS KNOWN
abstract.text: • Diagnosis of neonatal shock and initiating inotropes solely on the basis of clinical parameters like low BP or isolated tachycardia does not address the underlying physiology. • This practice may not help match the pharmacological action of drug to underlying cause.

abstract.label: WHAT IS NEW
abstract.text: • In a randomized trial of neonates with shock, adding protocolized functional echocardiography to clinical assessment increased survival without inotropic support at 72 h (74% vs. 33%). • Effects on survival to discharge (74% vs. 59%) and severe brain injury were imprecise; multicenter trials are needed before routine use.

articles.title: Caregiving networks and children with neurologic impairment: A multicenter social network analysis protocol.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Children with neurologic impairment (NI) often require care from multiple paid and unpaid caregivers-a "caregiving network"-yet little is known about how caregiving networks influence child health. Understanding how networks influence health could support innovative intervention designs targeting groups of caregivers.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This multicenter prospective cohort study will evaluate whether caregiving network characteristics are associated with serious health events and quality of life among children with NI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: THRIvE (Teamwork and Healthy Relationships Improving Engagement in Caregiving) is a multicenter prospective cohort study enrolling children ages 2-16 years with NI and at least one hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visit in the prior 12 months, along with primary caregivers (PCGs) and secondary caregivers (SCGs), at five academic medical centers. Caregiving networks will be assessed at enrollment using egocentric social network analysis administered to PCGs and validated with SCG surveys. Exposures include network density, centralization, triadic closure, network size, and composition. Primary outcomes at 12 months are serious health events (death or hospitalization) and child quality of life. Secondary outcomes include clinical symptoms, missed school days, and ED visits. Associations will be examined using mixed-effects regression models accounting for site clustering, confounding, and multiple comparisons.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This study will provide novel prospective evidence about how caregiving network configurations are associated with health outcomes in children with NI.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Findings may identify modifiable social network features that can inform future family-centered, network-based interventions to improve child health and quality of life.

articles.title: The cardiorespiratory sports clinic: A unique multidisciplinary program to care for young athletes with symptoms limiting performance.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of international medical research

abstract.text: Pediatric athletes with exercise-limiting symptoms frequently undergo fragmented evaluations across multiple specialties with overlapping cardiac, pulmonary, and musculoskeletal symptoms. To address this gap, Cincinnati Children's Hospital developed a multidisciplinary cardiorespiratory sports clinic integrating pediatric cardiology, pulmonology, and sports medicine to help athletes not only to return-to-play but to regain peak performance after injury or illness while promoting long-term health and resilience. The purpose of this narrative review was to outline the mission, development, and early results of the cardiorespiratory sports clinic, which was established to evaluate pediatric and young adult athletes (aged 12-21 years) with cardiopulmonary symptoms affecting athletic performance or concerns regarding safe sports participation. Standardized pre-visit testing, multidisciplinary assessment, and individualized management plans were implemented to improve diagnostic efficiency and expedite return-to-sport. Between August 2020 and December 2024, 393 athletes (including 42% men), with average age 13.9 ± 2.8 years and mean body mass index 22.6 ± 5.3 kg/m2 were evaluated. Two-third (66%) required no additional testing or subspecialty referral. Additional diagnostic testing was selectively pursued when indicated, resulting in identification of clinically significant cardiac or pulmonary disorders in 17% of the participants, including exercise-induced laryngeal obstruction, dysfunctional breathing, reactive airway disease, and primary cardiac pathology. In addition to clinical care, the program established a robust platform for multidisciplinary education, fellowship training, and research in pediatric exercise medicine. In aggregate, the multidisciplinary cardiorespiratory sports clinic presents an innovative and scalable framework for the healthcare assessment of pediatric athletes experiencing exercise-limiting symptoms. Through the consolidation of specialized expertise, this program optimizes clinical care delivery, expedites restoration to optimal athletic performance, and contributes to the advancement of education and research within the field of pediatric exercise medicine.

articles.title: Nationwide transcatheter aortic valve implantation rollout and cardiac-origin out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in the elderly.
authors: Japanese Circulation Society Resuscitation Science Study (JCS-ReSS) Group

articles.title: Association between direct admission of patients with severe injuries to a level 1 trauma centre and mortality: nationwide cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate whether direct admission to a level 1 trauma centre is associated with lower mortality among patients with severe injuries.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Nationwide cohort study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Dutch National Trauma Registry that includes data on patients admitted to all trauma receiving emergency departments in the Netherlands, 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2019.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: 6396 patients with severe injuries (Injury Severity Score ≥16), transported by professional emergency medical services to a level 1 or lower level (level 2 or 3) trauma centre.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: 30 day mortality for patients transported to a level 1 trauma centre compared with those admitted to a lower level trauma centre.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 6396 patients (36.1% women; median age 60.0 years, interquartile range 39.0-76.0) were included in the study and 4065 (63.6%) were admitted directly to a level 1 trauma centre. The 30 day mortality was 23.8% for patients admitted directly to a level 1 trauma centre compared with 18.5% for patients transported to a lower level trauma centre. Instrumental variable analysis showed that treatment of patients in a level 1 trauma centre was associated with reduced 30 day mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.61, 95% confidence interval 0.39 to 0.95). Similar results were found in patients with a traumatic brain injury and critical injuries (ie, Injury Severity Score ≥25), and in elderly people.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The findings indicate that the risk of death was significantly reduced when patients with severe injuries were directly admitted to a level 1 trauma centre. Optimising field triage to increase the proportion of patients with severe injuries directly admitted to a level 1 trauma centre may improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Alabama Perinatal Quality Collaborative Postpartum Bracelet Pilot.
articles.journal_full: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the feasibility of a pilot project implementing postpartum alert bracelets to support the timely identification and treatment of maternal complications.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Program evaluation.

abstract.label: SETTING/LOCAL PROBLEM
abstract.text: Seven urban, regional, and community hospitals in Alabama participating in the Alabama Perinatal Quality Collaborative. Inconsistent recognition of recent childbirth status in emergency settings and limited retention of discharge education can delay diagnosis and treatment.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Patients who recently gave birth (n = 1,237), Mother-baby unit (MBU) nurse leaders (n = 10), emergency department (ED) nurses (n = 35), and emergency medical technicians (EMTs; n = 79).

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS/MEASUREMENTS
abstract.text: The intervention included distribution of silicone postpartum alert bracelets designed for continuous wear, standardized patient education, and staff awareness efforts. Surveys assessed patient acceptance and perceived safety and ED nurses' and EMTs' awareness and perceived utility. Semistructured interviews explored nurse leaders' implementation experiences.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Patient acceptance was high (81.3% would wear; 79.9% felt safer). Compared with non-Hispanic White respondents, non-Hispanic Black respondents (odds ratio [OR] = 2.05, 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.67, 2.43]) and Hispanic respondents (OR = 2.23, 95% CI [1.78, 2.68]) were more likely to report willingness to wear the bracelet and perceived safety benefits. Awareness was 100% among MBU nurse leaders, 40% among ED nurses, and 19% among EMTs. However, both ED nurses and EMTs agreed that the bracelets could support timely recognition of complications and potentially reduce maternal mortalities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Postpartum alert bracelets are a promising, low-cost intervention highly accepted by patients. Statewide implementation requires standardized distribution and targeted education for patients, ED staff, and emergency medical services.

articles.title: Congestion Assessed With Inferior Vena Cava Ultrasound Predicts Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Inferior vena cava (IVC) parameters relate to clinical outcomes in retrospective acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) studies, but prospective data on long-term outcomes and quality of life are unavailable.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The objective of the study was to evaluate the prognostic value of IVC parameters for clinical outcomes and their association with quality of life.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients admitted for ADHF were prospectively enrolled from January 2022 to May 2024. Point-of-care IVC ultrasound was performed at admission and discharge. The Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) was evaluated at baseline, 1, 6, and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and ADHF rehospitalization at 12 months.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 100 patients (median age 67 years, 28% women, 45% NYHA functional class III/IV, 65% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction) were included. The primary endpoint occurred in 50 patients (9 deaths and 41 ADHF hospitalizations). In multivariable analysis, admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm (HR: 3.71; 95% CI: 1.97-7.01; P < 0.001), admission maximum IVC diameter >2.3 cm (HR: 2.70; 95% CI: 1.46-4.96; P = 0.001), discharge minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.3 cm (HR: 2.27; 95% CI: 1.24-4.14; P = 0.008), and discharge sniff IVC collapsibility index <36% (HR: 3.16; 95% CI: 1.64-6.06; P < 0.001) were independent predictors of the primary endpoint. KCCQ scores improved during follow-up (Ptime<0.001) but were not associated with the primary endpoint. Patients with admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm had lower KCCQ scores throughout the study period (Pgroup = 0.03).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In ADHF patients, IVC parameters predict 12-month outcomes and may serve as objective markers to identify residual congestion and stratify risk.

articles.title: The Effect of Care Team Composition on Healthcare Resource Use Among Rural Children Enrolled in Hospice.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of hospice & palliative care

abstract.text: ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the effect of care team composition on healthcare resource use among rural children enrolled in hospice during the last year of life.MethodsThe sample included 3131 children aged 20 years or younger who received concurrent hospice care, resided in rural communities in 28 Midwestern and Southern states, and were enrolled in Medicaid between 2011 and 2022. Analyses used multivariable logistic and Poisson regression models adjusted for demographic, health, and community characteristics and year of data collection.ResultsChildren had a mean age of 10.1 years (SD = 7.1); 42.1% received care from a medical subspecialist, 52.5% from a primary care provider, and the mean care team size was 9.1 providers (SD = 17.0). Multiple hospital admissions occurred in 80.3% of children, multiple ED visits in 40.4%, and children averaged 1.2 duplicate medications (SD = 0.90). Subspecialist involvement was associated with lower resource use: 69% lower odds of multiple admissions, 83% lower odds of multiple ED visits, and a 37% lower rate of duplicate medications. In contrast, primary care involvement and larger care team size were associated with significantly greater resource use, particularly ED visits and medication utilization.ConclusionCare team composition was significantly associated with healthcare use among rural children enrolled in hospice. Future research should examine the specific mechanisms through which care team composition influences healthcare use.

articles.title: IEPA scavenges reactive carbonyl species to mitigate oxidative stress in a rat model of acute radiation syndrome and modulates irradiation-induced transcriptomic changes.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Exposure to high doses of ionizing radiation may cause acute radiation syndrome (ARS), in which reactive oxygen and carbonyl species (ROS/RCS) and DNA damage contribute to cell death and depletion of bone marrow and peripheral blood cells. Although recombinant growth factor therapies reduce mortality in preclinical models, their reliance on parenteral administration may limit their utility in mass-casualty scenarios. Imidazolyl ethanamide pentandioic acid (IEPA) is an orally bioavailable small molecule that improves survival in rodent models of ARS. While in vitro data suggest an antioxidant mechanism, its mode of action in vivo remains incompletely understood.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Mechanistic studies were conducted in female WAG/RijCmcr rats exposed to 7.75 Gy total-body irradiation (TBI). Systemic oxidative stress was assessed by quantifying reduced glutathione levels in blood. Urine from IEPA-treated animals was analyzed by LC-MS/MS for metabolites indicative of RCS scavenging. Protein carbonylation was evaluated in vitro by Western blot. Transcriptomic alterations associated with IEPA treatment were characterized by RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of bone marrow and peripheral blood samples collected on days 4 and 14 post-TBI.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: IEPA increased reduced glutathione levels in the blood of irradiated rats by 21% (p = .035). A product of the direct scavenging reaction between IEPA and the prevalent RCS 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) was detected in urine. IEPA reduced 4-HNE-mediated protein carbonylation in vitro. In addition, IEPA treatment was associated with transcriptomic changes (132 differentially expressed genes with fold change > 2, p.adj < 0.05) particularly in the peripheral blood on day 14 post-TBI. Gene ontology analysis indicated modulation of immune cell differentiation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: IEPA attenuated irradiation-induced systemic oxidative stress, potentially in part through direct scavenging of RCS. Associated transcriptomic changes suggest modulation of immune differentiation pathways in peripheral blood. This warrants further study of RCS scavenging, oxidative stress reduction and immunomodulation in IEPA treatment in the future.

articles.title: Emergency department ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter insertion training with virtual reality.
articles.journal_full: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter (USG-PIVC) insertion is a challenging skill for emergency department (ED) clinicians to master. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising, cost-effective tool for procedural training. Unlike manikins or phantoms, VR enables immersive, repeatable and scalable training with real-time feedback, simulating real ED conditions to improve skill transfer and learner engagement. However, its use in USG-PIVC education within EDs has not been evaluated despite persistent training barriers to USG-PIVC insertion in this setting.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To assess the feasibility of conducting a large-scale randomised controlled trial (RCT) that integrates a VR intervention into USG-PIVC training, addressing these challenges before evaluating effectiveness.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-site feasibility RCT will be conducted in an Australian ED. Twenty ED doctors will be randomly assigned to either standard training or standard training plus VR simulation. In addition to feasibility outcomes, the study will assess clinical metrics including first-attempt success rate, number of attempts, time to insertion, vein difficulty, completion of procedural steps, immediate complications, time spent practising, and clinician confidence and satisfaction.

abstract.label: EXPECTED OUTCOMES
abstract.text: Although limited by a small sample size and single-site design, the findings from this pilot trial will provide valuable insights into the feasibility of integrating VR into USG-PIVC training. These results will help inform the design and implementation of a larger-scale, multi-site trial to evaluate effectiveness and broader applicability.

articles.title: Why standardised performance-based ultrasound mastery training is needed now: a narrative review.
articles.journal_full: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)

abstract.text: Difficult intravenous access is common in acute and emergency care and contributes to repeated peripheral intravenous cannulation attempts, delayed therapy and escalation to more invasive devices. Ultrasound-guided peripheral cannula placement is widely recommended as an escalation strategy, yet ultrasound education remains inconsistent across settings. Systematic reviews show heterogeneity in time spent in training, curricula, assessment methods, supervision, validation and competency pathways, while failure rates for peripheral intravenous catheters remain high. Performance-based mastery learning, particularly simulation-based mastery learning, addresses this gap by defining competence using a minimum passing standard score, structured checklists, deliberate practice and retesting until proficiency is demonstrated. Evidence supports the success of simulation-based mastery learning for ultrasound-guided vascular access, including improved performance, confidence and reduced use of midline devices in difficult intravenous access populations. This article outlines a standardised mastery curriculum and audit framework aligned with Association for Vascular Access clinical practice guidelines and Infusion Nurses Society standards and seal of approval.

articles.title: Predicting engagement in care before and during the COVID-19 pandemic among people with HIV.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Engagement in care is poor in the US for people with HIV (PWH) and may have been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, longitudinal study analyzed data from the IQVIA PharMetrics® Plus Claims database to assess engagement in care among PWH in the US 12 months before and during the COVID-19 pandemic (pre- and post-March 1, 2020). Eligible PWH had ≥ 2 medical claims with a HIV-1 diagnosis and continuous health plan enrollment. Three definitions of engagement in care were used: HIV-related healthcare visits, CD4 count/HIV viral load tests, and treatment adherence. Logistic regression compared pre- and during-pandemic engagement in care and identified factors associated with disengagement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In 19,782 PWH analyzed, the likelihood of engaging with care decreased significantly (p < 0.001) during the pandemic for HIV-related healthcare visits (odds ratio [OR] 0.65), laboratory testing (OR 0.55), and treatment adherence (OR 0.90). Strong predictors of disengagement included younger age, being female, insurance type, HIV treatment type, and having a pre-pandemic HIV-related emergency room visit.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Engagement in care for PWH declined during the pandemic, with a variety of characteristics predictive of disengagement. These findings may help to inform interventions and initiatives throughout the HIV care continuum.

articles.title: Fragmentation of Care in Violently Injured Patients.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Survivors of injuries due to violence are at risk for recurrent violent injury (RVI). After an initial violent injury, patients may seek care at multiple different health systems, leading to fragmentation of care, which is a barrier to secondary prevention efforts.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To quantify the missed opportunities for secondary prevention efforts in violent injury caused by fragmentation of care.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study used a regional health information exchange database for a major metropolitan area (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) from January 1, 2018, through November 30, 2023. Rates of and time to RVI were calculated and then types and locations of visits within the first postinjury year were tabulated. Using multivariable logistic regression, patient and injury factors associated with RVI were identified. Patients with a visit for violent injury between January 1, 2018, through November 30, 2023, were included. Any patients without a full year of follow-up were excluded. These data were analyzed from February 2025 through December 2025.

abstract.label: EXPOSURE
abstract.text: Fragmentation of care.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcome was RVI, defined as having another emergency department, observation or inpatient visit coded for injuries due to interpersonal violence. The association between fragmentation of care and RVI was examined, including the types of visits associated with RVI. Logistic regression modeling also examined demographic and clinical factors, as well as mechanism of injury associated with RVI.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 26 368 patients with a violent injury (mean [SD] age, 38.0 [14.8] years; 10 456 [39.7%] female and 15 894 [60.3%] male), 2591 (9.8%) recurred within 1 year and 4247 (16.1%) total recurred during the study period. Risk factors for recurrence included initial firearm injury (odds ratio [OR], 3.3; 95% CI, 3.0-3.6), substance use diagnosis (OR, 1.8; 95% CI, 1.6-1.9), and psychiatric diagnoses (OR, 2.4; 95% CI, 2.2-2.6). Among those with RVI, 1701 (40.1%) received treatment for their second violent injury in a different hospital system from their index injury. All patients with RVI (4247) had at least 1 health care encounter between their index and their recurrent injury, 66.0% of which (n = 2803) sought care at multiple institutions during the study period and ultimately, on average, received 42.5% of their care in a health care system different from their index encounter.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this study, recurrent violent injury was common in this major metropolitan area, and single-center studies would have missed at least 40% of recurrences. All patients who went on to recur had additional health care encounters prior to that recurrence, with 66% accessing care in multiple health care systems. This study quantifies the missed opportunities for secondary prevention efforts in violent injury and highlights the importance of collaboration in areas with fragmentation of care.

articles.title: Prevalence of positive eating disorder screens among adults attending an Irish emergency department: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Eating disorders are associated with substantial physical and psychiatric morbidity and increasing healthcare utilisation. The emergency department represents an important opportunity for early identification of patients with eating disorders; however, the proportion of adults attending Irish emergency departments who screen positive for a possible eating disorder is unknown.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To determine the proportion of adults attending an Irish emergency department who screen positive for a possible eating disorder, and the association of a positive screen with demographic characteristics and alcohol and substance use.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional screening study was conducted in the adult emergency department of a tertiary Irish teaching hospital between the 18th and 24th of March 2025. Medically stable patients aged ≥16 years were invited to complete an anonymous questionnaire. Participants were screened for a possible eating disorder using the modified Sick, Control, One, Fat, Food (mSCOFF) questionnaire (positive screen: score ≥2). Alcohol consumption was assessed using the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test-Consumption (AUDIT-C), while tobacco and drug use were evaluated using questions adapted from the Alcohol, Smoking and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST). Demographic and clinical characteristics were compared between mSCOFF-positive and mSCOFF-negative participants.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 292 participants completed the survey, with mSCOFF data available for 287. Overall, 70 of 287 participants (24.4%) screened positive for a possible eating disorder. Younger age was significantly associated with a positive screen (p = 0.004). Mean BMI did not differ significantly between mSCOFF-positive and mSCOFF-negative participants (28.7 vs 27.2 kg/m²; p = 0.1). Risky alcohol consumption was reported by 49.7% of participants but was less common among mSCOFF-positive participants (OR 0.5, 95% CI 0.3-0.9; p < 0.05). Non-prescribed sedative use was associated with a positive screen (OR 3.9, 95% CI 1.3-12.1; p = 0.01), while no significant associations were observed for tobacco, cannabis or stimulant use.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Almost one in four adults attending this Irish emergency department screened positive for a possible eating disorder on the mSCOFF. As the mSCOFF has not been validated against diagnostic interview, this is not an estimate of eating disorder prevalence. Younger age and non-prescribed sedative use were associated with a positive screen. Multicentre studies incorporating diagnostic assessment are needed.

articles.title: Bowel wall thickness across postmenstrual age in preterm infants: a prospective ultrasound study of intestinal structural development.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: The preterm intestine undergoes rapid structural and functional maturation during late gestation and early postnatal life. Although abdominal ultrasound is increasingly used in neonatal care, quantitative descriptions of developmental variation in bowel wall structure and motility remain limited. In this prospective observational study, preterm infants born at ≤ 34 weeks' gestation underwent serial abdominal ultrasound examinations in a level III neonatal intensive care unit. A total of 260 longitudinal ultrasound scans were performed from early postnatal life through term-equivalent age. Bowel wall thickness (BWT) was measured in four abdominal quadrants using a standardized high-frequency ultrasound protocol. Small-bowel loops were identified using established sonographic criteria. Peristaltic activity was graded semi-quantitatively (0 = absent, 1 = intermittent, 2 = active) during standardized cine observation. Associations between postmenstrual age and ultrasound measures were evaluated using regression and correlation analyses accounting for repeated measurements within infants. Fourteen preterm infants contributed serial examinations spanning 26 to 37 weeks' postmenstrual age. BWT demonstrated a progressive increase with advancing maturity and consistent regional variability across abdominal quadrants. Peristaltic activity similarly increased with postmenstrual age, with a transition from absent or intermittent motility in earlier scans to active peristalsis at later ages. Structural and functional findings showed parallel maturational trends.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Bedside ultrasound enables quantitative assessment of intestinal structure and motility during preterm development. These findings provide longitudinal developmental imaging data describing intestinal maturation and support future studies examining intestinal adaptation and clinical outcomes in preterm infants.

abstract.label: WHAT IS KNOWN
abstract.text: • Real-time assessment of neonatal bowel health remains a major clinical challenge with important knowledge gaps. Reliance on nonspecific clinical signs, delayed laboratory changes, and adjunctive abdominal radiographs often leads to late recognition of bowel injury, reducing opportunities for timely and targeted intervention. Abdominal ultrasound is emerging as a valuable tool for early detection of gut injury and for real-time monitoring, offering neonatologists a way to guide bedside decision-making more precisely..

abstract.label: WHAT IS NEW
abstract.text: • Provides prospective ultrasound characterization of bowel wall thickness across postmenstrual age in preterm infants. • Demonstrates maturational and regional variation in intestinal wall structure during early life. • Establishes foundational developmental imaging data to support future longitudinal and outcome-based studies.

articles.title: Abbreviated brain magnetic resonance imaging protocol using fluid-attenuated inversion recovery and diffusion-weighted imaging in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Rapid brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocols may reduce radiation exposure and sedation requirements in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical adequacy of an abbreviated brain MRI (abMRI) protocol featuring fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included pediatric emergency department patients who underwent abMRI between July 2023 and July 2025. The protocol consisted of axial diffusion-weighted imaging and axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery obtained with motion-resistant radial filling, with an acquisition time of approximately 220 s. Technical success and clinical adequacy were evaluated using image quality, emergency observation, pediatric neurology follow-up, and full-protocol MRI when clinically indicated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 971 attempted examinations, diagnostic-quality images were obtained in 951, yielding a technical success rate of 97.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 96.8-98.7%). The mean age was 7.61±5.46 years, and 480 patients (50.5%) were boys. Of the 951 diagnostic examinations, 649 underwent no further neuroimaging. Full-protocol MRI was performed in 302 patients. Eight false-negative cases were identified. The overall clinical adequacy rate was 99.2% (943/951; 95% CI 98.4-99.6%). Clinically inadequate examinations were more frequent in patients with suspected intracranial hypertension (P<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Diffusion-weighted imaging- and motion-resistant radial FLAIR-based abMRI appears feasible and clinically adequate as an initial imaging approach for selected pediatric emergency neuroimaging indications. Full-protocol MRI remains preferable when intracranial hypertension is suspected.

articles.title: Decision making around end-of-life: Focused ethnography in two intensive care units in Vietnam.

abstract.text: Literature on the quality of death and dying has predominantly drawn on high-income contexts, while much less is known about end-of-life care in low-middle-income settings. In Vietnam, policy and practice around palliative and end-of-life care has not kept pace with the ageing of the population. This study explores factors influencing end-of-life decision making in intensive care units (ICUs) where formal protocols are lacking. This analysis is a part of a larger ethnographic study examining vital sign monitoring in two ICUs in Vietnam, including observations, informal conversations and formal interviews with healthcare workers. In addition to learning about the care practices around vital sign monitoring, we noted the various complexities that influenced physicians and family members' end-of-life decision making in these contexts. Factors included patients' prognosis, family wishes, cultural practices surrounding death and financial considerations. Financial concerns were a significant factor in discontinuing treatment, particularly for uninsured patients. The lack of accessible out-of-hospital care made it difficult for patients to spend their final moments at home with their families, which is important in Vietnamese cultures. This paper sheds light on the preferences and practices of families and staff at the end-of-life with the longer-term goal of improving end-of-life care across Vietnam.

articles.title: Pediatric Frostbite and Cold-Weather Injuries in the United States: A Multi-Database Retrospective Analysis.
articles.journal_full: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association

abstract.text: Pediatric cold-weather injuries (frostbite and hypothermia) are uncommon but can lead to substantial morbidity, including amputation and long-term functional loss. National data on incidence, management, and outcomes are limited, particularly for fatalities outside healthcare settings. We conducted a retrospective analysis using three complementary data sources: an institutional registry at an American Burn Association-verified burn center (2018-2026), the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Readmission Database (NRD 2016-2021), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Storm Events Database (NOAA 2016-2023). Our institutional cohort included 16 patients (ages 1-17 years; 68.8% >13 years); treatments included rapid rewarming (43.8%), perfusion imaging (56.3%), thrombolytic therapy (18.8%), and hyperbaric oxygen therapy (31.3%). Two patients required amputation; both presented with hemorrhagic blisters, had delayed care, and did not receive thrombolytics. No thrombolytic-related complications were observed.
