Nationally, 2,155 pediatric cold weather injuries occurred; a national estimated hospitalization rate of 1.62 per 100,000. 79 pediatric frostbite admissions were identified, including 15 admissions designated as severe injury. NOAA data captured 16 pediatric deaths and 49 injuries across 30 states. Pediatric cold-weather injuries result in morbidity and mortality across diverse U.S. regions. Early aggressive management may reduce amputation and broader adoption of standardized protocols and public health prevention strategies are needed. Limitations of public health data emphasize the need for integrating diverse data sources to better understand the full impact of cold-weather injuries in the U.S.

articles.title: Propranolol administration following traumatic brain injury induces distinct neuroinflammatory gene expression profiles.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major cause of morbidity and is frequently followed by prolonged intensive care stays with sustained physiologic stress. Beta-blockade has been investigated as an adjunct therapy for TBI given its potential to reduce sympathetic hyperactivation. The molecular mechanisms underlying neuroinflammatory signaling remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol (BB) administration following TBI would modify neuroinflammatory transcriptional responses consistent with attenuation of maladaptive inflammatory signaling.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n=6-8/group) were divided into 6 groups: (1) TBI7d (controlled cortical impact) followed by 7 days of daily handling, (2) TBI7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI BB7d), (3) TBI with chronic restraint stress for 7 days (TBI CRS7d), (4) TBI CRS7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI CRS BB7d), (5) CRS7d (n=7) who underwent daily stress exposure for 7 days; and (6) CRS BB7d (n=7) underwent daily stress exposure with propranolol injections for 7 days. RNA was extracted from the injured frontal lobe and analyzed using the NanoString Neuroinflammation panel. Differential gene expression was analyzed using ROSALIND. Significant differentially expressed genes (sDEGs) were defined as fold change ≥1.5 or ≤-1.5 with p<0.05. Functional pathway analysis was performed using Qiagen Ingenuity Pathway Analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Compared with TBI alone, TBI BB7d demonstrated 83 sDEGs, including genes associated with neuronal signaling, neurotransmitter regulation, and epigenetic modulation. Pathway analysis identified significant involvement of the IL8 signaling and FXR/RXR. In the TBI CRS7d model, propranolol treatment yielded 21 sDEGs. These genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular stress responses and inflammatory regulation. Propranolol downregulated IL6, IL8, and neuroinflammation signaling pathways.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Propranolol administration following TBI, with and without stress, resulted in distinct neuroinflammatory transcriptional profiles. Propranolol was associated with alterations in multiple pathways involved in stress response, immune regulation, and neurorecovery. These findings suggest beta-blockade may modulate stress-related neuroinflammatory signaling following TBI.

articles.title: RECOVER CPR Guidelines: Preparedness and Prevention. Updated Evidence, Recommendations, Knowledge Gap Analysis, and Guidelines for Education in Veterinary CPR.
articles.journal: J Vet Emerg Crit Care (San Antonio)
articles.journal_full: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To update the RECOVER CPR Preparedness and Prevention Domain's recommendations on education through a systematic review of relevant evidence and the creation and presentation of recommendations, and to identify and present critical knowledge gaps.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Standardized, systematic evaluation of literature pertinent to didactic, simulated, and in-clinic education regarding CPR following Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation methodology. Identified literature regarding prioritized questions in the Population-Intervention-Comparator-Outcome (PICO) format was reviewed independently by Evidence Evaluators, and findings were reconciled by Domain Chairs and Reassessment Campaign on Veterinary Resuscitation (RECOVER) Co-Chairs to arrive at recommendations. This process used a standardized Evidence Profile Worksheet for each PICO question including introduction, consensus on science, recommendations, justification of recommendations, and knowledge gaps sections. Recommendations underwent a 4-week comment period among international veterinary stakeholders prior to finalization. This 2026 RECOVER CPR Guidelines: Preparedness and Prevention-Education paper summarizes recommendations for CPR education of veterinary professionals.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Transdisciplinary, international collaboration in university, specialty, and emergency practice.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seven PICO questions pertaining to CPR education were addressed in this section of the RECOVER CPR Preparedness and Prevention Domain. These seven PICO questions resulted in 14 recommendations. All recommendations are supported by very low-certainty evidence (11) or based on expert opinion (3).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This 2026 RECOVER CPR Guidelines: Preparedness and Prevention-Education update presents recommendations for individual and team CPR training to optimize veterinary resuscitation team readiness and, hopefully, improve patient outcomes. However, uncertainty remains regarding specific, ideal educational methods to optimize resuscitation team readiness, and high-priority knowledge gaps are presented to guide collaborative research in this area.

articles.title: Freshwater drowning with profound hypofibrinogenaemia and refractory vasoplegic shock.

abstract.text: We present a challenging case of freshwater drowning complicated by profound hypofibrinogenaemia and refractory vasoplegic shock in a 39-year-old male admitted following an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. The constellation of physiological and laboratory abnormalities initially precluded a unifying diagnosis. The haemolysis, hyper-fibrinolysis and disseminated intravascular coagulation observed in our patient were likely sequelae of freshwater drowning and cardiac arrest. The refractory vasoplegic shock necessitated rescue off-label administration of hydroxocobalamin, resulting in restoration of haemodynamic stability.

articles.title: Prevalence of Powassan Virus Infection in Children with Suspected Lyme Disease.
articles.journal_full: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Both Lyme disease and Powassan virus (POWV) are transmitted by the bite of the Ixodes tick. While severe POWV encephalitis cases are uncommon in children, milder infections may be underdiagnosed.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a case-control study nested within a prospective cohort of children < 21 years evaluated for Lyme disease at one of eight Pedi Lyme Net emergency departments. We selected children with early or early-disseminated Lyme disease (n=305) with age, sex, center and symptom matched clinical mimics (n=295). Using biobanked research specimens, we performed POWV two-tier serology with confirmatory focus neutralization testing (FNT) and a reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test. We defined a POWV infection with a positive two-tier serology or RT-PCR test. We compared the prevalence of POWV between children with Lyme disease and matched mimics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 600 included children, the median age was 9 years (interquartile range 6-14 years) and 377 (63%) were male. POWV infection was more common in the children with Lyme disease (8.5%, 95% confidence interval (CI) 5.4-11.7%) compared to matched mimics (0.7%, 95% CI 0.1-2.4%; difference 7.9%, 95% CI 4.6-11.1; adjusted odds ratio 5.0, 95% CI 1.2-21.9). Of the 28 children with a positive POWV two-tier serology test, 11 (39%) had a positive FNT test. None of the RT-PCR tests were positive (0%, 95% CI 0-0.7%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A substantial minority of children with Lyme disease had serologic evidence of POWV co-infection compared with matched clinical mimics. Clinically unrecognized POWV infections were more common than previously acknowledged.

articles.title: Comparative Accuracy of the European Society of Cardiology Rapid Rule-Out and Rule-In Protocols for Diagnosing Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The European Society of Cardiology rapid rule-out and rule-in protocols using hs-cTns (high-sensitivity cardiac troponins) with blood collection at 0 and 1 hour (0/1 hour), 0 and 2 hours (0/2 hours), and 0 and 3 hours (0/3 hours) are accurate and widely used for evaluating non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction. This network meta-analysis aimed to identify the best performing hs-cTn assay.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted database searches up to January 15, 2026, a dual screening and eligibility assessment, independent data extraction and risk of bias assessment, a network meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy, and assessment of the certainty of evidence. Only full-paired diagnostic accuracy studies conducted in the emergency department were included.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ten prospective studies (15 publications) comparing 10 assays using the 0-/1-hour algorithm (n=8769), 0-/2-hour algorithm (n=1881), and 0-/3-hour algorithm (n=1236) were included. Comparisons between newer and conventional assays largely stemmed from a single-source study. Across all assays, the European Society of Cardiology 0-/1-hour algorithm demonstrated high sensitivity (summary point estimate range: 97.8%-99.8%). Furthermore, it maintained high specificity (89.8%-98.1%), with no assay showing clear superiority. The summary sensitivity and specificity did not show significant differences across assays after adjusting for biases because of imperfect reference standards. Comparative data in the European Society of Cardiology 0-/2-hour and 0-/3-hour algorithms were limited.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Evidence remains insufficient to establish the superiority of any specific hs-cTn assay within the European Society of Cardiology 0-/1-hour algorithm. Although practical considerations may currently guide selection, continued validation of newer assays remains necessary.

articles.title: Standardized Ultrafast Transcranial Ultrasound Acquisition in Acute Stroke: The HYPER-AI-SCAN Pilot Study With Exploratory Artificial Intelligence Analysis.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intracerebral hemorrhage requires rapid mechanism-specific treatment, yet early stroke triage relies on clinical severity scales that do not reliably distinguish hemorrhage from ischemic stroke. We assessed the feasibility of a standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound protocol designed to support subsequent artificial intelligence (AI)-based intracerebral hemorrhage detection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: HYPER-AI-SCAN (Hyper-Acute AI-Assisted Sonographic Cerebral Hemorrhage Assessment Network) was a single-center prospective feasibility study with embedded exploratory AI analysis. Between March and December 2025, 102 adults with acute computed tomography (CT)-confirmed stroke were prospectively enrolled according to trained operator availability. Primary feasibility outcomes were protocol completion, operator-rated adequate transtemporal windows, and acquisition time. In patients with retrievable paired baseline CT, exploratory AI analyses compared CT-only, ultrasound-only, and cross-modal CT-guided ultrasound models using patient-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, and specificity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Two patients were excluded after acquisition because insonation depth was <19 cm, yielding 100 evaluable patients (33 intracerebral hemorrhage; 67 ischemic stroke). The protocol was completed in all evaluable patients; adequate transtemporal windows were identified in 87%, and median acquisition time was 22 seconds (interquartile range, 13-31). Paired baseline CT images were available in 91 patients. Mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.86 (SD, 0.07) for the CT-only model, 0.85 (SD, 0.14) for the ultrasound-only model, and 0.92 (SD, 0.07) for the cross-modal model.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound acquisition was feasible at the bedside in acute stroke and generated brief cine-loops suitable for exploratory AI development. Multicenter external validation is required before diagnostic or triage application.

abstract.label: REGISTRATION INFORMATION
abstract.text: Clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07319013.

articles.title: Could circulating lactate stimulate post-dive cardiac output in the American alligator?
articles.journal: Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol
articles.journal_full: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology

abstract.text: In several mammalian species, circulating lactate has been shown to stimulate an increase in cardiac output through changes in cardiac function and vascular tone. In aquatic air-breathing vertebrates, blood lactate is often elevated following extended or strenuous dives, and both heart rate and cardiac output increase during post-dive recovery. We therefore hypothesized that lactate may drive part of the post-dive cardiovascular response. To test this possibility, we studied the hemodynamic effects of 0.5 M sodium lactate (NaLact) and control equimolar sodium chloride (NaCl) infusion in a diving reptile, the American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis). In anesthetized animals, 1 h of lactate infusion elevated whole-blood lactate from 1.4 ± 0.7 to a peak of 11.1 ± 1.8 mmol l‒1. Heart rate followed different trajectories in the two infusion groups (infusion × time interaction, P=0.002), increasing from 14.6 ± 2.1 to 19.1 ± 4.3 beats min‒1 during NaLact infusion, while remaining relatively stable in NaCl controls. However, cardiac output (total systemic blood flow) and systemic vascular conductance rose similarly in response to both infusions. Preserved vasodilatory capacity was confirmed by a robust increase in systemic vascular conductance following sodium nitroprusside administration in both groups. These findings indicate that elevated circulating lactate has limited effects on systemic blood flow and vascular tone in anesthetized alligators, providing limited support for lactate alone as a major driver of post-dive cardiovascular recovery.

articles.title: Hypophosphatemia in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Incidence, Determinants, and Clinical Impact in a Tertiary Emergency and Intensive Care Cohort.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Serum phosphate levels commonly decline during treatment of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), but the determinants and clinical implications of hypophosphatemia remain incompletely defined. We aimed to determine its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact during pediatric DKA.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective study, 116 DKA episodes managed in a tertiary pediatric emergency department and intensive care unit between January 2022 and June 2025 were analyzed. Demographic characteristics, admission biochemical parameters, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Hypophosphatemia was defined according to age-specific reference ranges. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of hypophosphatemia, while length of hospital stay was assessed using multivariable linear regression of log-transformed values.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Hypophosphatemia occurred in 72/116 episodes (62.1%). Compared with those without hypophosphatemia, affected patients had lower admission pH (7.03±0.13 vs. 7.12±0.17; P=0.002), bicarbonate (7.8±2.4 vs. 9.8±3.3 mEq/L; P<0.001), and potassium levels (4.43±0.96 vs. 4.81±0.66 mEq/L; P=0.024). Hyponatremia and hypokalemia were more frequent, whereas hyperkalemia was less common (all P<0.05). Lower admission pH (OR: 0.008, 95% CI: 0.000-0.219; P=0.004) and lower baseline phosphate concentration (OR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; P=0.031) independently predicted hypophosphatemia. Although hospitalization was longer in the hypophosphatemia group (85.3±75.2 vs. 56.2±36.4 h; P=0.018), hypophosphatemia was not independently associated with length of stay. Higher admission pH independently predicted shorter hospitalization (β=-0.957, P=0.026). Baseline phosphate positively correlated with nadir phosphate during treatment (r=0.303, P<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hypophosphatemia is common during pediatric DKA and is closely associated with the severity of metabolic acidosis at presentation. However, it does not independently affect hospitalization duration, suggesting that it primarily reflects disease severity rather than independently determining short-term outcomes.

articles.title: Running Gait Biomechanics Associated With Tibial Bone Stress Injuries Among Adolescent Athletes.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Tibial bone stress injuries (BSIs) are common among adolescent runners; however, no studies have evaluated running biomechanics associated with tibial BSI in adolescents.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe biomechanical and clinical features among adolescents with a history of tibial BSI, and compare with healthy age- and sex-matched controls.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cross-sectional case-control study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Large tertiary-care hospital and affiliated sports injury prevention center.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Sixty-six adolescents with history of tibial BSI (16.2 ± 1.8 years, BMI: 21.4 ± 3.0 kg/m2) were compared with 66 age- and sex-matched adolescents without a history of tibial BSI (16.3 ± 1.9 years, BMI: 21.7 ± 2.6 kg/m2).

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: Medical record review was conducted for tibia BSI case participants. Data from gait analyses completed on an instrumented treadmill.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Participant demographics were compared using independent samples t-tests. Continuous outcome measures [stride length, cadence, %stance phase, and peak mass-normalized vertical ground reaction force (vGRF)], and vertical average load rates (VALR), were compared between groups using independent samples t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests, with Cohen d effect sizes reported.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Study participants with history of tibial BSI demonstrated increased VALR (μ = 1141, P = 0.01, d = 0.29), increased mass-normalized maximum vGRF (μ = 1657, P = 0.02, d = 0.24), and greater % stance phase (μ = 1392, P < 0.001, d = 0.36).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Adolescents with a history of tibial BSI demonstrated characteristic gait biomechanics including greater VALR, greater mass-normalized maximum vGRF, and more terrestrial gait pattern. These features should be considered in management of adolescent tibial BSI.

articles.title: Ambient temperature and cerebrovascular disease presentations in a rural Japanese emergency department: An 11-year time-stratified case-crossover study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Evidence on short-term temperature-stroke associations from rural heavy-snowfall settings is limited. We evaluated ambient temperature and cerebrovascular disease presentations to a rural Japanese emergency department and examined robustness across lag structure, snow adjustment, case-definition restrictions, and stroke subtype.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted an 11-year time-stratified case-crossover study of ED presentations coded ICD-10 I60-I64. Conditional logistic regression estimated associations for lag 0, lag 1, lag 2, cumulative lag 0-1, and cumulative lag 0-2 in paired models with and without six-category snow-depth adjustment. Sensitivity analyses examined admission-linked and JTAS level 1-2 presentations, ischemic versus hemorrhagic stroke, exclusion of 2020-2022, and additional precipitation adjustment. Correlations among four same-day temperature metrics were calculated after within-matched-set centering.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 93,474 ED visits, 3101 met the cerebrovascular case definition. Snow-adjusted ORs per 1 °C were 0.9800 (95% CI 0.9645-0.9958) at lag 0, 0.9840 (0.9685-0.9997) at lag 1, 0.9907 (0.9751-1.0066) at lag 2, 0.9792 (0.9627-0.9961) for lag 0-1, and 0.9805 (0.9628-0.9984) for lag 0-2; no-snow estimates were similar. No ischemic-hemorrhagic heterogeneity was detected (P = 0.693), and the case-definition, COVID-period-exclusion, and precipitation-adjusted analyses were directionally consistent. The three temperature level/departure metrics were strongly correlated within matched sets (r = 0.780-0.946).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Relatively lower short-term ambient temperature was associated with more cerebrovascular ED presentations. The estimate was broadly consistent across lag and snow specifications, while the three level/departure metrics had limited discriminating power under the matched design.

articles.title: Mental health literacy status and its related factors among emergency nurses in public hospitals of Hubei Province: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Higher mental health literacy (MHL) among emergency nurses is associated with lower levels of work-related stress and burnout, as well as an enhanced ability to identify and address patients' psychological needs. However, current research on the MHL status of this group and its related factors remains insufficient.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study aims to assess the level of MHL among emergency department nurses and to identify the factors associated with it.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: From June 2024 to September 2024, 221 participants were recruited from 10 public hospitals in Hubei Province. Data were collected using validated psychological instruments, including the Mental Health Literacy Scale, Basic Psychological Needs Scale, and Public Service Motivation Scale, along with demographic questionnaires. Statistical analyses were conducted using the Mann-Whitney U test, Kruskal-Wallis test, Spearman correlation analysis, random forest modeling, and multiple linear regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The results revealed that the standardized MHL score among emergency nurses was 69.0%. MHL showed significant positive correlations with public service motivation (PSM) and basic psychological needs (BPN). Random forest analysis indicated that the association between BPN and MHL had the highest relative importance among all predictors. Collectively, these variables contributed to the explanation of 41.4% of the variance in MHL.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Research suggests that the MHL of emergency nurses requires improvement. Both BPN and PSM were significantly correlated with MHL, with the correlation between BPN and MHL being stronger. However, the investigation reveals an imbalance within the emergency department nursing population, characterized by lower BPN scores and higher PSM scores.

articles.title: Emergency department care experiences of patients with a migration history: a systematic mixed-studies review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Migration is a global phenomenon with significant implications for healthcare systems, requiring emergency departments (EDs) to adapt to increasingly diverse populations. While the ED often serves as the primary access point to the healthcare system for patients with a migration history (PMH), their specific care experiences have remained fragmented across literature.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This systematic mixed-studies review synthesizes research on the care experiences of PMH in the ED in order to identify actionable insights for making ED care more equitable.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were systematically searched, complemented by reference screening. Eligible studies reported primary empirical data on adult PMH in general EDs. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed methodological quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Study characteristics were extracted using a piloted form. Findings were synthesized using convergent qualitative synthesis with inductive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 37 studies from high-income countries were included. The findings can be divided into three major themes: (1) patient evaluations of ED care, (2) language as a central barrier, and (3) perceived discrimination, fairness and exclusion. Satisfaction varied and was often lower for PMH in specific domains, while moderate to high overall satisfaction frequently coexisted with unmet needs. These evaluations were shaped by patients' prior experiences and expectations. Language barriers strongly influenced patient understanding, autonomy and participation, with inconsistent and ad-hoc interpreter use contributing to communication gaps. Many PMH reported experiences of discrimination or unfair treatment linked to race, ethnicity, language, or migration status, often embedded in broader structural conditions of healthcare.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Language barriers and discrimination are important factors shaping how PMH experience ED care, while satisfaction ratings may not reliably reflect the quality or equity of care. Addressing these inequities requires sustained institutional and policy-level action, including consistent access to professional interpreters, strengthened communication practices, and institutional strategies to prevent discrimination, support patient participation, and embed equity in clinical routines and policies.

abstract.label: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION
abstract.text: PROSPERO CRD42020105332.

articles.title: Automated pupillometry findings in intracerebral hemorrhage compared with acute ischemic stroke among patients with suspected emergent large vessel occlusion.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate whether quantitative pupillary responses measured by automated pupillometry upon emergency department arrival differed between patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS) triaged for suspected emergent large vessel occlusion (ELVO).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-center study included ELVO screen-positive patients presenting within 24 h of symptom onset who underwent automated pupillometry upon emergency department arrival and were diagnosed with ICH or AIS. Clinical and pupillometry variables were compared between groups. Receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with ICH.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 112 patients, 32 had ICH and 80 had AIS. Patients with ICH were younger, had higher systolic blood pressure (SBP), and showed impaired pupillary responses, particularly slower constriction velocity. Lower constriction velocity (odds ratio [OR], 0.92 per 0.1 mm/s increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85-0.99), younger age (OR, 0.93 per year; 95% CI, 0.88-0.97), and higher SBP (OR, 1.03 per mmHg; 95% CI, 1.01-1.04) were independently associated with ICH. An exploratory 3-point score incorporating age, SBP, and constriction velocity had an apparent area under the curve of 0.858 and an optimism-corrected area under the curve of 0.819.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among patients triaged for suspected LVO, ICH was associated with impaired quantitative pupillary responses, particularly slower constriction velocity. Automated pupillometry may provide complementary physiological information during early emergency stroke evaluation.

articles.title: Just the facts: emergency diagnosis and management of severe hyperkalemia.
Digital Necrosis as an Initial Manifestation of a Myeloproliferative Neoplasm.
articles.journal_full: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

abstract.text: Digital necrosis is a clinical presentation of the hand, which may indicate an underlying systemic condition. We report a 76-year-old woman who presented to the hospital with left ring fingertip digital necrosis. Despite prior blunt trauma, significant laboratory abnormalities suggested potential for alternative underlying causes. Inpatient care consisted of allopurinol, intravenous fluids, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. The region of dry gangrene eventually fully declared and autoamputated during outpatient workup. Two months later, the patient presented to the emergency department with idiopathic leukocytosis and was diagnosed with a JAK2 V617F myeloproliferative neoplasm via peripheral blood smear. Unfortunately, the patient died 2 weeks later due to hemorrhagic conversion of an ischemic stroke. Earlier consideration of underlying malignancy may be crucial in prompting appropriate treatment measures in patients presenting with unexplained digital necrosis.

articles.title: Long-Term Site Fidelity and Environmental Drivers of Short-Tailed Stingray (Bathytoshia brevicaudata) Occurrence in South Africa: Evidence From Decade-Scale Sightings Data and Photo-Identification.

abstract.text: Large coastal elasmobranchs face disproportionate extinction risk yet remain among the most data-deficient marine vertebrates globally. Photo-identification has emerged as a powerful non-invasive tool for studying individually recognizable species, though its application to batoids remains limited relative to sharks. This study applied decade-scale sightings data and photo-identification to characterize occurrence patterns, individual residency, and local abundance of the short-tailed stingray (Bathytoshia brevicaudata) at an aggregation site in Gansbaai, South Africa-a species for which site fidelity and population structure remain poorly characterized across most of its Southern Hemisphere range. Between 2014 and 2024, short-tailed stingrays were recorded on 1149 of 5730 standardized boat-based shark cage-diving trips, yielding 1351 sightings concentrated at a single shallow inshore site. A negative binomial generalized additive model identified sea surface temperature, depth, season, and time as significant predictors of occurrence, with sightings increasing above 15°C, peaking at 6-9 m depth, and displaying a bimodal seasonal pattern inconsistent with austral summer mating aggregations documented elsewhere in the species' range. Sightings increased markedly after 2017, coinciding with documented white shark displacement from the area. Photo-identification of dorsal spot patterns cataloged eleven individuals across 405 positive identifications, with residency spanning from single visits to near-decade repeated associations. An open population mark-recapture model estimated high apparent survival (0.95), moderate detection probability (0.76), and a super-population of eleven individuals with low annual recruitment. These results support the presence of a small, predominantly female, partially resident assemblage exhibiting long-term site fidelity embedded within a broader regional population. This study represents the first population-level assessment of short-tailed stingrays in South Africa and the longest continuous observational dataset on record of the species globally, demonstrating that shark cage-diving operations can serve as cost-effective, passive monitoring platforms for coastal elasmobranchs and validating photo-identification as a viable mark-recapture framework for batoids with naturally stable pigmentation patterns.

articles.title: Chest Pain in Children and Adolescents in the Emergency Department: A State-of-the-Art Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Risk Stratification, and Evidence-Based Management.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Chest pain accounts for approximately 0.5%-1% of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits and is a frequent source of anxiety for families and clinicians. Although concern for cardiac disease often drives evaluation, true cardiac etiologies are rare, typically representing only 1%-2.5% of cases. The challenge in pediatric emergency care lies in distinguishing the small subset of patients with potentially life-threatening conditions from the large majority with benign causes, while avoiding unnecessary testing and radiation exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a state-of-the-art narrative review synthesizing contemporary literature on the epidemiology, differential diagnosis, cardiac risk stratification, diagnostic testing, and emerging technologies relevant to pediatric chest pain evaluation in the ED. Emphasis was placed on structured clinical assessment and evidence-based use of diagnostic modalities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Most pediatric chest pain is noncardiac, with musculoskeletal causes predominating, followed by psychogenic, pulmonary, and gastrointestinal etiologies. Cardiac causes remain uncommon but require systematic identification through careful history, focused physical examination, and electrocardiography. High-risk features include exertional pain, syncope, abnormal examination findings, concerning family history, and abnormal ECG results. Standardized clinical pathways reduce unnecessary imaging and cardiac testing without compromising diagnostic safety. Chest radiography and troponin testing have limited utility when used indiscriminately, whereas point-of-care ultrasound offers a radiation-free adjunct in selected cases. Emerging tools such as teletriage and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics show promise but require further validation in pediatric populations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pediatric chest pain is usually benign but necessitates structured, risk-stratified evaluation to safely exclude serious disease. Judicious testing guided by clinical assessment improves efficiency, minimizes radiation exposure, and supports high-value, patient-centered emergency care.

articles.title: Central Cord Syndrome: An Oral Boards/Simulation Case for Emergency Medicine Residents.
articles.journal_full: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Central cord syndrome (CCS) is a spinal cord injury resulting from trauma. Given the potential morbidity, it is crucial for emergency medicine (EM) residents to recognize, implement proper precautions, and obtain necessary subspecialty consultations in treatment for this disorder.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This case was presented in oral boards format as a 15-minute case by multiple emergency department faculty members acting as the patient and necessary associated personnel. The case was designed to be adaptable to a 25-minute simulation scenario. Twenty-five second-year EM residents individually participated in this case of a 72-year-old man who presented to the emergency department following a fall, whose workup revealed a diagnosis of CCS. After the case, the residents were surveyed on their prior knowledge and familiarity with CCS and rated their confidence in managing such a patient pre- and postsimulation on a 5-point Likert scale.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 25 EM residents completed this case. After participating in the case, the residents' comfort with managing a patient with CCS increased from a mean of 2.8 to a mean of 3.7 points, P < .001 (1 = not at all comfortable, 5 = extremely comfortable).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: CSS is an uncommon but clinically significant spinal cord injury that many EM residents have not encountered in their training. As the presenting symptoms can be subtle, obtaining a careful history, performing a focused physical examination, and using appropriate imaging modalities are vital for diagnosing and appropriately treating these patients.

articles.title: Pediatric methemoglobinemia in the emergency department: etiology, treatment patterns, and short-term outcomes.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study aimed to characterize the clinical and etiological features of pediatric methemoglobinemia presenting to a pediatric emergency department, with particular attention to procedure-related local anesthetic exposure, and to explore short-term treatment responses to methylene blue and intravenous ascorbic acid.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective study included patients presenting between November 1, 2022 1 November 2022 1 November 2022, and November 1, 2025 1 November 2025 1 November 2025, with methemoglobin levels ≥ 5% measured by co-oximetry. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, G6PD, genetic, and disposition data were collected. Baseline characteristics and early treatment responses were compared between patients receiving methylene blue and intravenous ascorbic acid.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-four patients were included; the median age was 4 months (IQR, 2-5), and 21 (87.5%) were male. Median initial SpO2 was 88% (IQR, 85%-90%), initial methemoglobin was 25.5% (IQR, 21.4%-30.6%), and post-treatment methemoglobin was 5.8% (IQR, 2.6%-8.3%). Drug exposure accounted for 19 cases (79.2%), most commonly lidocaine (n = 10) and prilocaine (n = 7). Among the five patients without documented oxidant exposure, two had pathogenic CYB5R3 variants and two had likely pathogenic CYB5R3 variants. Eleven patients received methylene blue and 13 received intravenous ascorbic acid. Post-treatment methemoglobin was lower with methylene blue (2.6% vs. 7.8%; p = 0.024), whereas relative reduction did not differ significantly (88.8% vs. 72.8%; p = 0.118).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Methemoglobinemia predominantly affected young infants and was most often associated with procedure-related local anesthetic exposure, particularly in the context of circumcision. Topical oropharyngeal anesthetic exposure before intubation should also be recognized as a potential source of oxidant exposure. Treatment comparisons were exploratory, and underlying enzymatic or genetic susceptibility should be considered even when an acquired oxidant exposure is identified.

articles.title: For emergency department patients with alcohol withdrawal syndrome, a comorbid mood disorder is associated with increased system utilization representing illness burden.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The impact of comorbid mood disorders on emergency department revisits and hospitalizations among patients presenting with alcohol withdrawal is not well understood. We compared ED revisits and hospitalizations among those patients with alcohol withdrawal and mood disorder to those without mood disorder.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We included unique patients who presented to EDs in Vancouver, Canada, with a diagnosis of alcohol withdrawal. Structured chart reviews ascertained comorbidities and defined the presence of mood disorder based on documented diagnosis at or before the index visit. The primary and secondary outcomes were any ED visit or hospitalization in the subsequent year. We describe differences between patients using absolute difference and 95% confidence intervals [CI].

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 1010 unique patients; the median age was 46 (range 15-79), 73% were male, and 403 (40%) had a mood disorder. By 1 year, 78% of patients with mood disorders had at least one ED revisit, compared to 61% of patients without (difference 17% [11-22%]). Among patients with mood disorders, the median number of return visits was 3 [1-8] compared to 1 [0-5] for a patient with no mood disorder. By 1 year, 35% of patients with a mood disorder had ≥ 1 hospital admission versus 21% of patients without (difference 14% [8.5-20%]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among patients with alcohol withdrawal, those with mood disorders had nearly double the number of ED visits and more frequently required hospital admission within 1 year. These findings underscore the need for targeted interventions for patients with alcohol withdrawal and mood disorders.

articles.title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Point-of-Care Ultrasound for Detecting Reduced Left Ventricular Systolic Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess the diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) for detecting reduced left ventricular systolic function (LVSF) using visual qualitative assessment (VQA), E-point septal separation (EPSS), and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment, compared with transthoracic echocardiography (TTE).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from January 1, 1985, through July 8, 2025. Eligible studies compared POCUS-assessed LVSF with left ventricular ejection fraction measured by TTE (or cardiac MRI in one study). Data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis to determine the diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) and likelihood ratios (LR) for each of the three methods.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-eight studies, including 4,647 participants, met inclusion criteria. Nine studies evaluating VQA yielded a DOR of 40.53 (95% CI, 15.07 to 109.00; P < 0.001) and a positive LR (LR + ) of 6.90 (95% CI, 3.75 to 12.69). Seven studies evaluating EPSS resulted in a DOR of 21.77 (95% CI, 10.25 to 46.28; P < 0.001) and a LR + of 5.70 (95% CI, 2.89 to 11.22). Five studies evaluating AI-assisted POCUS resulted in a DOR of 47.35 (95% CI, 16.87 to 132.93; P < 0.001) and a LR + of 8.37 (95% CI, 4.40 to 15.93). Meta-regression analyses revealed no statistically significant differences in diagnostic performance among the three methods. Subgroup analysis by operator experience level also showed no statistically significant difference between novice and experienced operators for each method.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: VQA, EPSS, and AI-assisted POCUS all demonstrate moderate-to-high diagnostic accuracy for identifying reduced LVSF, with no significant differences among methods on meta-regression or by operator experience level. Moderately strong LR + across all three methods supports the use of POCUS for ruling in reduced LVSF. EPSS cutoffs at the lower and upper ends of the reported range showed higher sensitivity and specificity, respectively, suggesting utility as a rule-in or rule-out tool where formal echocardiography is not readily available.

articles.title: Plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins overlap with the hyperinflammatory phenotype in acute respiratory failure.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of acute respiratory failure (ARF) identifies patients with high mortality, but its underlying pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell injury in critical illness. We investigated whether plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins characterize the hyperinflammatory phenotype and whether they contribute to its association with mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed 285 emergency department patients with ARF and suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Inflammatory phenotypes were derived by latent class analysis using nine biomarkers and clinical indicators. A mitochondrial-protein score was calculated from 59 MitoCarta3.0-matched proteins, and mitochondrial clusters were derived by principal component analysis and k-means clustering. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Latent class analysis identified 185 hypoinflammatory (65%) and 100 hyperinflammatory (35%) patients, with a significant difference in 28-day mortality (14/185, 7.6% vs. 31/100, 31.0%; p < 0.001). The mitochondrial-protein score increased with the probability of hyperinflammation (ρ=0.46, p < 0.001). Forty-three of 59 mitochondrial-associated proteins were more abundant in the hyperinflammatory phenotype, with prominent differences in apoptosis regulation, oxidative stress, and oxidative phosphorylation proteins. In a mutually adjusted model, the hyperinflammatory phenotype remained associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR]=6.40, 95%CI:3.08-13.95; p < 0.001), whereas the mitochondrial-protein score was not (OR=0.83 per SD, 95%CI:0.58-1.17; p = 0.30). Mitochondrial clusters yielded consistent findings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of ARF is characterized by increased plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins, linking inflammation with mitochondrial biology and cellular injury. This mitochondrial signature did not account for mortality independently of inflammatory phenotype, suggesting that it represents a biological component of the hyperinflammatory state.

articles.title: Cardiac vagal and cardiac sympathetic activity in healthy humans during and after face immersion.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: The interaction between cardiac vagal and cardiac sympathetic activity during face immersion remains poorly understood, yet it is critical for identifying potential autonomic conflict. This study sought to disentangle the individual and synergistic contributions of breathing mode (apnea vs. snorkel breathing) and water temperature (10°C vs. 30°C) on heart rate, cardiac vagal (RMSSD), and cardiac sympathetic (PEP) indices before, during, and after exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a randomized within-subjects design, 52 healthy adults completed five 30-second conditions: 1) apnea in an empty bowl, 2) apnea in cold water, 3) apnea in warm water, 4) snorkel breathing in cold water, and 5) snorkel breathing in warm water. Heart rate, RMSSD, and PEP were measured for 30 seconds before, during and after each condition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant bradycardia occurred in all five conditions. Apnea in an empty bowl resulted in the smallest bradycardia and a decrease in RMSSD. While cold-water apnea caused the strongest bradycardia, snorkel breathing in cold water elicited the largest RMSSD increase. PEP remained stable throughout all conditions and time points.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These results demonstrate that face immersion triggers stimulus-dependent autonomic pathways. The observed decoupling of heart rate and RMSSD during apnea questions the validity of RMSSD as an index of cardiac vagal activity during breath-holding. The stability of PEP is consistent with predominantly cardiac parasympathetic involvement in diving bradycardia. These findings highlight limitations of RMSSD interpretation during apnea and emphasize the necessity of accounting for breathing modality in autonomic assessments. Applied interventions using cold-water face immersion under safe conditions are encouraged.

articles.title: Homelessness Is Associated With Increased Wound Complications and Revision Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: People experiencing homelessness face barriers to musculoskeletal care and may be at increased risk for adverse outcomes after major orthopaedic surgery. Outcomes after elective primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) remain poorly characterized in this population. We examined associations between homelessness and 90-day medical and 1- and 2-year surgical outcomes after primary THA.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a national healthcare database. Adults undergoing primary THA were stratified by documented homelessness within six months preceding surgery. A one-to-one propensity score matching was performed on age, sex, race/ethnicity, body mass index, and cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, nutritional, substance use, and psychiatric comorbidities. From 1,585 homeless and 287,986 non-homeless patients, matching yielded 1,582 per cohort with well-balanced baseline characteristics (all standardized mean differences less than 0.1). Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated; significance was set at P < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At 90 days, homeless patients had a higher risk of sepsis (RR 2.20, 95% CI 1.20 to 4.04), surgical site infection (RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.13 to 4.64), and wound dehiscence (RR 1.95, 95% CI 1.25 to 3.04). At one year, homelessness was associated with a higher risk of revision THA (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.05 to 2.29), periprosthetic joint infection (RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.00 to 2.36), and wound dehiscence (RR 2.18, 95% CI 1.37 to 3.49). At two years, elevated revision (RR 1.72, 95% CI 1.08 to 2.73) and wound dehiscence (RR 2.26, 95% CI 1.36 to 3.76) persisted. There were no significant differences observed in transfusion, pneumonia, or emergency department utilization.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: After matching on comorbidities, substance use, and psychiatric conditions, homelessness remained independently associated with a persistent two-fold elevation in wound complications and a 55 to 72% increase in revision risk through two years following primary THA. Housing status may warrant consideration in preoperative risk stratification and postoperative care planning, although prospective work is needed to clarify mechanisms and whether targeted interventions modify these associations.

articles.title: Survival after neonatal chest compressions at birth: Temporal trends and prognostic factors in a population-based cohort, Queensland, Australia.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To examine temporal trends and prognostic factors for 28-day survival among infants receiving chest compressions (CC) in Queensland, Australia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using the Queensland Perinatal Data Collection (2008-2024), including all liveborn CC recipients at birth. Temporal trends in crude 28-day survival were examined overall and by gestational age (GA) groups. Multivariable generalised estimating equations were used to identify factors independently associated with survival while accounting for clustering within birthing locations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3,077 CC recipients, 70.5% established regular spontaneous breathing within 60 minutes of birth, and 89.0% survived to 28 days. Crude 28-day survival improved from 82% in 2008 to 89% in 2024 and was consistently higher in term (GA ≥37+0 weeks) than preterm infants. Compared with term infants, adjusted odds of survival declined with decreasing GA: 32+0 to 36+6 weeks (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.77), 28+0 to 31+6 weeks (aOR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.54), and <28+0 weeks (aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.12-0.23). However, after adjusting for cord pH or epinephrine administration, survival in infants born at 32+0 to 36+6 weeks did not differ significantly from term infants.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Survival to 28 days among CC recipients was high and increased over time. Lower gestational age was the strongest independent prognostic factor for mortality, although the survival difference between term and moderate-to-late preterm infants was attenuated after adjustment for cord pH or epinephrine administration. Prospective studies assessing CC indications and measures of resuscitation quality are needed to optimise neonatal resuscitation and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Survival after out of hospital cardiac arrest in relation to AED usage in a multi response system including AED equipped drones.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early defibrillation is a key determinant of survival in out‑of‑hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). In multi-response systems, it remains unclear which responders contribute most to early AED use and survival. This study compared first AED-attaching responders and their association with 30-day survival in a regional multi-response system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This registry‑based cohort study included OHCA cases in Västra Götaland Region, Sweden, between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Data were obtained from EMS, dispatch, and registry databases. The primary outcome was 30‑day survival.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 9,413 OHCAs, EMS attached the first AED in 72% of cases, followed by on-duty first responders (ODFR) (18%), bystanders (6.0%), and community first responders (CFR) (4.5%). EMS attachment decreased from 77% to 67%, whereas CFR involvement increased from 1% to 13%. 30‑day survival was highest when AEDs were attached by bystanders (28%), compared with 9.0% for EMS, 8.7% for ODFR and 8.6% for CFR. Among witnessed OHCAs with an initial shockable rhythm, 30-day survival was highest in bystander-attached cases (62%), compared with 36% for CFR, 32% for ODFR, and 24% for EMS. In the multivariable analysis, bystander AED attachment was associated with higher odds of 30‑day survival compared with EMS (OR 2.25; 95% CI 1.77-2.85).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this multi-response system, survival was highest when AEDs were first attached by bystanders and remained higher after adjustment for known prognostic factors. This association likely reflects earlier access to defibrillation. These findings suggest that improving immediate access to defibrillation may have the greatest impact on OHCA outcomes.

articles.title: Early Prehospital Prediction of Neurological Outcome After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Derivation and External Validation of the MIRA-29 Score.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac (OHCA) arrest is a frequent emergency, and few patients will survive with good neurological outcome. Identification of patients with a low likelihood of meaningful recovery represents a major clinical challenge. Numerous scores have been developed to guide decision-making after OHCA, with variable goals and targets, but most of them have been validated on small cohorts, integrates variables not available in the prehospital field, or do have low prediction values. MIRA-29 score aimed to only rely on simple clinical variables, available in the prehospital setting. We hypothetized that such score will provide incremental neurological prognosis value at an early-stage following OHCA.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MIRA-29 score was derived and internally validated over a five-year period on a prospective cohort of 1099 adult patients, including all OHCA treated by our territory dispatch center. Multivariate analysis identified independent variables within the database, that were used to optimize the prediction model using machine-learning and genetic algorithms. The score was subsequently validated externally on 82 696 patients extracted from the French national cardiac arrest registry (RéAC).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Out from the 1099 patients, 85 patients (7.7%) had a favorable neurological outcome. Multivariate analysis identified five independent variables associated with neurological outcome: age, low-flow duration, number of external electric shock, epinephrine dose, and the OHCA site (street, public facility, home). After model optimization and machine-learning, age was not retained within the final model. External validation depicted a precision of 0.86 and a recall of 0.88 of the model. The F1-Score and accuracy are respectively 0.87 and 0.88, and specificity for a bad neurological prognosis is 0.99.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: MIRA‑29 strength lies on its ability to reliably identify patients with extremely high probability of poor neurological outcome, while being based on four simple clinical variables. The prospective validation of MIRA-29 in the clinical setting may evaluate its impact on clinical decision making.

articles.title: RescQTM: One-year implementation and feasibility results of a digitally enabled support pathway for bystanders of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Bystanders to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) are at significant risk of psychological distress, yet no standardised support pathway exists for them in the UK. RescQ™ is a digital-first bystander support pathway embedded within regional prehospital and cardiac arrest care services.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To evaluate the feasibility of embedding RescQ™ into routine emergency medical services (EMS) practice leading to appropriate contact with bystanders involved in OHCA. Secondary aims were to describe digital access, demand for liaison officer (LO) support, identification of younger bystanders, and EMS clinician acceptability.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Prospective one-year regional service evaluation of RescQ™ across Essex, UK. Bystanders involved in eligible OHCA events were registered by EMS clinicians and provided with immediate access to secure digital resources. Bystanders could self-refer for additional support through LO.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the one-year evaluation, 220 of 432 eligible OHCA incidents had at least one bystander identified and the incident entered into the RescQ™ pathway, representing an incident-level capture rate of 50.9%. Across these incidents, 298 bystanders were identified, of whom 260 eligible adults were registered with RescQ™. Of registered adult bystanders, 96.2% accessed the digital resources at least once. Among all identified bystanders, 30/298 (10.1%) were aged under 18 years. Approximately 10% of registered bystanders self-referred for additional personalised LO support. Among 25 EMS clinician survey respondents who had used RescQTM in clinical practice, ratings indicated acceptability.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: RescQ™ demonstrated the feasibility of identifying and supporting bystanders following OHCA through a digitally enabled pathway, achieving incident-level capture above the pre-specified feasibility threshold and high website access among registered adults. These findings support further multi-region evaluation of implementation, sustainability and scalability across different EMS systems.

articles.title: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrests due to foreign body airway obstruction: A CanROC registry, retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Foreign body airway obstruction (FBAO) is a treatable cause of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but North American data are limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Exploratory retrospective cohort study of EMS-treated OHCAs using the Canadian Resuscitation Outcomes Consortium (CanROC) registry (2005-2023), classified as obviously FBAO-related or of no obvious cause (presumed cardiac). Logistic regression compared Utstein characteristics between etiologies and identified factors associated with prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and survival to acute care discharge.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 105,178 EMS-treated OHCAs, 1,106(1.1%) were obviously FBAO-related. Compared with cases of no obvious cause, obviously FBAO-related cases were older (median 73 vs 68 years, p<0.001), more often witnessed (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.98[5.36-9.25]), more often attended by trained bystanders (aOR 3.30[2.41-4.41]), and less often had a shockable rhythm (aOR 0.11[0.07-0.15]). Obviously FBAO-related cases more often achieved prehospital ROSC (62.7% vs 37.8%; OR 2.77[2.44-3.13]), but survival did not differ (10.6% vs 9.0%,p=0.094). Within the obviously FBAO-related cohort, ROSC was associated with witnessed arrest (aOR 1.66[1.13-2.43]) and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.95 per minute[0.92-0.99]). Survival was associated with younger age (aOR 0.76 per decade[0.61-0.93]), initial shockable rhythm (aOR 4.76[1.55-13.30]), and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.81 per minute[0.66-0.98]). Survival was 18.1% and 0.8% among obviously FBAO-related OHCAs with and without prehospital ROSC, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Obviously FBAO-related OHCAs are uncommon but clinically distinct. ROSC is frequent, yet survival remains low and is associated with early prehospital factors, supporting choking prevention initiatives, bystander training, and rapid EMS response.

articles.title: Commercially available multimodal LLMs for EEG-based prognostication after cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Machine-learning and deep-learning approaches have been successfully applied to EEG-based prognostication in comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA), but typically rely on task-specific signal processing, feature extraction, and model development. Here, we investigated whether two commercially available multimodal large language models (LLMs) could predict neurological outcome directly from EEG images.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Thirty-three comatose patients on the first day after CA from a prospective cohort were included. For each patient, a single 10-second EEG segment displayed using a longitudinal bipolar montage was rendered as PNG image. ChatGPT 5.4. and Claude Opus 4.7 were instructed to estimate the probability for favorable outcome for each case based on the EEG and a generic information block describing conditions of recordings. Five different prompting strategies were used, including few-shot prompting where four exemplary EEGs (not from the 33 patients) were provided. Predictive performance was quantified using AUC and accuracy.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Across prompting strategies, the AUC ranged from 0.86 to 0.99 for ChatGPT and from 0.74 to 1.00 for Claude. The highest accuracy achieved by both models was 93.9% using few-shot prompting. As reference, a previously published dedicated deep-learning model achieved 100% on the same cohort.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this exploratory study of a small cohort, multimodal LLMs showed variable but potentially promising discrimination for predicting favorable outcome from single EEG image in comatose patients after CA. Performance depended substantially on prompt design. These findings require confirmation in a larger cohort.

articles.title: Community First Responder Activation Reduces the Negative Impact of AED Distance on Bystander Defibrillation After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Early defibrillation is critical for survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet bystander defibrillation remains uncommon despite the availability of automated external defibrillators (AEDs). We investigated whether HeartRunner community first responder activation increased the likelihood of bystander defibrillation and 30-day survival in relation to the distance to the nearest accessible AED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Linking data from the Danish Cardiac Arrest Registry, Danish AED Network, and HeartRunner application, we identified patients with OHCA eligible for HeartRunner activation during 2017-2021. Using street-network distances to the nearest accessible AED, we examined associations between HeartRunner activation, bystander defibrillation, and 30-day survival using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 5,753 OHCAs (median age, 74 years; 64% male; 78% in private locations), HeartRunner activation (41%) was associated with higher bystander defibrillation across AED distances (p-interaction = 0.004), with no interaction for 30-day survival (p-interaction = 0.054). Predicted bystander defibrillation with versus without HeartRunner activation was 9.6% vs 5.5% at Q1 (389 m), 10.0% vs 4.3% at median (717 m), and 13.0% vs 4.8% at Q3 (1,183 m). TMLE estimated a 6.1-percentage-point higher probability of bystander defibrillation (95% CI, 4.5-7.8; p<0.001) and a modest 1.8-percentage-point increase in 30-day survival (95% CI, 0.1-3.6; p=0.038) with HeartRunner activation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: HeartRunner activation attenuated the decline in bystander defibrillation with increasing AED distance following OHCA, without a corresponding distance interaction for 30-day survival. Overall, TMLE supported higher bystander defibrillation and suggested a modest increase in 30-day survival with HeartRunner activation.

articles.title: The SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol and Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS) for dynamic assessment of peripheral edema burden in critically ill patients: a prospective, longitudinal observational study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Excessive fluid resuscitation may lead to pathologic fluid accumulation and increased mortality. Cumulative fluid balance (CFB) correlates poorly with outcomes. Ultrasonographic central congestion metrics (VExUS/Lung ultrasound) inherently overlook critical fluid shifts within the peripheral reservoir. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed the SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol for standardized, semi-quantitative assessment of peripheral edema burden.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Ultrasonographic assessment was performed bilaterally across six core anatomical regions using the SUBCUT protocol on days 1, 3, and 7. Individual sites were graded semi-quantitatively using the Ultrasonographic Subcutaneous Edema Grade (USEG, 0-4), yielding the Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS, 0-48) as the cumulative sum across 12 evaluation sites. The primary endpoint was ICU mortality, evaluating the prognostic performance of Day 3 SWELS.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 111 patients analyzed (ICU mortality 23.4%; 26/111), baseline SWELS and CFB were similar between survivors and non-survivors. By Day 3, median SWELS surged in non-survivors (24 vs. 8; P < .001), yielding greater unadjusted, apparent discrimination than CFB (AUC 0.86 vs. 0.65). In competing-risk analysis, a 5-point increase in Day 3 SWELS was independently associated with ICU mortality (sHR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.22-1.86; P < .001). Incorporating Day 3 SWELS into a contemporaneous clinical base model (Age, Admission Sepsis, Day 3 SOFA) enhanced model fit and discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.043; P = .008).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The SUBCUT protocol provides a novel framework for assessing peripheral edema burden. At Day 3, its derivative, SWELS, demonstrates incremental prognostic association beyond contemporaneous organ dysfunction, offering an extravascular perspective for multi-compartment fluid mapping.

articles.title: Impact of Climatic and Environmental Conditions on Prehospital Emergency Medical Dispatches in Germany: Protocol for an Exploratory, Population-Based Observational Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Extreme temperatures and other climatic stressors are increasingly affecting population health, even in temperate regions such as Germany. Previous studies have demonstrated associations between extreme heat, cold temperatures, and health indicators, including emergency department visits and mortality. However, most analyses rely on coarse meteorological data and hospital-based outcomes, limiting insights into fine-scale spatial variability and prehospital emergency responses. Prehospital emergency medical dispatches (PHEMD) data offer a unique opportunity to capture acute, real-time health effects of climatic and environmental conditions at high temporal resolution.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study examines the association between climatic and environmental conditions and PHEMD use in 2 metropolitan regions in northern Germany. It will assess nonlinear temperature-response relationships, temporal lags, spatial and subgroup variation, and the added value of high-resolution vs station-based exposure assignment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is an exploratory, retrospective, population-based observational study using anonymized PHEMD data from the metropolitan regions of Hanover and Brunswick and their surrounding rural areas. PHEMD records will be linked to meteorological measurements and high-resolution urban microclimate data. Associations between climatic conditions and PHEMD use will be analyzed using quasi-Poisson regression with distributed lag nonlinear model structures. The main temporal analyses will use daily mean temperature and lags of 0 to 6 days, with longer lag periods of up to 14 days examined for cold-related effects. Models will account for temporal trends, seasonality, weekdays, public holidays, and, where appropriate, air pollution. Geographic information system-based maps will visualize the spatial distribution of effects.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Study funding began in July 2025. As of November 2026, acquisition and harmonization of emergency medical service and meteorological data are ongoing. The study dataset will include data through December 2030, with the final data export planned thereafter. All analyses are expected to be completed and the resulting manuscripts submitted for publication by May 2031.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study uses high-resolution environmental data and PHEMD records to examine climate-related emergency medical demand in northern Germany. By linking microclimate information with dispatch data, it aims to improve the understanding of spatial and temporal patterns beyond conventional approaches. The findings may support more targeted heat-health preparedness, improve emergency service planning, and inform local climate adaptation strategies.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Intervention to Enhance Treatment Engagement and Retention Following Nonfatal Opioid Overdose: Protocol for a Single-Arm Prospective Feasibility Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Substance use treatment engagement and retention after hospital discharge remain low among patients with nonfatal opioid overdose. It is critical to develop interventions targeting this population due to the persistent opioid overdose crisis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We conducted a single-arm prospective study, the first phase of a 2-phase study (R61/R33, funded by the National Institute on Drug Abuse; DA062351). The objective of the R61 phase was to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a 12-week bundled telehealth-enabled intervention aimed at improving treatment engagement and retention among patients with opioid use disorder and a recent nonfatal opioid overdose after hospital discharge.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The R61 phase was a single-arm study with no control group. The 12-week comprehensive intervention comprised 4 components, including buprenorphine treatment, telehealth physician visits (weeks 1, 3, 5, 9, and 12 and as needed), telehealth peer service (daily during week 1, every other day during week 2, weekly during weeks 3-12, and as needed), and facilitated linkage to community resources and ongoing treatment. Adults aged 19 years or older with a diagnosis of opioid use disorder and a nonfatal opioid overdose within the previous 12 months were recruited before they were discharged from the University of Alabama at Birmingham Hospital. After enrollment, buprenorphine treatment was initiated or continued, and peer support specialists began engaging and coaching patients. Participants completed validated surveys at baseline and 1 and 3 months. Feasibility will be measured using enrollment and retention rates (benchmark of ≥70% at 3 months). Acceptability will be measured using patient satisfaction and credibility and expectancy scores. Mental health, craving, repeat overdose, and emergency department revisits and readmissions are secondary outcomes. Outcomes will be summarized descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The R61 study was funded by the National Institute on Drug Abuse from October 1, 2024, to August 30, 2026. All 30 anticipated participants were enrolled, and 24 completed the intervention. The last participant completed the intervention in April 2026. Data analysis is currently ongoing, and results from the current study are expected to be published in January 2027. Funding for the subsequent R33 phase was awarded in September 2026.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of a bundled telehealth-enabled intervention for patients at high risk of repeat overdose and death, a patient population with low treatment uptake and retention after hospital discharge. The findings will inform the upcoming R33 phase, a randomized controlled trial aiming to demonstrate effectiveness in an estimated sample of 160 patients.

articles.title: Association Between Admission Serum Albumin Levels and INR-Defined Early Trauma-Induced Coagulopathy: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.journal_full: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis

abstract.text: BackgroundAdmission serum albumin may reflect multiple trauma-related processes. We examined its concurrent association with early trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC), defined by the international normalized ratio (INR).MethodsThis single-center retrospective study included patients with major trauma treated between January 2023 and December 2024 whose albumin and INR were measured concurrently within 6 hours after injury. Logistic regression evaluated early TIC (admission INR >1.2), adjusting for age, sex, Injury Severity Score, and time from injury to emergency department arrival. Continuous INR was analyzed using a gamma generalized linear model with a log link and the same covariates. Additional logistic models included shock index and hemoglobin.ResultsAmong 262 patients, 56 (21.4%) had early TIC. Per 1 g/L increase, albumin was inversely associated with early TIC (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.774; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.712-0.840; P<0.001) and continuous INR (adjusted mean ratio, 0.988; 95% CI, 0.984-0.992; P<0.001). The association with early TIC was attenuated after additional adjustment for hemoglobin (adjusted OR, 0.823; 95% CI, 0.737-0.919; P=0.001) and for shock index and hemoglobin jointly (adjusted OR, 0.862; 95% CI, 0.770-0.965; P=0.010).ConclusionsLower admission albumin was associated with concurrent INR-defined early TIC, with attenuation after additional adjustment for hemoglobin and shock index. These hypothesis-generating findings do not establish causality, temporal prediction, or a specific endothelial mechanism.

articles.title: A Mobile Application Improves Paramedic Performance in Simulated Trauma Care: A Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Clinical performance during prehospital trauma care varies among emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, particularly during high-stress critical responses. We developed a mobile application providing real-time access to local treatment protocols, decision support tools, and instructional procedure videos to supplement standard practice. We evaluated whether use of the application improved paramedic performance during simulated trauma scenarios.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a crossover randomized controlled trial between July 2025 and February 2026 comparing standard care alone with standard care plus the mobile application during two high-fidelity trauma simulations (one adult and one pediatric). Paramedics, working in pairs, were block randomized to one of four sequences, varying both the scenario order and the application use. Performance was assessed using predefined critical actions; completing all critical actions was required to successfully complete the scenario. A generalized linear mixed model with a binomial distribution and logit link function was used for each paramedic pair to estimate the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for successfully completing a scenario with or without the application.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 112 paramedics, 98 (88%) participated, forming 49 pairs. One pair withdrew before study completion, leaving 48 pairs for analysis. For scenarios using the application, 17/48 (35.4%) successfully completed the scenario compared to 3/48 (6.3%) for scenarios not using the application, adjusted odds 8.28 (95% CI 2.21-31.09). Among scenarios using the application, 10/25 (40%) adult scenarios and 7/23 (30.4%) pediatric scenarios met successful completion criteria compared to 3/23 (13%) adult and 0/25 (0%) pediatric with standard practice alone. User experience survey results demonstrated that participating paramedics assessed the application as being practical to use and valuable for clinical care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Use of the mobile decision support application improves odds of performing high-quality clinical care in simulated trauma patient scenarios. Further studies are needed to evaluate performance and usability in a field environment.

articles.title: Five-Year Experience with Automated Head Up Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Automated head-up position cardiopulmonary resuscitation (AHUP-CPR), the combination of a head and thorax positioning device, active compression-decompression CPR, and an impedance threshold device, lowers intracranial pressure and increases cerebral blood flow and neurologically favorable survival in animal models versus conventional CPR (C-CPR).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, observational, investigator-initiated registry study reports 5-year multi-center outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) from areas served by emergency medical services (EMS) agencies that implemented AHUP-CPR as their routine first-responder standard of care. Adults with non-traumatic OHCA were initially treated with immediate conventional (C-CPR) followed by rapid transition to AHUP-CPR. The primary study focus was on patients who survived to hospital discharge with favorable neurological function (HD-FN). Additional analyses included assessment of sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge (HD), outcomes based upon the presenting rhythm, and impact of covariates on HD-FN.

abstract.label: RESULTS
