Admission serum lactate did not differ significantly between the patients with abnormal CRT and those with normal CRT (2.6 [1.4-4.6] versus 1.9 [1.3-3.1] mmol/L; p = 0.07) while CRT and serum lactate levels were correlated (r = 0.33; p < 0.01). In multivariate analysis, continuous analysis of CRT was independently associated with serum lactate levels with a 15% increase in serum lactate per additional sec of CRT (95% CI 1.06-1.25; p < 0.01). Among patients with serum lactate >2 mmol/L, abnormal CRT was associated with longer vasopressor exposure at day 3 and increased ICU mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Admission lactate did not differ significantly between normal and abnormal CRT groups. Exploratory subgroup findings suggest that CRT may complement serum lactate in characterizing patients with severe trauma.

articles.title: Long-term market value decline after medial collateral ligament injury in professional football players did not differ statistically significantly from matched non-injured controls: A Transfermarkt-based cohort study.
articles.journal_full: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to characterize the longitudinal trajectory of estimated market value after medial collateral ligament (MCL) injury in professional football players and determine whether postinjury changes differed from matched non-injured controls.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Professional football players with a recorded MCL injury were identified from Transfermarkt injury records labeled as medial (collateral) ligament injuries (seasons 2007/08-2023/24); duplicate records of the same episode were merged, and injuries were not clinically verified. Market value was assessed during the season preceding injury (Tpre), the injury season (T0), and annually for five subsequent seasons (T1-T5). Linear mixed-effect models evaluated longitudinal changes and associations with age, playing position, league level, and injury-related absence. Segmented models assessed changes in temporal trajectory. MCL cases were also matched 1:2 to non-injured controls by competition, season, playing position, age, and preinjury market value, with group differences examined using a difference-in-differences model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-five players with 50 MCL injury episodes were included, 8 of which had an associated anterior cruciate ligament or meniscal lesion. Median age at injury was 26.5 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 23.0-28.7), and median time lost was 42 days (IQR: 21-76.5). In the adjusted model, market value did not differ statistically significantly from Tpre at T0 (P = 0.649), T1 (P = 0.813), or T2 (P = 0.064) but was statistically significantly lower at T3 (-34.25%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -51.21% to -11.38%; P = 0.006), T4 (-47.54%; 95% CI: -61.54% to -28.43%; P < 0.001), and T5 (-51.70%; 95% CI: -65.25% to -32.88%; P < 0.001). No statistically significant postinjury change in slope was observed (P = 0.103). Thirty-one of 48 eligible cases were matched to 62 controls; the remaining 17 had no eligible control within the matching criteria, mostly because of lower-tier competition or low preinjury market value. Difference-in-differences estimates were not statistically significant at any time point (P = 0.167-0.561; range: -10.9% [95% CI: -39.2% to 30.6%] at T0 to -24.6% [95% CI: -49.5% to 12.6%] at T3); the study could detect only differences of approximately 42%-46% or more. Results were unchanged when analyses were restricted to isolated MCL injuries.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Market value declined substantially during long-term follow-up after MCL injury, but this decline was not statistically significantly different from that observed in matched non-injured players (P = 0.167-0.561). Much of the apparent long-term depreciation may therefore reflect the underlying age- and career-related trajectory of professional footballers; however, the matched analysis was underpowered, and a modest injury-specific effect, particularly after more severe injuries with longer absence, cannot be excluded. Because injury grade and treatment were unavailable, these findings should not be generalized to high-grade or operatively treated MCL injuries.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: III, retrospective comparative cohort study.

articles.title: Radiology-to-Surgical Consultation Timing for Suspected Appendicitis in the Emergency Department: Retrospective Observational Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute appendicitis is a common condition that typically requires surgery, yet the workflow linking diagnostic imaging to surgical consultation varies substantially across emergency departments (EDs). Delays between imaging completion and consultation ordering may prolong care and contribute to avoidable clinical and operational inefficiencies.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to quantify real-world consultation delays among patients with radiology-confirmed appendicitis, identify factors associated with prolonged delays, and establish a manually adjudicated dataset linking radiology impression language to consultation behavior as an empirical foundation for future workflow automation. This study did not develop or evaluate a natural language processing (NLP) system; rather, the NLP and automation applications discussed represent potential areas for future work.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective observational study of ED encounters at a single academic medical center from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2025, during which abdominal imaging was obtained to evaluate possible appendicitis (N=1422). All radiology impressions were manually adjudicated and classified as positive, indeterminate, or negative. The primary timing measure was the interval from imaging completion to the placement of a surgical consultation order, which was analyzed within a predefined plausible window of -60 to +360 minutes. Mann-Whitney U tests were used to compare delays across imaging modalities and age groups. Logistic regression was used to assess predictors of prolonged delay (>30 minutes).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1422 encounters, radiology findings were classified as positive for appendicitis in 566 (39.8%), indeterminate in 675 (47.5%), and negative in 181 (12.7%). Surgical teams evaluated 99.8% (565/566) of patients with radiology-positive findings. Among 524 radiology-positive encounters with complete time stamps within the plausible window, the median time from imaging completion to consultation order was 30.8 (IQR 17.8-48.5) minutes, and 268 (51.1%) encounters exceeded 30 minutes. Delays were longer for computed tomography (CT) than for ultrasound (median 34.9 [IQR 21.7-53.0] vs 21.2 [IQR 10.9-36.4] minutes; P<.001). In adjusted analysis, CT was associated with prolonged delay (odds ratio [OR] 2.29, 95% CI 1.08-4.86; P=.03), whereas adult age group was not (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.52-2.28; P=.81). Across a typical year, cumulative imaging-to-consultation waiting time totaled approximately 58 patient-hours.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Radiology-confirmed appendicitis reliably triggered surgical evaluation, yet meaningful delays remained. This foundational timing analysis and the accompanying adjudicated dataset quantify the opportunity for future workflow improvements and can inform the development and evaluation of NLP-driven tools to automate consultation activation following clear radiologic diagnoses. Prospective studies are needed to develop and validate such systems.

articles.title: Patient Perspectives on a Symptom Assessment App in Emergency Care: Interview Study Among Patients in the AkuSym Trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Symptom assessment apps (SAAs) allow laypersons to input their medical history and symptoms, generating a report of probable diagnoses and recommending next steps for medical care. Numerous and varied research findings exist regarding their diagnostic and triage accuracy, usability, acceptance, and user characteristics, including use in various settings. However, the perspective of low-acuity emergency patients on the benefits and challenges of using SAAs has not yet been explored.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to explore patients' experiences and attitudes toward the use of SAA before consultation in the emergency department (ED) and to identify perceived benefits and challenges of integrating SAAs into emergency care from the patients' perspective.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted semistructured interviews with self-referred, walk-in patients at 2 EDs and an ED-associated outpatient on-call practice in Berlin, who were allocated to the intervention group of the AkuSym trial. Participants had self-assessed their health complaints using the Ada Health SAA before their first encounter with the treating physician. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with deductively and inductively developed categories.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighteen patients were interviewed between July 2022 and November 2022. Most participants stated that they would use an SAA again, including outside the emergency care setting. Key factors influencing reuse were precise symptom queries and clear, layperson-friendly medical content. Patients' trust in medical professionals was higher than in SAA assessments, and personal doctor-patient contact remained essential. The SAA was perceived primarily as a source of preliminary information and a supplement to doctor-patient contact. It helped participants reflect on and articulate their symptoms. Participants also saw potential for SAAs to support decisions about whether and where to seek medical care, to provide self-help recommendations for minor complaints, and to enable more informed participation in diagnostic discussions. Concerns included inaccurate or incomplete symptom input, difficulties understanding and interpreting SAA results, and receiving alarming or unclear information that could increase anxiety or complicate the subsequent consultation. Identified challenges included enabling information transfer through digital interfaces and ensuring data protection. Participants suggested solutions such as voluntary access via waiting-room QR codes, linking SAA reports to electronic patient records, and guiding patients to appropriate health care services.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Meaningful integration of SAA use into emergency care requires a clear understanding of how SAA assessments should be used during the doctor-patient consultation, and ensuring accessibility for patients with limited digital health literacy. Such tools have the potential to improve health literacy and empower patients, potentially leading to more efficient health care use. Linking SAA reports to a public website that provides evidence-based, layperson-friendly information and contact details for appropriate health care providers could help patients understand their results and identify suitable care options.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered prehospital thrombolysis for ST elevation myocardial infarction.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Guidelines recommend prehospital thrombolysis for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) if trained clinicians can interpret 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) on site. The Queensland Ambulance Service (QAS) has a well-established prehospital reperfusion program under which all paramedics are trained in prehospital STEMI diagnosis on 12-lead ECG and administering thrombolysis in the field to eligible patients. Whilst the clinical benefits of this treatment are proven, its cost-effectiveness remains to be established.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We developed a decision-analytic microsimulation model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered thrombolysis for prehospital STEMI in the state of Queensland, Australia. The comparator was a hypothetical counterfactual group of patients who were clinically eligible for prehospital thrombolysis but received an alternate treatment pathway. The analysis was conducted from a health provider (Queensland Government) perspective. A lifetime time horizon was used. Input values of the acute phase were derived from our prehospital and linked hospital database of all STEMI patients receiving prehospital thrombolysis from QAS paramedics between January 2022 and December 2024. Input values of the long-term phase were obtained from published literature. Cost was expressed in Australian dollars (AUD) and United States dollars (USD) in 2026 value, and effectiveness in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Prehospital thrombolysis improved outcomes at a cost of AUD 16,750.22 per QALY gained (95% uncertainty range AUD 15,477.48 - 18,422.84) or USD 11,725.15 (USD 10,834.24 - 12,895.99). In the sensitivity analysis, the cost-effectiveness of prehospital thrombolysis was robust to changes in input values.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Paramedic-administered thrombolysis in the field for prehospital STEMI, compared with no such treatment, represents value for money.

articles.title: A Lighter Approach to Language Access: Virtual Interpreter Utilization in Emergency Medical Services (EMS).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Limited English Proficiency (LEP) may create communication barriers during prehospital care. Although on-demand interpreter services are often available to emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, utilization may be limited by device accessibility, workflow barriers, and clinician adoption. Our objective was to evaluate whether implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with increased utilization of virtual interpreter services during prehospital care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted an observational retrospective pre-post cohort study of virtual interpreter service utilization within a large multistate Midwest EMS agency. On June 1, 2025, the agency issued smartphones (Apple iPhone 16, ∼6 ounces) to all clinicians, providing continuous access to virtual audio and video interpreter services (LanguageLine Solutions). Previously, interpreter services were accessed using large Toughbook laptops (∼6.1 pounds). Interpreter utilization was compared between pre-implementation (October 30, 2024, to May 31, 2025) and post-implementation (June 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025) periods. Interpreter requests per 100 encounters were compared using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Interpreter requests increased from 104 pre-implementation (0.19 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.15-0.23) to 326 post-implementation (0.57 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.51-0.63; RR= 3.04, 95% CI: 2.44-3.79; p < 0.001). Audio requests increased from 68 calls (0.12 per 100 encounters) to 271 calls (0.47 per 100 encounters; RR = 3.86, 95% CI: 2.96-5.03; p < 0.001). Video requests increased from 36 calls (0.06 per 100 encounters) to 55 calls (0.10 per 100 encounters), although the observed increase did not reach statistical significance (RR= 1.48, 95% CI: 0.97-2.25; p = 0.066). The most commonly requested languages were Spanish (n = 153, 36%), Somali (n = 146, 34%), and Arabic (n = 41, 10%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with a threefold increase in virtual interpreter utilization. This increase was driven primarily by audio interpretation, while the observed increase in video utilization did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest that improving point-of-care accessibility of interpreter services through lightweight mobile devices may facilitate greater utilization during prehospital encounters with patients with LEP.

articles.title: [Water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion-evidence and practical recommendations].

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Routine water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion have been recommended for decades, although their necessity remains controversial.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This narrative review aimed to evaluate the experimental and clinical evidence regarding water precautions in patients with tympanostomy tubes and to derive practical recommendations.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A narrative review of the experimental and clinical evidence on water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion was conducted.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Experimental studies have demonstrated that water penetration through tympanostomy tubes depends on the surface tension of the fluid, hydrostatic pressure, tube type, and the experimental model used. In contrast, clinical studies have consistently found no clinically relevant benefit of routine water precautions during normal showering, bathing, or surface swimming. Individual studies have suggested a potential benefit during the first postoperative month and indicated that the effect of water precautions may vary according to the type of water exposure.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The available evidence does not support routine water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion. No general ear protection is required for normal showering, bathing, or surface swimming. Ear protection may be considered during hair washing with shampoo based on experimental findings and when swimming in lakes or seawater. Individualized water precautions are advisable for patients with recurrent otorrhea or repeated symptoms following water exposure. Unprotected submersion and diving from height should be avoided, and patients with tympanostomy tubes are not considered fit for scuba diving.

articles.title: Research on the morphology and injury mechanism of pilon fractures.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Understanding the relationship between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures is essential for optimizing preoperative planning and surgical outcomes. To investigate the associations between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures and to provide a theoretical basis for precision diagnosis and treatment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included 192 patients with high-energy Pilon fractures treated at Lianyungang Second People's Hospital between January 2010 and December 2024. Using a standardized "trauma history-first plus imaging cross-validation" protocol, patients were categorized into 5 groups: dorsiflexion, varus, valgus, plantarflexion, and neutral. Two senior orthopedic surgeons (≥ 10 years of experience) independently and blindly assessed anteroposterior and lateral tibiofibular radiographs, CT scans, and three-dimensional reconstructions. Evaluated parameters included fibular fracture level and type, tibial fragment distribution, fracture angle, and Topliss classification. Interobserver reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient. Group comparisons were performed using the chi-square (χ²) test or Fisher's exact test with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Statistical significance was defined as P < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the 192 patients, 154 (80.2%) were male and 38 (19.8%) were female. The mean (SD) age was 43.38 (12.56) years (range, 14-71 years). Interobserver agreement was substantial for injury mechanism classification (κ = 0.82; 95% CI, 0.75-0.89) and core morphological assessments (κ = 0.87; 95% CI, 0.81-0.93). Fracture morphology differed significantly among mechanism groups (P < 0.05). Dorsiflexion injuries were characterized by the "medial + anterolateral + Die-punch" fragment pattern (45.0%; 95% CI, 23.1%-66.9%), fracture angles > 90° (65.0%), and coronal Y-shaped fractures (25.0%). Varus injuries predominantly showed the "anterolateral + posterolateral + medial + Die-punch" pattern (32.5%) and simple sagittal split fractures (40.0%). Valgus injuries were associated with comminuted fibular fractures (64.3%) and coronal V/Y-shaped tibial fractures (35.7%). Plantarflexion injuries typically involved posterolateral fragments (61.5%) and fracture angles > 90° (80.8%). Neutral injuries were characterized by complex multifragmentary comminuted fractures with Die-punch collapse (33.7%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: There is a significant and reproducible association between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures. This mechanism-based morphological characterization may provide an objective reference for preoperative assessment and individualized surgical planning. The clinical utility and prognostic value of this classification framework still need to be verified in further prospective studies with clinical outcome endpoints.

articles.title: Critically ill trauma in Portugal: a multicenter intensive care cohort study of frailty, organ dysfunction, and outcomes.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Multicenter data on critically ill trauma patients admitted to Portuguese intensive care units (ICUs) are lacking. We aimed to characterize their epidemiology, injury profile, organ dysfunction trajectories and outcomes, and to evaluate the prognostic performance of severity and frailty measures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Multicenter retrospective cohort study within the National Intensive Care Registry (RNMI) of adults (≥ 18 years) admitted to an ICU as a direct consequence of trauma (1 October-31 December 2024) in 32 of 50 voluntarily participating Portuguese ICUs; not nationally representative. SAPS II, ISS, TRISS, the Clinical Frailty Scale, daily SOFA scores, organ support, quality of life and mortality were collected. Prognostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis, multivariable logistic regression, calibration, and mixed-effects modelling of serial SOFA.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 457 patients were included; median age 61 years (IQR 45-74), 72.0% male. Falls were the leading injury mechanism (46.9%). Traumatic brain injury (32.9%) and thoracic trauma (21.4%) predominated. Observed ICU and hospital mortality were 11.0% and 15.3%, respectively. SOFA scores were consistently higher in non-survivors from day one. SAPS II showed the highest discrimination for hospital mortality (AUC 0.874, 95% CI 0.825-0.924), followed by TRISS (0.758) and the Clinical Frailty Scale (0.702). SAPS II, day-1 SOFA, and frailty were independently associated with hospital mortality. SAPS II over-predicted mortality (observed/expected 0.64), whereas TRISS showed a non-significant tendency to under-predict it (1.32, 95% CI 0.99-1.72).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this multicenter cohort from 32 voluntarily participating ICUs, patients were older, with frequent falls, neurotrauma and thoracic injury, and moderate mortality. Organ dysfunction trajectories and frailty were associated with hospital mortality, but incremental predictive value was not assessed; both merit inclusion in future trauma registry frameworks.

articles.title: Influence of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics on aseptic bone flap resorption: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Aseptic bone flap resorption (ABFR) remains a common complication after autologous cranioplasty following decompressive craniectomy (DC), with reported prevalences varying widely-often reported between 10% and 30%-likely due to inconsistent follow-up. Data on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics in pathogenesis of ABFR are scarce. Aim of the present study was therefore to identify potential risk factors, with a particular focus on CSF drainage procedures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective single-center study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent DC followed by autologous cranioplasty from 2015 to 2022. We collected demographics, clinical details, perioperative variables, and CSF interventions. Univariate and multivariate analyses identified associations, with subgroup focus on patients completing structured follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ABFR was diagnosed in 39/259 patients (15.1%), resulting in 38/101 (37.6%) in the 6-months follow-up cohort. Changes in CSF dynamics such as preoperative lumbar CSF drainage (p = 0.035) were identified as a risk factor, whereas ventriculoperitoneal shunt pressure adjustment was not associated with an increased risk of ABFR. After differentiation of the direction of adjustment, pressure reduction was not associated with ABFR. Especially preoperative lumbar CSF drainage remains an independent risk factor (p = 0.023) in multivariate analysis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Without structured imaging follow-up, ABFR rates are likely underestimated. CSF dynamic alterations beyond shunt presence alone may represent a relevant risk factor for ABFR. Our findings emphasize that primary alloplastic cranioplasty could be considered in at least a subgroup of patients.

articles.title: Trauma-associated cardiac arrest - insights and results from a German rescue helicopter station.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: In comparison with cardiac arrest attributable to other causes, trauma-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest has low survival rates, but survivors often show good neurological recovery. This study aimed to provide a deeper understanding of trauma-associated cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in terms of trauma mechanisms, injury patterns, CPR measures, and outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective single-center study, emergency physician reports on trauma-associated CPRs performed by the Christoph 22 helicopter emergency medical service (HEMS) from 2013 to 2023 at the study site in Ulm were analyzed using the chi-square test and binary logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 126 cases of prehospital trauma-associated CPR at the Ulm HEMS site were included. Four patients (3.2%) survived, with all four showing good neurological recovery. The most common cause of trauma was motorcycle accident. The patients most frequently presented with traumatic brain injury (TBI) (69.6%) and/or chest injuries (79.2%). Chest decompression was performed in 93.9% of the patients with chest injuries. TBI was the only injury to show a (negative) association with 30-day survival (1.1% vs. 7.9%; p = 0.049), this observation was independent of whether the TBI was isolated or occurred in combination with pelvic, abdominal, and/or chest injuries.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this study on trauma-associated CPR, the survival rate remained low, but the neurological recovery of survivors was often good. TBI, both isolated and in combination with chest, abdomen, and/or pelvic injuries, seemed to be a prognostically unfavorable factor. However, with only four long-term survivors, it is hardly possible to draw reliable conclusions.

articles.title: Carboxypeptidase B1: A novel, targetable contributor to thromboembolic complications in severe acute pancreatitis?
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with increased thrombotic risk. Systemic release of pancreatic proteases in SAP may alter susceptibility to endogenous fibrinolysis, but this remains unexplored. Pancreatic carboxypeptidase B1 (CPB1) is a protease activated by trypsin that shares cleavage specificity with thrombin-activatable fibrinolysis inhibitor, which cleaves C-terminal lysine residues off fibrin, impairing co-localization of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and plasminogen and rendering clots resistant to fibrinolysis. We hypothesized that circulating CPB1 would be elevated in SAP patients and contribute to fibrinolytic resistance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Plasma and clinical data were prospectively collected from SAP patients (n=15), matched critically ill controls without pancreatitis (n=13), and healthy controls (n=4) with IRB approval and informed consent. CPB1 levels were measured through ELISA. Clot lysis assays assessed fibrinolysis in response to tPA. Healthy control plasma was tested with and without porcine pancreas CPB1 to assess the effect of CPB1 on fibrinolysis. Transition midpoints (TM's) were defined as the time to 50% clot lysis. Clinical data were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U and Fisher exact tests. Assay results were analyzed using Kruskall-Wallis test. Significance was set at P<0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Demographics were similar between groups. SAP patients had markedly elevated CPB1 levels (154.0 [58.4-388.0] ng/mL) compared with sick (7.0 [4.1-15.6] ng/mL, P<0.0001) and healthy controls (4.0 [2.1-4.4], P<0.001). Healthy control plasma supplemented with porcine pancreas CPB1 demonstrated complete disruption of fibrinolysis compared with healthy plasma without CPB1. SAP patients had the highest resistance to tPA-induced fibrinolysis, with significantly higher baseline TMs than critically ill controls (42.0 [21.7-126.6] vs. 22.8 [18.3-33.7], P=0.04).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Patients with SAP have uniquely elevated circulating levels of CPB1, which may contribute to thromboembolism in SAP through fibrinolytic resistance. Further investigation into targeted CPB1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in SAP is warranted to potentially reduce development of organ failure and mortality.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: N/A (Basic Science).

articles.title: A Decade of Emergency Care for Incarcerated Adults at a Trauma Center in New York.
articles.journal_full: Journal of correctional health care : the official journal of the National Commission on Correctional Health Care

abstract.text: Previous research has highlighted low admission rates and assault and traumatic injuries in the acute care of incarcerated patients, often among those presenting from jail. We aimed to describe clinical characteristics and predictors of hospital admission among specifically state prison patients receiving emergency medical care. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all adults incarcerated in New York State prisons and treated in the emergency department of a Level 1 Trauma Center in Upstate New York from 2015 to 2024. They were predominantly male, younger, and healthy. Compared with previously reported jail populations, our state prison patient cohort had higher admission rates with more frequent medical, nonsurgical, diagnoses, suggesting that the health needs of patients from prison may differ from those in jail.

articles.title: Evaluating Clinical Features to Guide First-Line Imaging Selection in Suspected Cases of Acute Appendicitis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Imaging plays a major role in diagnosing appendicitis, the most common surgical emergency. Due to its availability and relatively low cost, many clinical guidelines recommend point-of-care or formal ultrasonography (US) as first-line imaging, although diagnostic information and accuracy vary. The current study provides clinical guidance to aid practitioners in selecting the most appropriate primary imaging modality among different patient populations in suspected cases of acute appendicitis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The authors performed univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses to evaluate the relationship between clinical features and US concordance in adults with suspected acute appendicitis. US concordance, defined as agreement between the diagnosis from US imaging and the final clinical and pathological diagnosis, served as the primary measure of diagnostic effectiveness.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Patients with a concordant US had significantly lower mean weight and body mass index, were less likely to originate from the emergency department, and more frequently presented with isolated right lower quadrant (RLQ) pain. In multivariable logistic regression of nongravid adults, high body mass index (≥ 25) was associated with 55% lower odds of concordant US, whereas isolated RLQ pain was associated with more than 2-fold greater odds of concordance. Additionally, although over one-fourth of patients received subsequent computed tomography imaging, leukocytosis and emergency department presentation were the only variables associated with obtaining follow-up computed tomography.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In conclusion, clinicians should avoid using US as the primary imaging modality among nongravid overweight patients, especially those who do not have isolated RLQ pain, when acute appendicitis is suspected.

articles.title: Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract.label: CONTEXT
abstract.text: Septic shock is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the pediatric population worldwide, and evidence comparing balanced crystalloids with normal saline (NS) for resuscitation remains inconclusive.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare balanced crystalloids with NS for fluid resuscitation in children with septic shock, incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: PubMed, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to May 2026, without language restrictions.

abstract.label: STUDY SELECTION
abstract.text: RCTs comparing balanced crystalloids with NS in patients aged 0 to 18 years with sepsis or septic shock were eligible.

abstract.label: DATA EXTRACTION
abstract.text: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; leave-one-out and post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the largest trial were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Six RCTs comprising 10,308 participants were included. RRs are reported with NS as the reference. Pooled mortality showed no statistical significance between groups (3.8% with balanced crystalloids vs. 4.0% with NS; RR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.67-1.27; P = 0.63). Acute kidney injury incidence also did not differ significantly between groups (19.7% vs. 29.6%; RR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.46-1.27; P = 0.29). The need for renal replacement therapy (RRT) was lower with balanced crystalloids (1.3% vs. 1.9%; RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.92; P = 0.01). Hyperchloremia incidence was lower with balanced crystalloids (32.3% vs. 49.9%; RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; P < 0.00001). After excluding the largest trial (PRoMPT BOLUS), mortality remained nonsignificant (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.45-1.50), and the reductions in RRT (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.87) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82) persisted.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Compared with NS, balanced crystalloids reduced the need for RRT and the incidence of hyperchloremia, without significantly affecting mortality or acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Revisiting the Risk of Bacteremia in Well-Appearing Infants With Fever Without a Source ≥40 °C: A Multicenter Study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Fever without a source (FWS) in infants is a frequent reason for emergency consultation. Historically, very high fever (≥40 °C) has been associated with an increased risk of bacteremia, prompting extensive diagnostic testing and empiric antibiotic therapy. However, recent epidemiological changes, including expanded vaccination and post-pandemic shifts in pathogen circulation, may have modified this risk. We aim to address this in our study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study in 2 tertiary hospitals in Catalonia (2018 to 2025). Well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months presenting with FWS ≥40 °C were included. The primary outcome was bacteremia. Clinical, laboratory, and microbiological data were analyzed descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 184 infants were included (median age 14.3 mo). Blood cultures were obtained in 168 (91.3%). Only one case of bacteremia (0.5%; 95% CI: 0.1-3.0) was identified, secondary to urinary tract infection (UTI), with no cases of occult bacteremia. UTI prevalence was 19.6%, and pneumonia 2.7%. Overall, 42.3% received antibiotics, and 16.3% were hospitalized, with all patients showing favorable outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months with FWS ≥40 °C, bacteremia appears uncommon, although the wide confidence interval precludes firm conclusions. These exploratory findings suggest that a more selective diagnostic approach may warrant consideration over routine blood cultures and empiric antibiotics, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Traumatic Diaphragmatic Crural Hematoma in Crush Trauma: Diagnostic Challenges and Management in a Rare Case.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of case reports

abstract.text: BACKGROUND Traumatic diaphragmatic injuries are uncommon in thoracoabdominal trauma, and traumatic diaphragmatic crural hematoma (TDCH) is even rarer in this context. Because of its retroperitoneal position, TDCH can be difficult to detect early. Although TDCH is usually not life-threatening and does not often require emergency surgery, it is important to note that it often coexists with other serious injuries. This report describes the case of TDCH and shock following crush trauma. After stabilization, whole-body contrast-enhanced CT identified TDCH and unstable pelvic fractures. She then underwent diagnostic angiography followed by surgical management of the pelvic injuries. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old woman with no prior health issues was brought to the emergency department after being accidentally crushed between 2 vehicles while her husband was reversing his car. She experienced pain in her chest, abdomen, and right hip. Initially in shock, she stabilized following initial resuscitation and blood transfusion. Initial evaluation, including extended FAST ultrasound (E-FAST), was negative. Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed fractures of the right sacrum, iliac wing, acetabulum, and pubic rami, along with a hematoma in the bilateral diaphragmatic crura (T12-L1) with contrast extravasation. Diagnostic angiography showed no active contrast extravasation from the diaphragm or pelvis. She subsequently underwent surgical fixation of pelvic fractures. Her postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged in stable condition. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights that TDCH is rare and may indicate a high-energy injury requiring prompt diagnosis. Whole-body contrast-enhanced CT is reasonable in patients presenting with shock and negative E-FAST findings. Management should be guided by bleeding status, and diagnostic angiography may be considered when active bleeding is suspected.

articles.title: How Discrimination Shapes Care-Seeking for Black Caregivers of Children With Medical Complexity.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Black children with medical complexity (CMC) experience a disproportionately high number of hospitalizations and emergency department (ED) visits. This disparity may reflect systemic and interpersonal racism and discrimination. Understanding Black caregivers' experiences is essential to designing programs that reduce acute care use. This study described caregivers' experiences of racism and discrimination and explored how these experiences influence care-seeking and communication among Black caregivers of CMC.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In partnership with family advocacy organizations, we recruited Black caregivers of CMC via national advocacy groups, social media, and electronic health record messaging. Eligible caregivers had a child aged 0 to 21 years with a hospitalization or ED visit in the previous year and a score of 3 or more on the Children with Special Health Care Needs screener. Purposive sampling ensured that one-third of participants were from rural areas. Semistructured interviews, guided by Critical Race Theory, were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-one caregivers completed interviews. Caregivers described discrimination in health care based on race and other characteristics. Five themes emerged in caregivers' experiences of racism: dismissal, stereotyping, fear of retaliation, dehumanization, and differential access to resources. These experiences contributed to distrust, caregiver burnout, and perceived negative health outcomes. Caregivers' responses to discrimination included withholding concerns, advocating, documenting, selecting specific clinicians, managing perceptions, and staying informed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Perceived racism and discrimination shaped how Black caregivers of CMC communicated with clinicians and navigated health care, underscoring the need for health care systems and clinicians to foster trusting partnerships, address structural inequities, and provide equitable, family-centered care.

articles.title: Social Media Asthma Education to Reduce Pediatric Health Care Use: A Bayesian Randomized Control Trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Traditional pediatric asthma education is often fragmented and time limited. Social media may provide a more sustained platform for education. We hypothesized that social media-based education (SME) about asthma would reduce health care use the year after asthma hospitalization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a 2-center Bayesian randomized trial, caregivers of patients aged 3 to 17 years hospitalized for asthma were randomly assigned to social media plus usual care or usual care alone, stratified by age (3-11 vs 12-17 years) and center. The SME group received at least weekly educational post via Facebook and Instagram. The primary outcome was total number of treatment days in a medical setting within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included treatment days across different settings, time to emergency department (ED) revisit or hospital readmission, missed school days, and patient satisfaction. Analyses were conducted using Bayesian generalized linear models with a neutral prior.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Two hundred participants were enrolled. Compared with usual care, SME had a 93% probability of reduced total treatment days (relative risk [RR] 0.80; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.59-1.07) and a 96% probability of decreased unplanned treatment days (RR 0.67; 95% CrI, 0.43-1.05). Mean time to ED revisit was 186 days in controls vs 225 days in the SME arm, with a 92% probability of reduction. Social media participants had longer time to readmission (293 vs 218 days; 81% probability of reduction) and greater satisfaction with education (73% vs 36%) than controls.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: SME was well accepted and likely reduced health care use and delayed posthospitalization ED visits and readmissions compared with usual care.

articles.title: Leading the Integration of Point-of-Care Ultrasound into Emergency Care in Somalia: A Proposed Health-System Framework Commentary.

abstract.text: Somalia faces substantial emergency-care demands alongside uneven diagnostic infrastructure and workforce capacity. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) can address focused bedside questions, but technology acquisition alone cannot create a reliable service. This commentary proposes a six-domain health-system framework covering governance, workforce capability, interdisciplinary integration, quality and safety, infrastructure, and learning and evaluation. It is a conceptual proposal for feasibility testing, not a validated intervention or report of original clinical outcomes. Published studies from the region, including a POCUS training evaluation in Hargeisa and an emergency-medicine training program in Tanzania, provide relevant implementation lessons but do not establish nationwide availability or effectiveness in Somalia. We recommend an initial assessment of equipment, staff skills, maintenance and referral pathways, followed by supervised pilot implementation, predefined safety and process indicators, and context-sensitive evaluation before scale-up. POCUS should complement formal imaging and specialist referral, and implementation decisions should account for recurrent costs, image review, credentialing and clinical escalation. This phased approach offers a testable service-development agenda; whether it improves patient outcomes in Somalia remains to be established.

articles.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: An Inferior Sinus Venosus Defect With Anomalous Right Middle and Lower Pulmonary Veins.

abstract.text: Sinus venosus defects are uncommon interatrial communications located outside the oval fossa. We describe a case of a seven-year-old girl with a history of fainting episodes, brought to the emergency department after several witnessed vacant episodes at school. Neurological examination was normal, but cardiovascular examination detected an ejection systolic murmur at the upper left sternal edge (pulmonary area). She was observed for 48 hours in hospital with ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring, which showed sinus rhythm with no arrhythmia. She was seen in the cardiology clinic six months later, where she reported to be well and asymptomatic. Initial transthoracic echocardiography showed right atrial and ventricular dilatation with a left-to-right shunt, which initially looked suspicious to be at or near atrial level, later confirmed on further transthoracic echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography to be a large inferior sinus venosus defect (approximately 11 mm in diameter on echocardiography and 16 x 8 mm on computed tomography), with anomalous connection of the right lower and right middle pulmonary veins to the right atrium through a common channel overriding the atrial septum, with associated marked right heart volume loading with preserved biventricular function. She is planned for surgical repair. This case shows how an unrelated presentation led to the diagnosis of a rare congenital anomaly and highlights the difficulty of identifying inferior sinus venosus defects on transthoracic echocardiography, and the less commonly described involvement of the right middle pulmonary vein, with an isolated anomalous connection of the right lower pulmonary vein being the usual finding.

articles.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Ambulance Transport for Suspected Bacterial Pneumonia and In-Hospital Mortality: A Population-Based ORION Study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To evaluate changes in difficult ambulance transport, in-hospital mortality, and ambulance transport rates for suspected bacterial pneumonia before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic in Osaka, Japan.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study used the population-based Osaka Emergency Information Research Intelligent Operation Network (ORION) registry (2018-2023). Patients with pneumonia (ICD-10 codes J13-J18) were identified independently using emergency medical technician diagnoses for transport analyses and physician diagnoses for mortality analyses. Periods were pre-pandemic (2018-2019), pandemic (2020-2022), and recovery (2023). Difficult transport was defined as four or more hospital selections and at least 30 min on scene. Annual ambulance transport rates and population-based in-hospital mortality were calculated per 100,000 residents.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 78,720 patients with suspected pneumonia identified by emergency medical technicians, difficult transport increased from 2.7% before the pandemic to 10.3% during the pandemic and 9.3% in recovery. Among 65,510 patients with physician-diagnosed pneumonia, in-hospital mortality was 7.8%, 10.7%, and 9.1%, respectively. Difficult transport was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.14; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.25). Population-based in-hospital mortality showed no corresponding increase. Annual ambulance transport rates decreased from 166.3 per 100,000 residents in 2018 to 117.3 in 2021, returning to 167.0 in 2023.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: During the pandemic, difficult transport and in-hospital mortality increased while ambulance transport rates for suspected pneumonia decreased. Changes in patient selection and case mix may partly explain the mortality trend.

articles.title: Competences of Paramedics in Prehospital Emergency Care: An Umbrella Review.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: The aim of this umbrella review is to describe and define the competences required of paramedics in out-of-hospital emergency medical care.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: The review was conducted in accordance with the methodological guidelines of the Joanna Briggs Institute.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: Keywords were defined according to the PCC-based inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were retrieved from the Medic, PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL and ProQuest databases. Publications in Finnish and English were included. The search was conducted in 2024.

abstract.label: REVIEW METHODS
abstract.text: Five reviewers independently screened the eligibility of reviews based on titles and abstracts (n = 2224) and full texts (n = 105). In the final stage, 20 studies were selected and critically appraised. Methodological quality was assessed using the JBI critical appraisal checklist. Data were analysed using inductive content analysis. Confidence in the synthesised findings was assessed using the GRADE-CERQual approach.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight reviews were included in the final synthesis. The competences required in out-of-hospital emergency medical care were categorised into five main domains: interpersonal and teamwork competence; cognitive and decision-making competence; professionalism and ethical competence; clinical competence; and competence across paramedic certification levels and in special or high-stress situations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This umbrella review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the competences required of paramedics in out-of-hospital emergency medical care, both currently and in the future. Furthermore, future research should examine which educational and assessment approaches most effectively support the ongoing maintenance and development of competence within a changing operational context and an expanding scope of practice.

articles.title: Cardiac Tamponade Masquerading as Lactic Acidosis.

abstract.text: An 85-year-old male presented with acute dyspnea and syncope, with pertinent initial vital signs including hypertension, normal heart rate, tachypnea, and hypoxemia requiring oxygen supplementation. The Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) team was consulted for treatment of acute hypoxic respiratory failure, severe hyperglycemia, and lactic acidosis; on MICU evaluation, bedside point of care ultrasonography (POCUS) revealed a large, circumferential pericardial effusion. Despite ongoing intravenous fluid resuscitation, the patient rapidly developed cardiac tamponade with pulsus paradoxus and hypotension. Given the severe hyperglycemia and likely resultant osmotic diuresis, his atypical presentation may have represented low-pressure cardiac tamponade phenotype. He was emergently taken for pericardiocentesis and drain placement with immediate resolution of clinical tamponade; the etiology of his pericardial effusion was deemed idiopathic, although a hemorrhagic effusion from anticoagulation use cannot be ruled out. Ultimately, this case highlights POCUS as an essential clinical tool that should be utilized upon initial assessment of ICU level of care patients to avoid missing indolent but fatal conditions, such as developing or manifest cardiac tamponade. Once cardiac tamponade is identified, careful intravenous fluid resuscitation may be appropriate under the correct circumstances, although definitive treatment involves emergent pericardiocentesis.

articles.title: Deterministic Noncontact Release and Transfer Through Programmable Interfacial Stress Reconfiguration.

abstract.text: Deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents is a central challenge in advanced electronic manufacturing, including chiplet integration and micro-LED assembly. Most switchable adhesives rely on contact-mediated detachment, which concentrates stress at the perimeter and causes slip and misalignment. Here, we report a diving beetle-inspired electroactive switchable adhesive (DESA) that achieves deterministic transfer through vibration-driven noncontact release enabled by interfacial stress reconfiguration. A perforated electrode couples a bioinspired adhesive layer to an electroactive PVC gel actuator, defining electrically contracting electrode-contact regions and mechanically linked gel-continuous hole regions. Under actuation, differential displacement between these regions deforms the adhesive layer and promotes partial peel-off at distributed interior sites rather than along a single perimeter front. At the 269 Hz resonance, vibration amplifies the displacement mismatch and spreads peel-off across the contact area, progressively reducing the load-bearing area. The resulting inertial stress completes noncontact separation, suppressing misalignment. The adhesive layer provides > 20 kPa dry and > 42 kPa wet adhesion across diverse substrates and retains stable performance over 1000 attachment-detachment cycles. On a robotic platform, the device transfers microcomponents with a lateral placement error of 318 ± 155 µm (≈99.5% placement accuracy). This interfacial stress reconfiguration offers a route to deterministic placement beyond adhesion-strength control.

articles.title: Can Pediatric Emergency Medicine Clinicians Identify Solid Organ Injuries Using Contrast-Enhanced FAST in Abdominal Trauma?

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Contrast-enhanced FAST (cFAST) has demonstrated superior sensitivity to B-mode FAST for detecting solid organ injury in blunt abdominal trauma, yet no prior study has evaluated cFAST image interpretation by pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) clinicians. We evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of cFAST interpretation for solid organ injuries by PEM clinicians following a web-based didactic.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, single-center study (February-May 2026), PEM clinicians credentialed in B-mode FAST without prior cFAST training completed a web-based didactic. Participants interpreted 12 simulated cases (25 cine clips), evaluating 41 organs (15 injured, 26 non-injured), all reviewed by a cFAST expert or cFAST-trained pediatric radiologist with CT confirmation. Pooled organ-level sensitivity and specificity were calculated with clustering correction using robust standard errors.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 41 participants, 1681 organ-level decisions were analyzed. Pooled sensitivity was 87.97% (95% CI: 84.96%-91.09%), specificity was 89.12% (95% CI: 86.53%-91.78%), negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.77% (95% CI: 90.99%-94.59%), and positive predictive value was 82.34% (95% CI: 78.68%-86.17%). False-negative decisions occurred in 4.4% (n = 74/1681).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: After a web-based curriculum, PEM clinicians achieved high sensitivity, specificity, and NPV with few missed injuries, supporting future investigation of cFAST as an adjunctive screening tool in pediatric blunt abdominal trauma risk-stratification assessments.

articles.title: Additional FiberTape-Cerclage® augmentation or "Bumper-plate" osteosynthesis for symphyseal arthrodesis - A biomechanical study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Chronic anterior pelvic instability may require symphyseal arthrodesis when conservative treatment and isolated plating fail. Therefore, dual plating has been clinically used to improve stability. As a novel augmentation FiberTape® cerclage may provide and alternative stabilization method with comparable mechanical stability, providing radiolucency for improved analysis of bone healing. Therefore, we conducted a biomechanical study to compare the effects of dual plating to a plate/ FiberTape® cerclage construct.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Twenty-four synthetic pelvic models (n = 8 per group) were stabilized using symphyseal plating, dual plating, or plate-cerclage constructs. Cyclic axial loading (50-400 N) was applied in a unilateral stance and bilateral-leg stance biomechanical model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The plate-cerclage resulted in significantly higher compression force (131.5 ± 31.7 N) compared to plate-only fixation (88.2 ± 20.9 N; p = 0.019), corresponding to a 49% increase. Dual plating reduced contact area (p ≤ 0.049). No significant differences were observed in one-leg stance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Fiber-Tape cerclage augmentation significantly enhances distraction resistance and preserves contact area compared to dual plating. Furthermore, this technique will potentially allow improved radiological visualization of the area of interest in the pubic symphysis after arthrodesis to analyze bone healing and osteointegration.

articles.title: Risk factors of in-hospital mortality in adult emergency department patients with atraumatic acute abdominal pain: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute abdominal pain (AAP) accounts for 7-10% of adult emergency department (ED) visits and represents a heterogeneous presentation. While diagnostic pathways have improved, early prognostic assessment remains limited. Identifying routinely available parameters associated with in-hospital mortality may provide prognostic information at initial triage. Therefore, we aimed to identify such parameters in adult AAP patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients assigned to the "abdominal pain in adults" Manchester Triage System flowchart at the University Hospital Bonn ED (2023-2025). Candidate predictors comprised all structured parameters available at initial triage. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. Group differences were assessed using Fisher's exact and Mann-Whitney U tests. We fitted a multivariable logistic regression model to assess associations between candidate predictors and in-hospital mortality. P-values were Bonferroni-adjusted. A focused literature search contextualized mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 6,370 encounters, 94 (1.5%) ended in death during the ED encounter or subsequent hospitalization. In-hospital mortality (1.5%) was within previously published ranges (0.4-8.0%). Patients who died were older and had lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure and SpO₂, higher pain NRS scores, and a different distribution of GCS scores at initial triage after adjustment for multiple testing. In multivariable analysis, age (OR 1.067 per year; 95% CI 1.052-1.082), lower diastolic blood pressure (OR 0.953 per mmHg; 95% CI 0.932-0.976), higher heart rate (OR 1.022 per beat/min; 95% CI 1.009-1.036), lower SpO₂ (OR 0.885 per percentage point; 95% CI 0.833-0.940), and higher pain NRS scores (OR 1.283 per point; 95% CI 1.126-1.462) were associated with mortality after adjustment for multiple testing. Among patients who died, vascular or bleeding disorders, bowel ischemia, and malignancy were the leading diagnostic categories.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In adult ED patients presenting with atraumatic AAP, in-hospital mortality was 1.5%, within the previously reported range. Age, lower diastolic blood pressure, higher heart rate, lower SpO₂, and higher pain intensity were independently associated with mortality after adjustment for multiple testing. These routinely available parameters may provide prognostic information at initial triage, but their value for improving risk prediction or clinical decision-making requires further investigation.

articles.title: Non-operative management after declining surgery in frail older adults with localised colorectal cancer: Survival, palliative interventions and healthcare utilisation in a prospective cohort.
articles.journal_full: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Surgery is the standard treatment for localised colorectal cancer, but its benefit-risk balance is heterogeneous in frail older adults. Evidence describing outcomes when frail patients decline surgery and are managed non-operatively remains limited. This study aimed to describe survival, palliative interventions and healthcare utilisation in frail patients with localised colorectal cancer managed non-operatively within a structured geriatric-oncology pathway.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This single-centre prospective cohort study included consecutive adults with non-metastatic colon or rectal cancer and a positive PRISMA-7 frailty screen between 2017 and 2024. Patients underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment, including IF-VIG frailty severity stratification. Outcomes were primarily described among patients who elected non-operative management; a contemporaneous frail surgical cohort was included for contextual comparison.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1028 patients assessed for curative-intent treatment, 115 screened positive for frailty: 74 (64.3%) were managed non-operatively and 41 (35.7%) underwent surgery. Mean follow-up was 24.5 months. In the non-operative cohort, 65 of 74 patients (87.8%) died, with a mean overall survival of 28 months. Compared with the surgical cohort, non-operative management was associated with higher mortality (87.8% vs 65.8%; p = 0.008) and shorter survival (28 vs 50 months; p < 0.001). Palliative interventions were required in 62.2% of non-operative patients. Emergency department attendance and hospital admission rates were 0.81 and 0.65 per patient-year, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In frail older adults with localised colorectal cancer, non-operative management after declining surgery was common and associated with shorter survival, frequent palliative interventions and measurable healthcare utilisation. Frailty severity stratification may support realistic surgical decision-making and goal-concordant treatment selection.

articles.title: Field Amputation by helicopter emergency service personnel: A cross-sectional survey of clinical practice and experience within air ambulance services in England.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Field Amputation (FA) is a rare, but potentially life-saving procedure undertaken by helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) in the UK. Literature pertaining to FA predominantly originates from outside the UK, where the operational, clinical and legal differences make its applicability to the UK uncertain. Consequently, the severe lack of FA reports from the UK mean that FA is poorly documented in this setting. The aim is to establish the current prehospital FA clinical guidance and practice in the UK.

abstract.label: METHOD/DISCUSSION
abstract.text: An electronic, cross-sectional survey was sent to all UK HEMS. The survey sought to improve understanding of clinical practice, including service provision, scope of practice, equipment, training, governance and incidences of FA. Surveys were analysed with descriptive statistics and descriptive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 15 HEMS responded, with 14 included for final analysis after one response was excluded. All respondents were from England. Every HEMS (n = 14, 100%) could provide FA, with 12 (86%) having a Clinical Practice Guideline specific to FA. Four services (29%) had undertaken FA within the last five years, totalling six cases, which were deemed notable given the absence of case reports from the UK in that time. A Gigli saw was the most popular instrument for bone disarticulation (n = 13, 93%). Unlike the USA and Korea, no respondents used hospital response teams to provide FA.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: FA service provision is widely available across England, with cases of FA being undertaken, yet little standardisation nationally. A national or international registry of every FA case could provide further insights into this area of clinical practice.

articles.title: Emergency medical service capacity and prehospital stroke care in Africa: a critical narrative review.

abstract.text: Stroke is a time-critical medical emergency in which rapid recognition, transport, and treatment are essential to preserving neurological function. Yet across much of Africa, the prehospital systems required to support timely stroke care remain fragmented, underdeveloped, or entirely absent. This critical narrative review examines the evidence on emergency medical service (EMS) capacity for acute stroke care in Africa. Available evidence demonstrates major deficiencies across the entire prehospital stroke pathway. Formal EMS systems are absent in many African countries, and where services exist, ambulance coverage is limited, unevenly distributed, and concentrated largely in urban settings. Community awareness of stroke symptoms and emergency response pathways remains critically low, while reliance on self-transport, pharmacies, traditional healers, and informal care pathways contributes to substantial delays in hospital presentation. Across multiple African settings, most patients with stroke arrive at healthcare facilities hours or days after symptom onset, well beyond established therapeutic windows for reperfusion therapy. The review argues that these delays are not isolated failures of individual behavior but manifestations of broader structural deficiencies in emergency care systems, transport infrastructure, health financing, and stroke preparedness. Limited integration of stroke into national EMS planning, inadequate investment in emergency care infrastructure, and the absence of African-specific implementation research have collectively constrained the development of effective prehospital stroke systems across the continent. Improving stroke outcomes in Africa will require coordinated investment in EMS infrastructure, culturally appropriate stroke awareness programs, community health worker training, mobile health-supported emergency coordination, and integrated prehospital-to-hospital stroke pathways. This evidence is drawn from Ghana, Nigeria, and South Africa, the minority of African countries with published, country-level EMS and stroke-pathway data. Findings and recommendations should be interpreted as characterizing this documented subset rather than the continent as a whole.

articles.title: ED red blood cell transfusion in severe anemia: stay and recurrent use-a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in the emergency department (ED) may occur during prolonged ED stays. We evaluated hospital stay and recurrent ED use among adults with severe anemia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort included ED encounters at a single tertiary academic hospital in Poland from January 2025-June 2026 with first hemoglobin <8.0 g/dL. Exposure was recorded ED RBC administration. Hospitalized encounters underwent propensity-score overlap weighting and patient-clustered bootstrap. Missing endpoints and available vital signs were recovered. Sensitivity analyses included 50 imputed datasets and weighted medians.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 131,711 ED encounters, 1381 met eligibility criteria; 742 involved ED RBC transfusion. The hospitalized cohort included 610 encounters (175 with and 435 without ED RBCs). The adjusted total stay difference among survivors was 10.9 h (95% confidence interval [CI], -42.5 to 65.8); downstream estimates remained imprecise. ED stay was 9.4 h longer (95% CI, 8.0-10.8). Among 341 patients with transfusion followed by direct discharge, recurrent patients generated 52.1% of 541 episodes; 31.7% returned within 30 days.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hospitalized encounters with recorded ED RBC administration had longer ED stays; treatment-related time could not be separated from waiting for inpatient beds. Downstream estimates allowed benefit or harm. Neither causal effects nor equivalence can be inferred. Pathways for stable recurrent anemia warrant evaluation while preserving urgent ED transfusion.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound for assessing the inferior vena cava: validity of an instructional video.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: to analyze the content validity evidence of educational videos for assessing the inferior vena cava using point-of-care ultrasound.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: a study of educational technology development and validity. The video was assessed by experts using Educational Technology in Health Appearance Validity Instrument (IVATES) in terms of clarity, practical relevance, and theoretical significance, and the Content Validity Ratio (CVR) was calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: the script was assessed by a focus group. Subsequently, it was recorded and assessed by 12 nurses, resulting in a CVR of 1.0 in relation to the assessed indicators, and a score close to 5 on the IVATES (high agreement).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: the video presented adequate evidence of content validity and can be used to train nurses in performing this assessment.

articles.title: Moral stress, support and professional quality of life among emergency department staff in Stockholm: a mixed-methods survey study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The demanding work environment in emergency departments (EDs) places staff at risk of experiencing moral stress and burnout. This study aimed to describe professional quality of life among ED staff and explore the support received, valued and requested by staff when experiencing moral stress.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All physicians, nurses and assistant nurses employed at two EDs in Stockholm were invited to participate. Of 637 eligible employees, 179 responses (28.1%) were included. Professional quality of life, perceived frequency of moral stress and both used and valued support were analysed descriptively. Free-text responses concerning requested workplace support were analysed using content analysis, and quantitative and qualitative findings were subsequently integrated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participants reported moderate levels of burnout (mean 23.6, SD 5.8) and compassion satisfaction (mean 37.9, SD 7.1) and low levels of secondary traumatic stress (mean 21.8, SD 5.5). Almost half (48%) reported experiencing morally stressful situations every shift or several times per shift. Informal support from colleagues was both the most commonly received and most highly valued type of support. Free-text responses highlighted requests for greater managerial involvement, structured reflection, education and formal support. Integration of the quantitative and qualitative findings indicated a gap between the support participants valued and the structured support available in the workplace.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Moral stress was frequently reported among participating ED staff, alongside moderate self-reported levels of burnout and compassion satisfaction. Informal collegial support was central, while participants also requested greater access to structured workplace support. Formal support structures may complement collegial support alongside organisational efforts to address workplace conditions contributing to moral stress.

articles.title: The epidemiology and burden of injury in The Gambia: A prospective trauma registry study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traumatic injury is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet robust prospective data characterizing injury epidemiology remain limited across sub-Saharan Africa. This study describes the demographic, injury, and initial treatment characteristics of patients enrolled in a hospital-based trauma registry in The Gambia. These data provide a foundation for characterizing the country's injury burden, guiding resource allocation, and informing continued trauma-system development.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective descriptive study was conducted using data from a hospital-based trauma registry established at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital, The Gambia's principal tertiary referral center for trauma and orthopaedic care. Injured patients presenting to the Trauma Emergency Unit from June 2022 through September 2025 were enrolled. Data included demographics, injury mechanism and setting, intent, anatomic injury location, injury type, and Trauma Emergency Unit disposition. Descriptive statistics were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 3380 enrolled patients, 76.1% were male, with a median age of 25 years. Most injuries occurred in villages (41.1%). Transport-related injuries were the leading mechanism (47.1%), followed by falls (29.3%) and violence/assault (21.4%). Streets/highways were the most common place of injury (43.3%), and nearly all injuries were unintentional (96.1%). The lower extremity below the knee (29.6%), head (22.3%), and hand (21.7%) were the most frequently injured body regions. Soft tissue injuries predominated (57.0%), followed by closed fractures (24.3%) and open fractures (11.7%). Overall, 55.9% of patients were discharged home, 29.3% were dispositioned to the operating theatre, and 10.1% left without being seen or before completing treatment. Among patients with recorded Trauma Emergency Unit disposition, 2.6% (n = 84) were categorized as 'mortuary or died.'

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: To our knowledge, this represents the largest prospective trauma registry analysis of injury epidemiology in The Gambia. Trauma disproportionately affected young males and was driven primarily by transport-related injuries, with a substantial burden occurring in rural settings. The frequency of fractures and incomplete treatment encounters highlights priorities for road-safety interventions, strengthened prehospital and referral systems, and expanded trauma, orthopaedic, and diagnostic capacity. Continued prospective trauma surveillance can support resource allocation, quality improvement, and national trauma-system development.

articles.title: Is it necessary to distally lock all pertrochanteric cephalo-medullary fixation in the geriatric population?
Serum lactate distribution across neurologic emergencies: implications for seizure identification.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Serum lactate is routinely measured in emergency departments (EDs) as a marker of systemic metabolic stress, but its distribution across neurologic emergencies is poorly characterized. We evaluated serum lactate distributions among patients with suspected neurologic emergencies and its utility for seizure identification.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed 22,430 consecutive ED visits and identified 637 ambulance-transported patients with suspected neurologic emergencies. All underwent venous blood gas analysis and non-contrast computed tomography on arrival. Serum lactate levels were compared among seizure (SZ), cerebral infarction (INF), transient ischemic attack (TIA), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), and other diagnoses. Multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), and classification and regression tree (CART) analyses were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Serum lactate differed significantly across diagnostic groups (P < 0.001) and was highest in patients with SZ and SAH. Among patients evaluated for ischemic stroke, age and serum lactate independently predicted SZ. ROC analysis showed moderate discrimination between SZ and ischemic stroke (INF/TIA) (area under the curve, 0.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.73-0.90). CART identified 4.05 mmol/L as the primary lactate threshold, with age providing additional stratification. Patients with lactate ≥4.05 mmol/L and age < 59.5 years had a 100% probability of SZ.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Serum lactate shows distinct distributions across neurologic emergencies encountered in the ED. Although not disease-specific, age-adjusted interpretation of serum lactate may improve seizure identification in patients presenting with suspected stroke. Because lactate measurement is rapid and routinely available, it may provide practical support for early diagnostic decision-making.

articles.title: [Crisis in sight: The gradual buildup to a crisis admission of people with dementia].

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine which clinical and contextual factors precede crisis admissions in people with dementia.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective medical record review within a nursinghome organization, comparing crisis and planned admissions.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Analysis of new admissions over a 3month preadmission period up to 2 weeks postadmission. Assessed variables included somatic stability, behavioral symptoms, caregiver burden, hospital and ED contacts, psychotropic use and legal status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 419 admissions were analyzed. Crisis admissions (n=304) involved individuals with apparent somatic stability but clear cognitive deterioration, increasing behavioral symptoms and rising caregiver burden. More ED visits without hospital admission, more behavioral incidents and higher psychotropic use occurred in the preceding period. The proportion of involuntary admissions was substantial.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
