abstract.text: Crisis admissions represent the endpoint of gradually increasing instability. Early recognition and proactive care planning within a strong primarycare network are essential to prevent, or prepare for, escalation and ensure care aligns with evolving needs.

articles.title: Hajj vaccination-related awareness, attitudes, perceptions, and post-vaccination experiences of local pilgrims and Ministry of Health workers: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal_full: Journal of infection and public health

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Vaccination is an important preventive measure during Hajj, but awareness and attitudes may vary among groups Hajj participants. This study assessed awareness, attitude and perceptions toward vaccination and described self-reported post-vaccination symptoms and subsequent healthcare utilization among local Hajj pilgrims and Ministry of Health (MOH) workers assigned to Hajj duties in 2025.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted using an electronic questionnaire distributed in November-December 2025 to local Hajj pilgrims and MOH workers assigned to Hajj. Descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher's exact tests, t-tests, and unadjusted analyses explored factors associated with awareness. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses examined factors associated with a positive attitude toward Hajj vaccination.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 953 participants (434 MOH workers and 519 pilgrims). Awareness of the health value of Hajj vaccination was higher among workers (87.6% vs. 74.8%, p < 0.001). Regarding attitude toward the mandatory Hajj meningococcal vaccine, 86.4% reported willingness to receive it even if optional, with no significant group difference. Awareness was associated with a positive attitude toward Hajj vaccination and remained associated with a positive attitude after adjustment (adjusted OR 4.31, 95% CI 2.84-6.56, p < 0.001). Older age, non-Saudi nationality, and absence of medical conditions were also independently associated with a positive attitude. More information about Hajj vaccines was reported by 60.6% of participants. Among participants assessed for post-vaccination symptoms, 26.0% reported one or more symptom, most commonly injection-site pain and low-grade fever/chills/headache, and healthcare utilization following symptoms was limited.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Awareness of the health value of Hajj vaccination was associated with a positive attitude after adjustment for relevant covariates. As awareness and attitude were measured simultaneously, this indicates an adjusted association, not a causal relationship. The findings support the importance of clear and accessible Hajj vaccination information and the need to strengthen vaccination-related awareness among Hajj participants and healthcare workers.

articles.title: Retrograde gearshift pedicle probe-assisted reduction of displaced superior pubic rami fractures: A technical note.

abstract.text: Percutaneous fixation of superior pubic ramus fractures relies on establishment of safe corridors. Rotational and multiplanar deformity due to fracture disrupts the corridors and percutaneous or open reduction of these fractures is challenging. Retrograde insertion of a curved gearshift pedicle probe allows the surgeon to create a joystick to affect translation, rotation and angulation with a single instrument to restore the superior pubic ramus corridor and allow passage of an antegrade wire or screw. Following corridor restoration, reduction was captured antegrade, while definitive implant type and trajectory were selected independently according to fracture and osseous corridor morphology. Three displaced superior pubic ramus fractures were treated using this technique including mid-ramus, high ramus and segmental fractures with translational and rotational components. The probe was effectively used to de-rotate and reduce the fractures to allow for safe insertion of internal fixation with full containment and no complications. The curved gearshift pedicle probe is a rigid intramedullary reduction aid capable of multiplanar fragment manipulation and restoration of superior pubic ramus corridor while preserving independent selection of definitive fixation.

articles.title: Latent Profile and Decision Tree Analysis of Humanistic Care Satisfaction in Critically Ill ED Patients in China.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patient satisfaction with humanistic care varies among critically ill patients in emergency departments, yet little is known about its subgroup characteristics in China.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore the latent classes of humanistic care satisfaction among critically ill patients in emergency departments in China and the factors associated with these classes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: From October 2025 to January 2026, a survey was conducted among 663 critically ill patients treated in the emergency departments of five tertiary hospitals in Jiangxi Province, China. Of the 712 questionnaires distributed, 663 valid responses were returned, yielding an effective response rate of 93.12%. Data were collected using a general demographic questionnaire, a perceived value scale, and an emergency humanistic care satisfaction scale. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was performed to identify distinct subgroups of humanistic care satisfaction, and multinomial logistic regression along with decision tree modeling was used to examine the factors associated with these latent classes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Three latent classes of humanistic care satisfaction were identified (entropy=0.996): a high-satisfaction group (57.5%), a moderate-satisfaction group (23.1%), and a low-satisfaction group (19.4%). Multinomial logistic regression revealed that age, education level, monthly household income, waiting time before treatment, and perceived value were significantly associated with the latent classes (P < 0.05). Among these, education level, waiting time, and perceived value were the most important associated variables, with perceived value positioned at the root node of the decision tree model. The decision tree model achieved an overall accuracy of 84.0%, but sensitivity for the low-satisfaction group was only 43.8%, limiting its clinical utility as a standalone screening tool.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Humanistic care satisfaction among critically ill emergency department patients in China exhibits distinct subgroup characteristics, which may inform the development of targeted quality improvement strategies.

articles.title: Does CT seatbelt sign, traumatic abdominal wall hernia or body habitus predict injuries and patient outcomes following a restrained motor vehicle collision? A New Zealand cohort study.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: to assess for associations between CT seatbelt sign (CTSBS), traumatic abdominal wall hernia and central adiposity with the severity of injury and subsequent management following a restrained motor vehicle collision.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Included patients were all major trauma patients (with an injury severity score ≥12), who were involved in a motor vehicle collision (MVC) and were restrained by a seatbelt, presenting to Christchurch Hospital between July 1st, 2018, and June 30th, 2023. Clinical data was collected prospectively by the Trauma team nursing staff at the time of injury and throughout the patient's admission. Original trauma CT imaging either performed at Christchurch hospital or the presenting hospitals were re-reviewed by a trauma specialist radiologist, as well as a post part 2 FRANZCR final year radiology trainee. The presence of a seatbelt sign, injuries and central adiposity were calculated from these images. Both univariable and multivariable analyses were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After exclusions 316 patients were included in the study. For CTSBS, there was Statistically higher incidence and grade of organ injury in both the thoracic and abdominal compartments except for large thoracic and abdominal vascular injuries, spinal injuries and pelvic injuries. Multivariable analysis demonstrated 10.41 times higher rates of death when CTSBS is present albeit with just 11 deaths. Outcomes were also worse when CTSBS was present; Injury severity score (13% higher), number of operating sessions (15% higher), length of ICU stay (64% higher) and hospital stay (32% higher). Regarding traumatic abdominal wall hernias, there was a higher incidence of any intra-abdominal organ injury (p = 0.042), as well as a higher incidence of GI tract (p < 0.001) and mesenteric injuries (p < 0.001). Regarding central adiposity, there was no significant difference of any of the measured outcomes when looking at different central adiposity groups except for number of operating sessions (p = 0.012).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The presence of a CTSBS or traumatic abdominal wall hernias are associated with a higher rate of organ injury and worse outcomes. Radiologists should include these signs in their reports. Differences in central adiposity have no significant associations with outcomes as the result of a restrained MVC.

articles.title: Activated partial thromboplastin time following Kcentra® versus Balfaxar® reversal of apixaban, rivaroxaban, and warfarin: a propensity-score matched cohort study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Kcentra® and Balfaxar® are the four-factor prothrombin concentrates (4F-PCCs) available in the United States. Both contain heparin to prevent in-vial activation, but Balfaxar® contains approximately 2-10 times more heparin versus Kcentra®. Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) is commonly used to monitor heparin activity. This study compared aPTT changes following administration of Kcentra® versus Balfaxar® for apixaban, rivaroxaban, and warfarin reversal.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, retrospective, propensity-score matched cohort study included adults given Kcentra® or Balfaxar® for apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin reversal. Patients had a baseline aPTT and a repeat aPTT within eight hours after 4F-PCC administration. Patients were matched 1:1 based on baseline aPTT and 4F-PCC dose. The primary outcome was aPTT change following administration. Secondary outcomes were hemostatic effectiveness within 24 h, new thrombotic events within seven days, and all-cause mortality within seven days.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1026 orders were screened, of which 46 patients had a 4F-PCC order meeting inclusion criteria and 30 were successfully matched (15 in each group). Median (IQR) aPTT change was -1.2 (-5.4 to 0.9) s with Kcentra® and -2.4 (-10.7 to -0.4) s with Balfaxar®. The median difference (95% CI) was 2 (-3.2 to 9.1) s and was not statistically different between groups (p = 0.468). There was not a statistical difference between groups for hemostatic effectiveness, new thrombotic event, or all-cause mortality, but the CIs for the between-group differences were wide.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this small propensity-score matched cohort of patients treated with apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin, Kcentra® and Balfaxar® were not associated with significantly different changes in aPTT despite their markedly different heparin content. No statistically significant between-group differences were identified for hemostatic effectiveness, thrombotic events, or all-cause mortality, but the wide CIs preclude any conclusion of clinical equivalence. Larger studies focusing on patient-oriented outcomes are needed.

articles.title: A Nomogram Based on MEWS, SpO2, Lactate, and Procalcitonin for Early Prediction of Septic Shock in Emergency Department Patients with Suspected Sepsis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore the early predictive value of a modified early warning score (MEWS) combined with bedside lactate, procalcitonin (PCT), and SpO2 for the development of septic shock in patients with suspected sepsis in the emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-center, prospective observational cohort study was designed, enrolling patients with suspected sepsis admitted to the emergency department of Beijing Electric Power Hospital of State Grid Corporation of China from June 2024 to June 2025. Early in the admission, MEWS, blood lactate, PCT, and oxygen saturation were collected. A multivariate logistic regression model was built, and the model's discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Internal validation was performed using the Bootstrap method, and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 302 patients were included, of whom 36 (11.9%) developed septic shock within 72 hours. Multivariate analysis revealed that lower SpO2, higher MEWS score, higher lactate, and higher PCT were independent predictors of septic shock. The final combined prediction model included SpO2, MEWS, lactate, and PCT, with an AUC of 0.775 (95% CI: 0.687-0.863) for predicting septic shock. After Bootstrap internal validation, the corrected C-index was 0.733 and the model calibration was good. Decision curve analysis showed that the model had clinical net benefit over a broad range of threshold probabilities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The combined prediction model based on SpO2, MEWS, lactate, and PCT can effectively identify high-risk patients who may progress to septic shock early in the emergency department.

articles.title: Modern Systemic Therapies for Psoriasis in Active-Duty German Soldiers: A Retrospective Single-Center Study of Treatment Outcomes and Service-Wide Operational Burden.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Several armed forces treat psoriasis as a categorical barrier to service, and systemic therapy can preclude enlistment or restrict deployment. These standards predate interleukin-17 and interleukin-23 inhibitors. We assessed efficacy, safety and drug survival of modern versus conventional systemic therapies in active-duty soldiers, and the psoriasis-attributable operational burden in the German Armed Forces.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Single-center retrospective cohort study. Of 142 active-duty soldiers with psoriasis seen in 2019-2023, 77 had received systemic therapy between 2004 and 2023 (first line 49 modern, 28 conventional, 127 treatment cycles in total). Endpoints were estimated Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) at initiation and at the last visit on first-line therapy, adverse events (CTCAE version 6.0), and drug survival (Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression). Operational outcomes came from four service-wide registries not linked to the cohort.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean estimated IGA improved by 2.0 points under first-line modern versus 0.8 points under conventional therapy (P < 0.001), and complete clearance (IGA 0) was reached by 38/49 (78%) versus 1/28 (3.6%) (P < 0.001). Adverse events caused discontinuation in 2/97 (2.1%) modern versus 14/30 (46.7%) conventional cycles (P < 0.001). No grade 3 or 4 laboratory abnormality occurred (0/60, 95% CI 0-6.0%). Modern therapy was associated with less discontinuation or switching (first-line hazard ratio 0.17, 95% CI 0.08-0.33; calendar-year adjusted 0.10, 95% CI 0.05-0.23). Service-wide, no declaration of permanent unfitness for service due to psoriasis was recorded over 20 years, and psoriasis caused 4 of 7096 repatriations (0.056%). Of 87 diving-fitness assessments documenting psoriasis, among 15,718 in total, one (1.1%) was negative, owing to psoriatic arthritis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this single-center military cohort, modern systemic therapies were associated with higher clearance, fewer adverse-event discontinuations and longer drug survival. Service-wide data showed a low observed psoriasis-attributable operational burden. These findings support giving demonstrated treatment response greater weight in individualized military fitness assessment.

articles.title: Application of environmental DNA (eDNA) technology in the investigation of oyster reefs in the Yellow River estuary.

abstract.text: Oyster reefs, the representative habitats in estuaries, have experienced substantial global declines as a result of coastal development and overfishing. Effective restoration of oyster reefs relies on accurate methods for assessing reef-building species. In this study, a species-specific environmental DNA (eDNA) method was developed to characterize the distribution of Crassostrea ariakensis, a key oyster species in the Yellow River estuary. Side-scan sonar surveys, scuba surveys and eDNA detection were conducted across three reported distribution zones of wild oyster reefs (Zone KL1, KL2 and S). The eDNA samples successfully detected C. ariakensis in the field when collected in close proximity to the oyster population. The results of the scuba surveys showed that the total wet weight of C. ariakensis ranked in the order KL2 > KL1 > S. The total eDNA copy number of C. ariakensis showed the same order KL2 (3951 copies) > KL1 (1470 copies) > S (below the LOD). Across all ten sampling stations in the three zones, the concordance rate between eDNA detection and scuba survey results was 80% with moderate concordance (K = 0.583, P < 0.05). Overall, oyster abundance in the Yellow River estuary was low, with individuals mainly consisting of small-sized specimens. A comparison with previous surveys suggest that the oyster reef area in the Yellow River estuary has declined. These findings demonstrate the potential of eDNA for field surveys of benthic mollusks and provide a preliminary basis for developing oyster reef restoration strategies.

articles.title: History of operative pelvic ring fixation is associated with increased risk of cesarean delivery: A matched retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pelvic ring injuries requiring surgical fixation are uncommon among women of childbearing age, and evidence to guide delivery in subsequent pregnancies is limited. Cesarean delivery (CD) is vital when indicated, but carries risk of complications, such as pulmonary and infectious complications in the child and an increased risk of infection, hysterectomy, and cardiac arrest in the mother. The purpose of this study was to compare the likelihood of CD in women with a history of pelvic fixation (HPF) and those with no history of pelvic injury (NPI) who were matched on factors related to CD.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective review of live deliveries among military beneficiaries in Birth and Infant Health Research program data between 2002 and 2021. All patients with HPF prior to delivery were selected. A cohort of patients with NPI were randomly selected in a 10:1 ratio, matched on age, year of delivery, number of prior births, and history of CD. The primary outcome of interest was CD. The secondary outcome of interest was indication for CD among the HPF cohort.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 79 patients with HPF who had a subsequent pregnancy that resulted in a live birth and 790 controls were selected based on the matching criteria, for a total of 869 patients. The average age at delivery was 26.8 years, 85% had no prior births, and 10% had a prior CD. Patients with HPF had higher prevalence of CD compared to those with NPI (54.4% vs 25.7%; risk ratio: 2.12; 95% confidence interval: 1.52-2.94). History of orthopedic fixation was the most common indication for CD in patients with HPF.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: HPF increased risk of CD, even when controlling for a history of CD. Women with HPF had approximately twice the prevalence of CD compared with matched women with NPI. Still, nearly half of women with HPF delivered vaginally, suggesting that prior pelvic fixation does not necessarily preclude vaginal delivery. Given that orthopedic fixation itself was frequently documented as an indication for CD, these findings highlight the need for individualized obstetric assessment and further evidence to guide delivery planning after pelvic fixation.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Prognostic Level III.

articles.title: Concomitant pelvic ring injury compromises acetabular reduction quality: A propensity score-matched analysis with surgical sequence subgroup study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Concomitant pelvic ring injury is reported to compromise acetabular fracture reduction, yet matched comparisons are scarce and the optimal surgical sequence remains debated. We assessed whether pelvic ring injury compromises anatomical acetabular reduction, and whether fixation sequence influences reduction quality and complications.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed 119 consecutive patients with isolated displaced acetabular fractures and 20 patients with combined pelvic ring and acetabular injuries treated at a tertiary trauma center (2004-2023). One-to-one propensity score matching using age, sex, and Letournel classification yielded 20 matched pairs (n = 40). Within the combined group, eight patients underwent acetabulum-first and 12 underwent pelvic ring-first fixation. The primary outcome was anatomical acetabular reduction (modified Matta criteria, 0-1 mm) graded by two independent reviewers. Secondary outcomes were pelvic ring reduction and postoperative complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Anatomical acetabular reduction was achieved in 14 of 20 isolated patients (70.0%) versus four of 20 combined patients (20.0%; p = 0.004). Within combined injuries, acetabulum-first showed a numerical trend toward better reduction (37.5% vs 8.3% anatomical; p = 0.132). Pelvic ring reduction did not differ between sequence subgroups (75.0% vs 83.3%; p = 0.450). Excluding pre-existing sciatic palsies, any complication occurred in two of eight acetabulum-first (25.0%) versus eight of 12 pelvic ring-first patients (66.7%; p = 0.170), driven by post-traumatic osteoarthritis (12.5% vs 41.7%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Concomitant pelvic ring injury significantly compromises anatomical acetabular reduction. Where precise pelvic ring reduction is achievable, pelvic ring-first fixation remains appropriate; where it is not, acetabulum-first or temporary pelvic stabilization followed by definitive fixation should be considered to avoid fixing the acetabulum onto a malreduced pelvic ring.

articles.title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection without chest pain identified on a triage electrocardiogram.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an uncommon but potentially devastating cause of myocardial infarction (MI) that may present without chest pain, making the diagnosis challenging. SCAD differs from atherosclerotic MI in both mechanism and risk profile: it predominantly affects women in midlife with few traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and is associated with fibromuscular dysplasia, recent emotional or physical stressors, and pregnancy. This report describes a 74-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department (ED) for a gastroenterology referral without chest pain and was found to have anterior ST elevations from a distal left anterior descending artery dissection. Although her age, atherosclerotic risk factors, and absence of chest pain were atypical, her sex and anterior ST changes were characteristic of SCAD, and a preceding period of physical stress may have contributed. A triage ECG led to catheterization before her troponin resulted.

articles.title: Co-administration of adrenaline and landiolol during cardiopulmonary resuscitation in a swine model of ventricular fibrillation.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: We examined whether early co-administration of landiolol and adrenaline improves successful extubation, hemodynamics, and 48-h outcomes in a swine ventricular fibrillation (VF) model.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, randomized, investigator-blinded study, VF was electrically induced in healthy piglets and left untreated for 8 min. Thirty-nine female Landrace/Large White piglets were randomized (1:1:1): adrenaline 0.02 mg/kg plus saline, adrenaline plus esmolol 0.5 mg/kg, or adrenaline plus landiolol 0.02 mg/kg. Treatment was administered at the initiation of mechanical cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), 2 min before attempting defibrillation. Primary outcome was successful extubation. Secondary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), 48-h survival, 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery, and hemodynamic variables during and after CPR.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Successful extubation occurred in 2/13 (15%) control, 6/13 (46%) esmolol, and 9/13 (69%) landiolol animals (overall p = 0.021); the rate was significantly higher with landiolol than with control (adjusted p = 0.046). ROSC rates were 46%, 69%, and 100%, respectively (p = 0.006); 48-h survival rates were 8%, 31%, and 54% (p = 0.046); and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery rates were 0%, 23%, and 46% (p = 0.022). The landiolol group had higher observed rates of ROSC and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery than the control group; these secondary analyses were exploratory. No pairwise difference was significant for 48-h survival. Exploratory analyses during the first 4 min of CPR identified higher observed values for selected hemodynamic variables and end-tidal carbon dioxide in the landiolol group at specific time points. Esmolol had intermediate observed outcome rates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Early administration of landiolol with adrenaline was associated with a higher successful extubation rate and better observed early CPR hemodynamics compared with adrenaline alone and had the highest rates of ROSC, 48-h survival, and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery. Secondary-outcome findings were exploratory, and landiolol was not statistically superior to esmolol.

articles.title: Emergency Physician-Performed Point-of-Care Ultrasound Identified Left Atrial Myxoma in Acute Cerebellar Infarction.

abstract.text: Cardiac myxoma is a rare but potentially curable cause of cardioembolic stroke. Early identification of a potential cardiac embolic source may be challenging when neurological symptoms predominate during the initial emergency department evaluation. A 72-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with acute-onset dizziness and vomiting. Although her National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was 0, she was unable to walk independently. Electrocardiography demonstrated newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation. Because a cardioembolic mechanism was considered, the emergency physician performed bedside cardiac point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), which revealed a highly mobile left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum. POCUS was performed 28 min after arrival, before brain magnetic resonance imaging, which demonstrated multiple acute cerebellar infarctions without large-vessel occlusion. Intravenous alteplase was not administered despite presentation within the therapeutic time window. Anticoagulation with intravenous unfractionated heparin was initiated. Surgical resection was postponed after hemorrhagic transformation of the cerebellar infarction was detected on hospital day 14. The patient underwent complete tumor resection on hospital day 41, and histopathological examination confirmed cardiac myxoma. She was discharged on hospital day 54 with a favorable outcome. This case illustrates the potential value of emergency physician-performed cardiac POCUS for early identification of structural cardiac abnormalities during the initial evaluation of selected patients with suspected cardioembolic stroke.

articles.title: Perioperative Management of a Breastfed Child Whose Mother Was Receiving Injectable Semaglutide: A Case Report Outlining Use of Gastric Point-of-Care Ultrasound.

abstract.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), including semaglutide, are increasingly used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus and for weight management. Although generally effective, specific end-organ effects, including delayed gastric emptying, may impact the perioperative care of patients receiving these agents. Given these concerns, guidelines have been suggested for the perioperative care of patients receiving GLP-1 RAs. However, these recommendations do not specifically address the increasingly encountered scenario in which a breastfeeding mother is taking a GLP-1 RA and the breastfed infant or young child is presenting for anesthetic care. We present a 15-month-old breastfed child who presented for surgery and whose mother was receiving once-weekly injectable semaglutide. Given limited evidence-based medicine to guide perioperative care in this clinical scenario, preoperative gastric point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) was used to evaluate gastric volume before induction of anesthesia. Perioperative care of breastfed children of mothers receiving GLP-1 RAs is discussed, the role of gastric POCUS is presented, and options for perioperative care are reviewed.

articles.title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Excess epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic dysfunction, but its assessment has traditionally required advanced imaging.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We investigated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled echocardiography could characterize epicardial adiposity and identify residual cardiometabolic risk.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We developed PanAdipo, a video-based deep learning model in 1,114,441 videos from 28,797 studies across the Yale-New Haven Health System (YNHHS) (2016-2022), using report-derived expert reader labels of prominent EAT (2.3% of studies). PanAdipo was evaluated in 5 testing cohorts: a temporally distinct YNHHS transthoracic echocardiography set (n = 4,588 patients contributing 5,130 studies), an emergency department point-of-care ultrasound cohort (n = 10,957), the geographically distinct MIMIC-IV (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care, version IV) data set (n = 4,549), the community-based MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) Exam 6 (n = 2,740), as well as in held-out YNHHS patients with paired coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography within 12 months (n = 5,167). Analyses examined discrimination of the report label and of CT-defined high indexed EAT volume, correlation with paired cardiac CT phenotypes, and body mass index (BMI)-adjusted associations with cardiometabolic biomarkers and newly documented metabolic disease.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the held-out health system test set, PanAdipo identified prominent EAT documented in clinical reports with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.91) across views. Against paired CT-derived measurements, PanAdipo discriminated age- and sex-specific high EAT (EAT / heart volume ≥95th percentile) with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 (95% CI: 0.89-0.92) overall and of 0.91-0.95 within age-sex groups, and correlated more strongly with indexed EAT volume (Spearman ρ = 0.76) than with BMI (Spearman ρ = 0.41; all P < 0.001); PanAdipo alone explained 53% of indexed EAT volume variance vs 23% for age, sex, and BMI combined. In MESA, higher scores were associated with an adverse metabolic profile (higher homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance [β = 0.17 per SD; 95% CI: 0.11-0.22; n = 950]) after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. In exploratory health system cohort analyses, higher scores were associated with newly documented steatotic liver disease (pooled BMI-adjusted HR: 1.33 [95% CI: 1.11-1.59] per SD of log[PanAdipo]) and hyperlipidemia (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.04-1.18), with modest precision (Hartung-Knapp intervals crossed 1).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: AI-enabled echocardiography provides a scalable digital biomarker that characterizes prominent epicardial adiposity and is associated with an adverse cardiometabolic profile, highlighting a role for echocardiography in metabolic risk stratification.

articles.title: Wastewater-Based Epidemiological Determination of Substances Used during the Super Bowl and Mardi Gras in New Orleans, Louisiana.

abstract.text: The unprecedented rise in drug overdose mortality over the past decade highlights the severity of ongoing public health crisis in the United States. Increasing polysubstance use involving synthetic fentanyl, psychostimulants, prescription opioids, veterinary tranquilizers, and nitazenes has further exacerbated this crisis, largely due to their unpredictable composition and pharmacological effects. Wastewater-based epidemiology was utilized to quantify 22 drug residues and metabolites, including psychostimulants, fentanyl, prescription opioids, medications for opioid use disorder, xylazine, and THC during the 2025 Super Bowl and Mardi Gras in New Orleans, Louisiana. Raw wastewater (n = 28) was collected during the Super Bowl and Mardi Gras weeks and typical weeks before or after the events. Samples were extracted and analyzed for residual drug residues employing isotopic dilution mass spectrometry using a state-of-the-art ultraperformance liquid chromatography and tandem mass spectrometry technique. The cocaine discharge during Mardi Gras (1220 ± 390 g/d) was significantly higher (p = 0.023) than a typical week. However, fentanyl discharge after Mardi Gras (4.43 ± 1.50 g/d) was significantly higher than during the Mardi Gras week (p = 0.015). This corresponds to an average daily discharge of 3.18 kg of cocaine (31,800 doses), 0.59 kg of methamphetamine (19,600 doses), 0.050 kg of fentanyl (49,600 doses), and 7.03 kg of THC (234,000 doses) during the 2025 Super Bowl and Mardi Gras in New Orleans. Average equivalent consumptions calculated based on estimated populations during the Super Bowl and Mardi Gras weeks, such as cocaine (5380-10,500 mg/d/1000 people), methamphetamine (1200-1780 mg/d/1000 people), and fentanyl (90.6-150 mg/d/1000 people), were not significantly higher than those during baseline weeks. Evidence-based mass loads of substances will be useful for the event planners, safety professionals, and emergency medical service personnel for improved understanding and prediction of spectator behavior to minimize associated public health risk.

articles.title: Pressure ulcer/injury risk assessment, prevalence and incidence in emergency room.

abstract.label: AIM OF THE STUDY
abstract.text: To analyse the pressure ulcer/injury risk assessment, prevalence and incidence in adult patients admitted to the emergency room in a Portuguese hospital.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: Quantitative, prospective, observational and cross-sectional study carried out between 1 November 2024 and 28 February 2025 in an emergency room of a Portuguese hospital. Skin and tissue integrity and pressure ulcer/injury risk assessment were performed at the time of emergency room admission and discharge, using the "Skin Assessment Tool" and the "Braden Scale". The participants recruitment and data collection were carried out by the nurses responsible for the emergency room in each shift, using a form developed specifically for this purpose. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sample of 156 participants. At the time of emergency room admission, 55.8% of the participants were at "high risk" of pressure ulcer/injury development. At the time of emergency room discharge the percentage of participants at "high risk" of pressure ulcer/injury development significantly increased up to 67.3%. The prevalence of pressure ulcers/injuries on admission was 2.6% and the incidence was 0%. Participants with "obesity", "altered state of consciousness"' and "advanced age" were more likely to be at "high risk" of pressure ulcers/injuries development. After the initial approach, 65.4% of the participants were transferred from the emergency room to other clinical areas of the emergency service/department.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The risk of developing pressure ulcers/injuries in emergency services/departments is a real problem. Preventive measures should be applied systematically since the moment of emergency room/service/department admission.

articles.title: Optimizing success in scalp replantation for total scalp avulsion injuries: A systematic review and case series.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Total scalp avulsion is a rare injury often caused by hair entrapment in rotary machinery. The avulsed tissue can include the eyebrows, eyelids, auricles, and rarely deeper facial structures. Microsurgical replantation is the gold-standard for management. This report provides an up-to-date systematic review of total scalp revascularization in adults and outlines principles to optimize outcomes in this challenging reconstruction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We reviewed 162 cases from 70 studies published between January 1976 (the first successful total scalp microsurgical replantation) and January 2025. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥ 16 years with total, near-total, or ≥ 70% scalp avulsion injuries.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean patient age was 31.4 years (range 17-64). Most patients were female (88.8%, n = 127). The average number of arterial and venous anastomoses was 1.8 and 2.5, respectively. The superficial temporal vessels were the most frequently utilized vessels for anastomosis and remain our preferred choice given their accessibility and suitability for reliable vascular reconstruction. Among articles reporting vein graft use, the average number was 1.7. Complete scalp survival (≥90%) was achieved in 64.2% of cases. Two patient cases from our trauma center are presented, along with technical recommendations.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Total scalp avulsion requires urgent microsurgical replantation for optimal outcomes. Our review underscores the importance of prioritizing superficial temporal vessels and performing multiple venous anastomoses to establish adequate venous drainage, although an optimal anastomotic ratio has not been established. Minimizing vein grafts may shorten operative time and decrease complications. Despite inherent challenges, over 60% of cases achieve excellent scalp survival. Close postoperative monitoring, anticoagulation, and psychiatric support are critical to managing physical and psychological sequelae. These findings support the need for specialized microsurgical expertise and multidisciplinary care to improve outcomes in this rare but severe injury.

articles.title: Did the affordable care act keep patients out of the emergency department? Changes in Illinois, 2016-2024.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: A central premise of the Affordable Care Act was that broader coverage would mean fewer emergency department visits. A decade later, has that happened? To address the need for longer term evidence, we describe changes in Illinois ED visits between 2016, two years after ACA Medicaid expansion, and 2024, after pandemic fluctuations in visit rates.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of Illinois Hospital Association discharge data for ED visits in 2016 and 2024 by Illinois residents aged 18-64, the most insurance-sensitive age group. We analyzed visits by patient, hospital, and clinical characteristics, including ED visits for ambulatory care sensitive conditions (ACSC), as defined by the AHRQ Prevention Quality Indicators in ED Settings. Multivariable logistic regressions were used to estimate changes in the likelihood of an ACSC visit.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Between 2016 and 2024, Illinois ED visits by residents aged 18-64 decreased from 3,168,399 to 2,653,154 (-16.3%). Visits identified as ACSC declined from 366,613 to 270,762, (-26.1%) with the largest decrease among the Medicaid-insured population. The odds of an ED visit for ACSC in 2024 compared to 2016 were lower for all patients (OR = 0.88 95% CI = 0.85-0.92). Decreases in odds were greatest for patients covered by Medicaid (17% lower) and Medicare disability (12% lower).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Declining ACSC visits, particularly among the Medicaid-insured, may reflect improved access to primary care. Insurance expansion is one part of the changing acute care delivery ecosystem, which includes increased telemedicine and urgent care centers as well as rising costs.

articles.title: Exploring and interpreting how nurses experience and attribute meaning during pediatric emergencies.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Appropriate and adequate use of clinical tools is important for achieving positive outcomes in patients during emergencies. This can be achieved when tools are understood based on their mode of Being and spatial value to Dasein rather being understood by the characteristics and properties they possess. However, there is little empirical research on how nurses deal with and encounter these tools, their lived experience of these tools, and their meaning-making of these tools in pediatric emergency care.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study aimed to explore and interpret how nurses experience and make meaning of the "mode-of-Being" and use of clinical tools in emergency pediatric care within the context of their everyday clinical practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A phenomenological design was adopted to explore tool use among pediatric emergency nurses in a hospital emergency ward. Qualitative data were collected through interviews and analyzed using Diekelman-Allan-Tanner's method.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Team application of the A, B, C, D, E (airway, breathing, circulation, dehydration, and exposure to trauma) protocol optimizes pediatric emergency care; work fashion as an ecosystem; human, institutional, and financial constraints; and three team-pillar approaches to professional development.

abstract.label: PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: This study will benefit children undergoing emergency treatment and enhance both experiential and theoretical knowledge of tools by nurses, thereby resulting in effective and efficient use of tools and higher-quality care outcomes.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen in cancer patients: a review of clinical safety, tissue selectivity, and therapeutic synergy.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: For decades, the clinical application of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (HBOT) in oncology has been constrained by theoretical concerns that hyperoxia might act as an unintended proliferative accelerator or tumor "fertilizer" by encouraging angiogenesis. This comprehensive review synthesizes the historical context, systematic review data, mechanistic literature, and clinical evidence to resolve three distinct questions: whether HBOT is safe in cancer patients, why its physiological effects diverge between healthy and malignant tissues, and how it can be leveraged synergistically with standard and novel oncological modalities.

abstract.label: SAFETY FINDINGS
abstract.text: The human clinical record demonstrates a consistent, reproducible record of clinical safety across published cohorts. More than 38 independent human clinical reports published since 1970 have examined HBOT in cancer patients, and all found no association with tumor growth, recurrence, or metastasis. This consistency is reinforced by 19 randomized trials comprising 1,103 tumor-bearing patients prospectively evaluated under hyperoxia, none of which showed malignant acceleration at any site. A mathematical power analysis applied to this clinical corpus demonstrates that the probability of a genuine, undetected oncological hazard is less than 1 × 10 - 11 .

abstract.label: TISSUE SELECTIVITY AND MECHANISMS
abstract.text: This safety profile rests on fundamental tissue selectivity. While intermittent hyperoxia drives tissue regeneration and upregulates antioxidant defenses in healthy host cells, malignant cells operating under the Warburg phenotype-characterized by severe mitochondrial structural degradation and cristolysis-possess a compressed redox margin. By reversing microenvironmental tumor hypoxia, hyperbaric oxygen destabilizes HIF-1alpha, suppresses glycolytic enzyme machinery, induces intrinsic mitochondrial apoptosis, and reverses epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.

abstract.label: THERAPEUTIC SYNERGY
abstract.text: Beyond clinical safety, hyperbaric hyperoxia acts as a potent therapeutic sensitizer. In randomized trials, adding HBOT to radiotherapy significantly reduced mortality and local recurrence in head and neck cancers. Mechanistically, HBOT dismantles dense extracellular matrix barriers, rebalances immunosuppressive myeloid components, and enhances T-cell infiltration, providing a clear rationale for combination with immunotherapies, chemotherapies, and ketogenic metabolic therapy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Active or historical malignancy is not a valid contraindication for hyperbaric oxygen intervention. Hyperbaric oxygen functions as a tissue-selective biological signal-safe in healthy host tissue, disruptive to malignant survival architecture, and synergistic with modern oncological therapeutics.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: integrating clinician-performed evidence and nurse-led implementation.

abstract.text: Neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is one of the most severe gastrointestinal emergencies in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), for which early identification, accurate assessment, and dynamic monitoring are critical for improving outcomes. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has emerged as a non-invasive, reproducible, and portable imaging modality with unique advantages for NEC assessment. However, direct evidence on nurse-led POCUS specifically in NEC remains scarce; most published ultrasound studies have been conducted by radiologists, sonographers, or neonatologists. This review synthesizes evidence from two sources: (1) clinician-performed POCUS technical evidence in NEC, including the detection of pneumatosis intestinalis, portal venous gas, and hemodynamic alterations; and (2) nurse-led implementation evidence derived from POCUS programs in other neonatal or critical care settings, including screening workflows, documentation standards, and training requirements. We discuss the current evidence base, highlight the gap between clinician-performed technical evidence and nurse-led implementation, and propose a framework for integrating POCUS into NICU nursing practice. By critically synthesizing the available evidence, this review aims to provide practical guidance for future nurse-led POCUS programs in NEC and to outline priority areas for prospective research.

articles.title: Healthcare workers' knowledge about essential emergency and critical care in primary health care in Tanzania.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Tanzania has recently introduced a national strategy for the provision of essential emergency and critical care (EECC) to all critically ill patients in the country. EECC is a simple and cost-effective approach for reducing mortality from critical illness, however, gaps in its provision remain, particularly in primary healthcare (PHC) facilities. Healthcare workers (HCWs) need to have adequate knowledge to be able to deliver EECC, but the baseline knowledge levels are unknown.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of EECC knowledge scores among acute HCWs from PHC facilities-comprising district hospitals, health centers and dispensaries in five regions of Tanzania and Zanzibar. Knowledge was assessed using a tool covering the foundational identification and treatment of critical illness that comprises EECC. Descriptive statistics were computed and results were described across subgroups stratified by cadre, facility level and years of professional experience.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean EECC knowledge score among HCWs was 31% (95% CI: 30-32). Knowledge score for the identification of critical illness was 19% and treatment was 32%. Medical doctors had mean knowledge scores of 44%, clinical officers 32% and nurses 29%. HCWs working in dispensaries, health centers and district hospitals scored 26%, 32%, and 31% respectively. No correlation was found between knowledge scores and years of professional experience in clinical care, nor in the critical care fields.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: HCWs in PHC facilities have a low level of knowledge about essential emergency and critical care. This is likely a significant barrier for the provision of effective EECC. The findings support prioritizing strategies to improve EECC knowledge as one component of improving care to critically ill patients.

articles.title: Prescription drugs and the risk of road traffic crashes in Bordeaux, France: a study matching emergency department health reports and a pharmaceutical reimbursement registry.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Prescription medications may impair driving ability and increase the risk of road traffic crashes (RTC). This study aimed to estimate the association between prescription medication use and RTC risk among patients attending the adult emergency department of Bordeaux University Hospital, France, assess trends in psychotropic medication use, and estimate the proportion of RTCs attributable to medication exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Emergency department records were linked with the French National Health Data System from 2013 to 2021. The study included 17 296 individuals aged 15 years or older presenting within 24 hours of an RTC. Drivers of motorised vehicles and vulnerable road users were included, whereas passengers were excluded. Acute and chronic effects were assessed using case-crossover and matched case-control designs, respectively. Medication exposure was classified according to the French pictogram-based driving risk classification (levels 0-3). ORs were estimated using conditional and multivariable logistic regression, and population attributable fractions were calculated using national prescription data.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: On the day of the RTC, 32.9% of individuals were exposed to at least one prescription medication. In the case-crossover analysis, level 3 medications were associated with increased RTC risk, particularly anxiolytics, opioids and antidepressants. In the case-control analysis, level 2 medications were associated with increased RTC risk (adjusted OR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17 to 1.38), as were level 3 medications (1.43, 95% CI 1.30 to 1.57). The highest risk was observed for centrally acting muscle relaxants (2.26, 95% CI 1.46 to 3.51). The population attributable fraction for level 2 and 3 medications decreased from 4.5% in 2013 to 3.8% in 2021.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prescription medications with a high driving-risk classification, particularly those acting on the nervous system, significantly increase RTC risk. Despite a slight decline in psychotropic use, a substantial burden of RTCs remains attributable to high-risk medication exposure, highlighting the need for continued public health interventions.

articles.title: Changes in earnings and employment after isolated traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injury.
articles.journal_full: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSES
abstract.text: Following traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries, the functional limitations and prolonged recovery can lead to time away from work, reduced productivity, and long-term economic consequences. This study aimed to assess the impact of isolated, traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries on changes in income and employment among working Canadians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, matched cohort study using linked Canadian health and tax administrative data (2007-2017). We included adults aged 18 to 64 years presenting to emergency departments (excluding Quebec) with isolated upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries. We estimated injury-attributable changes in income and employment using a difference-in-differences approach with linear and probit mixed-effects models, respectively.

abstract.label: MAIN FINDINGS
abstract.text: A total of 3300 cases (mean [SD] age, 37 [11] years; 2200 male [66.7%]) were matched to 2100 controls. Injured individuals experienced an average decline in income of Canadian dollars (CAD) $1718.96 (95% CI, -$2624.80 to -$813.12; p=0.0002) in the first year postinjury and CAD $1830.83 (95% CI, -$2627.61 to -$1034.03; p<0.0001) in the fifth year. Employment status also declined, with a difference of -2.71% points (95% CI, -3.26 to -2.16; p<0.0001) in the first year postinjury and -2.03 points (95% CI, -2.66 to -1.40; p<0.0001) in the fifth year.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries are associated with significant and sustained income loss, as well as modest but persistent declines in employment. These findings highlight the long-term economic burden of nerve injuries and underscore the importance of timely intervention and supportive return-to-work strategies.

articles.title: Pneumocephalus and pneumorrhachis after combined spinal-epidural anesthesia for labor analgesia: a case report.

abstract.text: Pneumocephalus is an extremely rare but potentially life-threatening complication of epidural anesthesia. We report the case of a 31-year-old woman who received combined spinal-epidural anesthesia for labor analgesia at 39 weeks of gestation. During the procedure, in which the loss-of-resistance-to-air (LOR-A) technique was used, approximately 2-3 mL of air was injected into the epidural space. The patient subsequently developed acute neurological deterioration, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 5 and flaccid quadriplegia. Emergency head computed tomography showed gas accumulation in the suprasellar and ambient cisterns, and spinal imaging revealed concurrent pneumorrhachis (intraspinal air) at the L2-L3 level. Due to incomplete recovery of consciousness and persistent quadriplegia, the patient underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) once daily for a total of seven sessions. Notably, transient psychotic symptoms developed during the fifth HBOT session. This case highlights that clinicians should consider intracranial pneumocephalus and intraspinal complications whenever a patient shows acute neurological deterioration after an intraspinal procedure. Although HBOT is a feasible option for pneumocephalus, clinicians should recognize that imaging improvement may lag behind or even diverge from clinical recovery, and decisions should therefore be made against the backdrop of repeated clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Baseline cognition accounts for most predictive information on cognitive recovery during rehabilitation after carbon monoxide poisoning.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cognitive change during rehabilitation after carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning may differ from prognosis at acute presentation. We examined whether information recorded in a rehabilitation pathway added predictive information beyond baseline cognition.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort included 200 patients who completed 30 repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) sessions and serial cognitive assessments between January 1, 2018, and January 31, 2026. Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores were assessed before rTMS and after 20 and 30 sessions. A MoCA increase of at least 5 points was the study-defined classification outcome; this threshold has not been validated for CO poisoning. Four exploratory algorithms were evaluated against a baseline-cognition benchmark. Performance was estimated from stratified five-fold out-of-fold predictions, with paired bootstrap comparisons of area under the curve (AUC) and Brier score.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: MMSE increased from 23.73 ± 2.85 to 27.83 ± 2.15 and MoCA from 21.58 ± 3.57 to 27.02 ± 2.78 after 30 sessions (both p < 0.001); 137 patients (68.5%) met the classification criterion. The baseline-cognition-only random forest had an AUC of 0.836 (95% CI 0.758-0.905) and a Brier score of 0.122, compared with 0.860 (95% CI 0.798-0.908) and 0.119 for the expanded model. Neither the paired AUC difference (0.024, 95% CI - 0.013 to 0.064; p = 0.219) nor Brier-score improvement (0.003, 95% CI - 0.008 to 0.014; p = 0.581) was statistically detectable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Baseline cognition dominated prediction of a score-change outcome that is mathematically linked to baseline and constrained by ceiling effects. The additional routine measures and coarse imaging categories available here showed no detectable incremental value. These preliminary findings describe selected rehabilitation completers and require external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Enhancing prognostic evaluation in cardiac amyloidosis: PALS, GLS and functional tests beyond KCCQ.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) often leads to reduced functional abilities, quality of life, and potential psychological repercussions. Several tests assess functional capacity, with the KCCQ score being the most widely used for heart failure symptoms, but it may overly rely on psychological factors. Left atrial (LA) strain indicates left ventricular (LV) diastolic function and filling pressure but doesn't correlate with KCCQ scores. The relationship between other tests and functional capacity or HRQoL (health-related quality of life) in CA remains unexplored.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This observational study aimed to assess the correlation between LA strain and LV global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) with functional tests. Furthermore, we aimed to examine their association with NT-proBNP levels and 6MWT in patients affected by CA, encompassing both AL and ATTR subtypes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We enrolled patients with CA during their follow-up visits. They underwent clinical, echocardiographic, functional capacity and quality-of-life assessments, including the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at baseline and after 3-6 months during follow-up visits, while subsequent clinical follow-up was used to ascertain the composite endpoint. The composite endpoint included all-cause mortality, hospitalization or emergency department visit for heart failure, and urgent cardiovascular visits for worsening heart failure symptoms. Deaths were further classified as cardiovascular or non-cardiovascular according to the predefined cause-of-death classification.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 67 patients diagnosed with CA (48 ATTRwt and 19 AL, average age 78 years, 21% female) were included. At baseline, patients had an LVEF of 53 ± 7%, a LVGLS of -13 ± 6% and mean PALS of 13 ± 7%. Global PALS demonstrated a positive correlation with DASI score (p = 0.06) and 6MWT (p = 0.004), and showed an inverse correlation with MLHFQ score (p = 0.005) and NT-proBNP (p = 0.003) while it was not correlated with KCCQ (p = 0.21). GLS demonstrated a positive correlation with NT-proBNP (p = 0.001), Minnesota score (p = 0.01), DASI score (p = 0.017). In contrast, the KCCQ did not correlate with NT-proBNP, PALS, 6MWT, or GLS. 42 patients (62.7%) experienced the composite endpoint. GLS was lower in the event group, PALS was lower, interventricular septal thickness (IVS) was larger, NT-proBNP was greater, and LAVi was higher. Our study showed that LVGLS, PALS, and apical sparing (RELAPS) were associated with the composite clinical endpoint, with LVGLS showing the numerically highest AUC among the evaluated parameters (AUC 0.704 (95% CI: 0.595-0.813) for LVGLS, 0.663 (95% CI: 0.549-0.777) for PALS, and 0.660 (95% CI: 0.545-0.775) for RELAPS).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: LVGLS showed significant associations with functional status and quality-of-life measures and had the numerically highest AUC for the composite clinical endpoint among the evaluated parameters.

articles.title: Bridging pathways after venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in infarct-related cardiogenic shock: a single-center real-world cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock remains highly lethal. We evaluated venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as a time-limited bridging platform rather than as stand-alone rescue support.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this single center retrospective observational cohort study, we retrospectively screened adults who received venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for infarct-related cardiogenic shock at Linyi People's Hospital from January 2021 to December 2025. Among 498 extracorporeal membrane oxygenation procedures, 218 infarct-related cardiogenic shock cases were identified. After excluding 76 extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation cases, 142 patients were analysed. Post-support pathways were classified as recovery surrogate, cardiac surgery, heart transplantation, durable left ventricular assist device support, or bridge failure. Cardiac surgery, heart transplantation, and durable left ventricular assist device support were combined as definitive downstream bridging. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression examined early characteristics associated with recovery surrogate versus bridge failure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean age was 57.5 ± 11.5 years, and 112 patients (78.9%) were male. Mortality at 28, 90, and 365 days was 33.8%, 40.8%, and 41.5%, respectively. Recovery surrogate was reached in 68 patients (47.9%), bridge failure occurred in 53 (37.3%), heart transplantation in 14 (9.9%), cardiac surgery in 5 (3.5%), and durable left ventricular assist device support in 2 (1.4%). Overall, 21 patients (14.8%) entered definitive downstream bridging. Older age and out-of-hospital cannulation were associated with lower odds of definitive downstream bridging. Among the 121 patients without definitive downstream bridging, higher left ventricular ejection fraction, younger age and lower creatinine were associated with recovery surrogate in multivariable analysis. In exploratory adjusted survival analysis, definitive downstream bridging was associated with lower 365-day mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Post-support pathways were heterogeneous. A pathway-based framework may better capture the clinical value of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation than mortality alone.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes and quality of life of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest survivors treated with extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation and their caregivers.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) are at risk of long-term neurological, cognitive, and psychological impairment, and this burden may extend to their caregivers. We evaluated long-term survival and multidimensional outcomes in survivors of refractory OHCA treated with extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) and in their caregivers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adults discharged alive after ECPR for refractory OHCA at a tertiary centre (2013-2024) were included. Survivors underwent long-term assessment of functional status and cognition, and self-reported psychological well-being, sleep, fatigue, return to work, and quality of life (QoL). One caregiver per survivor was evaluated for psychological distress, QoL, fatigue, and perceived burden.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 406 ECPR-treated patients, 63 (16%) were discharged alive. At a median follow-up of 3.1 (IQR 0.6-6.9) years, 38/62 (61%) were alive, of whom 31 (82%) had favourable neurological outcome. Only 7 of all 406 treated patients (1.7%) were alive with poor neurological outcome. Five-year mortality was higher in patients discharged with poor versus favourable neurological status (86% vs. 13%, p < 0.001). Among the 17 survivors and 19 caregivers assessed, QoL was preserved and comparable between groups (EQ VAS 70 [60-80] vs 80 [75-90]). Most survivors and caregivers reported no limitations in mobility, self-care, or usual activities. Mild cognitive impairment was found in 6/16 survivors and poor sleep quality in 10/17. Anxiety symptoms were more frequent among caregivers than survivors (6/18 vs 1/17). No participant met criteria for symptomatic post-traumatic stress disorder. Seven of 15 previously employed survivors and all caregivers returned to work.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Long-term survival after ECPR was largely confined to patients with favourable neurological recovery. Despite preserved overall QoL, survivors frequently showed cognitive impairment and reported sleep disturbances. Anxiety symptoms were common among caregivers. These findings support structured long-term follow-up programmes for both survivors and their families.

articles.title: Recovery trajectories of dizziness-related symptom burden and their associations with functional recovery and adverse post-discharge outcomes in older adults with ischemic vertigo: a prospective longitudinal study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Recovery after ischemic vertigo in older adults is heterogeneous, but longitudinal patterns of dizziness-related symptom burden and their clinical correlates remain insufficiently characterized. We aimed to identify distinct symptom-recovery trajectories, characterize functional recovery and adverse post-discharge outcomes across these trajectories, and examine clinical factors associated with unfavorable trajectory membership.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective longitudinal study of adults aged 65 years or older with confirmed ischemic vertigo who were recruited between February and December 2025 and followed for 6 months after discharge. Dizziness-related symptom burden was assessed using the Dizziness Handicap Inventory at discharge baseline, 7 days, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months. Latent class growth analysis was used to identify distinct symptom-recovery trajectories. Functional recovery, falls or near-falls, and healthcare reutilization were compared across the identified classes. All enrolled participants contributed available repeated measurements through full-information maximum likelihood, and factors associated with unfavorable class membership were examined using a three-step approach that accounted for classification uncertainty.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 231 enrolled participants, 214 completed at least three follow-up assessments and 189 completed all scheduled assessments; all 231 contributed available data to the trajectory analysis. A three-class solution was identified: favorable recovery (118 participants, 51.1%), intermediate recovery (74 participants, 32.0%), and unfavorable recovery (39 participants, 16.9%). Compared with the favorable class, the unfavorable class showed persistently higher dizziness-related handicap, slower Barthel Index improvement, lower recovery to pre-morbid mobility, and higher frequencies of emergency-department revisits and falls or near-falls. Prior stroke or transient ischemic attack, mobility limitation at discharge, and NIHSS score ≥3 were associated with unfavorable trajectory membership.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Recovery after emergency-department management of ischemic vertigo in older adults is heterogeneous. Early clinical features and recovery patterns were associated with persistent symptom burden, delayed functional recovery, and adverse post-discharge outcomes. Their potential role in guiding individualized follow-up and transitional care should be evaluated prospectively.

articles.title: [Organised de-shock: greater efficiency for improved safety].

abstract.text: A child's condition in the paediatric emergency department can deteriorate rapidly, requiring immediate care in the critical care unit. This situation causes stress for healthcare staff, as they must act quickly whilst drawing on specific skills and demonstrating good organisational skills. The reorganisation of this unit, centred on signage using specific colours, and the creation of care kits have led to improvements in safety, speed and efficiency.

articles.title: Bystander CPR Type and Outcomes After Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Compression-only cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CO-CPR) has been widely promoted to encourage bystander intervention in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but long-term trends in bystander CPR and the associations between CPR type and outcomes in pediatric OHCA remain unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate temporal trends in bystander CPR type and the associations with clinical outcomes among children with OHCA in Japan.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This cohort study included patients aged 17 years or younger with known receipt of bystander CPR documented in the nationwide All-Japan Utstein Registry from January 1, 2005, to December 31, 2023. Data analysis was performed from November 24, 2025, to September 2, 2026, including additional analyses conducted during the revision process.

abstract.label: EXPOSURES
abstract.text: Bystander CPR was categorized as rescue-breathing CPR (RB-CPR), CO-CPR, or no bystander CPR.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcome was 30-day neurologically favorable survival rate; secondary outcomes were 30-day survival rate and prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Temporal trends were assessed with multinomial logistic regression, and associations between CPR type and outcomes were evaluated using modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation, with CO-CPR serving as the reference.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 26 785 pediatric patients with OHCA (median [IQR] age, 2.0 [0-12] years; 16 254 males [60.7%]), 6543 (24.4%) received RB-CPR, 9112 (34.0%) received CO-CPR, and 11 130 (41.6%) received no bystander CPR. The adjusted probability of CO-CPR increased from 14.6% (95% CI, 13.1%-16.1%) in 2005 to 55.1% (95% CI, 52.5%-57.6%) in 2023, whereas RB-CPR declined from 41.7% (95% CI, 39.7%-43.7%) to 10.4% (95% CI, 8.7%-12.1%). The adjusted probability of receiving no bystander CPR plateaued at approximately 35.0% after 2013. Neurologically favorable 30-day survival rate occurred in 3.6% receiving no bystander CPR, 9.5% receiving CO-CPR, and 16.0% receiving RB-CPR. Compared with CO-CPR, RB-CPR was associated with a higher 30-day neurologically favorable survival rate (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 1.71; 95% CI, 1.57-1.86), 30-day survival rate (ARR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.42-1.61), and prehospital ROSC (ARR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.51-1.75), whereas receipt of no bystander CPR was associated with lower probabilities of these outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this cohort study of children with OHCA, increasing CO-CPR use coincided with declining RB-CPR but not with further reductions in untreated arrests after 2013. No bystander CPR was associated with worse outcomes compared with CO-CPR and RB-CPR. RB-CPR had more favorable outcomes than CO-CPR, supporting the continued importance of rescue breathing in pediatric resuscitation.

articles.title: Timing of Antenatal Care, Stillbirth, and Infant Mortality in Migrant Mothers in Australia.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Timely antenatal care (ANC) reduces pregnancy risks, yet the association between delayed ANC and stillbirth or infant mortality among migrant mothers in Australia has not previously been investigated.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine whether delayed ANC is associated with higher stillbirth and infant mortality among Australia-born compared with migrant mothers.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study assessed births to non-Indigenous mothers in New South Wales from January 1, 2002, to December 31, 2020, followed up to infant age of 1 year. Mothers were categorized as Australia-born, migrant from English-speaking country (ESM), or migrant from non-English-speaking country (non-ESM). Data were analyzed between August 2025 and June 2026.

abstract.label: EXPOSURES
abstract.text: Timing of first ANC, defined as 12 weeks or earlier, 13 to 19 weeks, 20 weeks or later, or no ANC.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The main outcome was stillbirth (at ≥20 weeks) and infant mortality (at prehospital discharge, posthospital discharge, or 1 year). Adjusted relative risks (ARRs) were estimated using Poisson regression models, stratified by migration group.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This study included 1 720 033 births (median [IQR] maternal age, 31.2 [27.4-34.8] years; 884 235 male infants [51.4%]), including 1 132 193 (65.8%) to Australia-born, 116 026 (6.7%) to ESM, and 471 814 (27.4%) to non-ESM mothers. Late ANC (>12 weeks) was more common in non-ESM mothers (190 338 [40.3%]) than Australia-born (334 790 [29.6%]) or ESM (41 029 [35.4%]) mothers. In cross-group comparisons, non-ESM mother status was associated with higher risk of adverse outcomes regardless of ANC timing. Compared with Australia-born mothers with early ANC (≤12 weeks), a higher risk of stillbirth (ARR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.18-1.33) and 1-year (ARR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.22-1.44), predischarge (ARR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.25-1.54), and postdischarge (ARR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.03-1.37) infant mortality was observed in non-ESM mothers accessing ANC by 12 weeks. Similar risk patterns were observed in non-ESM mothers with late ANC. In within-group comparisons, among Australia-born mothers, each category of delayed ANC was associated with higher risk. No ANC was associated with the highest risks across all maternal groups for stillbirth and 1-year infant mortality. For non-ESM mothers, late ANC (≥20 weeks) was associated with a lower risk of predischarge mortality (ARR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.61-0.92) but a higher risk of postdischarge mortality (ARR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.02-1.65).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this cohort study of 1.72 million births, higher risks of stillbirths and infant mortalities were observed in non-ESM mothers regardless of ANC timing, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Occupational heat stress in nurses working in hot environments and wearing personal protective equipment: mechanisms, health and safety implications, and prevention.

abstract.text: Climate change is increasing the frequency, intensity, and duration of extreme heat, while infection prevention and other clinical demands require many nurses to work in personal protective equipment (PPE). Hot environments and PPE use can coexist in emergency departments, intensive care units, infectious disease wards, operating rooms, prehospital services, and other settings in which workload, restricted recovery opportunities, and limited access to hydration may compound thermal strain. This narrative review integrates current evidence on the pathways through which environmental heat, metabolic workload, and PPE-related resistance to heat loss may affect nurses and other healthcare workers. An initial set of 31 references identified by the authors was updated through a PubMed search conducted on 2 September 2026 (three queries covering January 2024 to September 2026, plus one calibration query without date limits). For each cited study, the population, design, main findings, and directness to nurses were extracted, and the evidence was synthesized narratively across four domains: pathways, health and safety implications, risk assessment and monitoring, and prevention. Available studies, mostly of mixed healthcare-worker populations, consistently describe thermal discomfort, sweating, thirst, fatigue, headache, dizziness, and impaired well-being among PPE-exposed healthcare workers; however, nurse-specific longitudinal evidence and direct evidence linking heat strain to occupational injuries or patient-safety events remain limited. Effective prevention therefore requires more than individual coping. Healthcare facilities should combine environmental surveillance, task and PPE-sensitive risk assessment, accessible hydration and cooled recovery areas, work-rest and staffing arrangements, risk-appropriate PPE, personal cooling where feasible, symptom reporting, and emergency response. Future research should prioritize nurse-specific prospective cohorts, standardized exposure and outcome measures that include nurses' well-being and occupational safety, field-based intervention studies, and implementation outcomes across diverse climates and clinical settings. Integrating occupational heat protection into climate-resilient health-system planning may protect both the nursing workforce and continuity of care.

articles.title: Case Report: Raw grass carp gallbladder ingestion and acute liver injury.

abstract.text: Raw grass carp gallbladder ingestion for folk medicinal purposes may cause severe acute liver injury driven by the hepatotoxin 5α-cyprinol sulfate, yet high-dose human poisoning cases remain infrequently documented. We report a 60-year-old male (60 kg body weight) who developed severe intoxication 22 h after consuming six raw gallbladders from grass carps of approximately 1.5 kg each. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and watery diarrhoea occurred within 2 hours of ingestion. Laboratory testing on admission demonstrated extreme hepatocellular injury (ALT 6285 U/L, AST 9321 U/L). Conventional hepatoprotective agents plus pre-hospital haemoperfusion yielded limited biochemical improvement. While admitted to the intensive care unit, the patient received one session of double plasma molecular adsorption system, three sessions of plasma exchange and four sessions of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT, CVVHDF modality) alongside comprehensive supportive care. Liver function normalized within 14 hospital days; no acute kidney injury was observed.
