Complete symptomatic recovery was documented at the 4-week follow-up visit, though longer-term outcomes remain unknown given the limited follow-up duration. Toxin-mediated hepatocyte damage is partially supported by pre-clinical cyprinol-sulfate experimental work; many downstream oxidative, mitochondrial, endoplasmic-reticulum and inflammatory molecular pathways remain hypothetical and are largely extrapolated from unrelated liver-injury models, without direct validation in human carp-gallbladder-poisoning tissue specimens. Biochemical improvement was temporally associated with multimodal extracorporeal purification, but causal therapeutic benefit can't be proven from this uncontrolled single case; spontaneous hepatic regeneration may also contribute to recovery. This case highlights substantial hazards associated with folk-health beliefs promoting raw fish-gallbladder consumption, emphasising the need for early clinical recognition of fish-gallbladder poisoning.

articles.title: Sudden Deaths From Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage and Proximity to Neurosurgical Tertiary Care.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: A substantial proportion of deaths due to aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) occur without admission to neurosurgical units. Whether this proportion varies by geographic region is unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To determine the proportion of SAH deaths without neurosurgical unit admission across hospital districts in 2 high-income countries.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This retrospective, population-based cohort study used 2 externally validated nationwide administrative data collections in all 41 hospital districts and 10 neurosurgical units in Finland and New Zealand from January 1, 2001, to December 31, 2017. Participants included all hospitalized and fatal nonhospitalized cases with SAH. Data were analyzed from July 1, 2024, to September 7, 2026.

abstract.label: EXPOSURES
abstract.text: Hospital district of residence and its distance to the designated neurosurgical referral center, grouped into 4 zones.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcome was the death-based proportion of all 30-day deaths after SAH that occurred without neurosurgical unit admission (prehospital deaths plus deaths within 30 days after admission to a nonneurosurgical unit divided by all 30-day deaths from SAH). This proportion was estimated across 41 hospital districts and demographic groups, with age- and sex-adjusted risk ratios (RRs) and 95% CIs.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 12 912 patients with SAH (7856 in Finland and 5056 in New Zealand; median age, 58 [IQR, 49-69] years; 7924 [61.4%] women) were included. Of all 5418 SAH deaths, 3819 (70.5%) occurred without neurosurgical unit admission: 2203 of 3114 (70.7%) in Finland (interdistrict range, 403 of 644 [62.6%] to 5 of 5 [100%]) and 1616 of 2304 (70.1%) in New Zealand (interdistrict range, 111 of 190 [58.4%] to 22 of 23 [95.7%]). Compared with districts containing a neurosurgical unit (1723 of 2602 [66.2%]), the death-based proportions were higher in close-distance (1-130 km; 796 of 1129 [70.5%]; RR, 1.07 [95% CI, 1.02-1.12]), middle-distance (131-157 km; 469 of 599 [78.3%]; RR, 1.18 [95% CI, 1.12-1.24]), and far-distance (158-371 km; 831 of 1088 [76.4%]; RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.10-1.20]) zones. This proportion increased by 6.7% (95% CI, 4.9%-8.5%) for each additional 100 km to a neurosurgical unit. The proportions decreased in both countries over time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this cohort study of 12 912 patients with SAH, most deaths occurred without neurosurgical unit admission, and this proportion increased with distance to the neurosurgical referral center. Prevention and early management outside tertiary care may therefore warrant priority in reducing SAH mortality.

articles.title: Climate Vulnerability, Historical Redlining, and Children's Mental Health Care Use.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Structural inequities stemming from historical redlining and environmental injustice have created varying levels of risk among marginalized communities. However, the association of climate risk and structural racism with pediatric mental health care use remains underexplored.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To examine associations between climate vulnerability and pediatric mental health care use, and to assess whether these associations vary by historical redlining status.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study of children aged younger than 18 years residing in New York State between 2017 and 2022 used all-payer hospital administrative data from the New York State Department of Health. Statistical analysis was conducted from January 2025 through February 2026.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES
abstract.text: Outcomes included mental health-related emergency department (ED) and outpatient visits identified using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision-coded mental health diagnosis subtypes (eg, depression, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder), aggregated at the census-tract level. The primary exposure was climate-specific Climate Vulnerability Index quartiles (where 1 indicates low climate vulnerability and 4 indicates high climate vulnerability). Poisson regression models were conducted to examine associations between Climate Vulnerability Index quartiles and mental health-related health care utilization, including interactions with neighborhood-level redlining status (Home Owners' Loan Corporation grades C/D vs A/B) and subtype-specific analyses. Models adjusted for age, sex, self- or guardian-reported race and ethnicity, and neighborhood-level covariates, with coefficients reported as rate ratios (RRs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 553 134 mental health-related visits were included (mean [SD] age, 7.2 [5.8] years; 285 526 male [51.6%]). Compared with children living in areas with the lowest climate vulnerability, those living in the highest-vulnerability areas had higher outpatient visit rates (RR, 1.98; 95% CI, 1.72-2.27) and non-statistically significantly higher ED visit rates (RR, 1.14; 95% CI, 0.96-1.35). Associations between high climate vulnerability and mental health-related health care utilization varied by redlining status. In historically redlined neighborhoods, high climate vulnerability was associated with outpatient health care utilization (RR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.44-1.51; P < .001 for interaction) and, to a lesser extent, ED utilization (RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 1.02-1.09; P < .001 for interaction); in nonredlined neighborhoods high climate vulnerability was associated with lower outpatient health care utilization (RR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.45-0.49; P < .001 for interaction) and not associated with ED utilization (RR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.93-1.07). Associations also varied across mental health diagnosis subtypes, with higher climate vulnerability associated with increased health care utilization for most diagnosis subtypes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this cross-sectional study of children, residence in historically redlined and climate-vulnerable neighborhoods was associated with higher rates of mental health-related health care utilization. These findings highlight geographic patterns in mental health-related health care utilization that may be relevant to future research on climate preparedness, mental health services, culturally responsive care, and access to services for children experiencing climate-related stressors and structural inequities.

articles.title: Laryngeal involvement in chronic spontaneous urticaria-associated angioedema: Is there a genuine risk?

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) affects up to 1% of the population, and 40% of patients develop concomitant angioedema (CSU-AE). While clinically significant laryngeal involvement in mast cell-mediated CSU-AE is considered rare, and large cohorts report no fatal airway compromise, patients frequently present to emergency departments with symptoms perceived as potentially airway affecting.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe retrospective clinical observations of CSU-AE patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of upper airway involvement and to contextualize these findings within the existing literature.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective descriptive review of consecutive CSU patients evaluated between October 2017 and July 2018 at two tertiary referral centers (Milan, Italy and Sofia, Bulgaria). Medical records were screened for angioedema localization, history of physician-documented laryngeal involvement during emergency evaluations, history of airway interventions, medication exposure, and acute treatment response.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,098 patients, 530 (48%) experienced angioedema and wheals in the context of CSU-AE. Thirteen patients (2%) had objectively documented laryngeal involvement prompting emergency assessment; three patients (all female) underwent endotracheal intubation. No fatalities or loss of consciousness occurred. None had concurrent wheals during the reported laryngeal episodes. History of NSAID exposure preceded some laryngeal exacerbations, though not in intubated cases. None of the patients was receiving ACE inhibitor treatment, all had normal C1 inhibitor (antigen and function) and normal C4. Laryngeal symptoms resolved within hours following standard acute therapy with corticosteroids and/or antihistamines (AHs). Due to the retrospective design, diagnostic work-up for alternative angioedema mechanisms (genetic testing) was incomplete.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These observations do not indicate an increased intrinsic airway risk in CSU-AE. Rather, they illustrate diagnostic and management challenges in emergency settings and highlight the importance of mechanism-aware clinical assessment to avoid unnecessary invasive airway interventions. Laryngeal angioedema in CSU-AE is rare and presents with a mild clinical phenotype that does not typically require airway intervention.

articles.title: Opioid prescription patterns from 2019 to 2024: a multicenter analysis in Maryland, USA.

abstract.text: BACKGROUND: Prior to 2019, opioid prescriptions ordered by emergency clinicians were on the decline. However, the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic coincided with a reversal of this trend. Our study compares rates of opioid prescriptions in the pre- an during-pandemic period from emergency departments (EDs) in the state of Maryland, USA. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective pre-post observational study of opioid prescriptions for adult patients discharged from thirteen EDs and one urgent care in the University of Maryland Medical System (UMMS) who received opioid prescriptions from January 1, 2019 to January 1, 2024. The pre-pandemic period was defined as January 1, 2019 to February 29, 2020, and during-pandemic period as March 1, 2020 to January 1, 2024. Longitudinal trend analyses compared morphine equivalent dose (MED) per patient per week in the during-pandemic period to the corresponding week in the pre-pandemic period. Year-over-year analysis compared the MED of each week to the corresponding week from the previous year. We also performed a sensitivity analysis that excluded prescriptions with buprenorphine and methadone throughout the entire study period. RESULTS: We identified 121,889 patients who received opioid prescriptions. After excluding patients aged less than 18 years old and/or admitted to Psychiatric Emergency Services units or trauma patients, we included 117,912 patients, 26,606 (23%) in the pre-pandemic period and 91,306 (77%) in the during-pandemic period. The median MED dose increased significantly during the pandemic period compared with pre-pandemic levels (75 [60-90] vs. 60 [60-90], P<0.001). Year-to-year trend analyses demonstrated an initial increase in opioid prescribing in 2020, followed by a plateau when excluding buprenorphine and methadone, whereas prescribing continued to increase annually when these medications were included. CONCLUSION: Our results indicate that opioid prescriptions per patient from EDs within UMMS increased during the COVID-19 pandemic compared to the pre-pandemic period. Further studies with similar multicentered settings are necessary to confirm our observation and the impact of this new trend.

articles.title: Utilization of hands-free carotid artery Doppler ultrasound for noninvasive central venous pressure measurement: a prospective observational study.

abstract.text: BACKGROUND: Conventional central venous pressure (CVP) measurement requires central venous catheterization, which can be difficult to perform promptly in emergency settings. Bedside ultrasound provides an alternative approach by extracting CVP-related parameters. This study aims to evaluate the feasibility and accuracy of a hands-free carotid artery Doppler ultrasound (hCDU) method for noninvasive estimation of CVP in mechanically ventilated patients. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled adult patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit and receiving invasive mechanical ventilation from November 2024 to February 2025. Within 24 h of admission, blood pressure, heart rate, and CVP were collected. Conventional ultrasound was used to obtain carotid and internal jugular velocity time integrals (C-cVTI and C-jVTI) and the cross-sectional areas of the carotid artery (CSAa) and internal jugular vein (CSAj). Immediately, the carotid artery velocity time integral (H-cVTI) and the internal jugular vein velocity time integral (H-jVTI) were obtained by using the hCDU. Inter-rater reliability was assessed, and agreement between conventional ultrasound and hCDU measurements was evaluated using Bland-Altman plots. Correlation analyses and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were performed to evaluate correlations and diagnostic efficacy. RESULTS: A total of 94 patients were included. CSAj (r = 0.403, P<0.001) and CSAj/CSAa (r = 0.421, P<0.001) showed moderate positive correlations with CVP, whereas CSAa showed no significant correlation. H-cVTI (r = 0.384, P<0.001) was weakly positively correlated with CVP, H-jVTI (r = -0.677, P<0.001) was moderately negatively correlated, and H-cVTI/H-jVTI (r = 0.812, P<0.001) strongly positively correlated. A univariate linear regression equation, CVP = 6.703 × (H-cVTI/H-jVTI) + 3.603, yielded an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.961 (95%CI: 0.926-0.996) for predicting CVP > 10 cmH2O, with an optimal cutoff of 1.12, sensitivity of 90.5%, and specificity of 93.5%. CONCLUSION: The H-cVTI/H-jVTI ratio obtained via the hCDU method shows strong correlation with invasively measured CVP and may represent an alternative technique for noninvasive CVP estimation.

articles.title: Enhanced expression of osteopontin in experimental and clinical sepsis.

abstract.text: BACKGROUND: Osteopontin (OPN) has been implicated in sepsis pathophysiology, although its precise role remains contentious. The aim of this study was to investigate the role of OPN in sepsis, to preliminarily explore its major tissue source and to evaluate the association between circulating OPN levels and mortality in septic patients. METHODS: In a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia murine model, time- and dose-dependent changes in plasma OPN were assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and tissue OPN expression was evaluated by Western blotting (WB). The main tissue findings were further validated in a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) murine model. Clinical data were prospectively collected from sepsis patients admitted to the Emergency Department of Xiangya Hospital between June 2024 and February 2025. Plasma OPN levels were measured, and their association with 28-day mortality was analyzed. RESULTS: In LPS-treated mice, plasma OPN increased in a time-dependent manner, peaking at 24 h and remaining elevated at 30 h. Bone tissue showed the greatest OPN expression during endotoxemia. Similar tissue distribution pattern was observed in the CLP model. Plasma OPN levels were significantly higher in septic patients who died within 28 d (n=38) than those in survivors (n=83) (716.8 ng/mL vs. 348.4 ng/mL, P< 0.01). OPN yielded an AUC of 0.731 for the prediction of 28-day mortality (95% CI: 0.636-0.827), and the optimal cutoff value was 629.6 ng/mL. Higher plasma OPN levels were associated with 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis. CONCLUSION: In murine endotoxemia, OPN shows delayed and sustained upregulation after LPS stimulation. Findings from both LPS and CLP models support that bone tissue may serve as a major contributor to elevated circulating OPN in experimental sepsis. Plasma OPN levels are associated with mortality in sepsis.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for the detection of acute aortic syndrome in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.text: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic disorders with a wide range of presentations that are easily misdiagnosed in the emergency department (ED). The 2024 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines recommended focused transthoracic echocardiography as the first-line imaging tool for the detection of aortic dissection, but the performance of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in detecting AAS in ED varies considerably in the existing literature. We aim to gather and synthesize existing studies to provide a more comprehensive overview of the diagnostic accuracy and value of POCUS for the detection of AAS and its generalizability in the ED setting. METHODS: Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from 1 January 2000 to 21 July 2025. Diagnostic accuracy studies of POCUS in the ED for the detection of AAS were included. For included studies, the diagnostic accuracy of POCUS for detecting AAS was revealed by calculating the sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratio, and diagnostic odds ratio, with 95% credible intervals (CrI). The diagnostic performance of POCUS was evaluated by summary receiver operator curve (SROC). RESULTS: A total of 4,855 patients from seven studies were included in the meta-analysis. For any sonographic signs for detecting AAS, the pooled sensitivity and specificity of POCUS were 88.3% (95%CrI: 85.1% -91.2%) and 80.3% (95%CrI: 63.4%-92.9%), respectively. The area under the SROC of any sonographic signs for detecting AAS was 0.91 (95%CrI: 0.65-0.96). CONCLUSION: This systematic review provides support that POCUS may be a useful early imaging tool for ruling in AAS in the ED due to its high specificity for direct sonographic sign. While the overall certainty of evidence is moderate to low, larger-scale prospective studies on the use of POCUS with other diagnostic tools for detecting AAS are necessary in ED settings.

articles.title: Clinical Value of Procalcitonin and Sarcopenia Index in Evaluating Intra-Abdominal Infection in Trauma Patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The aim is to evaluate the predictive value of serum procalcitonin (PCT) and the sarcopenia index (SI) for intra-abdominal infection (IAI) during hospitalization in patients with abdominal trauma; to compare the discriminatory performance of single indicators versus their combination, and to conduct gender-stratified and clinical application assessments.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-center cohort study was conducted that included patients with abdominal trauma (n = 326) ad-mitted through the emergency department. PCT levels on days 1, 3, and 5 (denoted as PCT1, PCT3, and PCT5, respectively), and SI was calculated using creatinine (Cr) and cystatin C (CysC). The main outcome was IAI during hospitalization. ROC curves and DeLong's test were used to compare the discriminative ability of PCT at different time points. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed stratified by gender. A combined model and nomogram were developed based on PCT3 and 1/SI. Decision curve analysis (DCA) and calibration curves were applied to evaluate clinical net benefit and model consistency.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The IAI group had significantly higher PCT levels at all time points compared to the non-IAI group. PCT3 demonstrated the best discriminatory performance, and was significantly superior to PCT1 and PCT5. Baseline comparisons revealed gender differences in SI, with male patients having higher SI than females, while no significant gender differences were found for PCT3 or the proportion of IAI. In gender-stratified regression, PCT3 was a common independent predictor of IAI in both male and female patients, while SI was negatively correlated with IAI. The combined model (PCT3 + 1/SI) outperformed any single indicator in both male and female groups. DCA showed a stable net clinical benefit, and the model was well-calibrated. The nomogram could be used for individualized bedside risk assessment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: PCT3 is the strongest single predictor of IAI, and SI is negatively correlated with IAI. Their combination further enhances predictive discrimination, offering clinical net benefit and good calibration. Effective prediction of IAI can be achieved using routine serological indicators from hospital day 3 - serum PCT and SI calculated from routine Cr and CysC.

articles.title: The Perceived Buffering Role of Emotional Intelligence on Job Burnout Among Emergency Department Nurses: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To explore the perceived buffering role of emotional intelligence on job burnout among emergency department (ED) nurses from the perspective of their experiences.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A qualitative descriptive study using directed qualitative content analysis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Fifteen ED nurses from a tertiary hospital in China were purposively selected. Data were collected via semi-structured in-depth interviews and analysed using directed qualitative content analysis with the assistance of NVivo 12 software for data management and coding. The study adhered to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Studies (COREQ) checklist.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Six core themes emerged: (1) emotional awareness: Early warning signals of burnout; (2) emotional regulation: A toolkit for immediate coping; (3) cognitive reframing: Reinterpreting stressful events; (4) interpersonal resource mobilization: Strategic utilization of social support; (5) experiential growth: From passive endurance to active management; and (6) Boundary of protection: Contextual limitations of emotional intelligence. Emotional intelligence is experienced as an internal resource enabling early stress detection and cognitive reframing, though its perceived protective effect diminishes under extreme workload conditions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Emotional intelligence is perceived to buffer job burnout through various psychological coping processes. It is important to note that emotional intelligence was not formally measured in this qualitative study; rather, its protective role was perceived and described by the participants. However, this protection is not absolute and may be overwhelmed under conditions of extreme workload.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: Nursing administrators should integrate emotional intelligence training with organizational support strategies to prevent resource depletion and promote workforce sustainability, ultimately safeguarding nurse retention and patient safety.

abstract.label: PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: Patients or the public were not directly involved in the design, conduct, or reporting of this study, as the research focus was exclusively on nurses' occupational experiences.

articles.title: Recovery of Running and Technical Match Performance After Adductor Muscle Strain Injury in Male Professional Football Players: A Prospective Cohort Study of 27 Players From One LaLiga Team Across Five Seasons.
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports

abstract.text: Post return-to-play (RTP) running and technical match performance after adductor muscle strain injury remains unclear. The aim of the present study was to examine recovery of running and technical match performance after RTP following acute adductor muscle strain injury in professional football. This prospective longitudinal cohort study followed players from one team (n = 122) across five seasons (2020/2021-2024/2025). Injuries were recorded by the medical staff and confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging. Match performance variables included playing time, total distance, high-speed running distance (> 24 km/h), number of sprints (> 24 km/h), and offensive and defensive technical actions. First eight matches following RTP were compared with the four pre-injury matches. RTP required unrestricted team training and medical clearance for match selection. Data were analyzed using generalized estimating equations methods, adjusting event counts for the amount of playing time. Of the 122 players, 27 sustained at least one acute adductor muscle strain injury, accounting for 54 injury episodes. At Match 1, time played was -7.1% versus PRE (95% CI -16.7% to +3.5%), total-distance rate -0.4% (-2.4% to +1.5%), high-speed running distance +6.9% (-3.5% to +18.5%), and number of sprints +5.9% (-4.0% to +16.8%); none remained significant after FDR adjustment (p ≥ 0.182; pFDR ≥ 0.817). At Match 8, total passes were 26.5% below PRE (95% CI -50.0% to +7.9%; raw p = 0.116; pFDR = 0.567). Across all Match 1-8 contrasts, only long passes at Match 3 remained significant after FDR adjustment (-15.3%; 95% CI -22.4% to -7.6%; raw p < 0.001; pFDR = 0.022). In conclusion, there was little evidence of systematic population-level impairment in running or technical match performance after RTP. Late passing reductions warrant confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

articles.title: Subclinical Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Among Emergency Department Patients With Elevated Blood Pressure.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hypertension (HTN) is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet early detection of target organ damage is often missed, particularly in patients with limited access to care. The Emergency Department (ED), a key site of care for underserved populations, may offer an opportunity for risk stratification; we sought to determine the prevalence of LVH-a marker of subclinical disease and increased cardiovascular risk-among ED patients with asymptomatic elevated blood pressure and assess differences by sex, race, and insurance status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We enrolled a convenience sample of adults aged 18-65 years presenting to an academic ED with blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg systolic or ≥ 90 mmHg diastolic on two measurements. Subjects with prior LVH, active cardiac disease, hypertensive emergency, dialysis dependence, or pregnancy were excluded. LVH was identified using left ventricular mass indexed to height2.7 or body surface area via focused (point-of-care) cardiac ultrasound (parasternal long-axis view). Multivariate logistic regression assessed associations with LVH.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 155 subjects, 46 (29.7%, 95% CI 22.5%-36.9%) had LVH. Mean age was 46.9 ± 12.1 years; 53.6% were women. LVH was more prevalent in women (38.6% vs. 19.4%; p = 0.009) and remained independently associated with female sex (OR 2.44, 95% CI 1.14-5.22, p = 0.021) and prior hypertension (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.14-5.39, p = 0.023). Notably, 18.3% of patients without a prior hypertension diagnosis demonstrated LVH (p = 0.004).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nearly one-third of ED patients with elevated blood pressure had LVH, including many without known hypertension, with a higher prevalence among women.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05730309.

articles.title: Reduction in Emergency Department Attendances for Acute Bronchiolitis in Infants Aged Under 1 Year in England During Winter 2025/2026 Following Introduction of Maternal RSV Vaccination.

abstract.text: In September 2024, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) maternal vaccination was introduced to the UK schedule. Monitoring acute bronchiolitis emergency department (ED) attendance levels may provide a 'real-world' assessment of the likely impact. ED acute bronchiolitis attendances in England were substantially lower (-23%) in infants aged under 1 year in 2025/2026 compared to preceding seasons, consistent with bronchiolitis aetiology, vaccine efficacy and uptake and RSV immunisation programme impacts elsewhere. This work contributes to the evidence that maternal RSV vaccination is bringing about reductions in the RSV burden in young infants.

articles.title: [Comparison of prehospital management of selected emergencies between a paramedical team and a physician-led team : a retrospective study in Belgium].

abstract.text: In Belgium, the emergency medical system (EMS) coordinates mobile emergency and resuscitation units (SMUR) and paramedical intervention teams (PIT). As demand increases, greater use of PITs could help relieve SMUR workload, although comparative data remain limited. This retrospective study compared prehospital care by analysing 2,325 prehospital interventions (PIT = 1,377; SMUR = 948) involving cardiac arrest, trauma, seizures, chest pain, and acute respiratory disorders. Patient characteristics, response times, and management strategies were analysing. Management of cardiac arrest and seizures was comparable between the two intervention systems. In trauma cases, both patient characteristics and therapeutic interventions differed. In patients with chest pain, SMUR teams performed more electrocardiograms. For respiratory conditions, PIT teams more frequently administered oxygen therapy and aerosol treatment, whereas SMUR teams more often performed intubation. No difference was observed in response times. Overall, PIT appears to be a useful alternative when SMUR is unavailable; however, prospective studies are needed before confirming comparable performance between the two systems.

articles.title: [Gastric volvulus and wandering spleen : a case study].

abstract.text: A 2-year-old child is admitted in the emergency room for abdominal pain and signs of partial intestinal obstruction. Imaging highlights two rare digestive malformations: a gastric volvulus and a wandering spleen. The diagnosis can be challenging due to the non-specific nature of the symptoms in children but should be made early in order to avoid life-threatening complications.

articles.title: The Utility of systemic immune-inflammation index and Systemic inflammation response index in differentiating acute appendicitis from other causes of pediatric abdominal pain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The aim of our study is to evaluate the diagnostic value of newly identified inflammatory markers in differentiating acute appendicitis from other abdominal pain causes in pediatric patients.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included pediatric patients under 18 presenting to the emergency department with abdominal pain between January 2020 and August 2024. Patients were categorized into two groups: acute appendicitis (Group 2) and non-appendicitis-related abdominal pain (Group 1). Demographic data, clinical presentation, and inflammatory markers such as neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), pan-immune inflammation value (PIV), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), were recorded for analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 135 patients were included in this study (group 1: 100, group 2: 35). Group 2 had a significantly higher mean age (10.5 ± 4.5 vs. 7.6 ± 3.6 years, p < 0.001). Inflammatory indices were significantly elevated in Group 2 compared to Group 1, including median NLR (5.18 vs. 1.78, p < 0.001), PIV (1232 vs. 353, p = 0.001), SII (1743 vs. 528, p < 0.001), and SIRI (4.41 vs. 1.09, p < 0.001). For diagnosis, SIRI (cut-off > 2.56) demonstrated 80% sensitivity, 71% specificity, and an AUC of 0.772, while NLR (> 4) showed 69% sensitivity and 79% specificity. In multivariate logistic regression analysis, only Age > 11 years (OR = 5.45, 95% CI: 1.9-15.5, p = 0.001) and SIRI > 2.56 (OR = 10.8, 95% CI: 1.5-76.5, p = 0.017) remained as significant independent predictors for acute appendicitis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These markers, combined with clinical findings, can significantly enhance early diagnostic triage in the emergency department. Specifically, the high negative predictive value of SIRI suggests a strong rule-out utility, supporting safe and effective clinical decision-making regardless of whether the subsequent treatment pathway is operative or non-operative.

articles.title: Intervention-driven reduction in potentially inappropriate medication use amongst older adults in long-term care facilities in South Korea.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Polypharmacy and potentially inappropriate medication (PIM) use are common in long-term care facilities (LTCFs) and are associated with adverse outcomes; evidence from Asian settings is limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the effect of a multidisciplinary medication management programme on medication and PIM use and on serious adverse events (SAEs).

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Cluster randomised controlled trial in 28 LTCFs (16 intervention, 12 control).

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: LTCFs in the Seoul metropolitan area, South Korea.

abstract.label: SUBJECTS
abstract.text: 1672 residents aged ≥65 years (836 per group).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Intervention facilities delivered comprehensive medication review, deprescribing recommendations and multidisciplinary case conferences; control facilities provided usual care. Assessments were made at baseline and at 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 months. The number of PIMs and PIM user status were the primary outcomes; SAEs (falls, emergency department [ED] visits and hospitalisations) were pre-specified but not powered for. Medication outcomes were analysed with generalised linear mixed models and SAEs with Fine-Grey competing-risk models, both accounting for facility-level clustering and adjusted for 10 baseline covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Over 15 months, medication and PIM counts increased in the control but not the intervention group (time-by-group incidence rate ratio 0.993, 95% CI 0.990-0.996, P < .001, and .990, 0.983-0.997, P = .004). PIM users fell from 65.8% to 62.5% in the intervention arm and rose from 72.5% to 75.5% in the control arm (OR 0.981, 0.962-0.999, P = .043; not significant in the per-protocol analysis). ED visits or hospitalisations were less frequent in the intervention arm (27.6% vs 32.3%) but the difference was not significant (subdistribution hazard ratio 0.740, 0.493-1.112, P = .147); falls did not differ (P = .762).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A multidisciplinary medication management programme was associated with reduced medication and PIM use. ED visits and hospitalisations were less frequent in the intervention arm, but not significantly so after accounting for facility-level clustering; the trial was not powered for these events and confirmation is needed.

articles.title: Within-season recurrent sport-related concussions prolong return-to-play timeline in professional collision sport athletes.
articles.journal_full: Journal of science and medicine in sport

abstract.text: Return-to-play (RTPg) timelines were examined in professional Australian rules football and rugby league athletes following sport-related concussion (SRCh) during the 2024 season. Among 24 SRC cases, no significant differences in RTP duration were found between athletes with or without prior SRC history. However, a second SRC within the same season was associated with a substantially longer RTP duration. These findings highlight the importance of cautious, individualised RTP decision-making following repeat concussions, particularly in contact and collision sports.

articles.title: Improving the safety and efficacy of whole blood resuscitation from hemorrhagic shock with a novel scavenger protein cocktail.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hemorrhagic shock is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in trauma and surgery. Although blood component therapy is the standard of care, whole blood (WB) transfusion is becoming more popular as it may provide volumetric, hemostatic, and O2-carrying capacity benefits. It is unclear if stored WB is more susceptible to hemolysis than blood components.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study evaluates a novel experimental scavenger protein cocktail (PC) designed to bind hemoglobin, heme, and iron, mitigating toxicity from acellular hemolytic byproducts and enhancing the safety profile of stored WB.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adult male Golden Syrian hamsters outfitted with a dorsal window chamber were subjected to hemorrhage, kept in hypovolemic shock for 30 min, and resuscitated via transfusion of stored WB with low, moderate, or severe hemolysis, or each stored WB group pretreated with PC.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Stored WB hemolysis showed a significant negative correlation with hematocrit, microvascular flow, and functional capillary density at 30 and 60 min post-transfusion. Stored WB hemolysis showed a significant positive correlation with markers of cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic injury, as well as blood lactate accumulation at 60 min. Pre-treating stored WB with PC mitigated functional capillary collapse and tissue injury in moderate- and high-hemolysis WB groups. The PC's oncotic effects produced hemodilution, and there was no significant recovery of hematocrit, pH, or lactate levels to baseline in the WB + PC groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings suggest that hemolysis in stored WB determines resuscitation outcomes, and optimizing PC additive dosing can improve the safety and efficacy of WB transfusion.

articles.title: Vascular and Extremity Injuries in Disasters.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Disasters and mass casualty incidents generate extremity and vascular injury patterns distinct from routine civilian trauma. Blast injuries produce extremity vascular injury rates of 8.6% to 10%, earthquakes generate crush syndrome in up to 25% of victims with lower extremity involvement in 74% to 82% of cases, and mass shootings demonstrate vascular injury rates of 8% to 29%. This review examines the unique mechanisms and epidemiology of extremity injuries in these disaster scenarios and provides evidence-based management strategies including tourniquet application, temporary vascular shunts, damage control orthopedics, fasciotomy timing, and amputation decision-making.

articles.title: Sex differences in bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation and survival to hospital discharge for public out-of-hospital cardiac arrests in North Carolina and Singapore: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Women are less likely to receive bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in public. The study aims to assess if sex in patients with public out-of-hospital cardiac arrests (OHCAs), was associated with bystander CPR and survival to hospital discharge, in North Carolina and Singapore.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult (≥18 years) OHCAs of the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (North Carolina, 2013-2022) and the Pan-Asian Resuscitation Outcomes Study (Singapore, 2010-2020). Using multivariable logistic regression, we examined the association of sex with bystander CPR and survival to hospital discharge adjusting for potential confounding variables (e.g. age, year of arrest).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We analyzed data from 6828 OHCAs in North Carolina and 3617 OHCAs in Singapore. Public bystander CPR rates were 48% for males and 44% for females in North Carolina [adjusted odd ratio (aOR) 0.87; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.77, 0.99], and 59% for males and 52% for females in Singapore [aOR 0.78; 95% CI (0.62, 0.98)]. The proportion surviving to hospital discharge in North Carolina were 24% for males and 26% for females [aOR 1.15; 95% CI (1.00, 1.33)], and 12% for males and 9% for females in Singapore [aOR 0.63; 95% CI (0.43, 0.93)].

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Females were less likely to receive bystander CPR than males in public in both North Carolina and Singapore, irrespective of age. However, females were less likely to survive to hospital discharge compared to males in Singapore, whereas the opposite was seen in North Carolina.

articles.title: Beyond the Initial Impression: Diagnostic Anchoring in an Elderly Patient With Metastatic Gallbladder Cancer.

abstract.text: Persistent nonspecific symptoms in older adults can be diagnostically challenging, particularly when a plausible pre-existing diagnosis provides a satisfactory explanation. We report the case of a 72-year-old woman with a three-month history of chronic fatigue occurring in the context of a persistent ear infection and known cholesteatoma awaiting surgery. Her fatigue had previously been attributed to the otologic condition during repeated primary care consultations. She subsequently presented to the emergency department with worsening fatigue and five days of bilateral lower limb swelling and was found to have tachycardia, with a heart rate of 129 beats/minute, blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg, temperature of 37.3°C, and oxygen saturation of 95% on air. Given the physiological abnormalities and inflammatory response, an initial working diagnosis of infection/sepsis was considered, and antimicrobial treatment was commenced. Development of dyspnea and reduced right basal air entry prompted chest radiography, which demonstrated a right-sided pleural effusion. Congestive cardiac failure was initially considered; however, the reported N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) level was not supportive of heart failure. Further laboratory evaluation demonstrated an alkaline phosphatase of 307 U/L, bilirubin of 21 micromol/L, and albumin of 31 g/L. These findings, combined with persistent fatigue and a new pleural effusion, prompted diagnostic re-evaluation. Urgent computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis demonstrated extensive ill-defined liver lesions and abnormal gallbladder findings concerning for metastatic malignancy. Hepatopancreatobiliary multidisciplinary team review subsequently determined the disease to represent an unresectable gallbladder primary with metastatic involvement, and management was redirected toward palliative and supportive care. This case highlights the hazards of anchoring bias and premature closure when chronic symptoms are attributed to an established diagnosis. Persistent fatigue should remain an active clinical problem rather than being retrospectively incorporated into a pre-existing diagnosis without reassessment. In older adults, abnormal liver blood tests and an unexplained pleural effusion should prompt reconsideration of occult malignancy, particularly when the overall clinical trajectory is discordant with the initial diagnosis.

articles.title: Ethics in Disaster Management.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: In disaster medicine, the traditional pillars of bioethics, namely beneficence, nonmaleficence, autonomy, and justice can be strained. As medical resources are exhausted, providers often pivot from individual-focused care toward a utilitarian framework aimed at maximizing collective survival. This shift introduces complex challenges, including the moral burden of triage, the duty of providers to remain at their posts despite personal risk, and the necessity of grappling with socioeconomic inequities. Ultimately, an effective ethical disaster response requires protocols that preserve the humanity of both patients and providers while functioning within operational realities.

articles.title: Impact of an electronic health record visual cue on time to analgesia in patients with sickle cell in vaso-occlusive crisis.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Management of painful vaso-occlusive crises (VOC), a hallmark of sickle cell disease (SCD), is a critical responsibility of emergency physicians (EPs). However, timely administration of opioid analgesia remains below the American Society of Hematology (ASH) 2020 guideline target.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Our team implemented a technology-based intervention using a salmon-colored visual signal in the Electronic Health Record (EHR) to easily identify ED patients with SCD and prompt clinicians to prioritize patients with VOC. The study examined whether the intervention improved time to opioid administration for SCD VOC in a large urban academic ED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective pre-post intervention study used EHR data for adult ED encounters with a diagnosis of SCD VOC over one year. The primary predictor was pre-intervention and post-intervention visits. Mixed-effects models examined associations between clinical outcomes and the primary predictor while accounting for repeated visits for VOC by the same patient. The primary outcome was mean time from ED arrival to first opioid administration. Secondary outcome was whether patients received the opioid within 60 min of ED arrival. A sensitivity analysis excluded high ED utilizers at various thresholds; more than 5, 10, 24, and 29 ED visits for SCD VOC.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 841 ED encounters from 168 patients, mean time to first opioid was 66.3 min pre-intervention and 71.7 min post-intervention. Adjusted models indicated that time to first opioid administration was 2.50 min longer post-intervention (95% CI: -4.16 to 9.15). The odds of receiving first opioids within 60 min did not differ between intervention periods (aOR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.71 to 1.32, absolute difference = 1.7, 95% CI: -5.1 to 8.4). Sensitivity analyses excluding high ED utilizers at four thresholds showed consistent results with primary analysis: 5-visit threshold (247 visits, adjusted difference = 3.4 min, 95% CI: -16.1 to 23); 10-visit threshold (377 visits, adjusted difference = 1.2 min, 95% CI: -11.6 to 14); 24-visit threshold (514 visits, adjusted difference = 4 min, 95% CI: -7.0 to 15.1); 29-visit threshold (572 visits, adjusted difference = 3.5 min, 95% CI: -6.4 to 13.3). None of these results reached statistical significance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings suggest that passive EHR visual signals alone are insufficient to reduce analgesia delays in VOC, and that meaningful improvement will likely require multi-component, systems-based interventions integrating workflow redesign, nurse-initiated protocols, and automated clinical decision support.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes Associated With Intravenous Fluid Shortages in Emergency Department Patients: A Propensity Score Matched Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intravenous (IV) saline is critical for emergency department (ED) care, supporting resuscitation, rehydration, and electrolyte correction. National IV fluid shortages, including the shortage following Hurricane Helene in September 2024, may disrupt timely care, yet large-scale evidence on associated clinical outcomes is limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective observational cohort study using the TriNetX global federated electronic health record network, adult ED patients aged 18-65 years presenting during a nationwide IV fluid shortage (October 2024-May 2025) were compared with those presenting during a prior period of adequate supply. Cohorts were propensity score matched on demographics and comorbidities. Time-to-event outcomes within 7 days were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After matching, 2,767,318 patients were included in each cohort. Compared with the non-shortage period, ED visits during the shortage were associated with small but consistent increases in rates of sepsis (HR 1.066), gastroenteritis (HR 1.151), acute kidney failure (HR 1.006), and hyponatremia (HR 1.074). Fluid administration was reduced (HR 0.869), consistent with expectations during the shortage period. Hospitalization (HR 1.06) was more frequent, while mortality did not differ.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nationwide IV fluid shortages were associated with mild increases in acute complications and healthcare utilization among ED patients without increased short-term mortality. These findings underscore the need for preparedness strategies to mitigate the clinical impact of future IV fluid supply disruptions. Effect sizes were modest, and while statistically significant, they likely represent small individual level clinical differences. Given the large number of ED encounters affected, these patterns may reflect broader health-system strain during the nationwide shortage.

articles.title: Frailty is associated with longer time to hemorrhage-control surgery after trauma.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Frailty is associated with adverse outcomes after trauma, but whether it is associated with the timeliness of operative hemorrhage control is unknown. We evaluated the association between frailty and time to initiation of hemorrhage-control surgery after traumatic injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the 2023-2024 American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Participant Use Files. Adults undergoing hemorrhage-control surgery within 24 hours of arrival were included. Frailty was defined using the 5-factor modified frailty index, with a 5-factor modified frailty index ≥0.40 classified as frail. The primary outcome was time from hospital arrival to hemorrhage-control surgery initiation. Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood regression with robust standard errors was used to estimate adjusted mean time ratios, with age modeled using restricted cubic splines. Prespecified explanatory and sensitivity analyses evaluated physiologic urgency, preoperative computed tomography, age overlap, injury severity, procedure type, and extreme hemorrhage-control surgery times.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 29,762 patients, 1,804 (6.1%) were frail. Median hemorrhage-control surgery initiation time was 94.2 minutes (interquartile range, 46.2-190.8) in frail patients and 61.8 minutes (interquartile range, 34.2-126.0) in nonfrail patients (P < .001). After adjustment, frailty was associated with longer mean hemorrhage-control surgery initiation time (adjusted mean time ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.02-1.17; P = .007). Standardized adjusted mean times were 132.6 minutes for frail patients and 121.3 minutes for nonfrail patients, an adjusted difference of 11.3 minutes (95% confidence interval, 2.8-19.9). The association persisted after adjustment for physiologic urgency and preoperative computed tomography (adjusted mean time ratio, 1.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.02-1.16) and in age-restricted, blunt-trauma, direct emergency department-to-operating room, ≤360-minute, and median-regression analyses, although estimates were attenuated in Injury Severity Score ≥16 and laparotomy/pelvic-packing-only subgroups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Frailty was independently associated with a longer time to hemorrhage-control surgery initiation after trauma, beyond chronological age and measured clinical characteristics. These findings identify frailty as a marker associated with the pathway to operative hemorrhage control but should not be interpreted as evidence of inappropriate delay or a causal effect of frailty on care.

articles.title: [Delayed diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome in a patient with psychiatric illness].

abstract.text: In this case report, a 24-year-old woman diagnosed with psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, OCD and presumably a schizotypical disorder presented with symptoms of Guillain-Barré syndrome. The patient had a history of somatisation, which is why her symptoms were initially overlooked. After several contacts to the emergency department, the patient was hospitalised after finding bilateral lung embolisms. The patient deteriorated quickly and suffered shortly from hypoxic cardiac arrest. Whilst she was in the ICU, she was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome.

articles.title: Common Inpatient Procedures-Urinary Catheter Insertion and Intra-abdominal Pressure Measurement.
articles.journal_full: The Medical clinics of North America

abstract.text: This review provides a comprehensive guide to indwelling urinary catheterization and transvesicular intra-abdominal pressure measurement. It details essential anatomy, evidence-based insertion techniques for male and female patients, and the appropriate selection of catheter to minimize complications such as catheter-associated urinary tract infection and trauma. Furthermore, it highlights the integration of point-of-care ultrasound for troubleshooting and bladder volume assessment. By standardizing procedural steps and providing mitigation strategies for high-risk patients, this article aims to improve procedural success and enhance patient safety.

articles.title: Nerve Blocks.
articles.journal_full: The Medical clinics of North America

abstract.text: This article provides a clinical framework for implementing point-of-care blocks, distinguishing between precision-target and volume-dependent planar techniques for conditions like hip fractures and thoracic trauma. By focusing on sonographic anatomy, procedural ergonomics, and standardized safety protocols, the text outlines strategies to mitigate risks like Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity. Integrating New York School of Regional Anesthesia-standardized methodologies, the article emphasizes improving functional recovery through anatomy-driven, opioid-sparing interventions.

articles.title: Paracentesis.
articles.journal_full: The Medical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Abdominal paracentesis is a fundamental procedure for diagnosing ascitic etiologies and providing therapeutic relief for symptomatic tense ascites. The application of point-of-care ultrasound is the standard of care and enhances procedural success and minimizes complications such as hemorrhage or bowel perforation. While there are guidelines to help optimize bleeding diathesis, the clinician must perform an individual risk assessment and exercise sound clinical judgment to determine the optimal procedure approach to minimize bleeding complications. For large-volume paracentesis exceeding 5 L, albumin replacement (6-8 g per liter removed) is essential to mitigate postparacentesis circulatory dysfunction and acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Disaster Management and National Incident Management System.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Disasters overwhelm community and health care resources and are increasing in frequency and complexity. General surgeons play a critical role in disaster response, providing life-saving surgical care, participating in triage, and allocating scarce resources. Disaster management follows a continuous cycle of mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery, with health care systems emphasizing risk assessment, training, and surge planning. Effective response requires coordinated communication and resource management. The National Incident Management System provides a standardized framework for multiagency disaster response, incorporating the Incident Command System, Emergency Operations Centers, and coordinated communication structures to ensure organized, efficient, and scalable management.

articles.title: Improving Access to Specialty Care: Analysis of Factors Affecting Follow-up Patterns in an Outpatient Academic Pulmonary Clinic.

abstract.text: Prolonged wait times for appointments in pulmonary specialty clinics contribute to worse patient outcomes. We determined the follow-up patterns and factors associated with appointment no-show to identify opportunities to increase appointment availability while improving follow-up. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of patients scheduled from 2017-2019 in the outpatient pulmonary fellows' clinic of an academic tertiary care hospital. A successful visit was an appointment documented as completed. Appointment-level associations with no-show were evaluated using multivariable logistic generalized estimating equations. Among 1,612 patients, 4,689 appointments were scheduled. After excluding 1,247 cancellations and 6 appointments with indeterminate disposition, 3,436 appointments among 1,479 patients were included in the no-show analysis; 1,461 (42.5%) were no-shows. Average intended and actual follow-up intervals were 11.2 weeks and 24.8 weeks, respectively. In the complete-case adjusted analysis (3,427 appointments among 1,470 patients), substance use disorders (adjusted odds ratios [aORs], 1.86-3.43; P≤.011), inpatient referral (aOR, 2.41; P<.001), and pneumonia (aOR, 2.63; P=.046) were associated with greater odds of no-show. Spanish language (aOR, 0.59; P<.001), charity care (aOR, 0.63; P=.002), and external outpatient referral (aOR, 0.49; P<.001) were associated with lower odds. Emergency department referral and driving distance were not independently associated with no-show. Our clinic had short intended follow-up intervals and a high no-show rate. These appointment-level associations may inform continuity-focused scheduling and targeted attendance support. Standardizing follow-up intervals and using prediction-based overbooking should be prospectively evaluated for effects on access, workflow, and patient experience.

articles.title: Central Venous Access.
articles.journal_full: The Medical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Central venous catheterization (CVC) is a commonly performed procedure in which an indwelling catheter is placed within a central vein to facilitate administration of vasoactive medications, chemotherapy, parenteral nutrition, and extracorporeal therapies, as well as hemodynamic monitoring. This article reviews the indications and contraindications for CVC placement, bleeding risk considerations, and factors influencing site selection. Methods for confirming catheter position, including sonographic and radiographic approaches, are discussed. Mechanical, thrombotic, and infectious complications are reviewed, along with strategies for prevention and postprocedural monitoring. Common technical and sonographic pitfalls encountered during CVC placement are also highlighted.

articles.title: Saved by Bell's Palsy: Recurrent Facial Weakness in a Patient With a Cerebellopontine Angle Mass.

abstract.text: Bell's palsy is a common cause of acute unilateral facial weakness, but recurrent symptoms or additional neurologic findings should prompt evaluation for another cause. A 59-year-old woman with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes mellitus and cirrhosis presented to the emergency department with posterior headache, recurrent right facial weakness and numbness, and vertigo that started the previous night. She had a previous episode of similar facial weakness that was initially diagnosed as Bell's palsy. Subsequent evaluation identified a right cerebellopontine angle mass, and she was followed by neurology but was later lost to follow-up for approximately three years. Examination demonstrated right-sided facial weakness involving both the upper and lower face, with frontalis weakness, lagophthalmos, flattening of the right nasolabial fold, decreased sensation over the right cheek and perioral region, and right-sided dysmetria on finger-to-nose testing. Gait was normal. Strength and sensation were normal in the bilateral upper and lower extremities, and biceps and patellar reflexes were normal and symmetric. Computed tomography of the head showed a 2.0 cm right cerebellopontine angle mass. A previous magnetic resonance imaging study from 2023 showed the same lesion measuring 1.6 cm and was interpreted as consistent with a meningioma. Because the measurements were obtained using different imaging modalities, the apparent increase in size was interpreted cautiously. Serum glucose was 508 mg/dL; however, a serum bicarbonate of 24 mmol/L, an anion gap of 10 mmol/L, and absence of ketonuria did not support diabetic ketoacidosis. She received intravenous fluids and 10 units of regular insulin, after which point-of-care glucose decreased to 347 mg/dL. Although she did not require emergent neurosurgical intervention, a neurosurgeon at a tertiary center recommended urgent transfer because neurosurgical services were not available locally. The available imaging did not establish a direct causal relationship between the mass and the facial weakness. Recurrent facial palsy with sensory symptoms, asymmetric hearing findings, vertigo, headache, or cerebellar findings should not be assumed to represent another episode of idiopathic Bell's palsy.

articles.title: Beyond Respiratory Failure: Unmasking Myasthenic Crisis in the Emergency Department.

abstract.text: Myasthenic crisis is a life-threatening complication of myasthenia gravis (MG), typically presenting in patients with a known diagnosis. However, the absence of collateral history can delay recognition when respiratory failure is the initial manifestation. We report a 34-year-old male patient who presented to the emergency department with acute respiratory failure. Initial evaluation suggested airway compromise, but standard pulmonary, cardiac, and airway investigations were unrevealing. During hospitalization, he developed progressive bulbar and limb weakness, and a collateral history later revealed a prior diagnosis of MG treated with pyridostigmine. He required multiple intubations due to fluctuating muscle weakness and repeated extubation failures. The patient was treated with serial plasma exchange and corticosteroids, eventually stabilizing with a tracheostomy for prolonged ventilatory support. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of myasthenic crisis when collateral history is unavailable. Repeated extubation failures underscore the importance of careful assessment of bulbar and respiratory muscle function. Early, targeted interventions such as plasma exchange and corticosteroids are crucial to improving outcomes. Acute respiratory failure may be the initial presentation of myasthenic crisis. Prompt recognition, vigilant airway management, and early disease-specific therapy are essential for optimal patient outcomes.

articles.title: Head Impacts in Long-Term Care Falls Are Common but Often Underrecognized: A Video-Based Analysis of Injury and Transport.

abstract.text: Falls are the leading cause of injury-related morbidity and mortality among older adults, particularly in long-term care (LTC) facilities. Although head impacts are common during falls, the relationship between impact occurrence, injury characteristics, and hospital transport remains inadequately defined. The objectives of this study were to (1) compare falls with and without head impact, (2) quantify unrecognized head impacts and their contexts, (3) examine factors associated with head injury occurrence, and (4) identify predictors of hospital transport following head impacts. This secondary analysis used an open-source video dataset from two LTC facilities. Three raters reviewed each of the 300 fall videos to determine the presence of head impact. Transport and injury data were extracted directly from the open-source, observational video dataset. Falls were characterized using the Fall Video Analysis Questionnaire. Generalized estimating equations evaluated predictors of head injury, and logistic regression modeled predictors of hospital transport. Head impacts were common yet often underrecognized when relying on reported or visible injuries. Many falls without documented head injury demonstrated clear head impact on video, indicating that visible injury is a poor proxy for impact. Hospital transport following head impact was uncommon and was primarily associated with visible injuries rather than patient characteristics or fall history. Most head impacts, including those without obvious injury, did not result in transport. These findings suggest that reliance on external injury may lead to underrecognition and potential under-triage of head trauma. Improved detection strategies beyond visible injury are needed to better identify clinically significant head impacts.

articles.title: Intrathecal hyperbaric versus isobaric bupivacaine for caesarean delivery: A meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Intrathecal bupivacaine facilitates caesarean delivery and is available in two forms: isobaric or hyperbaric with differing pharmacokinetic profiles. This meta-analysis primarily aimed to compare the incidence of hypotension (defined as a drop ≥20% from baseline systolic or mean arterial pressure) when used in caesarean delivery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intrathecal isobaric and hyperbaric bupivacaine for caesarean delivery were identified from MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and Cochrane databases. Secondary outcomes included incidence of ephedrine use, nausea/vomiting, bradycardia, maximum block height, time to maximum block height, and offset of block. Jadad scores evaluated the trials' quality. RevMan statistical software® calculated the standardised mean difference with 95% confidence intervals for continuous variables. The Mantel-Haenszel test and a random effect model were used to calculate the odds ratio for dichotomous variables. Included articles were assessed for risk of bias and consistency with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation guidelines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nineteen articles with 1501 patients were analysed with 722 patients receiving isobaric bupivacaine versus 779 receiving hyperbaric bupivacaine. There was no significant difference in the rates of hypotension [odds ratio (OR) 1.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.63 to 2.46] or incidence of ephedrine use (OR 1.44, 95% CI 0.75 to 2.77). There was a faster onset of motor block with hyperbaric bupivacaine (standardised mean difference -0.46, 95% CI -0.86 to -0.05) but no other differences in secondary outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Despite differences between isobaric and hyperbaric bupivacaine, neither caused a significantly higher incidence of hypotension. Both produce similar clinical profiles except for onset of motor block. High levels of heterogeneity between the studies indicate the need for focused RCTs on this topic.

articles.title: ROX vs. HACOR: early prediction of HFNC failure in ICU patients admitted from the emergency department with lung cancer-related hypoxemia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Delayed intubation in lung cancer patients receiving high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is associated with increased mortality. Reliable bedside tools are essential for early risk stratification. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of the ROX index and HACOR score for the early identification of HFNC failure in this high-risk population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included 176 ICU patients with lung cancer and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure who received HFNC. Time-point analyses of the ROX index and HACOR score at 1 and 3 h were restricted to patients with complete physiological data at both time points (n = 88). The primary outcome was clinician-determined HFNC failure, defined as endotracheal intubation within 48 h after HFNC initiation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: HFNC failure occurred in 50 of 176 patients (28.4%) in the overall cohort and in 39 of 88 patients (44.3%) in the complete-case analytical cohort. Patients who required endotracheal intubation exhibited higher baseline illness severity (SOFA and APACHE II) and persistent tachypnea. At the 3-hour assessment, the ROX index showed higher observed discrimination than the HACOR score (AUROC 0.860 [95% CI 0.760-0.960] vs. 0.740 [95% CI 0.590-0.890]). Only the prespecified 1- and 3-hour time points were evaluated; therefore, these findings do not establish 3 h as the optimal assessment time. In an exploratory analysis in which the threshold was derived and evaluated in the same analytical cohort, a 3-hour ROX value ≤ 5.1 identified patients at higher risk of HFNC failure; this threshold has not been independently validated. Respiratory rate alone also showed high prognostic value at 3 h (AUROC 0.850 [95% CI 0.730-0.970]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Within the complete-case cohort, which represented half of the overall population, the 3-hour ROX index showed higher observed discrimination for clinician-determined HFNC failure than HACOR. However, selection and incorporation bias may have affected this comparison. The data-derived threshold should not be used as a stand-alone intubation criterion and requires prospective validation using standardized serial measurements and independently adjudicated outcomes.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not applicable; this was a retrospective observational study.

articles.title: Thoracoabdominal Trauma in Disaster.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Disasters and mass casualty incidents overwhelm resources and force deviations from conventional care. Thoracoabdominal trauma involves 2 unforgiving compartments in which exsanguination, tension physiology, tamponade, and contamination are rapidly lethal. This article reviews the operational management of thoracic and abdominal injury when volume, personnel, and blood products are constrained. Topics include rapid recognition and decompression of tension pneumothorax, massive hemothorax, and cardiac tamponade; indications for damage control thoracic surgery, thoracic packing, temporary closure, and vascular shunting; hemorrhage and contamination control by retroperitoneal zone; and temporary abdominal closure options. Emphasis is placed on triage, resource stewardship, and deferring definitive reconstruction.

articles.title: Prehospital Triage and Transport During Mass Casualty Incidents and Disasters.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: This article outlines a systems based approach to the EMS management of mass casualty incidents, emphasizing early recognition, escalation of resources, and coordinated communication. The article promotes Sort, Assess, Life-saving interventions, Treatment/Transport as the Model Uniform Core Criteria-compliant national triage standard, highlighting dynamic primary, secondary, and tertiary triage with ongoing retriage to minimize overtriage. It details the use of Casualty Collection Points and Ambulance Exchange Points, and underscores Incident Command System-structured, triage-driven transport led by a designated transport officer.

articles.title: Care of Special Populations in Disasters.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Disasters and mass casualty incidents disproportionately harm elderly, pediatric, and pregnant patients, yet most triage algorithms and preparedness plans are built around the healthy adult. This review examines the physiologic, anatomic, and social characteristics that make each population vulnerable, drawing on experience from Hurricane Katrina and contemporary armed conflict. For older adults, frailty, rather than chronologic age, drives outcomes, and polypharmacy complicates resuscitation. Children require age-adjusted triage, weight-based dosing, and protection from family separation. Pregnant patients require simultaneous maternal and fetal assessment, as the physiologic adaptations of pregnancy mask hemorrhage. Systems-level preparedness remains the strongest determinant of outcome.

articles.title: An evaluation of a newly implemented stroke team activation protocol in Manitoba.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: The purpose of this study was to evaluate a revised stroke 25 protocol in Manitoba, which integrated Stroke Team Activation by the Virtual Emergency Care and Transfer Resource Service (VECTRS), and to determine whether its implementation reduced time to acute stroke treatment compared to the previous protocol.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective chart review utilized Emergency Medical Services (EMS) data from the Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service (WFPS) and hospital electronic medical records from the Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre (HSC), comparing 12 months before and 12 months after implementation of the revised Stroke 25 protocol. For each patient, the interval from EMS arrival at HSC to initiation of acute stroke treatment was calculated. Mean times to thrombolysis and EVT were compared between pre- and post-implementation cohorts.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the pre-intervention cohort, 757 patients with suspected stroke were triaged to HSC, of whom 131 received Alteplase or Tenecteplase (TNK) and 33 underwent EVT. In the post- intervention group, 717 patients were triaged, with 110 receiving Alteplase/TNK and 30 undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Mean time to thrombolysis decreased from 59.1 min pre- intervention to 52.8 min post- intervention, while mean time to EVT decreased from 92.2 min to 84.1 min, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Implementation of the revised Stroke 25 protocol was associated with modest reductions in absolute time to treatment for patients with acute ischemic stroke; however, while these differences were not statistically significant, the impact for these patients may still be clinically significant.

articles.title: Quality of life and musculoskeletal function among small-scale fishers in Yucatán, Mexico: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal_full: Revista brasileira de medicina do trabalho : publicacao oficial da Associacao Nacional de Medicina do Trabalho-ANAMT

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Small-scale fishers face occupational hazards and physical demands that may affect musculoskeletal health and quality of life.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To assess health-related quality of life, low-back disability, and upper-limb disability among small-scale fishers from two coastal communities in Yucatán, Mexico.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study included a convenience sample of 55 artisanal fishers. Health-related quality of life, low-back disability, and upper-limb disability were assessed using SF-36, Oswestry Disability Index, and QuickDASH, respectively. Shoulder range of motion and handgrip strength were also measured. Descriptive analyses and exploratory comparisons (by community and by diving status) were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median age was 33 years; 94.5% were men. The lowest SF-36 scores occurred in the role-physical (50), general-health-perception (62), and role-emotional (66.6) domains, whereas social functioning scored highest (87.5). Among 17 participants reporting low-back pain, 14 (82.4%) had minimal disability. The median QuickDASH score was 11.4. Mental health scores were higher in Rio Lagartos than in San Felipe (88 vs. 72; p=0.042); other SF-36 domains did not differ by community. No significant differences in SF-36 domains or QuickDASH scores were detected by diving status, although only seven participants were non-divers. Among divers, SF-36 domain scores did not differ significantly by self-reported episodes consistent with decompression sickness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The lowest median SF-36 scores were observed in physical and emotional role limitations and general health perceptions, whereas social functioning had the highest median score. Low-back disability was predominantly minimal, and upper-limb disability was low. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger, representative studies.

articles.title: A descriptive analysis of Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act cases involving disruptive patient behavior, 2023.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) requires emergency departments (EDs) to provide a medical screening examination (MSE) and stabilizing care regardless of ability to pay. While EMTALA protects access to care, its application can be challenging when patients are disruptive or violent. This study estimates the proportion of EMTALA citations for MSE deficiencies involving disruptive behavior and describes case characteristics.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, descriptive analysis of Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) EMTALA citations for MSE deficiencies from 2023. We screened narrative inspection texts using predefined keywords, then manually reviewed them to identify disruptive behavior and assess whether it appeared willful. Case characteristics were recorded and described.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 227 EMTALA citations involving MSE deficiencies with narrative inspection reports available for review, 49 (21%) were determined to involve disruptive behavior. Common behaviors included verbal abuse, refusal of care, threats, and violence, most often directed at nurses. Ten cases (20%) were considered likely willful; the remainder stemmed from acute psychiatric conditions, intoxication, or medical illness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Disruptive behaviors appear in a notable proportion of EMTALA citations for MSE deficiencies, highlighting the challenge of balancing regulatory compliance with staff safety and ED operations.

articles.title: Health and Emergency Preparedness for Mass Gatherings at the 2034 FIFA World Cup in Saudi Arabia: A Systematic Review and Targeted Evidence Update.

abstract.text: The Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) World Cups are complex mass gatherings that place simultaneous demands on public-health surveillance, environmental risk management, emergency medical services, crowd safety, and health-system resilience.
