Saudi Arabia's selection to host the 2034 tournament creates an opportunity to adapt capabilities developed through decades of Hajj operations to the very different context of a global football event. This review synthesises evidence from major mass gatherings and incorporates post-Qatar 2022 and World Cup 2026 evidence to define practical priorities for 2034. The original review searched PubMed, the Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for 2000-2025 and retained 43 records according to the documented screening log. A targeted update undertaken in September 2026 searched PubMed/MEDLINE and primary sources from major international, national, and sporting authorities. Because this update was not a complete rerun of the original four-database strategy, newer evidence was synthesised narratively and was not added to the original screening denominator. Post-Qatar studies support dedicated tournament medical services, improved clinician notification, open-source epidemic intelligence, and wastewater surveillance. World Cup 2026 evidence adds cross-jurisdictional dashboards, port-health surveillance, early-warning systems, pathogen-specific risk assessment, and multi-hazard environmental planning. Contemporary Saudi Hajj operations demonstrate large-scale heat prevention, surge care, referral, and emergency logistics. For Saudi Arabia 2034, the evidence favours an all-hazards model built around heat action plans, interoperable multi-layer surveillance, unified incident command, distributed emergency care, crowd-safety intelligence, mental-health pathways, multilingual communication, and predefined post-event evaluation. The central implementation principle is to strengthen routine national systems rather than construct temporary parallel systems for the tournament.

articles.title: Postpartum "Hypercoagulable Storm" With Extensive Iliocaval Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism in a Patient With Heterozygous Factor V Leiden.

abstract.text: A 26-year-old woman presented to the emergency department four weeks after a lower segment cesarean section with a four-day history of progressive dyspnea, bilateral lower limb swelling, and leg pain. At presentation to the emergency department, she was tachycardic (150 beats/min), hypotensive (88/60 mmHg), and tachypneic (38/min), with an oxygen saturation of 93% on room air. Venous Doppler ultrasonography demonstrated extensive bilateral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) involving the iliac veins, right external iliac vein, infrarenal inferior vena cava (IVC), and right popliteal vein, with left popliteal involvement. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography demonstrated acute pulmonary embolism (PE) involving the right pulmonary artery and multiple segmental branches, with right lower lobe pulmonary infarction. Thrombophilia evaluation identified heterozygous Factor V Leiden, with negative antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant and normal protein C, protein S, and antithrombin III levels. The initial presentation raised concern for high-risk acute pulmonary embolism physiology, with hypotension (88/60 mmHg), marked tachycardia, and respiratory compromise requiring high-flow oxygen. Category D1+R was considered provisionally; however, definitive classification was limited by the absence of documented hypotension duration and fluid responsiveness, lactate, echocardiographic right ventricular assessment, and computed tomography (CT) right ventricular (RV)/left ventricular (LV) ratio. A Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) was activated, and intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) was initiated. A retrievable suprarenal IVC filter was placed, followed by mechanical thrombectomy extending from the right popliteal vein to the IVC. At three months, the patient remained ambulatory without exertional dyspnea, and bilateral lower limb swelling had completely resolved. Repeat venous Doppler demonstrated recanalization of the previously thrombosed segments without significant residual occlusive thrombus. This case is presented because of the uncommon combination of extensive bilateral lower limb and iliocaval thrombosis with acute PE and pulmonary infarction in the early postpartum period in a patient with heterozygous Factor V Leiden. It highlights how postpartum hypercoagulability may interact with inherited thrombophilia to produce extensive multisite thrombosis and emphasizes the importance of early recognition, severity-based risk stratification, and coordinated multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Detection of Acute Myocardial Dysfunction Following Bupropion Overdose: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Bupropion overdose is associated with significant morbidity and mortality due to severe neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, including seizures and life-threatening arrhythmias. Early recognition of electrocardiographic, clinical, and echocardiographic abnormalities is critical for prompt intervention and prevention of clinical deterioration. We present a case of a 21-year-old female who presented to the emergency department following an intentional polysubstance overdose involving suspected bupropion ingestion. The initial electrocardiogram (EKG) demonstrated sinus tachycardia. However, during continued monitoring, the patient developed QRS widening and seizures. Treatment included benzodiazepines, calcium, and sodium bicarbonate. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) revealed a reduced ejection fraction (EF) of less than 30%, which was later confirmed on formal transthoracic echocardiography. These findings prompted escalation of care, intubation for airway protection and deep sedation, and transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU). During admission, she developed torsades de pointes (TdP), resulting in cardiac arrest. Despite her critical presentation, repeat echocardiography upon resolution of overdose toxicity demonstrated recovery of left ventricular systolic function, with improvement of EF to 50-55% during hospitalization. This case demonstrates the potential role of POCUS in the early recognition of myocardial dysfunction associated with bupropion toxicity. Together with serial EKG monitoring, these findings identified a patient at high risk for clinical deterioration and supported early escalation of care.

articles.title: Clinical and laboratory characteristics associated with in-hospital mortality in methanol poisoning: A 5-year retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare the demographic, clinical, and laboratory characteristics of survivors and non-survivors presenting to the emergency department with methanol poisoning and to identify variables associated with in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective observational cohort study included all consecutive adults (≥18 years) diagnosed with methanol poisoning at the emergency department of Giresun Training and Research Hospital, Türkiye, between September 01, 2021, and May 01, 2026. Patients were categorized as survivors and non-survivors. Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, laboratory parameters, severity scores (Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS], Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II [APACHE II], and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment [SOFA]), and treatment variables were compared using univariable analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 26 patients were included, and 9 (34.6%) died. At emergency department presentation, loss of consciousness was more frequent among non-survivors (88.9% vs. 11.8%; p<0.001). Non-survivors also had lower GCS scores (median 4 vs. 15; p<0.001) and admission pH (7.00 vs. 7.11; p=0.011), together with higher lactate (7.1 vs. 2.9 mmol/L; p<0.001), creatinine (1.52 vs. 1.00 mg/dL; p=0.001), glucose (194 vs. 123 mg/dL; p=0.029), and anion gap levels (27.0 vs. 20.9 mmol/L; p=0.018). Within the intensive care unit (ICU) subgroup (n=20), ICU non-survivors (n=9) had higher APACHE II and SOFA scores than ICU survivors (n=11) (p=0.002 and p<0.001, respectively). During the subsequent hospital course, all non-survivors required invasive mechanical ventilation compared with none of the survivors (100% vs. 0%; p<0.001); this finding was considered a marker of greater clinical severity rather than a baseline prognostic characteristic.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this small exploratory cohort, non-survivors showed greater neurological impairment and a general pattern of more severe metabolic derangement at emergency department presentation. Within the selected ICU subgroup, ICU non-survivors had higher APACHE II and SOFA scores than ICU survivors. These findings are hypothesis-generating and may help identify clinical features warranting heightened concern; however, they should not be interpreted as validated prognostic criteria or as a risk-stratification tool.

articles.title: [AI-manipulated medical records as part of medical child abuse].

abstract.text: This case report describes a rare case of Medical Child Abuse (MCA) where AI-manipulated videos were used to fabricate seizures. A two-year-old boy was admitted to a pediatric emergency department under suspicion of epilepsy after his mother reported frequent seizures. During a five-day hospitalisation, the mother described two daily seizures, only witnessed by her. To substantiate the seizures, she presented three videos. Normal clinical findings and suspicious video footage led to concerns of MCA. When confronted, the mother admitted using generative AI tools to create the videos.

articles.title: Purple Haze as a Tell-Tale Sign: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Patients with urinary tract infection (UTI) symptoms report dysuria, urinary frequency, fever, and/or urinary urgency. In addition, those with catheter-associated UTIs may have flank pain or suprapubic or costovertebral tenderness. We present a case of a rare physical examination finding that can also aid in the diagnosis of a catheter-associated UTI: purple urine bag syndrome (PUBS). An 84-year-old man with a past medical history of metastatic prostate cancer complicated by a rectourethral fistula, status post ileal conduit and loop colostomy, presented after his daughter noticed what she believed was blood in the overnight drainage bag connected to his ileal conduit. The patient had previously required bilateral percutaneous nephrostomy tubes for malignant extrinsic ureteral compression from progressive prostate cancer, but the right nephrostomy tube had subsequently been removed after identifying that the left-sided obstruction was the culprit. The patient was reporting right-sided abdominal pain and fatigue. On examination, the patient was lethargic and unable to provide a history. Examination revealed dark purple discoloration of the ileal conduit tubing and overnight drainage bag. A Foley catheter placed by the emergency department did not drain urine because of the patient's ileal conduit and was subsequently removed. Urinalysis did not demonstrate hematuria, indicating that the discoloration perceived as blood was the purple hue shown in the clinical photograph. Urine specimens were obtained from the functioning urinary drainage sites, and the culture obtained from the ileal conduit collection bag was positive. The patient was started on ertapenem and daptomycin due to a history of severe sepsis secondary to vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) UTI from his ileal conduit and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing (ESBL) Escherichia coli from his catheter site. CT of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated hydronephrosis of the right kidney with concern for developing pyelonephritis. The right-sided hydronephrosis was attributed to malignant extrinsic ureteral compression from progressive prostate cancer. The urine culture from the ileal conduit collection bag grew Providencia stuartii, Proteus mirabilis, E. coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, all of which were susceptible to meropenem. Due to concern for pyelonephritis and a rise in the patient's creatinine, a right-sided percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube was placed, and the patient's condition improved after a six-day course of meropenem. This case is notable for purple discoloration of the ileal conduit tubing and overnight collection bag, consistent with PUBS. This syndrome is associated with UTIs in elderly people, particularly those who are constipated. The source of the pigment has been attributed to altered tryptophan metabolism related to prolonged intestinal transit time and the production of indole derivatives by bacteria. The tryptophan metabolites produce red and blue pigments that combine to form the purple color seen in PUBS. In this patient, the culture obtained from the ileal conduit collection bag grew predominantly Providencia stuartii and Proteus mirabilis, both of which have been implicated in this syndrome. The patient's right-sided hydronephrosis occurred in the setting of malignant extrinsic ureteral compression from progressive prostate cancer rather than obstruction of the bladder or urethra.

articles.title: Combined arterial and venous reconstruction with Artegraft after common femoral artery and vein ballistic injury.
articles.journal: J Vasc Surg Cases Innov Tech
articles.journal_full: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques

abstract.text: Combined injuries to the common femoral artery and common femoral vein resulting from penetrating trauma are associated with high-mortality rates. In such cases, conduit selection is critical when autologous veins are not available, and time is critical. Bovine carotid artery vascular graft (Artegraft; LeMaitre Vascular, Inc) has demonstrated patency comparable with autologous vein in arterial trauma repair. This report describes a 21-year-old man who sustained a gunshot wound resulting in both common femoral artery and common femoral vein disruption, massive hemorrhage, and cardiac arrest necessitating emergency department thoracotomy with aortic cross-clamping for proximal hemorrhage control. Artegraft was used for both arterial and venous reconstruction. The patient survived and achieved limb salvage with maintained graft patency at 6 weeks.

articles.title: Normative Distal Radius Radiological Measurements: The Influence of Age, Gender, and Menopause.
articles.journal: Clin Med Insights Arthritis Musculoskelet Disord
articles.journal_full: Clinical medicine insights. Arthritis and musculoskeletal disorders

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Distal radius fractures are prevalent, with management dependent on accurate radiological assessment. Most morphologic reference values derive from Western cohorts, raising questions about their generalizability. This study established reference distal radius radiological parameters in the Israeli population derived from emergency department patients with non-fractured wrist injuries and explored the effects of age, gender, and menopause.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review included adults with wrist contusions at an Israeli emergency department. Exclusions were prior fractures, surgery, or poor radiographs. Standardized anteroposterior and lateral wrist radiographs were reviewed for 6 parameters: radial height, inclination, radiocarpal angle, volar angulation, volar tilt, and ulnar variance, measured twice by a blinded observer (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.92-0.98). Stratification by age and gender used 50 years as a menopause proxy. Statistical analysis included t tests (Bonferroni correction, α = 0.010) and effect sizes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 585 patients, 466 met criteria (mean age, 45 years; 40.6% female). Mean values were 13.4 mm for radial height, 25.4° for inclination, 11.6° for radiocarpal angle, 145.1° for volar angulation, and 17.1° for volar tilt. Radial height was significantly greater in males than in females (P < .001). Ulnar variance was neutral in 69.5%, negative in 17.8%, and positive in 12.7%. Volar angulation declined significantly with age in women, especially post-menopause (P < .01), but not in men.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Distal radius morphology in Israelis aligns with international norms. Age-stratified differences in volar angulation among women over 50, which may reflect menopausal bone remodeling, indicate that both age and sex should be incorporated into individualized assessments. In the management of distal radius fractures in postmenopausal women, baseline volar angulation is approximately 3° lower than in younger women, a factor that may influence reduction targets.

articles.title: Pediatric Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor With Extensive Necrosis: A Case Report.

abstract.text: We describe an unusual presentation of a pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). A 17-year-old previously healthy male presented to the emergency department with altered mental status, lethargy, nausea, vomiting, fever, and tachycardia. Head imaging incidentally demonstrated a large expansile sellar/suprasellar cystic and solid mass displacing the optic chiasm, invading bilaterally into the cavernous sinuses, and encasing the internal carotid arteries. He developed decreased vision of the left eye on hospital day two and underwent urgent endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal resection of the mass. Pathology demonstrated a PitNET with extensive necrosis, lactotroph differentiation, and changes suggestive of superimposed tumoral infection. His postoperative course was complicated by panhypopituitarism, chronic diabetes insipidus, and a cerebrospinal fluid leak managed with lumbar drainage. His presenting symptoms resolved completely, with no tumor recurrence at two-month follow-up. The initial clinical manifestation in this case was suggestive of adrenal crisis secondary to pituitary hypofunction and secondary adrenal insufficiency, attributed to significant tumor compression and pituitary necrosis, and surgical decompression was performed for new visual loss.

articles.title: Spontaneous Heterotopic Pregnancy in a Primigravida: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Heterotopic pregnancy is the coexistence of an intrauterine pregnancy and an ectopic pregnancy. It is uncommon after spontaneous conception and may be overlooked once a normal intrauterine pregnancy has been identified. We report the case of a 33-year-old primigravida at approximately seven weeks of gestation who presented to the emergency department with sudden severe lower abdominal pain radiating to the back. Conception had occurred spontaneously, without assisted reproductive technology. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a viable intrauterine pregnancy together with a separate viable left tubal pregnancy and free intraperitoneal fluid. Initial investigations showed microcytic anemia, with a hemoglobin concentration of 7.6 g/dL and a mean corpuscular volume of 66.6 fL. Laparoscopy demonstrated approximately 150 mL of hemoperitoneum and a macroscopically unruptured left tubal ectopic pregnancy with a fimbrial hematoma. A left salpingectomy was performed while preserving the intrauterine pregnancy. Histopathologic examination of the excised tube confirmed chorionic villi. Recovery was uncomplicated, and ultrasonography the following day confirmed continued viability of the intrauterine pregnancy. Subsequent first-trimester follow-up showed appropriate progression. The intrauterine pregnancy continued to term, with cesarean delivery of a live male infant at 39 weeks and four days for breech presentation in labor. This case emphasizes that identification of an intrauterine pregnancy should not end the evaluation of a pregnant patient with significant abdominal pain. Careful assessment of the adnexa remains important even after spontaneous conception.

articles.title: Prolonged symptom-to-door time, cardiogenic-shock status and adverse in-hospital outcomes in emergency department patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a retrospective cross-sectional study with statistical pathway decomposition.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To quantify the association between prolonged symptom-to-door (StD) time and adverse in-hospital outcome status in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and what share of it is statistically represented by cardiogenic-shock status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Record-based retrospective cross-sectional study of 760 completed index hospital episodes among adults presenting directly to one emergency department with STEMI (March 2020 to August 2025), each contributing one record built at final in-hospital disposition. The exposure was prolonged StD time (>6 h), the pathway variable cardiogenic-shock status, and the outcome a composite of death, cardiac arrest, sustained ventricular arrhythmia, stroke or mechanical complication, from which shock was excluded. Sequentially adjusted logistic models, standardized decomposition with 500 bootstrap resamples, component-specific decomposition, E-values and sensitivity analyses were applied.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median StD time was 3.34 h (IQR 1.85-5.93); 24.5% exceeded 6 h. Cardiogenic-shock status was present in 10.8% patients and the composite outcome in 15.7%. Prolonged StD time was associated with the outcome in the fully adjusted model (OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.48-3.53, P<0.001) and with cardiogenic-shock status (OR 4.57, 95% CI 2.77-7.53), retaining a residual association after shock was included (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.13-2.83). Decomposition attributed 30.9% (95% CI 13.0-75.1%) of the log-scale association to shock, concentrated in death and cardiac arrest. The E-value was 3.34.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prolonged StD time was associated with higher odds of adverse in-hospital outcome status, and cardiogenic-shock status statistically represented about one third of this association. Because all variables were summarized at a single record-closure assessment, these are statistical associations, not causal mediation.

articles.title: Readying Asia-Pacific health systems for integration of blood-based biomarkers in mild traumatic brain injury assessment: An expert opinion review.

abstract.text: Rapid screening tests incorporating brain biomarkers offer a practical solution to some persistent challenges in acute mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) assessment by functioning as high-negative predictive value rule-out tools for unnecessary computed tomography (CT) scans; however, their implementation is not uniform globally. Emergency physicians and pathologists from across the Asia-Pacific region convened to examine current evidence on diagnostic tests utilizing the biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) for acute mTBI. This narrative expert review reflects the discussions and conclusions of the advisory board meeting and is intended to serve as an educational resource for decision makers in the region. As region-specific data are scarce, most data derive from non-Asian and non-Pacific Islander populations. Pivotal mTBI studies conducted in the United States and Europe have demonstrated that the GFAP/UCH-L1 biomarker panel achieves high diagnostic sensitivity (ranging from 95% to 100%) for detecting CT-positive intracranial lesions, and high negative predictive value for ruling out traumatic intracranial injury on head CT, exceeding 99.6% in combined panel testing. A point-of-care GFAP/UCH-L1 whole blood test provides results within 15 minutes, supporting rapid decision-making, and is cleared for use up to 24 hours after injury in adults with suspected mTBI (Glasgow Coma Scale 13-15), extending its utility to assessment settings beyond the emergency department. Although barriers to widespread implementation of biomarker testing persist across the Asia-Pacific region, we are taking steps to close the gap by outlining expert recommendations for incorporating GFAP/UCH-L1 biomarkers into acute care pathways.

articles.title: Dual-Energy Computed Tomography in the Emergency Department for Body Imaging Applications: An Update.

abstract.text: Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) has moved from a niche technique to a routine problem-solving tool in the emergency department. By using the energy-dependent attenuation of different materials, DECT provides material-specific characterization not available in conventional single-energy CT. Low-keV reconstructions, virtual noncontrast, and iodine maps improve the detection of subtle bowel ischemia, occult gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and active vascular extravasation. This article outlines the fundamentals of DECT and highlights its clinical utility in addressing acute abdominopelvic and thoracic emergencies as well as new emerging technologies.

articles.title: Military-Civilian Partnerships in Disaster Management.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) are a strategic necessity for modern medicine. By bridging the gap between military medical providers and local civilian hospitals, these alliances ensure both sectors are prepared for the changing environment of large-scale disasters. MCPs enable a two way transfer of knowledge between military and civilian medical providers and institutions. For civilian providers, MCPs offer access to effective triage and complex casualty management. For military providers, providing clinical repetitions helps maintain skills. The future of MCPs and evolving disaster management is critical for the readiness of medical centers.

articles.title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, or Nuclear-related Injuries in Disaster.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: In a disaster involving chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) agents, the surgeon must lead the medical response by merging standard trauma protocols with response to specific CBRN agents. This article outlines the management of CBRN-related injuries, integration of Advanced Trauma Life Support and CBRN, and decontamination. The article details the physiologic impact of specific agents, the necessity of rigorous decontamination, and the specialized surgical timelines needed for casualties suffering from combined injuries of CBRN and trauma.

articles.title: DNA Barcoding Identifies the Final Pelagic Larval Stage of the Mantis Shrimp Lysiosquilloides taiwanicus Ahyong & Lin, 2022 (Crustacea, Stomatopoda, Lysiosquilloidea) from Taiwan and Japan.

abstract.text: Understanding the occurrence and developmental stages of larvae is essential for ecological studies and the effective resource management of stomatopods. However, reliable species identification of stomatopod larvae remains limited, even for species of commercial interest. During a scuba diving survey off Okinawa Island, a larva exhibiting a distinctive carapace shape was collected. DNA barcoding identified the specimen as Lysiosquilloides taiwanicus Ahyong & Lin, 2022, representing the first confirmed record of the pelagic larval stage of this species. This Japanese larval specimen is also morphologically identical to a larva of this species recently collected off southeastern Taiwan. The morphological characteristics of the larva are described and illustrated herein. One of the most remarkable characteristics of this larva is the shape of the carapace: almost triangular in dorsal view; armed with a long rostrum, a long median spine, and a pair of posterolateral spines; posterolateral spines extending laterally. The uropodal protopod is forked, with the inner fork longer than the outer, as observed in other lysiosquillid larvae. Both the Japanese and Taiwanese specimens represent the final pelagic larval stage, there is a high possibility that adult L. taiwanicus also occurs in Japanese waters. Morphological comparisons with previously described larvae tentatively assigned to the family Lysiosquillidae demonstrate that these specimens represent the first documented larval form of L. taiwanicus worldwide.

articles.title: Pediatric Thoracic Imaging Emergency: Practical Approach for Daily Practice.

abstract.text: Imaging of thoracic emergencies in children is crucial for early diagnosis, guiding treatment, and avoiding severe complications. Radiography, ultrasound, and computed tomography are the most common modalities in emergency imaging. Radiologists should be familiar with the appropriate choice of imaging modality and the radiologic characteristics of serious conditions that can present acutely in the pediatric emergency room. This article discusses a practical overview of the major pediatric thoracic emergencies, including pulmonary infections, airway abnormalities, neoplasms, air leaks, traumatic injuries, and foreign bodies. An up-to-date review of key imaging findings is provided, with emphasis on features that are unique to children.

articles.title: Increasing Emergency Department Burden of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Injuries: A National 10-Year Analysis of Mechanisms and Severity Predictors, 2015-2024.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) is a rapidly growing grappling-based combat sport, but emergency department (ED) surveillance and sport-specific mechanism classification are limited.

abstract.label: HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: We hypothesized that BJJ-related ED visits have grown disproportionately compared with overall martial arts ED presentations and that sport-specific mechanisms predict nonroutine disposition.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Descriptive epidemiology study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS), 2015-2024. BJJ cases were identified from product code 3257, which corresponds to martial arts equipment and activity-related injuries, followed by a 2-reviewer narrative review. Trends were analyzed using survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression. An 11-category force vector mechanism taxonomy was developed from narratives. Pre- versus post-COVID eras were compared with false discovery rate correction. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of nonroutine disposition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 7618 martial arts ED visits, 1448 (19.0%) were BJJ related (58,170 weighted national cases). Annual BJJ volume rose nearly 5-fold (incidence rate ratio, 1.148/year; 95% CI, 1.090-1.209; P < .001) while total martial arts volume remained stable; BJJ's share climbed from 7.3% to 27.7%. The cohort was 78.0% male (mean age 25.7 ± 12.3 years); pediatric patients (≤17 years) comprised 29.5%. Strain/sprain (23.2%), fracture (15.5%), and contusion/abrasion (9.3%) predominated. The taxonomy classified 69.8% of cases into 8 defined categories, led by direct impact (21.8%), joint torque (16.4%), and fall (11.2%), with the remaining 30.2% indeterminate; the era profile was stable after multiplicity correction. Four independent predictors of nonroutine disposition emerged: internal injury (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 20.62; 95% CI, 7.55-56.26), neck compression (aOR, 5.26; 95% CI, 1.84-14.98), fracture (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 1.30-10.90), and age (aOR, 1.50 per decade; 95% CI, 1.18-1.90); optimism-corrected C-statistic = 0.748.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our study showed that BJJ-related ED presentations are rising rapidly while the injury profile remains stable; because denominators are unavailable, these are presentation counts rather than a measured change in per-capita injury risk. The injury taxonomy and disposition model further identified predictors of injury patterns and ED disposition. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective, exposure-denominated validation.

articles.title: Impact of portable point-of-care ultrasound on clinical decision-making and referrals in general practice: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in general practice, but evidence on its impact on clinical decision-making when performed with portable devices remains limited. Most existing studies have used cart-based systems, which may not reflect real-world general practice.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Cross-sectional observational study conducted over 12 months in a primary care centre in Barcelona, Spain. Three general practitioners with accredited training performed POCUS examinations using portable devices in 108 patients. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥15 years requiring clinical ultrasound. Clinical management plans were documented before and after POCUS using same questionnaire. Changes in decision-making and referral patterns were analysed using McNemar's test. Reporting followed the STROBE statement for cross-sectional studies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: POCUS changed clinical decision-making in 66.7% of cases. Intended referrals to secondary care decreased from 44.4% to 25.0% (absolute risk reduction 19.4%, 95% CI 8.4-30.5%, relative risk reduction 44%). Musculoskeletal examinations represented 73.1% of cases, with management modified in 63.3%. All seven patients with suspected deep vein thrombosis were managed without hospital referral. Referrals for conventional radiology ultrasound decreased from 32.4% to 12.0%, while GP-performed invasive procedures (infiltrations) increased from 0.9% to 18.5%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Portable POCUS substantially influences clinical decision-making and reduces secondary care referrals in general practice. Further research is needed, especially longitudinal studies, to evaluate whether these changes translate into improved health outcomes for patients.

articles.title: Anatomic Ulnar Collateral Ligament Repair With Internal Brace and Palmaris Longus Graft Using a Suture Bridge Construct.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) and lateral collateral ligament (LCL) injuries of the elbow are common in athletes, particularly those involved in overhead sports. Traditional repair techniques may not always provide optimal long-term outcomes, necessitating the development of advanced reconstruction methods. Over the years, techniques such as the Modified Jobe and Docking Methods have been refined to improve graft fixation and reduce complications. Emerging strategies, such as suture augmentation and internal bracing, have demonstrated potential to enhance biomechanical stability and facilitate early rehabilitation.

abstract.label: INDICATIONS
abstract.text: UCL/LCL reconstruction techniques, including those that utilize joint-spanning and/or internal brace augmentation, are indicated in cases where joint instability and dysfunction cannot be adequately addressed via traditional reconstruction or primary ligament repair alone.

abstract.label: TECHNIQUE DESCRIPTION
abstract.text: In the first step, the native UCL is repaired with a running, locking 2-0 FiberWire suture and reinforced with a spanning-suture bridge using linked, knotless suture anchors integrated into a spanning-suture construct. Next, the UCL reconstruction is performed using palmaris longus autograft passed through ulnar tunnels and docked into a humeral socket, with final graft tensioning to complete the reconstruction.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In our experience, UCL reconstruction with an internal brace yields superior functional outcomes, including improved time-zero biomechanics and overall reconstruction outcomes, particularly in younger, high-demand athletes.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Evolution of UCL reconstruction techniques has led to improved surgical outcomes and patient recovery. While traditional methods, such as the Jobe and docking techniques, remain widely used, advancements such as suture augmentation and internal bracing offer promising enhancements in biomechanical stability and clinical efficacy. As research continues to validate these approaches, their integration into clinical practice may further optimize ligament reconstruction strategies, particularly in high-performance athletes requiring rapid return to play.

abstract.label: PATIENT CONSENT DISCLOSURE STATEMENT
abstract.text: The author(s) attests that consent has been obtained from any patient(s) appearing in this publication. If the individual may be identifiable, the author(s) has included a statement of release or other written form of approval from the patient(s) with this submission for publication.

articles.title: Bathrooms as a Patient Safety Blind Spot in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review and Nursing Practice Framework.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) bathrooms preserve privacy and dignity but interrupt direct observation. Risks described across clinical publications and professional guidance include falls, unrecognized deterioration, overdose, hazardous ingestion, infection, inaccessible environments, and unmet elimination needs. This review integrated those risks and translated them into a nursing practice framework.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: For the structured narrative review, PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL Plus, and Scopus were searched on July 30, 2026, without date, language, age, or publication-type filters. Backward and forward citation chasing and a targeted search for professional documents supplemented database searching. Publications were categorized by ED relevance and synthesized thematically. Professional guidance was analyzed separately.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 659 records, 248 duplicates were removed and 311 records were screened. Of the 53 reports sought, 12 were not retrieved, 41 were assessed in full text, and 40 were included; citation chasing evaluated 15 candidates and added 3, yielding 43 publications/reports. Direct or contextual ED evidence was provided by 32 publications, and 11 were transferable. The synthesis identified 6 domains: falls and deterioration; fundamental care, continence, and dignity; overdose, self-injection, hazardous ingestion, and surveillance; infection and equipment; accessibility and design; and privacy and clinical use. Evidence was heterogeneous and largely descriptive, qualitative, quality-improvement, or case-based.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The ED bathroom should be managed as a clinical space rather than an environmental afterthought. This review proposes the original Assess-Assist-Observe-Respond-Document framework, which connects individualized risk assessment, proactive assistance, proportionate surveillance, rapid response, and reassessment. Local validation is required before implementation.

articles.title: Critical Care Catalyst: The Impact of Trauma Nurse Leads on Mortality, Patient Outcomes, and Throughput.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Trauma is the leading cause of years of life lost in the United States. Dedicated trauma nurse leaders (TNLs) coordinate resuscitation and streamline care, but data evaluating their clinical impact at level I trauma centers are limited. We evaluated the association between a newly implemented dedicated TNL program and patient outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, preimplementation and postimplementation observational study at an urban level I trauma center compared adult tier 1 and tier 2 trauma activations from the pre-TNL period (January 1, 2017, through April 30, 2020) with the post-TNL period (May 1, 2020, through December 31, 2023; 8 dedicated TNLs). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality (including hospice discharges). Secondary outcomes included time to initial computed tomography (CT), time to operating room, emergency department length of stay (LOS), hospital LOS, and ventilator days. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for Injury Severity Score (ISS), demographics, payor status, frailty, and activation acuity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 9112 activations included (pre-TNL, n = 2943; post-TNL, n = 6169), crude in-hospital mortality was unchanged overall (3.53% vs 3.55%; P = .97), but crude mortality decreased significantly among high-severity cohorts: ISS greater than 15 (20.1% vs 12.6%; P < .001), ISS greater than 24 (25.8% to 15.7%; P < .001), and emergent laparotomy (22.2% to 18.5%; P < .001). Median time to CT decreased from 34.48 to 29.64 minutes (P < .001), and mean hospital LOS decreased from 5.57 to 4.93 days (P = .018). After multivariable adjustment, TNL implementation was independently associated with a 36% reduction in odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio = 0.64; 95% CI, 0.48-0.84; P = .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Implementation of a dedicated TNL program was independently associated with significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality, driven primarily by survival gains in severely injured patients, faster time to initial diagnostic CT, and reduced hospital length of stay.

articles.title: Time to Antibiotic Administration in the Treatment of Sepsis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines recommend antimicrobial therapy within 1 hour for probable septic shock, while the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) mandates a 3-hour window. Current literature presents conflicting evidence on whether these universal time thresholds yield a definitive survival benefit. This study aims to evaluate the real-world impact of delayed antibiotic administration on patient mortality and length of stay (LOS).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted analyzing 62 153 adult encounters with severe sepsis or septic shock at emergency departments (EDs) between December 31, 2023, and December 31, 2025. Time to first antibiotic was categorized into 5 intervals (<1, 1-3, 4-12, 13-24, >24 hours). The primary outcome, in-hospital mortality, was analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. The secondary outcome, LOS, was analyzed among survivors using a gamma generalized linear model to calculate adjusted mean ratios (aMR).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort was clinically complex, with 63.5% of patients demonstrating a high Elixhauser comorbidity score (≥ 4). Only 2.8% of patients received antibiotics within the first hour. Mortality odds were significantly higher for patients receiving antibiotics after 24 hours compared to the less than 1 hour baseline (odds ratio = 1.52, 95% confidence interval: 1.18-1.95, P = .001). No statistically significant mortality difference was observed for the 1-3, 4-12, and 13-24 hour intervals relative to baseline. However, delayed administration increased LOS incrementally, with a 9% longer stay for the 13-24 hour group (adjusted means ratio [aMR] = 1.09, P = .003) and a 56% longer stay for the >24 hour group (aMR = 1.56, P < .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Achieving a less than 1-hour door-to-antibiotic time is operationally challenging. Delays up to 24 hours did not significantly increase mortality risk compared to immediate administration, though administering antibiotics before 13 hours offered modest improvements in hospital LOS.

articles.title: A Nurse-Driven Escalation in Trauma Team Activation Reduces Mortality of Injured Patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: There is a dearth of literature examining the clinical outcomes of injured patients who experience physiological deterioration in the emergency department (ED). At our trauma center, injured patients who develop hemodynamic, respiratory, or mental status instability after arrival are retriaged and upgraded to a full trauma team activation (fTA). The purpose of this study was to compare the clinical outcomes of patients with fTA based on prehospital signs and symptoms (initial) versus upgraded fTA patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study of injured patients presenting to a tertiary trauma center between June 1, 2022, and June 30, 2024. The study facility is a state-designated level I trauma center, an American College of Surgeons (ACS)-verified level II trauma center with a catchment area of 17 800 square miles, serving a population of 3.1 million in the central, southeastern region of the United States. The primary exposure was retriage with an upgrade in patient status to fTA. Bivariate analyses with Wilcoxon rank sum, Chi-square, and Fischer's exact tests were used, where appropriate. Binary logistic regression analyses were applied, adjusting for fTA status, Elixhauser comorbidity index (ECI), payer type, race, and sex, to determine if upgraded fTA status was independently associated with injured patient mortality, high-intensity time-sensitive (HITS) interventions, and discharge disposition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1538 fTA occurred during the study period with 66 patients (4.3%) upgraded to fTA after hospital arrival. In-hospital mortality or hospice discharge was less common among upgraded fTA patients compared to initial fTA patients (9.1% vs 19.7%; P = .032). After adjusting for ECI, payer type, race, sex, and trauma activation group, patients initially activated as fTA had 2.64 times higher odds of mortality or hospice discharge compared with patients upgraded to fTA (OR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.10-6.30; P=.029). Within the HITS subcategories, upgraded fTA patients were more likely to receive blood transfusion (63.6% vs 40.8%; P <.001) and less likely to receive mechanical ventilation (24.2%; vs 38.5% P = .020). Upgraded fTA status was not associated with patient discharge disposition.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Injured patients in the ED who develop signs and symptoms consistent with severe injury benefit from retriage and nurse-driven upgrades to fTA status. A hospital safety culture empowers bedside nurses to act on patients' physiologic changes, resulting in the rapid marshalling of health care resources for life-saving interventions.

articles.title: Emergency Room Nurses' Perceptions of Transformational Leadership and Its Role in Their Well-Being: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency room (ER) nurses work under conditions frequently associated with burnout, emotional exhaustion, and turnover intention. Leadership behavior is one of the few workplace conditions that can be modified without additional capital investment, and transformational leadership (TL) has been examined predominantly through cross-sectional survey designs. How ER nurses themselves describe these leadership behaviors and what they attribute to them remains poorly documented in Saudi public hospitals.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To describe ER nurses' perceptions of their nurse managers' TL behaviors and how these behaviors were perceived by the participants to shape their emotional and psychological well-being.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This qualitative descriptive study used non-probability convenience sampling to recruit eight frontline registered nurses from an ER in Saudi Arabia, each with at least six months of ER experience. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews of 45-60 minutes were audio recorded and transcribed verbatim. The analysis followed Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis using a deductive coding strategy; NVivo 14 supported the data management. Two researchers independently coded the data and resolved discrepancies by consensus.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Three main themes emerged from the data analysis: (1) clinical credibility and professional security, (2) individualized consideration and personal advocacy, and (3) empowerment and intellectual stimulation. The participants described managers' visible clinical presence during crises, bedside teaching, personal advocacy during family emergencies, recognition, and invitations to contribute to workflow decisions as conditions they connected to feeling calmer, safer, and more willing to remain in their ER.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The participants perceived clinically credible, personally attentive, and intellectually engaging leadership as supporting their well-being while also describing clear limits to what leadership behavior alone could offset. The findings are descriptive and self-reported at one point in time; no causal or mediating relationship is claimed.

articles.title: [Chinese expert consensus on the emergency diagnosis and treatment of acute exacerbation of asthma (2026)].
articles.journal: Zhonghua Wei Zhong Bing Ji Jiu Yi Xue
articles.journal_full: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
authors: Emergency Physicians Branch Of The Chinese Medical Doctor A
Working Group Of The Chinese Expert Consensus On The Emergency Diagnosis And Treatment Of Acute Exacerbation Of Asthma

abstract.text: Asthma is a heterogeneous disease with complex etiologies and predisposing factors. Its pathogenesis involves the interaction between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors. Chronic airway inflammation, including type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation, is a central feature and contributes to reversible airflow limitation and airway remodeling. Acute asthma exacerbations involve the sudden onset or worsening of wheezing, dyspnea, cough, or chest tightness, accompanied by reduced expiratory airflow and often by expiratory wheezes on auscultation. Exacerbations are commonly triggered by allergens, irritants, or infections and require urgent treatment. The Emergency Physicians Branch of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association convened a panel of experts in emergency medicine, respiratory medicine, critical care medicine, and general practice. The panel developed the Chinese expert consensus on the emergency diagnosis and treatment of acute exacerbation of asthma (2026) using a modified Delphi method, based on current evidence and emergency care practices in China. The consensus addresses 13 clinical issues related to emergency diagnosis and treatment of acute asthma exacerbations, and recommendations are proposed accordingly. Topics include identification and management of triggers; urgent assessment and initial treatment following first medical contact; ancillary investigations; recognition of life-threatening features, severity assessment, and management according to severity; assessment of inflammatory phenotypes; identification of risk factors for asthma-related death; respiratory support; nebulized drug administration; commonly used emergency medications; the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation; and pre-discharge management. The consensus strives to make the diagnosis and treatment process simple and clear, providing practical guidance for emergency and primary care, aiming to standardize the diagnosis and treatment of acute asthma exacerbations and achieve a seamless connection with specialist diagnosis, treatment, and management.

articles.title: The effects of common emergency call system applications in pre-hospital emergency medical services from a lean management perspective: The case of Ordu province, Turkiye.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of a centralized Common Emergency Call Center (CECC) system on prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) efficiency through the lens of Lean Management principles.

abstract.label: METHODOLOGY
abstract.text: This retrospective, longitudinal study analyzed secondary data from Ordu province, Turkey, comparing a 36 months pre-CECC period (2018-2020) with a 48 months post-CECC period (2021-2024). The dataset comprised 2,346,774 calls and 721,897 cases. Key performance indicators, selected as proxies for lean waste (communication, time, transport), were compared using independent samples t-tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Following CECC implementation, significant improvements were observed (p<0.001). The call-per-incident ratio, a proxy for communication waste, decreased by 49.0% (from 4.63 to 2.36). Time-based waste was reduced, with respond time of ambulance teams falling by 36.9% and ambulance mobilization time by 23.7%. Transportation waste, measured by distance per incident, decreased by 15.1%. On-time arrival rates improved significantly in both urban (93.9% to 98.4%) and rural (82.2% to 89.2%) areas. These gains were achieved without a statistically significant increase in the patient load coefficient.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The centralized CECC system, acting as a structural lean intervention, significantly reduced operational waste and improved efficiency in prehospital EMS. This centralized CECC model offers a scalable blueprint for health systems seeking to enhance emergency care delivery.

articles.title: Return to Play and Performance After Operative Repair of Scapholunate Interosseous Ligament Tears in National Basketball Association Athletes.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The rate of scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) injuries in National Basketball Association (NBA) players continues to increase. There is a paucity of data regarding return-to-play (RTP) rates and performance metrics after sustaining SLIL injuries in these athletes.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To determine the rate of RTP and performance outcomes in NBA players following a SLIL tear.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Case series; Level of evidence, 4.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review was conducted in January 2024 using the Pro Sports Transactions database of NBA injury notifications to identify isolated SLIL ligament injuries in NBA athletes between the 1956-1957 and 2022-2023 seasons. Confirmed injuries were matched with healthy controls based on similar career trajectories, and demographic, injury-related, and performance data were collected. Statistical analyses compared performance up to 2 seasons pre- and postinjury and assessed differences between the injury and control cohorts. Paired t tests were used to compare parametric performance data, and Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank tests were used for nonparametric data. Unpaired t tests were used to evaluate differences in means between injury and control cohorts, while Mann-Whitney U tests were used to compare medians for nonparametric data. Shapiro-Wilk testing was used to determine normality for all continuous variables before analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 863 wrist injury reports identified, 18 NBA athletes with confirmed SLIL tears met the inclusion criteria, alongside 18 matched healthy controls. The injury cohort had a significantly higher body mass index than controls. After surgical repair, 94.4% of injured athletes returned to play within an average of 6.2 months, with a significant reduction in points per game during their first season back (14.99 to 13.29 after; P = .0433) and a decrease in games played in their second season postinjury.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our study showed that NBA athletes have a high rate of return after sustaining and undergoing surgery for repair of a torn SLIL. Players may experience an initial decrease in playing time and performance; however, these variables returned to baseline by season 2 postsurgery. NBA players who tear their SLIL and undergo surgical fixation are expected to make a full recovery and return to play at their previous level of performance.

articles.title: Outcomes of Primary and Revision UCLR: Return to Play, Performance, and Role Adaptation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction (UCLR) is a common procedure among Major League Baseball (MLB) pitchers, but the effects of revision UCLR on performance and career longevity remain unclear.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To compare return-to-play (RTP) and return-to-level (RTL) rates, performance metrics, and role transitions between pitchers undergoing primary and revision UCLR.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Cohort study; Level of evidence, 3.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 177 MLB pitchers who underwent primary or revision UCLR between 2015 and 2021 were included. Performance metrics, including fastball velocity, spin rate, fastball usage, fielding independent pitching, and pitch movement, were analyzed up to 3 years postreconstruction (PRY1-PRY3). Role transitions between starter and reliever positions were also evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: RTP (P = .046) and RTL (P = .039) rates were significantly lower after revision UCLR. After stratification by pitcher role, revision starters demonstrated greater increases in fastball usage (P = .014) and horizontal break (P = .031) at PRY3, whereas no significant differences were observed among relievers. Revision UCLR remained independently associated with lower RTL, but not with RTP, after multivariable analyses. Starter-to-reliever transitions were common after surgery, with no significant between-group difference.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study underscores the importance of recognizing role changes and reduced recovery success in revision cases, as well as the need for tailored strategies to support long-term performance and durability.

articles.title: Return to play rate and performance after ulnar collateral ligament repair with suture tape augmentation in major league baseball players.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) repair with suture tape augmentation has emerged as an alternative to traditional reconstruction in appropriately selected patients. While clinical outcomes of UCL repair have been reported in amateur athletes, data evaluating performance outcomes in Major League Baseball (MLB) players remain limited. The purpose of this study was to evaluate return to play (RTP) and changes in performance metrics among MLB players undergoing UCL repair with suture tape augmentation. We hypothesized that UCL repair would allow a faster RTP compared with historical reconstruction data while maintaining player performance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MLB players who underwent UCL repair with suture tape augmentation between 2016 and 2024 were identified using publicly available injury databases. Player performance metrics were obtained from publicly available databases including MLB Statcast. The primary outcome was time to RTP. Secondary outcomes included traditional and advanced performance metrics. For pitchers, metrics included earned run average, innings pitched, strikeouts, walk rate, fastball velocity, fastball spin rate, fielder independent pitching, fangraphs wins above replacement (fWAR), and Statcast-based metrics. Position player metrics included fWAR, fielding run value, and arm strength. Pre-operative and post-operative metrics were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests or Mann-Whitney tests with statistical significance set at P < .05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-two MLB players met inclusion criteria. RTP to the MLB level was 81.8% (18/22). The mean RTP time was 10.98 months (range, 5.9-34). Pitchers had a mean RTP of 13.51 months (range, 9-34) and position players had a mean RTP of 7.51 months (range, 5.9-8.5). There were no statistically significant differences between pre-operative and post-operative performance metrics, including earned run average (3.66 ± 0.7 vs. 3.95 ± 1.9; P = .765), fastball velocity (93.0 ± 1.7 vs. 92.7 ± 1.9 mph; P = .609), innings pitched (42.1 ± 39.0 vs. 23.0 ± 28.0; P = .266), strikeouts (31.7 ± 53.7 vs. 23.5 ± 27.4; P = .247), or fastball spin rate (2,241 ± 131 vs. 2,235 ± 122 rpm; P = .496). Similarly, position players demonstrated no significant differences in fWAR, fielding run value, or arm strength after RTP.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: UCL repair with suture tape augmentation in MLB players demonstrates a high rate of RTP with preservation of traditional and advanced performance metrics. Position players returned earlier than pitchers; overall RTP remained favorable. UCL repair with suture tape augmentation provides an effective surgical option allowing return to elite-level performance.

articles.title: Emergency Department Management of Traumatic Pneumothorax and Hemothorax.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Thoracic trauma is commonly encountered in the emergency department, often with severe injuries including pneumothorax and hemothorax. This article reviews the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and emergency management of pleural injuries, emphasizing rapid recognition and intervention of tension physiology and massive hemothorax in unstable patients. It reviews and compares imaging modalities for diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making. Management has shifted from routine large-bore chest tubes toward selective observation and smaller drainage devices in carefully chosen patients. The article also addresses ventilated patients, procedural complications, tube malfunction, retained hemothorax, persistent air leak, antibiotic prophylaxis, secure tube placement, and disposition planning.

articles.title: Pharmacology in Emergency Trauma Management.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Pharmacotherapy is an important aspect of management of the acutely injured trauma patient to address symptoms, to facilitate evaluation and emergent interventions, as well as to manage the physiology present in trauma patients. Important pharmacologic categories include analgesia, sedation, rapid sequence intubation, antibiotics, management of hemorrhage, addressing intracranial pressure and vasopressors. Consideration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic changes in the critical trauma patient as well as knowledge of benefits and risks across this range of pharmacotherapies can optimize patient management.

articles.title: Emergency Department Management of Geriatric Trauma and Falls.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Trauma in older adults is a growing public health challenge due to age-related physiologic changes, frailty, comorbidities, and reduced reserve, which increase morbidity and mortality after injury. Falls are the leading cause of trauma, while motor vehicle crashes are the second most cause of injury-related death. Frailty is a stronger predictor of outcomes than age alone and guides evaluation and disposition. Older adults are at increased risk of traumatic brain injury, hip fractures, rib fractures, spinal injuries, and elder abuse. Liberal use of computed tomography imaging, comprehensive geriatric assessment, multidisciplinary care, and geriatric-specific trauma pathways improve outcomes and care quality.

articles.title: Nerve Blocks for Traumatic Injuries.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Ultrasound-guided nerve blocks are important for modern, opioid-sparing trauma care. Proficiency in select, high-yield blocks can provide rapid targeted analgesia and improve clinical outcomes. For example, in a patient with multiple rib fractures, performing an erector spinae or serratus anterior block can alleviate chest wall pain and improve respiratory function. Similarly, a fascia iliaca block in an elderly patient with a hip fracture minimizes pain while also reducing the risk of delirium. Safety requires precise needle visualization and proper anesthetic dosing. Standardizing workflows with dedicated carts and documentation templates promotes efficiency. This approach delivers effective pain managment while maintaining the speed and safety necessary in emergency settings.

articles.title: Spinal Cord Injury.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: The emergency physician plays a key role in detecting initial and evolving injury by correctly restricting spinal motion and using imaging criteria to diagnose unstable fractures and compressive bleeding within the spinal canal. The ED physician must also focus on stabilizing the polytrauma patient and begin blood pressure treatment after ruling out other traumatic causes of hypotension. Most importantly, the emergency physician must lead a team approach, communicating early with consultant trauma surgeons, spine surgeons, and intensive care unit providers to prevent delays in critical early decompression and stabilization surgery or transfers to appropriate trauma centers.

articles.title: Resuscitation of the Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: This article provides a practical overview of modern trauma resuscitation for emergency clinicians. It emphasizes early recognition of shock, timely hemorrhage control, and activation of massive transfusion protocols. Guidance is provided on fluid resuscitation, permissive hypotension, airway management, and treatment of agitation in critically ill trauma patients. Personalized management of trauma-induced coagulopathy using viscoelastic testing, along with monitoring biomarkers such as lactate and base deficit, is highlighted. The importance of effective team coordination, leadership, and rapid decision-making to improve outcomes in high-acuity trauma care is emphasized.

articles.title: From backbone to bedside: Nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding spinal cord injury care.
articles.journal_full: The Southern African journal of critical care : the official journal of the Critical Care Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Spinal cord injury (SCI) represents one of the most severe forms of central nervous system damage and has profound effects on the physical, psychological and social wellbeing of affected individuals. Patients with SCI are particularly vulnerable to secondary complications such as pressure ulcers, deep vein thrombosis and urinary tract infections. Nurses play a pivotal role in the prevention and management of these complications.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate nurses' knowledge and attitudes before and after implementation of a digital educational application focused on the care of patients with SCI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, two-phase study was conducted between January 2023 and July 2024. During the first phase (January - May 2023), 86 nurses employed in the intensive care unit (ICU), emergency department and rehabilitation centre completed a structured 21-item questionnaire assessing baseline knowledge and attitudes. During the second phase (May - July 2024), the same nurses were reassessed using the same questionnaire following a digital educational intervention. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The findings demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in nurses' knowledge and attitudes following the intervention. Notable improvements were observed in areas related to complication prevention, the use of assistive devices, caregiver education, nutrition, bowel management and remaining informed about updates in patient care. Statistically significant correlations were identified between improvement and both department of employment and level of education. Nurses working in the ICU showed the greatest improvement (phase 1 v. phase 2: 3.1 v. 4.1), while nurses with postgraduate education also demonstrated statistically significant improvement (p=0.007).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The digital educational application was effective in enhancing nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding the care of patients with SCI. Continuous education, particularly within specialised clinical settings, is essential for optimising patient outcomes and maintaining high standards of care.

abstract.label: CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY
abstract.text: This study evaluated nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding spinal cord injury (SCI) care across intensive care, emergency and rehabilitation settings, and tested whether a low-cost, custom-built digital educational application could improve these outcomes. The intervention was associated with significant improvements in knowledge and attitudes, particularly around complication prevention, caregiver education and psychosocial support, with the largest gains seen among ICU nurses and those with postgraduate qualifications. These findings support digital training tools as an accessible way to strengthen nursing capacity for SCI care, especially where structured in-person continuing education is difficult to sustain.

articles.title: Abdominopelvic Imaging Emergency in Children: A Comprehensive Update and Review.

abstract.text: Abdominopelvic emergencies are one of the most common causes of pediatric emergency department visits, frequently resulting in urgent surgical management. Because conditions such as midgut, volvulus and torsion are time-sensitive, accurate and timely diagnosis is essential and imaging evaluation plays a crucial role. Following abdominal radiograph, ultrasound remains the preferred next imaging modality in most conditions to avoid radiation, even more so with the introduction of contrast-enhanced ultrasound. Advancements in computed tomography and MRI continue to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient safety. This article provides an up-to-date review of current imaging protocols and imaging characteristics of pediatric abdominopelvic emergency conditions.

articles.title: A narrative review of airway changes after prolonged use of supraglottic airway devices: Molecular mechanisms, pathophysiology, and preventive strategies.

abstract.text: There has been an exponential increase in the use of supraglottic airway devices (SGAs) to provide a secure airway without tracheal intubation. They are widely used for many elective surgeries, rescue ventilation after failed intubation, and have been widely recommended for prehospital care. However, its use for extended periods when endotracheal intubation is not feasible may lead to tongue engorgement, mucosal injury, nerve palsy, and subsequent difficult intubation. This narrative review aims to synthesize current evidence on difficult airways and airway-related complications following prolonged use of SGA placement. Here we describe plausible mechanisms, including inflammatory and ischemic pathways, and discuss the severity patterns, risk factors, and preventive/management strategies of a possible difficult airway after prolonged use of SGA in perioperative and intensive care unit settings. Preventive strategies across concentric petals, highlighting correct SGA device and its size selection, minimal cuff inflation in devices that have a cuff, continuous monitoring of cuff pressure, early replacement with an endotracheal tube, appropriate head positioning, device replacement, humidification, and sedation. Implementing these measures can minimize the complications as well as the risk of a difficult airway after prolonged SGA use. Literature on this topic is difficult to find, and definitive recommendations need research, which should prioritize standardization and robust study designs, which may help guide practice. Mechanistic and translational research work should explore pressure-ischemia and inflammatory pathways to facilitate device design improvements and evidence-based protocols for monitoring, timing of exchange to a definitive airway, and safe removal strategies.

articles.title: Mass Religious Gathering-Associated Nationwide Salmonella Outbreak in South Korea, 2025.

abstract.text: A foodborne outbreak associated with a mass religious gathering occurred in South Korea on August 30, 2025. A retrospective cohort investigation was conducted among 1,677 participants. The attack rate of clinical cases was 48.7% (816/1,677), and 36 laboratory-confirmed Salmonella Typhimurium infections with an identical PFGE pattern were identified. Consumption of a pre-packaged meal was strongly associated with illness (relative risk, 17.69; 95% confidence interval, 7.53-41.57). Epidemiologic findings supported a common-source outbreak. Prolonged storage at ambient temperature was a likely contributing factor. These findings emphasize the importance of food safety management and coordinated response systems in mass gathering settings.

articles.title: Barriers and Enablers of Trauma Triage Tool Implementation in Ireland: A Qualitative Study of First Responders.

abstract.text: The trauma triage tools play an important role in assisting first responders in deciding who needs to be taken to specialist trauma services urgently. However, time pressure, limited training, resource problems, and clinical judgment are factors that hinder the use of these tools in prehospital care. This qualitative study considers the factors that can hinder and facilitate the use of the Health Service Executive Trauma Triage Tool amid the evolving trauma system in Ireland. The study examines a range of individual, organizational, and system-level factors that influence the adoption of the tool among first responders and senior managers using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). In order to capture the participants' lived experiences and professional perspectives, a descriptive phenomenological design is used. Semi-structured interviews and, more so focus groups with a maximum of 30 Dublin Fire Brigade paramedics, advanced paramedics, emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and managers who participate in trauma response or management are being conducted. Interviews are conducted online or in person and are 45-60 minutes in duration. All audio recordings will be verbatim transcribed, verified, and analyzed using framework analysis with NVivo. Inductive and deductive coding will be employed, and themes will be related to CFIR domains. The study should aim to identify practical barriers to implementing the trauma triage tool, including training needs, resource limitations, communication difficulties, and reluctance to change, as well as enablers such as leadership, interagency collaboration, and clear implementation processes. Findings will contribute to future trauma triage implementation strategies in Ireland.

articles.title: Management of the Anticoagulated Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: The management of anticoagulated trauma patients is an increasingly common, high-risk challenge driven by an aging population and expanding use of oral anticoagulants, particularly direct oral anticoagulants. Up to 4% to 7% of trauma patients are present on preinjury anticoagulation, facing higher rates of hemorrhagic complications, morbidity, and mortality. This article reviews a systematic approach spanning epidemiology, emergency department (ED) evaluation, and the primary and secondary surveys, emphasizing rapid identification of anticoagulant use and liberal computed tomography (CT) imaging. It details agent-specific laboratory assessment, transfusion principles, and tailored reversal strategies.

articles.title: Diagnostic Pitfalls in Emergency Chest Imaging.

abstract.text: The high-volume, fast-paced, and high-stakes nature of emergency department (ED) imaging poses substantial challenges to the interpreting radiologist. This article lays an inside-to-outside framework for approaching cardiothoracic findings in ED patients from the heart and vasculature (often the most urgent findings and diagnoses) through the bones with an overview of acute cardiothoracic imaging findings and their potential pitfalls.

articles.title: Trauma in Pregnancy.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Trauma is the leading cause of death in reproductive-aged individuals, complicating 6% to 8% of pregnancies and accounting for approximately 20% of maternal deaths. This article reviews a maternal-first resuscitation approach, emphasizing that fetal survival hinges on maternal stabilization. It details pregnancy-specific alterations affecting the primary survey including difficult airway, respiratory compensation, aortocaval compression, and delayed recognition of hemorrhagic shock. It also provides guidance on blood product resuscitation, RhD considerations, TXA, and resuscitative hysterotomy. Diagnostic evaluation covers imaging recommendations and laboratory nuances. Finally, it addresses mechanism-specific injuries, intimate partner violence, fetal monitoring, patient counseling, and criteria for discharge.

articles.title: Metabolic risk factors on pediatric hidradenitis suppurativa: A retrospective multicenter cohort analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder that affects a clinically significant proportion of pediatric patients. Metabolic syndrome has been associated with HS in adults; however, its influence on disease characteristics and healthcare utilization in pediatric populations remains poorly understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the relationship between metabolic comorbidities and pediatric HS outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX collaborative network. Patients aged 0-18 years with an HS diagnosis were categorized into HS with metabolic components (HS+MetC) and HS alone (HS only). Propensity score matching was performed 1:1 based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, and age at diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, treatment patterns, and healthcare utilization outcomes were compared.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 4,392 HS+MetC and 3,783 HS only patients were identified prior to matching. HS+MetC patients were diagnosed at a younger age and were more likely to be Black/African American or Hispanic/Latino. After matching, HS+MetC patients demonstrated significantly higher rates of emergency department visits, ambulatory visits, hospitalizations, surgical interventions, and most therapeutic treatments.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pediatric HS patients with metabolic comorbidities experience higher healthcare utilization and more intensive treatment needs. Early identification of metabolic risk factors may support earlier diagnosis, improved disease management, and reduce morbidity.

articles.title: The psychosocial resilience experiences of healthcare workers following the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes: a qualitative study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study explores the under-researched experiences of healthcare workers navigating a "dual-role" paradox, functioning simultaneously as traumatised disaster survivors and active responders during the 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes. Disasters fracture a community's social fabric, highlighting the need to understand the dynamic interactions that shape the adaptive capacities of frontline healthcare workers in disrupted environments.
