Moving beyond individual-centric approaches, this research provides a socio-ecological framework demonstrating that resilience is a multidimensional outcome, offering critical insights for post-disaster mental health strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: To investigate the psychosocial resilience and resource mobilisation of these professionals across individual, interpersonal, and organisational levels, a qualitative approach was employed. In-depth interviews were conducted with 33 frontline healthcare workers (paramedics/ emergency medical technicians [EMTs], nurses, emergency physicians, and psychosocial staff) active in the immediate aftermath. Data were evaluated via thematic analysis and interpreted through the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The sample (mean age: 32.00 ± 5.33) primarily comprised pre-hospital emergency personnel (n = 16, 48.5%). Highlighting the extreme demands of their position, all participants worked continuously for over 72 h acutely, despite their own homes sustaining mild damage. The thematic analysis identified three main themes: Psychological Resilience, Social and Communal Support, and Organisational and Occupational Challenges. Healthcare workers experienced severe occupational role conflict, ethical distress, and security vulnerabilities. Despite the psychological toll, participants exhibited psychological flexibility and a heightened awareness of life's fragility. Family bonds, collegial solidarity, and community support emerged as essential support systems.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Integrating the SEM with the dual-role framework of healthcare workers, this study reinforces that disaster resilience is a socially and organisationally embedded process shaped by complex interactions. Shifting from traditional individual paradigms, these findings offer policymakers and crisis managers strategic guidance on developing multi-layered support systems that address the unique role conflicts faced by healthcare workers in future disasters.

articles.title: Clinical features and comparative outcomes of antiviral treatment in children with influenza A and B: a propensity score-matched cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Comparative evidence on antiviral treatment in pediatric influenza remains limited. We compared the clinical features of influenza A and B and assessed the comparative outcomes of oseltamivir, baloxavir marboxil, and peramivir in children.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-center cohort included 3,718 children with nucleic acid-confirmed influenza A or B who presented to a tertiary pediatric emergency department between November 2023 and April 2024 and initiated antiviral treatment within 48 h of fever onset. Primary endpoints were time to fever resolution and time to full symptom resolution. Propensity score matching was performed separately within the influenza A and influenza B cohorts for prespecified pairwise comparisons, followed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3,718 children, 1,717 had influenza A and 2,001 had influenza B. Influenza A was more often associated with higher fever and neurologic complications, whereas influenza B more commonly presented with gastrointestinal symptoms. After propensity score matching, baloxavir and peramivir were associated with shorter times to fever resolution than oseltamivir in both cohorts (influenza A: baloxavir 1.57 days vs. oseltamivir 2.11 days, peramivir 1.72 days vs. oseltamivir 2.23 days; influenza B: baloxavir 1.50 days vs. oseltamivir 2.29 days, peramivir 1.71 days vs. oseltamivir 2.25 days). Differences in time to full symptom resolution were smaller and less consistent across comparisons. Overall adverse events were documented in 16.5% of children receiving oseltamivir, compared with 5.0% receiving peramivir and 3.6% receiving baloxavir; notably, no serious adverse events were observed across the cohorts.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Influenza A and B showed distinct clinical phenotypes in this pediatric cohort. In propensity score-matched analyses, baloxavir and peramivir were associated with modestly faster fever resolution and lower recorded rates of adverse events than oseltamivir. Given the retrospective, non-randomized design and the modest absolute differences observed, these findings should be interpreted as associative and hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence of causal superiority. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized outcome assessment are needed.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Long-term health-related quality of life and mortality in chronic critically ill patients.
articles.journal_full: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The increasing prevalence of chronic critically ill patients makes it essential to understand the impacts of this condition, through studies that include multidimensional assessments. The aim of this study is to assess long-term mortality and health-related quality of life in chronic critically ill patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Prospective cohort study with chronic critically ill patients after intensive care unit discharge. The baseline health status was assessed using the following scales: EuroQol 5 Dimensions 3 Levels, 36-Item Short Form, Rankin Scale, Barthel Index, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Score. The same questionnaires plus the Impact of Event Scale were applied in the 3- and 6-month follow-up. After 3 years, vital status was checked and the EQ-5D-3L was applied.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 130 patients were included, with a median age of 60.5 years (IQR 42-70). All participants included in the study completed the questionnaires at baseline. Responses were obtained from 44 participants at 3 months, 29 participants at 6 months, and 66 participants at 3 years. Overall, 26 participants contributed to the 3 years complete-case longitudinal EuroQol 5 Dimensions 3 Levels analysis. Compared with retrospectively recalled pre-hospital baseline, physical and functional health measures were numerically worse at 3 months after intensive care unit discharge and showed partial improvement at 6 months and 3 years. Furthermore, on the 36-Item Short Form, overall differences across timepoints were observed in the domains of functional capacity (p = 0.003) and social aspects (p = 0.01). In the forward stepwise multivariable Cox model, the variables independently associated with death were age (adjusted HR 1.04 per year; 95% CI 1.02-1.06; p < 0.001), the modified Rankin Scale score (adjusted HR 1.23; 95% CI 1.06-1.43; p = 0.006), and number of comorbidities (adjusted HR 1.26; 95% CI 1.04-1.52; p = 0.01).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among survivors with available follow-up data, physical and functional health measures showed results suggesting lower scores at 3 and 6 months than at the retrospectively recalled pre-hospital baseline. In the subgroup with complete longitudinal health-related quality of life data, the 3-year unadjusted median index value remained below the recalled baseline. Age, number of comorbidities, and the modified Rankin Scale score were associated with death.

articles.title: Debriefing in prehospital simulation-based education: a scoping review of ambulance nurse and paramedic literature.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Simulation is fundamental to the education of paramedics and ambulance nurses, with debriefing widely recognised as the educational component through which much of the learning is consolidated. However, how debriefing is implemented and reported within prehospital simulation for practising clinicians remains poorly understood. This scoping review mapped and critically examined debriefing approaches used in simulation involving paramedics, ambulance nurses, flight paramedics, and flight nurses.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using Arksey and O'Malley's (2005) scoping review framework and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guideline, MEDLINE, EMCARE, CINAHL Plus, SCOPUS, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published in English or Arabic between 2005 and 2025. Following editorial review, all included studies were re-examined against the predefined eligibility criteria, and studies involving student-only populations were excluded. Findings were charted and synthesised thematically.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From 974 identified records, 18 studies met the final inclusion criteria. Most studies originated from the United States, employed quantitative designs, and were published between 2012 and 2025. Two themes were identified: guided debriefing (n = 15) and tool- and technology-assisted debriefing (n = 3). Across the included literature, debriefing was associated with improvements in technical performance, communication, teamwork, clinical reasoning, and reflective practice. However, reporting of debriefing interventions remained inconsistent, with considerable variation in facilitation, structure, outcome measures, and theoretical underpinning. Many studies relied on self-reported educational outcomes, making it difficult to distinguish the specific contribution of debriefing from the broader effects of simulation-based education.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Debriefing remains a central component of prehospital simulation-based education for practising clinicians, yet its design and reporting vary considerably across the literature. Guided debriefing was the predominant approach, while evidence supporting technology-assisted debriefing was comparatively limited. Future research should adopt clearer descriptions of debriefing interventions, strengthen theoretical and pedagogical foundations, and incorporate objective measures of learner performance to better understand how different debriefing approaches influence clinical practice.

articles.title: Recurrent acute limb swelling with mild D-dimer elevation leading to longitudinal recognition of characteristic imaging findings consistent with multisite calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) disease is a crystal-associated arthropathy that may present with acute monoarticular inflammation and mimic thrombotic, traumatic, or degenerative conditions. Definitive diagnosis requires synovial fluid analysis; however, aspiration may not be feasible in the setting of minimal effusion. Imaging findings such as fibrocartilage chondrocalcinosis and peri-odontoid calcification may provide critical diagnostic clues. This case highlights the importance of longitudinal diagnostic reasoning and retrospective imaging synthesis when recurrent inflammatory episodes are initially evaluated as isolated events.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A Black woman in her late 60s was referred for outpatient musculoskeletal evaluation following a motor vehicle accident. During care she developed acute right knee swelling with calf tenderness, prompting evaluation for deep venous thrombosis and gout, including D-dimer and serum uric acid testing. Normal uric acid and mildly elevated D-dimer levels prompted referral for lower extremity duplex ultrasonography (US). Review of prior emergency department records revealed a similar episode of acute wrist swelling associated with mildly elevated D-dimer and negative duplex ultrasound imaging. Expanded retrospective imaging review demonstrated linear calcification of the triangular fibrocartilage complex, lamellar meniscal calcification at the knee, bilateral hip chondrocalcinosis, and peri-odontoid calcification consistent with a crowned dens configuration. Synovial fluid analysis was considered on two occasions but deferred because of minimal effusion. Integration of multisite fibrocartilage calcifications supported a working diagnosis of probable imaging-supported recurrent CPPD rather than thrombotic disease.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case underscores the importance of cross-episode diagnostic integration of history and imaging in patients with recurrent inflammatory limb swelling and mild D-dimer elevation. Recognition of characteristic fibrocartilage and peri-odontoid calcification patterns may facilitate identification of probable CPPD when aspiration is not feasible and broaden the differential diagnosis in patients with recurrent inflammatory limb swelling.

articles.title: Perceptions of surrogate decision-makers of cardiac arrest patients on engaging in research during high emotional distress.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The perception that individuals in crisis experience undue psychological burden by participation in research is a barrier to including surrogate decision-makers to critically ill patients in research studies. Importantly, perceptions from those who have engaged as surrogates are necessary to develop interventions to better support the process of decision making and recovery.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study will explore surrogates' perceptions on participating in research during high emotional distress.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a sub-study of a larger qualitative study of surrogates for comatose survivors of out of hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) entitled "Experience of Surrogate Decision-Makers in Post Cardiac Arrest Decision-Making". Surrogates were approached in the intensive care unit at a single US academic hospital to consent for follow up contact 30-days after patient discharge or death. On follow up, participants were consented to participate in a semi-structured interview. Based upon the Grounded Theory, interviews were conducted, recorded, transcribed, coded and analyzed thematically.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Between 9/2017 and 7/2019, 34 surrogates agreed to be contacted and 12 (35%) consented to participate. Median time to interview was 48 days. Of the 12 participants, 8 were grieving the death of their loved one (bereaved surrogate) and 4 surrogates had their loved one survive to hospital discharge (defined as "co-survivor"). Most participants were women (n = 5, 75%) and just under half identified as the spouse/partner of the patient (n = 5, 42%). Three themes emerged on perceptions of participation in research (1) the importance of contributing their perspectives to improve future surrogates' experiences, (2) even in the context of emotional challenges, 3.Surrogates appreciate willingness to delay follow-up depending on their emotional needs, endorsing a personal approach to participation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Surrogate decision-makers of OHCA patients emphasized the importance of their perspective in research, despite the emotional challenges they might be facing. Further research is needed that incorporate surrogates' perspectives to develop interventions to support surrogate decision making and to improve outcomes for all who experience out of hospital cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Clinical analysis of 549 patients undergoing emergency debridement and suturing.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Open wounds in the emergency department are one of the most common conditions seen in emergency trauma surgery clinics, and debridement and suturing are the primary treatment methods for such wounds. With improvements in healthcare conditions, advancements in medical technology, and increasing public awareness of emergency open wounds, there have been new developments in the treatment of such injuries within medical institutions. Therefore, this study analyzes and summarizes the clinical data of patients with emergency open wounds treated at the Luoyang Central Hospital Affiliated to Zhengzhou University from January 2025 to June 2025, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for the prevention and treatment of emergency open wounds.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 549 patients with emergency open wounds treated at the Emergency Trauma Surgery Outpatient Clinic of Luoyang Central Hospital Affiliated to Zhengzhou University from January 2025 to June 2025. The analysis examined patient gender, age, time of presentation, injury site, mechanism of injury, antibiotic use, and infection status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The age group with the highest number of patients presenting with open wounds in the emergency department was 31-40 years old, with a total of 100 cases (18.21%); this was followed by the 0-10 age group, with 96 cases (17.49%). The number of patients aged 40 and older was significantly lower than that of patients younger than 40, with 83 cases (33.31%) in the 40-and-older group. Among them, 350 were male (63.75%), and 199 were female (36.25%), with a male-to-female ratio of 1.76:1. The time from injury to the start of medical treatment was primarily within 1 h of the injury, totaling 446 cases (81.24%); the total number of patients treated within 6 h of the injury was 526 (95.81%). In terms of the mechanism of injury, sharp-object injuries accounted for the highest proportion, totalling 178 cases (43.41%); the main causative agents included knives, glass, sheet metal, shards of porcelain and splinters of wood. Antibiotics were administered to 38 patients (6.92%), while 511 patients (93.08%) did not receive antibiotics; 3 cases (0.55%) developed infections; among these, 1 patient was prescribed oral antibiotics, and the infected wound was debrided to control the infection before being re-sutured and healed. Among patients treated in the emergency trauma surgery department, upper limb injuries were the most common, with 268 cases (48.82% of the total); among upper limb injuries, open wounds of the hand were the most frequent, with 195 cases (35.52% of the total); followed by scalp lacerations, with a total of 156 cases (28.42%); lower limb injuries were relatively less common, with 117 cases (21.31%); and injuries to the chest, abdomen, and buttocks were the least frequent, with 12 cases (2.18%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Open wounds in the emergency department are relatively common, primarily resulting from accidental injuries, and have shown an upward trend in recent years. Emergency open wounds predominantly occur in males, the 31-40 years age group, and the hand region. Cut wounds inflicted by sharp knives are the leading cause of emergency open wounds. The majority of patients undergo debridement and suturing within one hour post-injury, and a delay in treatment time does not increase the risk of infection. With timely management and thorough debridement, most emergency open wounds can achieve favorable treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Comparing flipped classroom and lecture-based education on clinical competency in electrocardiogram interpretation among prehospital emergency personnel.

abstract.label: BACKGROUNDS
abstract.text: Cardiovascular diseases are among the most prevalent health conditions worldwide. One of the fastest methods for assessing cardiac rhythm and electrical activity is the electrocardiogram (ECG). Prehospital emergency personnel are usually the first healthcare providers to encounter cardiac patients outside the hospital setting. Since prehospital interventions performed by emergency medical personnel can influence factors such as ischemic time, clinical competency in ECG interpretation among prehospital providers is vital. Currently, various educational methods are available. One such approach is the flipped (or inverted) classroom model. In contrast, the traditional lecture-based method remains widely used. Lecturing is the most common instructional strategy in which all learners receive the same education regardless of individual differences. With advances in technology and widespread access to modern communication tools, education can increasingly be delivered through these platforms, allowing the utilization of innovative methods such as the flipped classroom in educational settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This quasi-experimental interventional study with a pretest-posttest design was conducted to compare the effects of flipped classroom and lecture-based educational methods on clinical competency in ECG interpretation among prehospital emergency personnel in Iran in 2025.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: To compare competency scores before the intervention, two weeks after, and one month after the intervention, independent t-tests were performed. The results showed no statistically significant difference in clinical competency scores between the two groups before the intervention (p = 0.10). However, at the two subsequent time points-two weeks and one month after the intervention-significant differences were observed in the flipped classroom group. Specifically, the mean competency score in this group significantly increased, to 6.84(p = 0.002). two weeks after the intervention, and to 7.73 one month after the intervention.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The results demonstrated that clinical competency in ECG interpretation among prehospital emergency personnel in the flipped classroom group was higher than that of the lecture-based group at both two weeks and one month after the intervention. The findings of this study may be useful in designing educational programs aimed at strengthening clinical competency in this group. Furthermore, considering the critical role of ECG interpretation competency in the management of cardiac patients-particularly during the prehospital phase prior to transfer to advanced medical facilities-it is recommended that ECG interpretation training be incorporated into continuing and in-service education programs for prehospital emergency personnel.

articles.title: A matched, real-world observational study of the burden of osteogenesis imperfecta and healthcare resource utilization in Ontario, Canada.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by bone fragility and deformity. This study aimed to estimate the incidence and prevalence of OI in Ontario, Canada, and to describe the burden of illness (BOI) among patients with OI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective, population-based, matched observational study was conducted using Ontario health administrative data from ICES (formerly Institute for Clinical Evaluative Sciences). Patients with OI were identified using ICD-10-CA codes from hospital and emergency department records between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2021. The study included an incidence and prevalence cohort and a BOI cohort, with the latter exact-matched to controls (general population without OI) on age, sex, and geography. The BOI cohort was followed for one to three years. Outcomes included OI incidence and prevalence, patient demographics, healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), direct healthcare costs, and fracture rates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study identified 565 patients with OI, with a median (IQR) age of 14 (5-37) years (57% children aged 1-17) and 48% male. The annual incidence of OI ranged from 0.14 to 0.46 per 100,000, while prevalence stabilized at 3.9 per 100,000 over the study period. Fracture rates were higher among patients with OI than controls, with a mean (SD) rate of 0.7 (0.9) fractures per person per year. Rates were particularly high among children, at 0.8 (0.9) fractures per person per year. Patients with OI had significantly higher HCRU compared to controls, with greater mean numbers of specialist visits (29.1 [35.8] vs. 4.9 [12.4]), general practitioner visits (18.8 [32.1] vs. 7.6 [9.7]), emergency department visits (4.9 [10.1] vs. 1.1 [2.1]), and hospitalizations (1.7 [2.0] vs. 0.1 [0.5]) (all p < 0.001) over the follow-up period. The mean total cost (excluding Ontario Drug Benefit costs) per OI patient over the three-year follow-up was also higher than controls ($47,348 [$77,161] vs. $4,667 [$16,480]; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study provides the first real-world estimates of OI incidence and prevalence in Ontario, highlighting its significant healthcare burden, as well as the need for improved interventions to reduce fractures and associated burden and further research to improve the management and outcomes of OI patients.

articles.title: Incremental prognostic value of inflammatory biomarkers for 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis presenting to the emergency department: a retrospective 24-hour landmark cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Inflammatory biomarkers are associated with outcomes in sepsis, but prognostic association does not necessarily imply additional predictive information beyond clinical severity. We evaluated the incremental prognostic value of procalcitonin (PCT), the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR) at a 24-hour landmark.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort included 248 adults admitted through the emergency department with sepsis between January 2024 and April 2026. The primary analysis included 243 patients alive 24 h after arrival and used 50 multiply imputed datasets. Fixed-horizon logistic models compared a clinical base model comprising sex, albumin, lactate, and APACHE II with models that added continuous PCT alone or PCT, NLR, and MLR together. Internal validation used ordinary bootstrap optimism correction with 1000 patient-level resamples and multiple imputation nested within resampling; within each resample, separate MICE runs completed the incomplete bootstrap sample and the original cohort used to evaluate the bootstrap-fitted models (five imputations each). A 0-3-point equal-weight inflammatory score based on within-cohort Youden cut-offs was examined as a secondary exploratory analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-six patients in the landmark cohort died by day 28. Exploratory pooled comparisons did not provide evidence that adding PCT improved the clinical base model (P = 0.775) or that adding PCT, NLR, and MLR together improved it (P = 0.428). The odds ratios per doubling were 0.943 (95% CI 0.817-1.089) for PCT, 1.350 (0.937-1.943) for NLR, and 0.866 (0.681-1.101) for MLR. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.749, 0.743, and 0.728 for M0, M1, and M2, respectively. The corrected AUC difference between M2 and M0 was -0.022 (95% CI -0.030 to 0.023). The apparent association of the fixed-cut-off score was no longer supported after repeating the complete cut-off search procedure (selection-adjusted P = 0.295). A first-laboratory sensitivity analysis retaining all 248 patients and 51 deaths yielded a similar pattern (exploratory pooled P = 0.951).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: PCT, NLR, and MLR did not provide evidence of incremental predictive value in this exploratory single-center cohort. The within-cohort equal-weight inflammatory score was subject to substantial cut-off selection uncertainty and remains exploratory. Neither the model nor the score should guide clinical decisions before independent evaluation.

articles.title: Exploring disaster risk management strategies for strengthening resilience in rehabilitation hospitals: a qualitative case study of Rofeideh Hospital.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Rehabilitation hospitals care for highly vulnerable populations with limited mobility and complex care needs, making them particularly susceptible during disasters. Disaster risk management (DRM) in such settings has received limited attention. This study aimed to explore DRM strategies that can strengthen resilience in rehabilitation hospitals.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: This qualitative case study used purposive sampling to recruit 16 key informants affiliated with Rofeideh Hospital. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with hospital managers, risk management committee members, supervisors, head nurses, ward nurses, and administrative staff involved in disaster preparedness and management. Data were analyzed using inductive content analysis following Graneheim and Lundman's method.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Six main categories and 16 sub-categories emerged as critical for strengthening DRM in rehabilitation hospitals: incident command and coordination system (two sub-categories), preparedness and capacity building (four sub-categories), strategic response & recovery (three sub-categories), disaster information and communication management (two sub-categories), financial and logistical support (two sub-categories), and non-structural infrastructure resilience (three sub-categories). Among these, incident command and coordination, along with preparedness and capacity building, were the most consistently endorsed by participants. Distinctive rehabilitation-specific priorities included patient-centered evacuation planning, rehabilitation-focused workforce preparedness, and tailored emergency planning for patients with disabilities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: To keep rehabilitation hospitals resilient during disasters, a flexible approach is essential, one that integrates preparedness, clear communication, strong planning, and efficient resource use, all tailored to the unique needs of patients with disabilities. Future multi-site qualitative and mixed-methods studies across rehabilitation hospitals with different organizational structures and resource levels are needed to evaluate the transferability and implementation of these strategies in diverse settings.

articles.title: Ultrasound-assisted dynamic bladder function for predicting successful catheter removal in male ICU patients: a prospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Optimal timing for urinary catheter removal in intensive care unit (ICU) patients remains challenging, as conventional static measurements often fail to accurately reflect true bladder function in the critically ill. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of ultrasound-assisted bladder emptying dynamics for successful spontaneous voiding and to develop a practical predictive nomogram for male ICU patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational cohort study included male ICU patients scheduled for urinary catheter removal between July 2021 and October 2023. Bladder emptying time, actual bladder capacity, and intravesical pressure at 200 ml (P200) were dynamically measured using a standardized saline infusion protocol with bedside ultrasound assistance. The primary outcome was successful spontaneous voiding within 24 h after catheter removal. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to identify independent predictors and construct a nomogram. Model performance was assessed via discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, with internal validation using 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 87 patients were included, of whom 60 (69.0%) achieved successful spontaneous voiding. Multivariable analysis revealed that a longer bladder emptying time (OR: 0.992, 95% CI: 0.985-0.997; P = 0.009) and a larger actual bladder capacity (OR: 0.991, 95% CI: 0.983-0.998; P = 0.023) were independently associated with a decreased likelihood of successful voiding. In contrast, static P200 was not a significant predictor (P = 0.763). The developed nomogram demonstrated acceptable discrimination (apparent AUC = 0.766; optimism-corrected AUC = 0.721) and excellent calibration (Brier score = 0.176). Decision curve analysis indicated a higher net clinical benefit compared with empirical "treat-all" or "treat-none" strategies.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Ultrasound-assisted dynamic bladder functional parameters may offer potential clinical utility for predicting voiding outcomes after catheter removal in ICU patients, providing additional functional insights compared to conventional static manometry. The proposed non-invasive nomogram may serve as a practical, physiology-driven tool to support individualized bedside decision-making.

articles.title: Concussion in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Traumatic brain injuries (TBIs) account for a significant number of emergency department (ED) visits each year. Concussions, a type of mild TBI, represent the majority of these cases; however, there is no clear consensus on ED-based management. Concussion is a clinical diagnosis made through careful history and focused physical examination as there are no definitive pathognomonic signs. Management in the ED is primarily supportive, but patients require education and counseling to better understand their diagnosis, expected trajectory, follow-up plans, and need for aftercare. Improving ED-based concussion diagnosis and follow-up has strong potential to positively influence patient recovery and outcomes.

articles.title: Co-Designing a mobile health intervention for cardiac arrest survivors and co-survivors: Mapping experiences and unmet needs to digital design features.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: As survival rates for sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) have increased, so has the imperative for advancing survivorship support. Previous work suggests a massive gap in understanding of post-acute care needs and how best to support survivors and families (co-survivors) after hospital discharge. Although clinical models for post-SCA care exist, there have been few studies that seek to understand cardiac arrest survivor and importantly co-survivor experiences. Applying qualitative methods can be valuable to identify opportunities for developing tailored support that is grounded in the needs and experiences of survivors and co-survivors.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: This study aimed to specifically understand out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) survivor and co-survivor perspectives, experiences and support needs during the first year of their survivorship journey and to identify pain points where digital interventions could play a role in enhancing survivorship experiences.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used an interpretive descriptive approach to qualitative inquiry within an overarching co-design process. As an additional means of triangulation, focus groups and individual interviews with clinicians and rehabilitation specialists were also conducted.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Survivors (n = 9) and spouses (n = 5) of survivors, averaging 7.71 years since SCA, participated in four focus groups. One focus group and two individual interviews were conducted among six clinicians. Two major themes reflect OHCA (co-)survivorship experiences and support needs: (1) navigating new territory without a map, and (2) the impact of time and evolution of needs. Within each theme, several sub-themes indicate pain points for OHCA survivors and co-survivors, highlighting specific opportunities to design support that enhances recovery experiences for both.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: By first understanding survivor and co-survivor experiences of recovery along with where they felt supports were missing, we identified key pain points that represent opportunities for enhancing recovery experiences through digital health. The results of this work contribute significantly to the broader cardiac arrest survivorship agenda by not only confirming key challenge areas, support needs and "turning points" of cardiac arrest survivors and co-survivors but highlighting the novel concept of the evolution of survivorship needs over time, a key consideration for intervention development.

articles.title: Accountability in emergency surgery: moving beyond blame toward high reliability: a WSES-JMESE position paper.
articles.journal_full: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency surgery is characterized by clinical uncertainty, time pressure, evolving information, physiological instability, and substantial variability in available resources. In this setting, adverse outcomes may occur despite timely and appropriate care and should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of professional failure. Nevertheless, surgeons may be exposed to retrospective, outcome-driven, and overly individualized attribution of blame when the complexity of the original decisional environment is insufficiently considered. A structured framework is therefore needed to support fair, proportionate, and learning-oriented accountability in emergency surgical practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This evidence-informed position paper was developed through a structured multidisciplinary review of literature from patient-safety science, cognitive psychology, medical ethics, health-systems research, surgical professionalism, and high-reliability organization theory, complemented by iterative expert discussion within the World Society of Emergency Surgery-Journal of Medical and Surgical Errors working group. The literature was synthesized narratively to identify the principal contextual, cognitive, ethical, professional, and organizational domains relevant to fair accountability and adverse-event review in emergency surgery. The resulting statements were framed as ungraded evidence-informed Good Practice Statements according to the GRADE framework rather than clinical practice recommendations based on comparative effectiveness evidence.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The synthesis identified seven interrelated principles for fair accountability in emergency surgery: contextual proportionality; distinction between accountability and blame; mitigation of hindsight, outcome, and attribution bias; recognition of distributed responsibility across individuals, teams, and systems; protection of professional integrity; procedural fairness and institutional responsibility; and application of high-reliability principles. Particular attention is given to the dynamic and time-dependent nature of emergency surgical decision-making, the incomplete representation of clinical reasoning in contemporaneous documentation, the limitations of population-based scoring systems and benchmarks, and the influence of resource availability on feasible treatment options. These principles were integrated into a structured framework for adverse-event review aimed at supporting proportionate analysis of adverse outcomes and avoiding premature attribution of individual blame when harm reflects interacting clinical, cognitive, team-level, and system-level factors.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Accountability in emergency surgery should evaluate decisions according to the information, physiological condition, reasonable alternatives, and resources available at the time of care. Contextualization should not eliminate individual responsibility; rather, it should make responsibility attribution more accurate, proportionate, and fair. A bias-aware, procedurally fair, and high-reliability approach can protect surgeons from premature, punitive, outcome-driven blame while preserving legitimate accountability for unsafe practice, reckless conduct, or misconduct. Such a framework may strengthen patient safety, professional integrity, organizational learning, and public trust.

articles.title: Evolution of surgical indication strategies and their impact on treatment outcomes in acute superior mesenteric venous thrombosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: To compare how different surgical indication strategies affect treatment patterns and outcomes in patients with acute superior mesenteric vein thrombosis (SMVT), and to identify independent risk factors for intestinal wall full-thickness necrosis and in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed 125 patients with acute intestinal ischemia secondary to SMVT from October 2014 to October 2025. Patients were divided into two chronological cohorts according to the change in surgical indication strategy implemented at our institution: the liberal surgical indication period (October 2014 - October 2023, n = 102) and the strict surgical indication period (November 2023 - October 2025, n = 23). Baseline characteristics, treatment pathways, and in-hospital outcomes were compared between the two periods. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality and for full-thickness necrosis in patients undergoing surgery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The two periods were comparable with respect to baseline characteristics (P > 0.05). Compared with the liberal period, the strict period had significantly lower rates of early surgery (4.3% vs. 63.7%, P < 0.001) and overall surgery (26.1% vs. 80.4%, P < 0.001). Full-thickness necrosis was identified in a significantly higher proportion of surgical specimens in the strict period than in the liberal period (83.3% vs. 18.3%, P = 0.002). Patients in the strict period had a longer median hospital stay (19 days vs. 12 days, P = 0.011), a trend toward lower ICU admission (30.4% vs. 50.0%, P = 0.089), and no significant difference in mortality (13.0% vs. 7.8%, P = 0.423). Multivariate analysis showed that lactate ≥ 4 mmol/L (aOR = 7.545, 95%CI: 1.827-31.149, P = 0.005) and elevated D-dimer (aOR = 1.047, 95%CI: 1.012-1.084, P = 0.008) were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Given the limited number of death events (n = 11), the above multivariate analysis results should be considered exploratory findings that require validation in larger prospective cohorts. In surgical patients, CT evidence of impaired bowel wall perfusion independently predicted pathologically confirmed full-thickness necrosis (aOR = 6.236, 95%CI: 1.663-23.388, P = 0.007).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A strict surgical indication strategy with an anticoagulation-first approach was associated with a lower rate of surgery in SMVT patients and directs surgical intervention more precisely to those with established full-thickness necrosis. CT evidence of impaired bowel wall perfusion is a key warning sign for full-thickness necrosis and warrants urgent surgical evaluation. Hyperlactatemia and elevated D-dimer independently predict in-hospital mortality and should serve as core elements for early risk assessment and dynamic monitoring.

articles.title: A hub-and-spoke network organizational model in Liguria (Italy) for managing anaphylaxis in pediatric age: a retrospective analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction for which intramuscular epinephrine is the sole non-deferrable first-line treatment. Despite well-established international guidelines, real-world adherence remains critically suboptimal, particularly in peripheral emergency settings. This study examines anaphylaxis management in children aged 0-16 years presenting to the emergency department within the Gaslini Diffuso initiative, a structured Hub-and-Spoke pediatric network in Liguria, Italy, to evaluate inter-institutional variability in clinical practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter retrospective observational study spanning 10 years at the Hub Center (IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini, Genoa; January 2013 - December 2023) and 2 years across all network centers (January 2022 - December 2023). Anaphylaxis was defined according to the NIAID/FAAN 2006 criteria.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort comprised 168 patients aged 0-16 years, distributed across the Hub Center and four Spoke Centers. Epinephrine was administered in only 34.9% of patients overall (rising to 52.8% in the 2022-2023 period), with marked inter-institutional variability across the network (Hub 52.8% vs. La Spezia 6.7%). Antihistamines (89.2%) and corticosteroids (87.3%) dominated clinical practice despite lacking proven efficacy in preventing anaphylaxis progression. Tryptase measurement was performed in 43.4% (acute) and 21.1% (baseline) of Hub patients. Autoinjector prescription was documented in only 26.5% of newly eligible patients, and as low as 5.3% at Savona-Pietra Ligure.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings suggest significant gaps that may contribute to suboptimal outcomes, underscoring the urgent need for network-wide epinephrine-first protocols and structured training programs.

articles.title: Early prediction of clinical deterioration in older adults with suspected infection admitted from the emergency department to general wards: a multicenter machine learning study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Older adults with suspected infection admitted from the emergency department (ED) to general wards remain at considerable risk of early clinical deterioration. Conventional early warning scores may perform suboptimally in this population. We aimed to develop and externally validate machine learning models to predict early clinical deterioration within 48 h among older adults with suspected infection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter retrospective study used electronic medical records from two tertiary medical centers for model development and internal validation between 2016 and 2023, with external validation using data from a regional hospital. Eligible patients were aged 65 years or older with clinically suspected infection. All records from the same patient were assigned to a single partition. Predictors included demographics, comorbidities, laboratory results, and vital signs recorded at emergency department triage and before ward transfer; missing data were handled using MissForest imputation with missingness indicators. Logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost models were developed and compared with conventional early warning scores (NEWS, MEWS, mSOFA). The primary discrimination metric was the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration, decision-curve analysis, and Shapley Additive Explanations as secondary analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The development cohort comprised 96,871 ED visits, and the external validation cohort comprised 35,361 ED visits. CatBoost achieved the highest AUROC among all evaluated models (internal AUROC, 0.851; external AUROC, 0.829) and significantly outperformed the conventional early warning scores (external AUROC ≤ 0.70; all DeLong p < 0.001). For precision-recall performance (external event-rate baseline, 0.017), CatBoost achieved the highest external AUPRC (0.134), approximately eight times the baseline and more than three times the best conventional score, with the other machine-learning models ranging from 0.093 to 0.119. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed risks for the gradient-boosting models, whereas logistic regression showed greater deviation from the ideal diagonal.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Gradient boosting models, particularly CatBoost, achieved good discrimination for early clinical deterioration in older adults with suspected infection admitted from the ED to general wards, and outperformed conventional early warning scores. These models may support pre-ward-transfer risk assessment at the time of the ward-admission decision; prospective studies are warranted to confirm real-world effectiveness and guide clinical implementation.

articles.title: Oral health behaviours and shift work barriers among Hungarian EMS personnel: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Shift-working emergency medical services (EMS) personnel face structural barriers to preventive oral care, yet national workforce data remain scarce.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To estimate prevalence of oral symptoms, behaviours, dental attendance, and psychosocial OHRQoL impacts among Hungarian National Ambulance Service (OMSZ) staff; assess associations with occupational enablers/barriers; and evaluate acceptability of employer-supported screening.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Nationwide cross-sectional anonymous online survey (13 Sep 2024-17 Apr 2025; n = 1,061; 73% men, 74% 24-hour shifts). Logistic regression examined a priori outcomes (ORs, 95% CI), adjusted for age/sex/attendance; STROBE-compliant.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,061 respondents, 74% reported 24-hour shifts as their primary duty pattern. Over half reported current or recent dental/oral problems (54.9%), and 20% had not attended a dental check-up within the previous two years. Off duty, 33% brushed twice daily, whereas during duty about two-thirds reported regular brushing. Workplace hygiene kits were reported by 40% of respondents and were more common among 24-hour shift workers. In regression analyses, kit availability was strongly associated with daily or more frequent on-duty brushing among 24-hour staff (85% vs. 21%). Daily brushing was associated with lower odds of toothache, non-use of interdental cleaning with higher odds of hiding teeth, and rare on-duty brushing with higher odds of halitosis. Psychosocial impacts were similar across roles, and 88-90% were willing to undergo workplace screening.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Shift-constrained EMS staff face substantial, preventable oral health burdens amenable to occupational solutions. Enabling on-duty hygiene and supporting routine care are key priorities. High screening readiness supports integrating teledentistry. Consistent gaps across roles underscore the need for further longitudinal and interventional studies.

articles.title: Bone Marrow Biopsies.
articles.journal_full: The Medical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy are foundational diagnostic procedures in hematology, supporting evaluation of peripheral blood abnormalities, malignancy, infection, infiltrative disease, and rare systemic disorders. This article reviews contemporary indications and contraindications, with emphasis on safe patient selection and individualized management of bleeding risk. Key anatomic landmarks are summarized, highlighting the posterior superior iliac spine as the preferred adult site and describing point-of-care ultrasound to improve localization. Step-by-step techniques for powered and manual approaches are outlined, along with best practices for specimen handling, post-procedure monitoring, billing considerations, and common technical pitfalls, affecting diagnostic yield.

articles.title: Pain Management in the Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Effective pain management in adult trauma patients is essential to improve recovery, reduce complications, and prevent long-term consequences such as chronic pain, depression, and PTSD. Multimodal analgesia combines medications and nonpharmacologic strategies to achieve better pain control while minimizing opioid use and associated risks. Key agents include acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents, ketamine, topical and systemic lidocaine, gabapentinoids, muscle relaxants, and carefully selected opioids when necessary. Pain management should be individualized based on patient factors, including age, comorbidities, traumatic brain injury, and substance use disorders. Early assessment, regular reassessment, and coordinated multidisciplinary care optimize outcomes across trauma settings.

articles.title: High-Value Emergency Department Interventions for the Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Trauma remains a major cause of death and disability, making early emergency department interventions crucial. This review highlights evidence supporting high-value trauma interventions, particularly in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and damage control resuscitation (DCR). For TBI, preventing secondary brain injury through avoidance of hypoxia, hypotension, and abnormal carbon dioxide levels is essential, although evidence is largely observational. Recommended targets include SpO2 greater than 92%, Pao2 80 to 100 mm Hg, normocapnia, and age-appropriate blood pressure goals. In hemorrhagic trauma, DCR strategies such as tranexamic acid administration, tourniquet use, balanced transfusion, permissive hypotension, temperature control, calcium replacement, and anticoagulation reversal improve outcomes.

articles.title: Research on a prediction model for outcomes of cardiopulmonary resuscitation in community out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients based on the Utstein model.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To construct an automated machine learning (AutoML)-based prediction model for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) outcomes in community out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients using the Utstein model, systematically identify key predictive factors, and provide a basis for clinical risk stratification and individualized intervention.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-center retrospective study design was employed, including all adult non-traumatic OHCA patients managed by the Emergency Department of The First People's Hospital of Lin'an District, Hangzhou, from March 2019 to March 2024. All OHCA patients were analyzed to identify key factors associated with achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). In the second stage, a sub-cohort of patients who successfully achieved ROSC was selected to further investigate predictors influencing their 30-day survival status, ultimately developing the final prognostic prediction model. The Improved Fast Tree-seed Algorithm (IFATA) was utilized within the AutoML framework to optimize model hyperparameters. Feature importance was validated through dual-dimensional LASSO regression and SHAP interpretability models. An interactive web-based clinical decision support tool was developed for risk assessment and clinical communication.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 370 enrolled patients, 256 (69.19%) died after resuscitation, while 114 (30.81%) achieved ROSC. The AutoML model demonstrated comprehensive optimal performance, with a ROC-AUC of 0.9891 and PR-AUC of 0.9490. Key features selected by AutoML were: on-site defibrillation, cumulative epinephrine dosage, time from cardiac arrest (CA) to CPR initiation, time from CA to endotracheal intubation, PCO2, and time from CA to intravenous access establishment. When evaluated on the test set, AutoML exhibited the strongest robustness, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.9815 and PR-AUC of 0.9515. Its predictive calibration significantly outperformed other models, with the lowest Brier score (0.127). SHAP analysis ranked feature importance as follows: on-site defibrillation > cumulative epinephrine dosage > time from CA to CPR initiation > time from CA to endotracheal intubation > PCO2 > time from CA to intravenous access establishment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: By integrating multidimensional clinical data with interpretable machine learning techniques, this study confirms the core role of the Utstein model in predicting CPR outcomes for OHCA patients. It achieves real-time translation of risk assessment into intervention decisions, providing innovative tools and methodologies for precise OHCA resuscitation.

articles.title: Nutrition assistance program participation, healthcare access, and perinatal health among U.S. Latinos in the context of the "public charge" rule: a systematic review.
articles.journal_full: International journal for equity in health

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The "public charge" rule assesses whether an immigrant to the U.S. is likely to become dependent on government assistance, particularly for potential use of cash-benefit programs or long-term institutionalization at government expense. Being deemed a public charge can make an applicant for legal status inadmissible. Although the rule applies to specific immigration determinations, its effects may impact health outcomes. This systematic review synthesized evidence on public charge policy and health-related outcomes among U.S. Latino populations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following PRISMA guidelines and a PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD42024507861), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published in English or Spanish from January 1996 through February 20, 2026. Eligible studies included U.S.-based Latino populations, examined the public charge rule as exposure, and reported health-related outcomes, health behaviors, healthcare access, or use of health or social programs. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, with disagreements resolved by consensus and, when needed, a third reviewer. Data were extracted using a standardized PECO-based form and narratively synthesized.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 157 citations identified, 19 studies met inclusion criteria. Studies examined program utilization and access (n = 13, 68%), maternal health (n = 4, 21%), or both domains (n = 2, 10%). Nearly all used cross-sectional designs (n = 18, 95%); 9 used qualitative and 10 quantitative data. Across studies, fear, misinformation, and concerns about immigration and legal consequences were the most consistent barriers to nutrition assistance programs, healthcare, Medicaid, and government-funded perinatal services. During the policy changes briefly implemented in 2018, Latino children with medical needs had the highest estimated risk of losing Medicaid, CHIP, or nutrition assistance benefits (79.8%; 95% CI, 74.4%-85.1%). Among likely undocumented Latino patients, self-pay emergency department visits increased after the 2018 proposed rule expansion. Maternal health studies documented delayed perinatal care, reduced Medicaid-funded prenatal care initiation, higher odds of preterm birth, and lower birth weights.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The public charge policy may function as a structural determinant of health for Latino families by discouraging the use of safety-net programs, including among eligible individuals. Additional research is needed to assess downstream health consequences, reduce misinformation, strengthen trusted communication, and protect access to healthcare and social welfare programs.

articles.title: Predicting operational risks in an O2O home nursing platform in China: machine learning models with SHAP-based explanations.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The rapid expansion of Online-to-Offline (O2O) home nursing services addresses the growing continuity of care demands of aging populations but introduces complex operational risks due to spatial dispersion and dynamic community environments. Traditional retrospective management approaches are inadequate for addressing these highly non-linear spatiotemporal uncertainties, highlighting an urgent need for proactive risk stratification.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To develop, compare, and interpret predictive models utilizing traditional machine learning and Tabular Transformer architectures for stratifying two core operational risks (service overtime and long service duration) and one fee-structure classification task (high-cost orders) in digital nursing delivery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study analyzed 89,623 continuous operational records from the "Yujian Nursing at Home" platform in 2025. The dataset was strictly partitioned into training, validation, and independent test sets. We compared the predictive performance of six traditional baseline classifiers against deep learning architectures, specifically comparing a simplified Minimal Transformer and a standard TabTransformer. Model efficacy was evaluated using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC), Sensitivity, F1-score, and Precision-Recall curves. TreeSHAP for the Random Forest models and KernelSHAP for the TabTransformer were applied to extract global feature importance and interpret the decision-making mechanisms.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the full operational monitoring scenario, the Tabular Transformer achieved an AUC of 0.934 for high-cost order risks, while Random Forest achieved AUCs of 0.789 and 0.794 for long service duration and overtime risks, respectively. However, under the strict pre-dispatch setting (using only features available at order submission), predictive performance experienced an expected decrease: AUCs were 0.856 for high-cost risks (TabTransformer), 0.726 for long duration, and 0.744 for overtime (Random Forest). Identifying minority class cases in the highly imbalanced overtime task (9.78% positive rate) remained challenging under fixed thresholds, resulting in a low positive predictive value (PPV). SHAP analysis revealed that geospatial impedance and specialized service items were the features with the largest model-attributed contributions across all tasks.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Advanced machine learning algorithms can stratify multidimensional operational risks in O2O home nursing platforms. By quantifying the impact of geospatial impedance and clinical complexity, these interpretable models facilitate a critical paradigm shift from retrospective quality control to proactive, algorithm-driven nursing governance, potentially generating hypotheses for optimizing human resource allocation, exploring interventions to mitigate occupational burnout, and informing equitable digital health policies.

articles.title: Joint modeling of hypertension and cardiovascular disease among Iranian Hajj pilgrims using Bayesian multivariate generalized linear mixed model.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hypertension (HTN) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) are major contributors to global morbidity and mortality and represent important health concerns during the Hajj pilgrimage, where large numbers of pilgrims are exposed to substantial environmental and physical stress. Despite their close biological relationship and frequent co-occurrence, HTN and CVD have largely been investigated as independent outcomes, potentially overlooking their shared determinants and underlying correlation. Therefore, we jointly modeled these conditions to provide a more comprehensive assessment of cardiovascular risk among Iranian Hajj pilgrims.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, medical records of 478,360 Iranian Hajj pilgrims participating in seven pilgrimage seasons (2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2022) were analyzed. A Bayesian multivariate generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was employed to jointly analyze HTN and CVD, allowing the correlation between these outcomes to be modeled while accounting for geographic clustering among individuals through province-level random intercepts. Associations with demographic and clinical risk factors were estimated using adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% credible intervals (CrIs), and model performance was evaluated using the Deviance Information Criterion (DIC). Spatial analyses were performed to characterize regional variation in disease burden.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The prevalence of HTN and CVD was 20.90% and 3.93%, respectively. Among all included pilgrims, the mean age was 54.87 ± 10.92 years, and 49.96% were women. Compared with separate univariate models, the joint Bayesian GLMM demonstrated substantially better model fit (ΔDIC = 51,720.5) and identified a strong residual correlation between HTN and CVD (ρ = 0.75). Age, sex, chronic renal failure, thyroid dysfunction, and diabetes (DM) were significantly associated with both outcomes. Representative estimates from the joint model showed that each additional year of age increased the odds of HTN (OR = 1.14, 95% CrI: 1.13-1.15) and CVD (OR = 1.11, 95% CrI: 1.10-1.11). Women had higher odds of HTN (OR = 2.15, 95% CrI: 1.99-2.32) but lower odds of CVD (OR = 0.80, 95% CrI: 0.76-0.84) compared with men, whereas DM was associated with substantially increased odds of HTN (OR = 9.15, 95% CrI: 7.57-10.95) and CVD (OR = 3.07, 95% CrI: 2.90-3.27). Temporal variation was observed across pilgrimage years, with HTN risk highest in 2018 and lower in 2022 relative to 2013, while CVD risk was also reduced in 2022. Geographic heterogeneity was evident, with HTN prevalence ranging from 13.52% in Qom to 32.39% in East Azerbaijan and CVD prevalence ranging from 1.87% in Esfahan to 8.93% in Ilam.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The Bayesian multivariate GLMM provided an informative framework for jointly evaluating correlated HTN and CVD outcomes in a large clustered population. By accounting for the correlation between outcomes and identifying shared determinants, this approach can inform integrated cardiovascular risk assessment, targeted pre-Hajj screening, and region-specific preventive strategies for high-risk pilgrims.

articles.title: A scoping review on the economic burden of falls among older adults.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Falls are the second leading cause of unintentional injury death globally, and the World Health Organization estimates that approximately 82% of fall-related mortality occurs in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite this disproportionate burden, the economic impact of falls among older adults in resource-limited settings remains poorly documented. This scoping review aimed to map the existing evidence on the economic burden of falls among older adults, describe the extent and nature of available cost data, and identify evidence gaps, with particular attention to LMICs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The protocol was registered with the Open Science Framework ( https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/N23H5 ). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Semantic Scholar were searched for studies published between January 2010 and January 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data, and findings were summarised using narrative synthesis. Eligible studies reported quantitative monetary cost data associated with falls or fall-related injuries in populations aged 60 years and older.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 198 records identified (183 after de-duplication), 33 studies met the inclusion criteria, originating from 12 countries and one multi-country European study. Most studies (n = 30, 90.9%) were conducted in high-income countries (HICs); two (6.1%) were from upper-middle-income countries (Iran and Mexico) and one (3.0%) from a lower-middle-income country (India). No studies were identified from low-income countries, Sub-Saharan Africa, or most of Southeast Asia. In the United States, reported total medical costs of falls rose from US$50.0 billion (2015) to US$80.0 billion (2020). Reported per-episode costs ranged from US$5,974 (emergency department) to US$48,679 (inpatient admission). Hip fractures were consistently reported as the most costly injury type. Seven studies (21.2%) reported indirect costs, and a single study quantified informal caregiving costs (US$4,274 per faller per year). Fifteen studies (45.5%) included cost-effectiveness components, all conducted in HIC settings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This review maps a marked geographic mismatch: although LMICs are estimated to bear the majority of global fall-related mortality, only 9.1% of the economic evidence identified originated from these settings. The limited cost data from LMICs constrains evidence-based fall-prevention policy in the regions where the demographic transition is most rapid. Further investment in LMIC-specific economic research on falls among older adults would help inform resource allocation and policy in ageing low-resource settings.

articles.title: Endotracheal intubation practices, success rates and adverse events in four Dutch emergency departments: a multicentre retrospective study.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Endotracheal intubation in the emergency department (ED) is a high-risk intervention associated with significant complications. Contemporary European data on emergency airway management remain limited, and no published data are available from the Netherlands. This study aimed to describe endotracheal intubation practices, success rates, and adverse events in four Dutch EDs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing endotracheal intubation in four teaching hospital EDs in the Netherlands between January 2019 and December 2023. Patients were identified using procedure registrations, diagnostic codes, billing information and disposition records. Trained abstractors collected standardized data on patient characteristics, indications, provider characteristics, intubation techniques, medications, first-pass success and adverse events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1250 intubations were included. The most common indication was post-return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after cardiac arrest (47%), followed by neurologic pathology (14%), cardiac arrest (12%), respiratory insufficiency (8%), intoxication (8%), and trauma (5%). Emergency medicine and intensive care physicians performed most intubations. Videolaryngoscopy was the primary technique in 89.5% of cases, and etomidate was the most frequently used induction agent (73.5%). The overall first-pass success rate was 93.8% and did not differ by provider specialty or level of training. Adverse events occurred in 181 patients (14.5%), with hypotension (6.5%) and desaturation (4.7%) being most common. Increasing age (OR 1.07 per year, 95% CI 1.04-1.10) and cardiac pathology as indication for intubation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 1.03-11.88) were associated with hypotension. A higher body mass index (OR 1.08 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.13), younger age (OR 0.98 per year, 95% CI 0.96-1.00, p = 0.022) and multiple intubations attempts (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.12-7.33) were associated with desaturation. Lower pre-intubation oxygen saturation was associated with peri-intubation cardiac arrest (OR 0.96 per point, 95% CI 0.92-0.99).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study provides the first multicentre description of emergency airway management in Dutch EDs and demonstrates a distinctive emergency intubation population, characterised by a high proportion of post-ROSC intubations. Contemporary practice was characterised by widespread adoption of videolaryngoscopy, frequent use of etomidate, and high first-pass success rates. Peri-intubation hypotension and desaturation remained common and represent important targets for quality improvement.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: clinicaltrials.gov NCT06374030.

articles.title: Associations of ambient temperature and PM2.5 concentration with temporal variability in emergency department visits for acute gastrointestinal illnesses in central Bangkok, Thailand: a 5-year retrospective analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The combined effects of temperature and air pollution on acute gastrointestinal (GI) illnesses remain underexplored in tropical settings. This study examined the association between ambient temperature, fine particulate matter (PM2.5), and emergency department (ED) visits for gastritis and gastroenteritis in Bangkok, Thailand.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis of ED visits from 2018 to 2023 at a large urban hospital in Bangkok, Thailand. The effects of heat index (HI) levels and daily PM2.5 were assessed using generalized additive and distributed lag non-linear models, with stratified analyses to explore interaction effects.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Higher HI and PM2.5 levels were associated with increased acute GI-related ED visits. PM2.5 concentrations exceeding 139.8 µg/m³ were associated with elevated risk compared with the mean daily level. Conversely, HI below 30 °C was linked with a lower cumulative risk. Stratified models suggested that extreme heat may exacerbate the adverse impact of elevated PM2.5.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In the urban setting of Thailand, very high PM2.5 (> 139.8 µg/m³) may be associated with increased patients presenting to the ED with acute GI illnesses. The risk of increased patient counts appeared to be higher with greater PM exposure, particularly when elevated PM levels coincided with a high heat index, whereas cooler conditions appeared protective. These findings highlight the need for further investigation of interactive environmental exposures to inform public health and adapt the ED management strategies.

articles.title: Discrimination of the National Early Warning Score versus the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard for in-hospital mortality in emergency department patients with confirmed high-risk cardiovascular and aortic emergencies: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is a physiological severity score, whereas the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard is a categorical triage system used to assign treatment priority. Both use information available at first emergency department (ED) assessment, but their relative ability to discriminate mortality risk in high-risk cardiovascular and aortic emergencies has not been directly compared. We compared their discrimination for all-cause in-hospital mortality and explored a possible adjunctive role for NEWS in routine triage.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included adults presenting to the ED of a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2023 with a confirmed high-risk acute cardiovascular or aortic emergency, including acute myocardial infarction, acute pulmonary embolism, acute aortic syndrome, or aortic aneurysm. A retrospectively reconstructed NEWS (supplemental-oxygen status was unavailable and scored 0 for all patients) was calculated from data recorded at first ED triage. Triage grade, assigned by the triage nurse according to the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard, was extracted as a recorded variable. The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC) and compared using DeLong's test. Internal validation was performed by bootstrap resampling, and associations between vital signs and mortality were explored using restricted cubic splines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3,168 included patients, in-hospital mortality was 4.1% (129/3,168). NEWS showed higher discrimination for in-hospital mortality than the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage grade (AUROC 0.750 [95% CI 0.706-0.794] vs. 0.584 [95% CI 0.538-0.629]; DeLong's test P < 0.001). At the Youden-optimal threshold of NEWS ≥ 3, sensitivity was 68.2% and specificity was 71.6%. Discrimination was similar when NEWS was recalculated without the respiratory-rate component (AUROC 0.758 [95% CI 0.715-0.800]), and bootstrap internal validation showed negligible optimism. Higher NEWS was associated with increased mortality, and several vital signs showed non-linear associations with mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this retrospective single-centre cohort of patients with confirmed high-risk acute cardiovascular and aortic emergencies, a retrospectively reconstructed, incomplete NEWS discriminated all-cause in-hospital mortality better than the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard. Whether NEWS adds prognostic value beyond triage grade requires prospective evaluation. Improved physiological data recording, prospective multicentre validation, and development and external validation of an appropriate NEWS-to-risk mapping are needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: The diagnostic value of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for sepsis: to provide early warning before clinical deterioration.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's abnormal immune response to infection.Current diagnostic criteria is affected by multiple clinical factors, resulting in a diagnostic delay.Objective To investigate the diagnostic value of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in patients with sepsis, to provide a simple and practical laboratory index reference for the early diagnosis of sepsis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 18,570 patients from the MIMIC database (2015-2020). After screening, 11 858 patients were included and classified into sepsis (n = 10 145) and control (n = 1713) groups based on Sepsi3.0. Biomarkers measured within 24 h when admitted in Intensive Care Unit(ICU) before diagnosed with sepsis which were analyzed using logistic regression. Diagnostic performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.Restricted cubic spline (RCS) logistic regression model to explore the nonlinear association between MLR and the odds ratio (OR) of sepsis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: MLR and NLR in the sepsis group were significantly higher than those in the non-sepsis group (all P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified that MLR (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.40-1.74, p < 0.001) and NLR(OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02, p < 0.001) was strongly and independently associated with sepsis. The ROC curves showed that the areas under the curve of PLR, NLR and MLR levels alone and in combination for predicting sepsis were 0.496, 0.545and 0.571, respectively. The RCS identified OR for sepsis remained consistently below 1.00 when MLR was less than 0.69. Beyond this threshold, the OR increased sharply above 1.00.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified MLR and NLR were strongly and independently associated with sepsis after confounders are adjusted( P < 0.001).the markedly imbalanced study population substantially may influence ROC performance, MLR and NLR have a weak diagnostic value for sepsis as independent laboratory markers.The Restricted cubic spline logistic regression model (RCS) showed MLR > 0.69 could serve as a potential warning threshold for identifying patients at elevated sepsis risk, as simple and easy-to-obtain inflammatory ratios reducing misdiagnosis and missed diagnoses.
