articles.title: Factors influencing willingness to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation and use an automated external defibrillator: a convergent parallel mixed-methods study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study applied the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Intention-Focused Model for Bystander Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) Performance to examine the associations between attitude, perceived norms, self-efficacy and intention to perform CPR and use an automated external defibrillator (AED); the mediating role of intention and the moderating roles of knowledge, training, and barriers concerning behavioral willingness; and stakeholder perspectives regarding factors influencing willingness to perform CPR and use an AED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The present convergent parallel mixed-methods study collected quantitative and qualitative data concurrently, analyzed them independently, and integrated the data during interpretation to compare, contrast, and synthesize the findings. The quantitative strand was prioritized and involved 449 participants from a CPR program (2018-2020) who met the inclusion criteria. The quantitative data were collected using the Factors Influencing Community Willingness to Perform CPR and Use an AED (FIXED) questionnaire and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The qualitative strand involved 10 stakeholders (basic life support [BLS] instructors, healthcare staff, village community members, community leaders, nongovernmental organization [NGO] representatives) to explain and contextualize the quantitative results. The qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews and underwent deductive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Partial least squares-SEM demonstrated that self-efficacy was the strongest predictor of intention (effect size: large, β = 0.515, p < .001, f² = 0.353). Attitude was positively associated with intention despite its small effect (β = 0.206, p < .001, f² = 0.053). Perceived norms had a statistically significant but practically negligible association with intention (β = 0.094, p = .014, f² = 0.010). Intention significantly mediated the relationships between self-efficacy, attitude, perceived norms, and behavioral willingness, with self-efficacy having the strongest indirect effect. Knowledge, training, and barriers did not significantly moderate the intention and behavioral willingness relationship. Qualitative findings identified psychological factors, skill-related factors, and contextual constraints influenced behavioral willingness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Self-efficacy was the strongest factor associated with intention to perform CPR and use an AED, whereas attitude and perceived norms contributed to a lesser extent. The findings highlighted the importance of confidence-building strategies in CPR and AED education programs and supported theory-informed interventions to strengthen intention and behavioral willingness to respond to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Epidemiology, outcomes, and associated factors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Zhejiang, China: a province-wide registry study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major public health challenge with poor survival worldwide. Although previous studies have described OHCA epidemiology and outcomes in China, province-wide data comprehensively characterizing patient and arrest characteristics, clinical outcomes, and factors associated with survival and neurological recovery remain limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To characterize the epidemiology and outcomes of OHCA and identify factors associated with 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome in Zhejiang, China.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the Zhejiang Emergency Registry (ZER), a mandatory province-wide emergency medical services (EMS) registry based on Utstein-style standardized reporting in Zhejiang, China. Adult EMS-treated OHCA cases of medical etiology between January 2024 and December 2025 were included. Patient characteristics, arrest circumstances, community response, dispatcher-related factors, EMS characteristics, prehospital interventions, and clinical outcomes were described. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 17,646 EMS-treated OHCA patients, 531 (3.0%) survived to 30 days and 345 (2.0%) achieved favorable neurological outcome. Bystander CPR was performed in 47.7% of cases, while dispatcher recognition of OHCA, dispatcher-assisted CPR, and bystander automated external defibrillator (AED) use occurred in 25.1%, 20.0%, and 1.8% of cases, respectively. Home arrests accounted for 64.3% of cases and had a 30-day survival rate of 2.2%. Both 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome progressively declined with increasing EMS response time. In multivariable analysis, shockable rhythm showed the strongest association with both 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome. Younger age, witnessed arrest, bystander CPR, bystander AED use, dispatcher recognition, dispatcher-assisted CPR, and shorter EMS response time were independently associated with improved 30-day survival.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this province-wide registry study, 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcomes after OHCA remained low in Zhejiang, China. Low rates of dispatcher recognition, dispatcher-assisted CPR, and bystander AED use were observed, and outcomes declined progressively with increasing EMS response time. Several factors were independently associated with 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome. These findings provide population-level evidence to inform future quality-improvement strategies for OHCA care.

articles.title: Intravesical tranexamic acid for gross hematuria in the emergency department: a prospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Gross hematuria is a common emergency department(ED) presentation that is often managed with continuous bladder irrigation(CBI). Intravesical tranexamic acid (TXA) has been proposed as an adjunct, but supporting evidence is limited. We evaluated whether adding intravesical TXA to CBI improves the rate of ED discharge in patients with gross hematuria.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective, single-center cohort study in an academic ED between June and December 2025. Adults presenting with gross hematuria and a hematuria grading scale (HGS) score ≥ 6 were included.Treatment was assigned by calendar date rather than randomization: CBI alone on odd-numbered days and CBI plus a single 1 g intravesical TXA instillation(15-minute dwell) on even-numbered days. The primary outcome was successful hemostasis permitting ED discharge (HGS ≤ 3, no residual clots, no urology-wardadmission). Among discharged patients, secondary outcomes were irrigation fluid volume, ED length of stay, and one-week revisit. Effect estimates were reported as odds ratios (OR) or median differences with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 94 patients, 57 received CBI alone and 37received CBI+TXA; baseline characteristics were comparable. ED discharge was achieved in 45/57 (79%) versus 31/37 (84%) (OR 1.38, 95% CI 0.47-4.06;p = 0.560). Among the 76 discharged patients, there were no significant differences in irrigation fluid volume (2750 vs 2250 mL; p = 0.106), length ofstay (350 vs 365 min; p = 0.828), or revisit rates (22.2% vs 16.1%; OR 0.67, 95%CI 0.21-2.21; p = 0.512). In univariable analysis, a recurrent hematuria episode was associated with lower odds of discharge (OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.10-0.91;p = 0.028), whereas TXA was not. No systemic adverse events occurred.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Adding intravesical TXA to CBI was not associated with a statistically significant difference in ED discharge or secondary outcomes. Given the non-randomized design, limited sample size, and wide confidence intervals, these findings indicate a lack of demonstrated benefit rather than proof of no effect; larger, adequately powered randomized trials are warranted.

articles.title: Prehospital tranexamic acid in trauma and traumatic brain injury: a systematic review with meta-analysis of randomized comparative evidence.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is commonly used in trauma care to decrease bleeding, but its effectiveness and safety in prehospital settings, notably in traumatic brain injury (TBI), remain controversial. This review aimed to systematically evaluate the evidence on prehospital tranexamic acid (TXA) use in trauma and traumatic brain injury (TBI), with quantitative meta-analysis restricted to randomized comparative evidence and non-randomized evidence summarized narratively.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a systematic review with quantitative meta-analysis restricted to independent randomized comparative studies evaluating prehospital TXA versus placebo, usual care, or no TXA. Observational studies, secondary analyses, and survey studies were summarized separately and were not pooled with randomized trials in the primary efficacy or safety meta-analysis. outcomes included mortality (28/30-day, in-hospital), thromboembolic events, seizures, and neurological consequences. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane risk of bias tools for randomized controlled trials (RoB2) and non-randomized studies by Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-one reports met the broad review criteria. The RCT-only analysis of 28- or 30-day mortality included three independent parent randomized trials: PATCH-Trauma/Gruen et al. 2023, STAAMP/Guyette et al. 2021, and ROC-TXA/Rowell et al. 2020. Prehospital TXA was associated with lower 28- or 30-day mortality (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.68-0.95). The TBI mortality result was derived solely from ROC-TXA/Rowell et al. 2020 and was therefore a single-study estimate rather than a pooled estimate (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.64-1.20). In-hospital mortality was reported only by STAAMP/Guyette et al. 2021 and was also a single-study estimate (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.57-1.33). No statistically significant increase in thromboembolic events or seizures was demonstrated. However, the DVT and PE point estimates were above the null, and their wide confidence intervals did not exclude a clinically relevant increase in thromboembolic risk.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prehospital TXA may reduce 28- or 30-day mortality in selected broader trauma populations, particularly among patients at risk of hemorrhage. No statistically significant increase in thromboembolic events or seizures was demonstrated; however, clinically relevant thromboembolic harm cannot be excluded because the DVT and PE point estimates were above the null, and the confidence intervals were wide.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with wild honey poisoning: a five-year retrospective study from Nepal.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Wild honey poisoning caused by grayanotoxin-containing honey is an important toxicological emergency in the hilly and Himalayan regions of Nepal, where traditional consumption of wild honey remains common. However, systematic hospital-based data on its clinical presentation and outcomes remain limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective observational study of all eligible patients presenting with wild honey poisoning to a tertiary care hospital in eastern Nepal between January 2019 and January 2024. Demographic, clinical, management, and outcome data were extracted from medical records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-one patients were included, with a median age of 51 years (IQR, 37-58.5); 71% were male. Neurological manifestations were the most common presentation (87.1%), particularly dizziness/light-headedness (64.5%), altered sensorium (48.4%), and loss of consciousness (38.7%). The median estimated honey ingestion was 30 mL (IQR, 17.5-30), and the median time to symptom onset was 45 min (IQR, 30-60). Bradycardia (74.2%) and hypotension (58.1%) were common at presentation, with median pulse rate and blood pressure of 48 beats/min and 90/50 mmHg, respectively. Most patients received intravenous fluids (93.5%), and 58.1% received atropine. The mean hospital stay was 1.48 ± 0.85 days. Most patients recovered and were discharged (93.5%), 6.5% left against medical advice, and no deaths occurred.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Wild honey poisoning commonly presents with neurological symptoms accompanied by characteristic cardiovascular manifestations, particularly bradycardia and hypotension. Early recognition and supportive management are associated with favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Impact of a prolonged nationwide residents' strike on acute ischemic stroke care in a metropolitan city.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) requires timely management in both prehospital and in-hospital phases to optimize outcomes. In 2024, South Korea experienced a prolonged nationwide residents' strike that disrupted the healthcare system, potentially affecting AIS management. This study evaluated the impact of the residents' strike on time-to-management outcomes in patients with AIS.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective multicenter study of AIS patients who presented within 24 h of symptom onset to six major hospitals in Daegu, South Korea, between March and December in both 2023 and 2024. Clinical characteristics and management times were compared according to strike status and further analyzed by dividing patients into early and late strike phases.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 2,059 AIS patients were included. A total of 2,059 AIS patients were included. Door-to-CT time decreased after the strike (23 min vs. 20 min, p < 0.001), while door-to-IVT and door-to-EVT times did not differ significantly. Multivariable analyses also demonstrated that door-to-CT time was shorter during the post-strike period, (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.47; 95% confidence intervals [CI], 1.21-1.79) whereas door-to-IVT and door-to-EVT times remained unchanged between the pre-strike and post-strike periods. (Door-to-IVT; aOR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.29-1.02; Door-to-EVT; aOR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.45-1.20) CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter study, overall in-hospital acute ischemic stroke care timelines were largely preserved during the residents' strike, with door-to-CT time notably shortened during the strike period.

articles.title: Using the WHO Hospital Emergency Unit Assessment Tool to assess changes in Emergency Care Capacity in a United Kingdom Major Trauma Centre.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: We reviewed a Major Trauma Centre (MTC) in the UK over an Emergency Department (ED) transition using the World Health Organization (WHO) Hospital Emergency Unit Assessment Tool (HEAT). HEAT has previously been used in low- and middle-income countries. This is the first time it has been used to explore resource constraints and predict potential barriers to emergency care capacity in a higher-income country. Our primary outcome was to find any difference in emergency care capacity with a change in emergency care resources. Secondary outcomes included qualitative data collected by key informant (KI) interviews both on the suitability of the tool itself and on its use in a higher-resourced system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All areas of the MTC that impact emergency care capacity were studied, with multiple KIs in each area interviewed. The HEAT-adjusted Emergency Care Capacity Score (HEAT-ECCS) was used for quantitative analysis of the MTC's emergency care capacity. Qualitative data was collected for analysis of barriers to availability of emergency care. Data collection was before and after an ED transition in 2024, with the extension to the original ED of an additional 12-cubicle resuscitation unit and associated infrastructure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The overall HEAT-ECCS improved from 77% to 83%. Each of the 5 parameters also showed higher availability ratings, with biggest parameter improvements found in Infrastructure (83% to 93%) and Human Resources (61% to 72%). KI comments on the applicability of HEAT to this setting fell into 4 themes: 1. Equipment / process in this context. 2. Skill in this context. 3. Question clarity. 4. Streaming CONCLUSIONS: This study provides context to barriers to availability of emergency care and suggests some solutions may be found through similar ED transitions. By exploring emergency care systems from a global health perspective, using tools such as HEAT, we believe that learning can be shared between higher and lower-resourced systems, and strategies found to strengthen them.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: This study received local Research and Innovation approval, and registered as a health improvement project (reference 24HIP31) to hold interviews, store and analyse anonymised KI responses and disseminate findings through publication and conference presentation.

articles.title: Evaluation of a clinical decision support tool to promote early palliative care for seriously ill emergency department patients (PRIM-ER): a mixed-methods RE-AIM study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early initiation of palliative care improves care for patients with serious, life-limiting illness in the emergency department (ED). The Primary Palliative Care for Emergency Medicine (PRIM-ER) study aims to optimize early initiation of palliative care through the use of an electronic health record -based clinician decision support (CDS) tool (Support-ED) to identify high risk patients most likely to benefit from primary palliative care and provide clinician training and "nudges" within the emergency department setting. Best Practice Alerts (BPAs), automated notifications either interruptive or non-interruptive to help guide clinicians, were one component of the Support-ED suite.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance (RE-AIM) framework, we evaluated the Support-ED tool at the delivery-site level through mixed-methods analysis of implementation audit feedback, post-implementation surveys, and in-depth interviews with site Principal Investigators (PIs) and physician champions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 33 sites completed audit feedback and post-implementation surveys, and 7 sites participated in interviews.

abstract.label: REACH
abstract.text: Providers (Physicians, Physician Assistants and Nurse Practitioners) were considered the primary stakeholder for the intervention, followed by nurses and trainees.

abstract.label: EFFECTIVENESS
abstract.text: A majority (23/33, 70%) of site PIs said they would recommend the tool to other EDs. BPAs identifying hospice patients were most favorable.

abstract.label: ADOPTION
abstract.text: Half of the sites (n = 17) implemented more than one BPA, with 36% of sites (n = 12) implementing three BPAs. One-third of sites implemented a non-interruptive banner instead of a BPA (11/33, 33%).

abstract.label: IMPLEMENTATION
abstract.text: Overall, 82% (n = 27) of sites reported making changes to the intervention during implementation. Common barriers included providers perceived relevance, competing department priorities, and provider's alert fatigue. The COVID-19 pandemic was a facilitator in creating role relevance and a barrier due to staff turnover.

abstract.label: MAINTENANCE
abstract.text: One-year post-intervention, almost all sites (n = 31) were still using a component of the intervention and a majority (n = 26, 79%) had plans for continued use.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Health systems can effectively integrate and maintain ED-based palliative care electronic CDS tools, provided the EHR components are thoughtfully tailored and adaptable to unique workflows and environments, and are considered clinically relevant to the contexts of care and clinical end-users. Opportunities exist to optimize CDS maintenance and explore considerations.

abstract.text: Clinicaltrials.gov, NCT03424109 Registered 6 February 2018, https://classic.

abstract.text: gov/ct2/show/NCT03424109 .

articles.title: The Australian Capital Territory breathlessness intervention service (ABIS): a co-designed feasibility study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Breathlessness intervention services (BIS) coach people with chronic illness to self-manage persistent breathlessness using non-pharmacological strategies like positioning, breathing techniques and airflow. The Australian Capital Territory BIS (ABIS) Project aimed to co-design, implement and evaluate the feasibility of a home-based BIS delivered by a private physiotherapy provider. ABIS was evaluated against two goals: 1) 100 patients completing the program within 12 months; 2) ≥ 75% of patients reporting benefit on ≥ 1 outcome.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: ABIS and its evaluation framework were co-designed by persons with breathlessness, carers, clinicians and researchers. Patients were referred by GPs/medical specialists. Number of visits was tailored to patient/carer need. Evaluation used a mixed methods approach. Quantitative data consisted of process measures and clinical assessments double-purposed as outcome measures. Qualitative data included team meeting minutes and semi-structured interviews with patients, carers and referrers. The project team convened after 3-monthly plan-do-study-act (PDSA) cycles to review data and decide service refinements. Findings were integrated using the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance) Framework.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Reach: In the first 12 months, 64 patients completed the program, falling short of the 100 goal. Over 22 months, 140 patients completed ABIS (4% of the eligible population), including people who were older, less mobile and unable to access rehabilitation.

abstract.label: EFFECTIVENESS
abstract.text: All patients reported improvements on ≥ 1 outcome: 90% on activities of daily living (ADLs), 70% 'worst' breathlessness, and 68% mastery. 21% reported having avoided calling an ambulance for breathlessness using the strategies they had learned through ABIS. As participants' ADLs increased, breathlessness severity and mastery tended to worsen temporarily, with number of follow-ups being largely determined by how quickly mastery could be regained. 79% of carers reported improved confidence in supporting breathlessness. Adoption: GP engagement remained limited, with 47% referrals from specialist care.

abstract.label: IMPLEMENTATION
abstract.text: The median number of visits was 4 (range 1-6). Mean cost per-patient was AUD1,576.86. Maintenance: Most patients maintained outcomes at 3/6-month follow-up. ABIS built system-level capacity for provision of ongoing breathlessness support after the project period.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The ABIS Project offers new insights to inform community BIS design and adaptation. Future trials should compare cost-effectiveness of single- versus multi-disciplinary BIS.

articles.title: Risk of falls and delirium associated with dual orexin receptor antagonists versus benzodiazepines and Z-drugs in older adults with dementia.

abstract.text: Insomnia in older adults with dementia is commonly treated with benzodiazepines (BZDs) and Z drugs, despite safety concerns. Evidence on dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) in this population remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to compare safety outcomes of DORAs versus BZDs/Z drugs in older adults with dementia and insomnia. This retrospective observational cohort study used electronic health records from TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. From 17,226 eligible adults aged ≥65 years with dementia and insomnia, 734 matched pairs were included after propensity score matching. Participants received DORAs (suvorexant, lemborexant, or daridorexant) or BZDs/Z drugs within 1 month of dementia diagnosis. Primary outcomes were falls and delirium over 12 months. Secondary outcomes included hospitalization, mortality, and emergency department visits. Among 734 matched pairs (mean age 83.5 years; 65-66% female), DORA use was associated with significantly lower risk of falls (HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.18-0.71; P = 0.003), delirium (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.23-0.65; P < 0.001), hospitalization (HR 0.31, 95% CI 0.21-0.47; P < 0.001), and emergency department visits (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.20-0.50; P < 0.001). No significant difference in mortality was observed (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.53-1.11; P = 0.154). In conclusion, DORA was associated with substantially lower risks of falls, delirium, hospitalization, and emergency visits compared with BZDs/Z drugs in older adults with dementia. DORAs may offer a safer alternative to BZDs/Z drugs for managing insomnia in older adults with dementia, potentially reducing fall-related injuries and healthcare utilization.

articles.title: Refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmia following a suicidal massive caffeine overdose: a case report and review of emergency management.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Caffeine is one of the most widely consumed psychoactive substances worldwide and is readily accessible in tablet formulations and caffeinated beverages. Although moderate caffeine intake is generally considered safe, massive acute ingestion can result in severe toxicity involving the central nervous and cardiovascular systems. Life-threatening manifestations include seizures, profound electrolyte disturbances, metabolic derangements, and malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Because caffeine has favorable dialyzable properties, including low molecular weight, low protein binding, and a relatively small volume of distribution, extracorporeal toxin removal may play a critical therapeutic role in severe intoxication refractory to conventional supportive and antiarrhythmic management.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We report the case of a previously healthy 16-year-old Iranian adolescent girl who intentionally ingested 10.8 g of caffeine in a suicide attempt. Approximately two hours after ingestion, she presented with markedly reduced consciousness, agitation, generalized tremor, intermittent tonic/myoclonic seizure-like activity, sinus tachycardia (180-190 beats/min), hypokalemia (serum potassium 2.7 mEq/L), primary metabolic acidosis, significant rhabdomyolysis, and electrocardiographic abnormalities including mild QRS widening and QTc prolongation (~ 500 ms). Urine toxicology screening was positive for caffeine, supporting the diagnosis in conjunction with the clear ingestion history and subsequent patient confirmation. Despite early airway protection, gastrointestinal decontamination, electrolyte and acid-base correction, dual antiarrhythmic therapy with amiodarone and lidocaine, and repeated synchronized electrical cardioversion, she developed recurrent refractory sustained ventricular tachycardia, transient progression to asystole requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and persistent severe metabolic instability. Emergency intermittent hemodialysis was initiated approximately 3-4 h after emergency department arrival, resulting in rapid correction of metabolic acidosis, complete cessation of malignant ventricular arrhythmias, and sustained restoration of stable sinus rhythm. The patient subsequently demonstrated progressive neurological recovery without persistent cardiac or neurological sequelae.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the potentially catastrophic cardiovascular consequences of massive caffeine intoxication and emphasizes the importance of early recognition, aggressive supportive care, rapid correction of metabolic abnormalities, and timely escalation to extracorporeal toxin removal in refractory cases. In patients with persistent malignant ventricular arrhythmias despite optimized pharmacologic and electrical management, intermittent hemodialysis may represent a life-saving therapeutic intervention capable of rapidly reversing toxicity and improving clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Body mass index and diaphragm dysfunction in critically ill adults: a prospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Diaphragm dysfunction (DD) may be present at ICU admission or be detected during subsequent critical care. Body mass index (BMI) influences respiratory loading and diaphragm morphology, yet it has usually been treated as a descriptive characteristic or adjustment variable rather than as the exposure of primary interest. We therefore examined the association between BMI and protocol-defined DD in critically ill adults.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 221 adult ICU patients between January and June 2023. BMI was analyzed primarily as a continuous exposure; World Health Organization BMI categories were examined as exploratory analyses. The primary endpoint was DD detected at one or more scheduled ICU assessments, including day 1, defined as quiet-breathing diaphragm excursion ≤ 10 mm on bedside ultrasound. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with adjustment for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, SOFA score, mechanical ventilation, and surgery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 126 of 221 patients (57.0%; 95% CI 50.4%-63.4%) had DD detected at least once. The proportions with DD were 0.0% (95% CI 0.0%-43.4%) among 5 underweight patients, 48.0% (95% CI 38.3%-57.7%) among 98 normal-weight patients, 68.1% (95% CI 58.1%-76.6%) among 94 overweight patients, and 62.5% (95% CI 42.7%-78.8%) among 24 patients with obesity. Patients with DD had higher BMI than those without DD [25.40 (23.70-28.30) vs. 24.50 (21.50-26.40) kg/m²; P = 0.0018]. Each 1-kg/m² increase in BMI was associated with higher odds of DD in univariable analysis (OR = 1.116, 95% CI 1.034-1.204) and after prespecified adjustment (adjusted OR = 1.126, 95% CI 1.040-1.218).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Higher BMI was associated with greater odds of DD being detected during scheduled ICU assessments. Because the endpoint included DD present on day 1 and the study was observational, these findings should not be interpreted as showing that BMI causes incident DD. BMI may nevertheless identify patients in whom closer, context-aware respiratory-muscle assessment is warranted.

articles.title: Trauma undertriage at a University Hospital in North Norway: the need to look beyond mechanism of injury.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early multidisciplinary management through trauma team activation (TTA) improves outcomes for severely injured patients. Previous studies at the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) Tromsø conducted in 2006 and 2013, using Injury Severity Score (ISS) ≥ 16 as reference, found high rates of undertriage at 32% and 28% respectively. The aim of this study was to assess the current undertriage at UNN Tromsø using both ISS ≥ 16 and the New Injury Severity Score (NISS) ≥ 16 as reference.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed trauma patients admitted to UNN Tromsø in 2018 and 2023. The study included all patients met with TTA as well as all severely injured patients that did not receive TTA during the period. Data were obtained from the local trauma registry and electronic medical records. Undertriage was defined as patients with ISS ≥ 16 and no TTA, and NISS ≥ 16 and no TTA.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 527 trauma patients were included. Undertriage based on ISS was 15% overall for 2018 and 2023. When NISS ≥ 16 was applied, the undertriage increased to 18% (31/171). A total of 63% of undertriaged patients fulfilled one or more national TTA criteria but was not admitted with TTA. Low-energy falls were the predominant mechanism of injury (73%) among undertriaged patients. A total of 70% of undertriaged patients had single region injuries, and 40% had organ failure.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The undertriage rate at UNN Tromsø was 15% in 2018 and 2023, still exceeding the recommended level of < 5% according to American College of Surgeons-Committee on Trauma. Undertriage appears largely related to the system's non-compliance with trauma criteria, and injuries sustained in low-energy trauma mechanisms. Use of NISS identifies a larger group of potentially undertriaged patients, including more patients with organ failure who may benefit from TTA.

articles.title: A multilevel analysis of demographic and contextual factors associated with emergency department visits and access block in Queensland.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Studies on factors associated with emergency department (ED) use, including demographic and contextual factors such as the remoteness of the area of residence and the availability of home support programs, are scarce but may better explain ED demand than studies based only on demographic factors. Furthermore, most studies are based on the nonplausible assumption that there is no geographical variation in factors associated with ED use across states or territories.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to assess whether contextual factors related to context or the environment, in addition to demographic factors, can improve our understanding of ED use in Queensland, Australia. Spatial analyses were performed to understand the factors more likely to drive ED demand and access block (AB) in different areas of the state.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data on all ED visits in Queensland in 2021 were aggregated by 1-year age groups for each postcode of patients' residential area and matched to the corresponding denominator population as well as to demographic and contextual factors.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: When assessing factors associated with ED demand and AB, including contextual factors improved model fit compared with models comprising demographic factors only. The associations between ED visits and age appeared nonlinear. The highest rates of ED visits were observed among residents aged > 75 years, followed by those aged < 5 years and those aged 20-35 years. Across the state, a 1-year increase in patient age was associated with a 2% increase in the rates of AB. Queenslanders with low education levels are more likely to experience ED visits and AB. Residents living outside of metropolitan areas were less likely to access the ED but were more likely to experience AB when they attended the ED. Interestingly, increased numbers of Prolonged Level D GP visits (40 + minutes) and aged care places were associated with decreased rates of ED visits. Prolonged Level D GP visits were substantially more likely to be associated with reduced ED visits outside of the capital city and its neighbouring areas.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prolonged GP visits (especially in remote areas), multidisciplinary case conferences and other forms of integrated care should be considered in policies aimed at reducing ED demand.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Timing of mechanical CPR deployment and defibrillation process quality in shockable cardiac arrest: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mechanical cardiopulmonary resuscitation (mCPR) may support consistent compressions but could interfere with early defibrillation when deployed before the first shock. We examined the association between pre-shock mCPR activation and defibrillation-process quality in adults with an initial shockable rhythm.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adults resuscitated between January 2022 and December 2024. Exposure was defined as manual CPR until the first shock versus mCPR active before the first shock. The primary outcome was CPR-to-first-shock time; secondary outcomes captured rhythm-analysis-to-shock timing, shock-related pauses, chest compression fraction, and prespecified delay thresholds. Multivariable regression with marginal standardization was used, with propensity-score weighting, complete-cohort, alternative-threshold, adjudication, operational-complexity, and OHCA/IHCA interaction analyses assessing robustness.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 486 patients, 386 (79.4%) received manual CPR until the first shock and 100 (20.6%) had pre-shock mCPR. Median CPR-to-first-shock time was 112.2 seconds (Q1-Q3, 91.9-132.1) and 201.6 seconds (178.8-220.7), respectively. Pre-shock mCPR was associated with a longer CPR-to-first-shock interval (adjusted time ratio, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.74-1.93) and an adjusted absolute difference of 90.8 seconds (95% CI, 82.1-100.8). Rhythm-analysis-to-shock time, pre-shock pause, and peri-shock pause were also longer, whereas chest compression fraction was lower. The adjusted probability of first-shock delay >180 seconds was 3.0% with manual CPR and 75.9% with pre-shock mCPR. There was no strong evidence of OHCA/IHCA effect modification for the primary outcome (P interaction=0.080). Sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary findings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pre-shock mCPR activation was associated with substantial delay and interruption in the initial defibrillation sequence. In patients with a shockable rhythm, mCPR should not be initiated before the first shock when effective manual compressions can be maintained; initial defibrillation should be completed first.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Call-taker recognition of stroke and TIA in emergency calls in Region Zealand, Denmark.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Rapid recognition of stroke/transient ischaemic attack (TIA) in the emergency telephone is crucial to ensure timely intervention and direct transport to stroke centres. Our study investigated the diagnostic accuracy via the 1-1-2 emergency line (1-1-2) call-takers in Region Zealand, Denmark, and examined whether recognised cases had a higher chance of referral to a primary stroke centre and receiving thrombolysis.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: We retrospectively analysed calls linked to hospital discharge codes for stroke/TIA. Call-taker stroke/TIA suspicion was documented. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were calculated. Additionally, we calculated the relative risk of receiving intravenous thrombolysis and direct stroke-centre transport for recognised versus unrecognised calls.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 196,235 calls to 1-1-2 from 2021 to 2024, 2581 patients had confirmed stroke/TIA. Dispatcher sensitivity was 0.75, with a PPV of 0.18. Recognised patients compared to unrecognised cases had a higher chance of direct admissions to primary stroke units with a RR of 1.46 (95% CI = 1.38;1.54) and a higher chance of receiving thrombolysis with a RR of 1.43 (95% CI = 1.12;1.82).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Correct call-taker recognition of stroke/TIA was significantly associated with improved acute management, chance of thrombolysis and correct hospital pathway. A substantial proportion of stroke cases remain unrecognised. Enhanced decision-support tools could potentially improve call-taker performance and patient outcomes in Region Zealand.

articles.title: Paired case report: hypothesized association between prolonged dermal contamination and delayed lung injury after shared-source occupational nitrobenzene exposure.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nitrobenzene poisoning causes severe methemoglobinemia and multi-organ injury; lipophilicity allows accumulation in adipose tissue, which may trigger delayed lung damage. Existing literature only contains isolated single-case reports, lacking paired patients with identical chemical exposure but different dermal decontamination strategies to verify the correlation between skin contamination duration and toxic organ complications. This paired occupational poisoning case generates testable clinical and toxicological hypotheses for emergency critical care management.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: Two male workers simultaneously splashed by >99% nitrobenzene at a chemical plant in 2025 were enrolled. Patient 1 completed full-body decontamination within 3 minutes, while Patient 2 kept nitrobenzene-soaked trousers for over 2 hours with sustained occlusive skin absorption. Both presented with initial methemoglobin (MetHb) >70%. Patient 1 received timely antidote and extracorporeal therapy, had rapid MetHb clearance, no acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) or acute kidney injury (AKI), and was discharged on hospital day 30 with complete organ recovery at 2-month follow-up. Patient 2 had delayed methylene blue treatment, slower MetHb elimination, developed Berlin-criteria ARDS on day 6 requiring 6-day venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), complicated with KDIGO Stage 3 AKI, and was discharged on day 44. Serial laboratory and chest imaging confirmed more severe and prolonged organ dysfunction in Patient 2. Multiple combined interventions including methylene blue, partial blood exchange, hemoperfusion, plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy were administered to both patients.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prolonged occlusive dermal nitrobenzene contamination is potentially associated with elevated risks of delayed ARDS and severe AKI, possibly explained by the adipose toxic depot hypothesis. Immediate full-body skin decontamination is the core frontline intervention for occupational nitrobenzene exposure. For high-risk patients with delayed decontamination, early partial blood exchange and urgent consultation with ECMO-capable critical care centers are recommended. This paired observation provides rare comparative clinical data, yet large prospective cohorts are needed to validate the predictive risk markers and toxicokinetic mechanism proposed herein.

articles.title: Integrating clinical research into emergency medical services: lessons from the PreMeFen trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Clinical research in the pre-hospital setting is essential to advance evidence-based care. However, integrating research into emergency medical services (EMS) is challenging, as trial protocols must coexist with delivery of time-critical patient care. The PreMeFen randomised controlled trial, undertaken in a regional EMS system in Norway, provided an opportunity to examine operational challenges related to trial conduct and implementation through the experiences of ambulance personnel and linked trial process data.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a cross-sectional survey addressing training, motivation, communication, and experiences related to trial conduct in the pre-hospital setting. Ambulance personnel who had at least one patient in the PreMeFen trial were invited to participate. Descriptive statistics summarised survey responses. Additional data included protocol adherence, deviations, and communication logs collected during the 18-month PreMeFen trial period.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 70 invited ambulance personnel, 67 (96%) responded. Most felt well prepared following mandatory training, and 65 (97%) found training beneficial. Initial motivation to participate was high (median 8, inter quartile range (IQR) 8-10), but declined over time (median 7, IQR 5-8). Among 338 patient inclusions, 94 (28%) protocol deviations were recorded, most occurring early in the trial period, where missing measurements were the most common cause. Communication from the central study team was extensive. Although 60 (90%) felt well informed, 34 (51%) found the information excessive. Despite these challenges, 60 (90%) expressed willingness to participate in future research.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Integrating clinical research into EMS is feasible but can be operationally demanding. Adequate training, ongoing support, and balanced communication appear to be important for maintaining motivation and protocol adherence among ambulance personnel involved in clinical studies.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: The randomised controlled trial component of this study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05137184) and EudraCT (2021-000549-42).

articles.title: Road traffic injuries among older adults before and after a major earthquake: a single-center retrospective study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Road traffic injuries are a major cause of morbidity and mortality among older adults, frequently leading to prolonged hospitalization, functional decline, and loss of independence. Large-scale disasters, such as earthquakes, may act as important modifiers of mobility patterns and environmental risk exposure, potentially reshaping road traffic injury characteristics. This study aimed to compare road traffic injury patterns and short-term clinical outcomes among older adults between the pre- and post-earthquake periods.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, retrospective, hospital-based study included patients aged ≥ 65 years who presented with road traffic injuries to a tertiary emergency department during two equal 25-month periods before and after February 6, 2023. Injury mechanisms, anatomical distribution, and clinical outcomes were compared.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 427 older adults were included (pre-earthquake: 174; post-earthquake: 253), corresponding to a 1.45-fold increase in absolute case volume and an increase in the rate of traffic injury presentations from 2.3 to 2.8 per 10,000 emergency department visits in the post-earthquake period. Motorcycle-related injuries increased from 10.3% to 18.2% (p = 0.026), while in-vehicle incidents decreased from 58.0% to 47.0% (p = 0.025). Although head and neck trauma remained most common, lower extremity injuries rose significantly (29.9% vs. 41.1%; p = 0.018), as did femoral fractures (1.1% vs. 5.1%; p = 0.028). In-hospital mortality and length of stay did not significantly differ between periods.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The post-earthquake period was associated with a measurable shift in road traffic injury patterns among older adults, characterized by increased motorcycle-related trauma and a higher orthopedic injury burden without deterioration in short-term clinical outcomes. These findings underscore the need for geriatric-focused trauma preparedness, adaptive healthcare strategies, and targeted injury prevention measures during disaster recovery phases.

articles.title: Heterogeneity in diagnosing heart failure - real world data from electronic health records.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Heart failure (HF) prevalence is increasing and is relatively well described. Less is known about using tests in diagnosing HF in clinical practice. The aim of this article was to describe the diagnostic practices among incident HF patients in Estonia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Electronic health records and healthcare provision claims from 1st January 2012 to 31st December 2019 for a random sample of 10% of the Estonian population (N = 150 824) were used to retrieve data about newly diagnosed HF patients focusing on natriuretic peptide and echocardiographic testing. The incident HF was defined as the first occurrence of International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision codes I50.x or I11.0, with no occurrence of I50.x or I11.0 during the previous four years. The group differences were analysed using the Wilcoxon rank sum test for continuous variables. For categorical variables, the chi-square test and binary logistic regression, controlled for gender and age, were used.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Within one year before and after the HF diagnosis, 31.0% of patients underwent echocardiography and natriuretic peptide testing, but 40.7% did not receive either investigation. Most diagnostic assessments were performed in three months before HF diagnosis with 41% of patients receiving at least one test. We observed that patients diagnosed with HF in emergency departments were most likely to undergo at least one HF test (81,3%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In clinical practice, HF may be diagnosed in the absence of sufficient diagnostic evidence. By highlighting key shortcomings in the routine clinical diagnosis of HF, this study underscores the potential to enhance patient care (e.g. creating HF pathways).

articles.title: The khat ulcer: a silent perforation from a daily habit - a case report from East Africa.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Perforated peptic ulcer (PPU) is a critical surgical emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality. Traditional risk factors include Helicobacter pylori infection, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use, smoking, and severe physiological stress. Khat (Catha edulis) is a widely consumed plant stimulant in the Horn of Africa and the Arabian Peninsula that alters gastric physiology, delays gastric emptying, and reduces mucosal blood flow, yet its specific association with acute PPU remains underreported.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 40-year-old male driver with no prior medical history or baseline peptic ulcer symptoms presented with a 1-week history of progressive abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, and absolute constipation. Social history was notable for daily consumption of ~ 30 g of khat for five years, alongside irregular meal patterns. Examination revealed tachycardia and generalized peritonitis with guarding. Laboratory workup demonstrated prominent leukocytosis. Contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (CT) confirmed pneumoperitoneum secondary to acute perforation of a chronic anterior duodenal ulcer. The patient underwent emergency exploratory laparotomy and successful surgical repair using an omental (Graham) patch. Postoperative recovery was uneventful; he was discharged on day 7 on an 8-week oral proton-pump inhibitor regimen, tested negative for H. pylori, and was referred for behavioral khat-cessation support.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case highlights an acute perforation of a chronic peptic ulcer in a heavy khat user lacking conventional risk factors. It underscores the importance of obtaining a detailed regional substance use history and utilizing targeted contrast-enhanced CT imaging when clinical or plain radiological findings require definitive surgical localization. Further epidemiological studies are needed to evaluate khat habituation as an independent risk factor for peptic ulcer complications.

articles.title: Clinicoepidemiological profile and outcome of geriatric trauma in the emergency department of tertiary care centre - an ambispective observational study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Geriatric trauma is a major public health concern in low- and middle-income countries such as India, where population aging, high-energy motor vehicle collisions, and increasing comorbidities contribute to disproportionate morbidity and mortality among older adults. Older patients exhibit atypical physiological responses and reduced physiologic reserve; however, Indian data on their emergency department (ED) presentations and outcome predictors remain limited. This study aimed to describe the clinico-epidemiological profile of geriatric trauma patients presenting to a tertiary ED and identify factors associated with in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This ambispective observational study was conducted in the emergency department (ED) of a tertiary academic hospital in South India. We enrolled consecutive trauma patients aged ≥ 60 years who presented within 24 h of injury. Data collected included demographics; injury mechanism and severity; physiological parameters; injury patterns; and scores such as the Emergency Severity Index (ESI), Injury Severity Score (ISS), Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), and Geriatric Trauma Outcome Score (GTOS). Patients were followed until hospital discharge or death. Continuous variables were assessed for normality using the Shapiro-Wilk test and visual inspection of histograms and Q-Q plots. As all were non-normally distributed, continuous variables are presented as medians with interquartile ranges (IQRs), and categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. We compared survivors and non-survivors using the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables, as appropriate. Variables with p < 0.10 on univariate analysis, along with clinically relevant factors, were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality. To minimize overfitting due to the limited number of outcome events, we restricted the number of predictors and excluded physiologically dependent variables, such as ESI and massive transfusion protocol (MTP) activation, from the final model. Multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors (VIFs); influential outliers were evaluated using Cook's distance and standardized residuals. The model was fitted using the enter method. Model calibration was assessed with the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test, and explanatory power with Cox & Snell and Nagelkerke pseudo-R² values. We report adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 360 geriatric trauma patients were included (67.8% male; median age, 65 years [IQR, 62-70]). Motor vehicle collisions were the most common injury mechanism (56.9%), followed by falls (26.4%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 11.7% (42/360), with 83.3% of deaths occurring within the first week; traumatic brain injury accounted for 73.8% of deaths. On multivariate analysis, higher ISS (AOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16), lower GCS (AOR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.58-0.87), higher pulse rate (AOR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.002-1.093), and cervical spine injury (AOR, 8.73; 95% CI, 1.1-68.5) independently predicted in-hospital mortality. GTOS showed good discrimination, with significantly higher scores among non-survivors.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this tertiary Indian ED, geriatric trauma resulted predominantly from high-velocity motor vehicle collisions and was associated with substantial early mortality, largely attributable to traumatic brain injury. Simple bedside variables (ISS, GCS, pulse rate) and geriatric-specific tools such as GTOS enabled early risk stratification. These findings highlight the need for geriatric-focused trauma protocols and system-level improvements to support rapid assessment and aggressive management in resource-limited emergency care settings.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Return to sports after pediatric brain tumors: Time to move beyond survival.

abstract.text: Brain tumors are the second most common malignancy in children and adolescents and the leading cause of cancer-related death in this population. While survival rates have improved, survivors are at risk of neurocognitive, motor, and psychosocial sequelae due to both tumor location and treatments used. Participation in sport is increasingly recognized as beneficial for functional recovery, cardiorespiratory fitness, and overall well-being in children and adolescents treated for brain tumors. However, return to play (RTP) may pose some challenges, particularly in the presence of neurosurgical devices, cranial radiotherapy, or residual neurological deficits. This narrative clinical review summarizes current evidence on the risks of sport-related injuries in pediatric brain tumor patients and survivors, highlighting factors influencing vulnerability, including treatment history and specific sport characteristics. We propose a risk-based framework for RTP evaluation emphasizing individualized coordinated assessment by pediatric oncologists, neurosurgeons, and sports medicine specialists. Protective strategies are discussed, although evidence for concussion prevention remains limited. A safe RTP should be enhanced by the here-proposed structured evaluation, balancing safety with the physical, cognitive, and psychosocial benefits of active participation. This framework aims to support clinicians and families in facilitating safe and effective reintegration of pediatric brain tumor survivors into both recreational and competitive sports.

articles.title: Approach to the Agitated or Violent Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Care for the agitated or violent trauma patient presents multiple medical, ethical, legal, and logistical challenges for the emergency physician and care team. There are multiple competing medical considerations, including identifying and treating the underlying causes of agitation, identifying and treating traumatic injuries, and treating complex metabolic or hemorrhagic derangements. These treatments are only possible once patient and staff safety have been addressed via a multimodal approach including verbal de-escalation, trauma informed care, physical restraint, and chemical sedation.

articles.title: Necrotizing fasciitis of breast: a systematic review of a potentially lethal surgical emergency.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Necrotising fasciitis (NF) is a rare surgical emergency characterized by spreading necrosis of subcutaneous tissue and fascial planes that is associated with significant systemic toxicity. The aggressive nature of this disease process correlates with its high morbidity and mortality rates.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to review the profile of patients treated for NF of the breast, as documented in the recent literature.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: In September 2025, a thorough literature search was carried out using the keywords and terms "breast necrotizing fasciitis", "breast tissue necrosis", and "necrotizing soft tissue infection of the breast" across electronic databases, including PubMed, Medline (OVID), Embase, PsycINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science. The study's five-year period was set between 2020 and 2025, and only English-language literature was taken into consideration.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 43 cases reported in 34 case reports were included in the review. Cases ranged in age from 19 to 83 years (median 47.5 years; IQR: 35-60 years), and there were 42 (97.5%) females. Breast pain and discoloration were the presenting complaints in 42 (97.7%) cases. NF in 24 (55.8%) cases was secondary in nature, and more than half (51.2%) were hemodynamically unstable upon presentation. The median delay in seeking medical care after the onset of symptoms was 7 days (IQR: 4-10 days). Aggressive surgical management, including wide debridement and various modifications of mastectomy, was undertaken in 42 cases (97%). The survival rate was about 91%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: NF of the breast is a rare surgical emergency that often gets misdiagnosed, leading to adverse outcomes. A high level of suspicion on the part of the physicians can help with prompt diagnosis, the identification of related risk factors, and implementation of appropriate treatment. The cornerstones of management include aggressive surgical removal of necrotic tissue, dedicated supportive care, and careful wound care.

articles.title: Palliative Care and Discontinuation of Resuscitative Efforts for the Trauma Patient: A Paradigm for Concurrent Care.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Trauma care is undergoing a paradigm shift toward a "concurrent care model" that aims to actively integrate palliative care principles alongside life-sustaining interventions. This review outlines current recommendations for emergency medicine clinicians on these best practices, including reframing the primary survey to assess for goal concordance, ethical discontinuation of resuscitative efforts, and management of the actively dying trauma patient. Active integration of palliative care principles during the care of trauma patients will align care with patient values and support both health care teams and families.

articles.title: Suicidal Ideation and Behavior: Development of a Real-time Data Visualization Dashboard.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Epidemiological surveillance is crucial for informed health decision-making, with data visualization playing a pivotal role. The aim was to describe the design, implementation, and use of an electronic dashboard for identifying and monitoring adult patients with "suicidal behavior" in an emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data were collected from a high-complexity hospital in Argentina. Patients were identified using the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) during each Mental Health team consultation. Two indicators were defined: (a) "suicidal ideation" (specific suicidal thoughts with or without intent to act) and (b) "suicidal behavior" (concrete actions such as actual, interrupted, or aborted suicide attempts).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the pilot, 13 patients were registered, 8 of whom were identified as positive for suicidal behavior. The dashboard, launched in January/2024, featured an intuitive interface and real-time data transmission and ensured confidentiality with restricted access. Dynamic features like filters and sliders allowed expanded searches. Time series graphs and administrative lists facilitated effective monitoring.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This innovative IT tool integrates technologies in a locally underexplored area of public health relevance, aiding in professional work organization, resource management, and patient care quality. Further research is needed to validate the tool across different settings and larger populations.

articles.title: An evaluation of the effect of ambulance strategy on patient mortality outcome from hospital systems: A simulation study in the context of industrial disaster response.

abstract.text: The management of emergencies entails efficient coordination and execution of human and material resources to lessen the effects of a disaster while simultaneously protecting both life and property, including critical infrastructure. The objective of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness and impact of ambulance dispatch strategies in a disaster response scenario. The researchers focused on a case where a mobile field hospital (MFH) was deployed to assist a regional hospital in the aftermath of an explosion in the oil and gas industry. The strategy employed by the researchers includes utilization of the agent-based modeling and simulation (ABMS) tool (NetLogo 6.3.0). This approach involves the representation of agents within a system governed by simple rules and objectives and their interactions with each other and their environment. Furthermore, the model framework was sampled and analyzed using the NetLogo BehaviorSpace, and appropriate Python libraries were then utilized to plot and perform sensitivity analysis (SA) on the dataset (Pandas, SAlib, NumPy, Matplotlib). The assessment revealed the value and promise of employing a combination of ABMS and SA techniques for the evaluation and comprehension of the impact of emergency dispatch strategies in disaster response in the oil and gas industry. The study emphasized the significance of the assessment of emergency dispatch strategies in dedicated industries. The methodologies adopted revealed the need for effective resource management, recognizing protocols for emergency scenarios while lessening deaths and simultaneously improving overall response time. The researchers propose further study and fine-tuning of their model to improve the simulation accuracy and optimize the results based on the availability of local data. There is strong evidence of substantial value in the utilization of NetLogo (ABMS) and the use of Python libraries as modeling, simulation, and evaluative instruments for emergency response in the oil and gas industries. Findings from this study established that deploying MFHs during disasters is advantageous in reducing mortality outcomes and underlined how essential policy assessment can be to refining disaster response strategies.

articles.title: Successful Implementation of Early Total Care in Polytrauma.

abstract.text: Polytrauma management demands a precise balance between early physiological stabilization and definitive anatomical restoration. While damage control orthopedics (DCO) uses a staged approach to avoid physiological overload, it can increase hospital stay and risks like infection, joint stiffness and muscle contractures. Early total care (ETC) involves the definitive fixation of all injuries in a single surgical setting. We present a case of a 27-year-old male who sustained polytrauma following a road traffic accident under the influence of alcohol. Following successful initial resuscitation by an interdisciplinary team of emergency physicians, surgeons, and anesthesiologists, the patient underwent early total care incorporating dynamic hip screw fixation, interlocking nailing, Ilizarov fixation, and pinning. The management results in an uneventful intraoperative and postoperative course. This case highlights that with rigorous multidisciplinary resuscitation and precise patient selection, single-stage early total care remains a safe, highly effective strategy to optimize early outcomes and streamline recovery in complex polytrauma.

articles.title: Emergency Preparedness for Dialysis Nurses: Optimizing Emergency Crash Cart Readiness.
articles.journal_full: Nephrology nursing journal : journal of the American Nephrology Nurses' Association

abstract.text: Medical emergencies in the outpatient dialysis setting can occur without warning, requiring an immediate, coordinated, and competent response from the health care team. Patient outcomes depend on emergency preparedness, including a fully stocked and maintained emergency crash cart, properly functioning equipment, well-trained staff, effective registered nurse (RN) leadership, and the ability to recognize and anticipate clinical deterioration. This article highlights the essential components of emergency readiness in the outpatient dialysis clinic and emphasizes the RN's critical role in coordinating emergency care. Through a series of case studies, we examine real-world emergency scenarios that demonstrate how preparedness, rapid assessment, timely intervention, teamwork, and clinical decision-making contribute to successful patient outcomes. Practical strategies for strengthening emergency preparedness and fostering a culture of safety within outpatient dialysis facilities are also discussed.

articles.title: Face-Blind but Cyborg-Sighted: Immunological Barriers to the Patient-Paramedic Articulation.

abstract.text: Immunity is the body's concept of recognizing where one's self ends and non-self begins. The paramedic (oneself)/patient (non-self) barrier has long been institutionalized; healthcare workers are trained to disarticulate from the patient to reduce physical and infectious harm to self. Harm may include psychological trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder, especially routinely witnessing people in distress. Using magical realism in experimental autoethnographic reflection, the author applies established conceptualizations of "articulation" to his experiences as a prosopagnosiac, transgender person, and paramedic while exploring how applying the Science and Technology Studies concept of "articulation" to healthcare can reduce trauma in care settings.

articles.title: Stability study of performance impairing drugs in whole blood and urine.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Screening for performance impairing drugs in postmortem biological specimens of air crash victims is important to formulate guidelines for collection, preservation, and dispatch of autopsy specimens, as well as for better interpretation of the results.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In the present study, the stability of 20 different drugs from antihypertensive groups and from miscellaneous drug groups were spiked in blood and urine and their stability studied at different time intervals (0 hrs, 24 hrs, 48hr, and 72 hrs) post storage at 4 °C and room temperature. The percentage decrease in the concentration was calculated for all drugs both in blood and urine stored at 4 °C and room temperature after estimation of the concentration at different intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The results revealed that the stability of most of the drugs was affected post incubation at different storage conditions, both in blood and urine matrix. A clear trend in the degradation of all most all drugs was observed as the storage time interval increases. There is slight decrease in the concentration of all drugs stored at room temperature as compared to the degradation of drugs stored at 4 °C. The variation among the different groups of drugs and individual drugs has been explained in the discussion.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The results of the present study will help in the formulation of suitable guidelines for proper collection, preservation, and dispatch of autopsy specimens in stipulated time for analysis but also give valuable guidance for interpretation of results.
